docs.text: Checklist: migrate an existing driver ¶ Use this to move a driver from an older repository (for example a HardFOC hf-<chip>-driver ) to a new driver-<chip> built from the template. It adds the migration steps to the new driver checklist, which still applies in full. It was written during the first migrations (AS5047U over SPI, PCAL9555A over I2C, then the AT25040B EEPROM) and is updated with each one. The principle: the old repository is a source of chip knowledge : the register map, the protocol, the timing and the procedures the datasheet asks for. Its API, error model and structure are not carried over; the new driver is written on the template's architecture, and the old repository stays untouched until every driver has moved. Drivers that are already proven on hardware ¶ Some old drivers run in shipped or bench-tested firmware that used them: its hardware records cover the MAX22200, the TLE92466ED, the TMC9660, the ADS7952 and the PCAL9555A, partly the AT25040, and leave others (the AS5047U among them) with none. That evidence belongs to the old code at a given commit, on a given board, by a given procedure . A rewritten driver is new code: it inherits the knowledge, never the verification. So for a proven driver the migration adds four things: Record the evidence as it is. docs/limitations.md of the new repository lists, per chip, what was verified on hardware, with which old repository and commit, which board, which procedure and which evidence folder, and says plainly that it applies to the old driver until the new one is verified the same way. Keep every quirk the hardware taught. Comments such as "workaround", "errata", "second write", the firmware's retries and its call sites are chip knowledge (step 2). Each one becomes a fault in the chip model and a test, or a documented reason it no longer applies. Example: acknowledged writes to the PCAL9555A were lost on hardware with the old driver, so the model can drop writes and the driver reads each write back ( WriteMismatch ). Fit the firmware's real use. Before the API is final, list how the firmware's handler calls the old driver (which calls, how often, from which thread, what it does on error) and check the new API covers each one, or name the replacement. A call the firmware depends on and the new driver lacks blocks the merge (the PCAL9555A migration found four: output-latch read-back, a verified write, variant choice, retry guidance). Verify on the same bench before claiming it. The status stays "not yet verified on hardware" until the new driver runs behind the same handler on the same board, through the same procedure, and its evidence folder is linked from docs/limitations.md with the driver's commit. Only then does the README's status say "verified on hardware: , ". Order the migrations so that a proven driver is moved when its firmware user can take the new version to the bench soon after; a driver with no hardware user can move at any time. ### 0. Before starting - [ ] Hardware evidence found and recorded (section above): old commit, board, procedure, evidence folder; and the firmware's handler and call sites read - [ ] Licence and authorship of the old code checked ( `LICENSE` , `git log --format='%an <%ae>' | sort | uniq -c` ). Relicensing (for example GPL-3.0 to MIT) needs every copyright holder's agreement; commits made with an employer address may belong to the employer. Record the decision in the tracking issue before the repository is made public - [ ] The chip's real part number decided; it becomes the repository name, the namespace and every file name (an old repository name may be misspelt: `hf-pcal95555-driver` drives the PCAL9555A) - [ ] Datasheet URL and revision noted; the PDF is never copied (ADR-0019) ### 1. Scaffold (no chip code yet) - [ ] `gh repo create kokeb-labs/driver-<chip> --private --template kokeb-labs/driver-template` ; public only after the licence decision and the first green CI - [ ] `git switch -c feat/initial-driver` , then `python3 tools/setup.py --non-interactive --bus <bus> --description "..." --datasheet <url>` - [ ] The scaffold's own host tests pass; commit that state alone ( `git commit -s -m "Scaffold <CHIP> from driver-template"` ) ### 2. Extract the chip knowledge from the old driver - [ ] Register addresses, field positions and reset values (cross-checked against the datasheet, figure by figure) - [ ] Frame or transaction format, CRC or PEC, read latency (for example "the reply answers the previous frame") - [ ] Timing: power-up, reset, conversion, programming times - [ ] Multi-step procedures (OTP or NVM burn, calibration) with their datasheet step numbers - [ ] Error and status bits, and which of them mean "the value is not a measurement" - [ ] The bus's burst semantics (auto-increment, or a pointer that toggles within a register pair) and the longest burst the driver needs ( `kMaxBurst` ) - [ ] For a family with variants (PCA9555 and PCAL9555A): what the datasheets guarantee about a register a variant lacks. Configure the variant ( `Config` field) unless detection is guaranteed, and never write a register before the variant is confirmed - [ ] Old behaviour that is deliberately dropped is listed in the PR (for example `printf` dumps, retry parameters, sticky global flags, `std::function` callbacks) ### 3. Write the driver, in this order - [ ] `inc/<chip>_registers.hpp` : addresses, masks and shifts as `constexpr` ; no bit-field unions (their layout depends on the compiler) - [ ] `inc/<chip>_types.hpp` : base `Error` set unchanged; chip-specific values from 16, each returned somewhere; unreturned base values listed on the API guide; `Config{}` equals the chip's reset state; `Validate()` - [ ] `inc/<chip>_<bus>_interface.hpp` : the bus's standard hooks; remove hooks the chip has no use for. No reset pin: delete `CtrlPin` , `GpioSignal` , `GpioSet` , the `DeclaresGpioSet` / `HasGpioSet` concepts, `HardwareReset()` , `pulseResetPin()` and the `gpio_set_returns_void` compile-fail test - [ ] `DelayUs` stays required only if some call waits (a reset, a conversion, a programming time); then the `port_without_delay` compile-fail test calls that operation. A chip with no timed procedure drops the hook, the `detail::DelayUs` helper and the test - [ ] I2C: replace the scaffold's default address ( `0x48` ) with the chip's, and check the address range in `EnsureInitialized()` ( `InvalidArgument` , no I/O) - [ ] Lifecycle per [ ADR-0021 ]( ../adr/0021-one-start-up-entry-point.md ): `Config` is the constructor's last parameter, the start-up is a private `initialize()` , `EnsureInitialized()` is the only public start - [ ] A chip with neither an ID register nor a reset (a GPIO expander): the identity check is "write every register, read every one back", and the missing reset and ID are listed as deviations on the Contract page - [ ] `Validate()` returns `InvalidArgument` , or `Unsupported` for a setting the configured variant lacks - [ ] `inc/<chip>.hpp` and `src/<chip>.ipp` : every fallible call returns `Result<T>` ; every port failure propagates; destructive operations need an explicit confirmation argument - [ ] A `Config` flag that leaves the chip's settings alone (an OTP- or NVM-programmed part) also reads them back into `GetConfig()` , so a later setter cannot write defaults over the programmed values - [ ] Every register field the chip has is a `Config` field or deliberately kept as read (Dia bits, reserved); none is silently cleared by a write - [ ] Multi-step procedures with a compare step use the protected frame format for every frame, reads included - [ ] `tests/mock_<chip>.hpp` : a model at the protocol level (frames, latency, CRC, clear-on-read registers, timed procedures) with fault injection, not a register array. It has its own register map with datasheet page references and does not include `<chip>_registers.hpp` ; `tests/test_model.cpp` static_asserts the two maps against each other (KB-TST-030) - [ ] Every header has the KB-CPP-019 include guard ( `python checks/source_checks.py guard --repo . <path>` from the handbook prints it); no `#pragma once` is left - [ ] `inc/<chip>_<bus>_interface.hpp` declares the bus requirements as `constexpr` (KB-CPP-123), the Porting page lists them, and each example port static_asserts its settings against them - [ ] A single-shot raw access and a `GetLast*()` accessor (KB-CPP-129); clear-on-read flags ORed into one latch with `GetLatched*()` / `ClearLatched*()` (KB-CPP-119) - [ ] The hardware-proven rules on the driver contract: replies proven before they are decoded, line patterns refused, resync after a failed transfer, idempotent bounded retries, setters that change only what they name, start-up that waits for ready and clears inherited faults ([driver.md](../standards/driver.md#replies-retries-and-resynchronisation)) ### 4. Tests - [ ] Behaviour of every public call, including each error it documents - [ ] The lifecycle: a second `EnsureInitialized()` does no I/O, a failed start is retried, reads before the start return `NotInitialized` and send nothing, `Deinitialize()` then `EnsureInitialized()` restarts, `ApplyConfig()` before the start stores without I/O - [ ] `test_bus_faults.cpp` : every transfer of every operation failed in turn, each reported as `Bus` - [ ] `test_errors.cpp` : each chip-specific error produced by a real call - [ ] `test_kconfig.cpp` and `_config/Kconfig` : only options that map to `Config` fields - [ ] Compile-fail tests for every compile-time contract that remains (missing hook, wrong signature) - [ ] `tests/docs/*.cpp` : every snippet the pages show, rewritten for the new API - [ ] `tests/fuzz/fuzz_<chip>.cpp` : the bus under the fuzzer's control (failed, corrupted, replaced and, where the bus allows it, lost transfers), the driver's promises checked after every call, the corpus replayed as a CTest; every crash it finds is fixed with a unit test and kept as a `regress-*` input - [ ] Every quirk found on hardware is a fault in the model and a test (section above) ### 5. Local gates (the same tools and versions as CI) - [ ] A few GB free on the disk: the coverage, clang-tidy and docs builds each create their own build directory - [ ] `ctest` passes with GCC and Clang - [ ] clang-format 20.1.8 clean over `.hpp` , `.cpp` and `.ipp` . It reflows tables inside comment blocks into one paragraph: wrap a Doxygen comment that holds a table in `// clang-format off` / `// clang-format on` - [ ] clang-tidy 20.1.0 clean with the compile database. CI runs it on Linux (libstdc++), which reports checks a macOS run (libc++) misses, such as `modernize-use-std-numbers` and `modernize-use-integer-sign-comparison` : treat CI's lint as the authority ( `-DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON -D<CHIP>_BUILD_TESTS=ON` ); intentional findings in tests (out-of-range enum casts that test `Validate()` ) carry a `NOLINT` with the check name - [ ] lizard 1.24.1 with the files listed explicitly ( `inc/*.hpp src/*.ipp` ): within the level's limits - [ ] gcovr 8.7 on GCC `-O0 --coverage -fcondition-coverage` over every CTest binary, with `--merge-lines` as CI uses (ci-tools 1.5.2): at or above the level's floors. Without it each template instance counts separately - [ ] `ru-handbook-check` locally: `python3 tools/handbook_check/handbook_check.py --repo .` from ci-tools, 0 errors - [ ] The handbook's source checks: `python3 checks/source_checks.py scan --repo <driver>` from the handbook, 0 findings (include guards, bus requirements, raw access) ### 6. Documentation - [ ] Every page rewritten for the chip; nothing about the template's example chip remains, in `.claude/skills/` too (including `new-driver-from-template` ) - [ ] Facts from the datasheet text, not from memory: a fetched PDF comes back as raw data, so extract it locally ( `pdftotext -layout` ) and cite sections and figures - [ ] Chip-specific pages added where the chip needs them (an OTP or calibration procedure) - [ ] `kokeb-docs figures && kokeb-docs gen && kokeb-docs check` , `mkdocs build --strict` , markdownlint - [ ] Hardware-dependent statements marked **not verified on hardware** , with bench steps ### 7. Pull request and release - [ ] PR from `feat/initial-driver` lists: what was carried over, what was dropped and why, the gate figures (coverage, complexity) and the hardware steps still to run - [ ] `CI gate / gate` green - [ ] Owner applies [ repository setup ]( https://github.com/kokeb-labs/driver-template/blob/main/docs/repo-setup.md ) and decides visibility; `v0.1.0` released through the gated flow - [ ] The old repository is not archived or deleted until every driver has moved and kb-core is in place; its README may point to the new repository What the pilots found ¶ Finding Where it was fixed lizard skips .ipp files in a directory, so the complexity gate never measured a header-only implementation ci-tools 1.5.1 lists the files itself The lint default extensions left .ipp out of clang-format ci-tools 1.5.1 default, template lint caller Coverage counted each template instance separately: a happy-path example made failure paths look untested (73.8 % instead of 94.5 % of branches) ci-tools 1.5.2 ( --merge-lines ) clang-tidy on Linux reports checks a macOS run misses Step 5: CI's lint is the authority Two public start-up calls ( Initialize , EnsureInitialized ) ADR-0021: one entry point A GPIO expander has no ID register and no reset Step 3: write-and-read-back identity, deviations recorded An old repository name was misspelt ( pcal95555 ) Step 0: decide the real part number first Old drivers are GPL-3.0, some commits under an employer address Step 0: licence decision before going public clang-format merged the rows of the hook tables in the Doxygen comments (the template has the same) Step 5 note; template fix A burned part's settings were overwritten by the first setter after write_settings = false Step 3: read the settings back The OTP compare reads ran without CRC in 16-bit mode Step 3: protected frames for the whole procedure The fuzzer found that a lost data frame of a two-frame write turned the next command into data: losing "PROG = PROGOTP" let the next read burn the AS5047U's OTP Driver: a NOP read after any failed transfer; step 4: fuzz every driver SetZeroHere() left the zero at 0 when its angle read failed (fuzzer) Driver: restore the old zero; a failed call has no side effect The firmware checks the PCAL9555A's output latch after every write because the bench lost acknowledged writes Driver: read-back calls and verify_writes ; section above The port's Log() hook was a C variadic function, and the examples passed driver text as a format string Plain-text hook; clang-tidy cert-* A dead bus passed the old EEPROM probe: a MISO floating low reads 0x00, the same as an idle AT25040B, twice Driver: an active identity check (toggle the write enable latch, which a stuck line cannot follow); step 3: prefer a check the chip must answer over one a line can fake One status byte lost to noise read "idle" during a write cycle, so a read went ahead and returned the busy chip's 0xFF as data (fuzzer) Driver: an idle status counts only when a second read confirms it The old handler released WP for every probe and read and parked it only after a successful write Driver: WP raised only for a write, parked after on success and failure; the fuzzer checks "WP parked after every call" The scaffold wrote "EEPROMs It follows" when the description had no full stop driver-template: the description gets a full stop in AGENTS.md README docs and API links pointed at GitHub Pages, which a private repository on the free plan does not serve README links to docs/ ; docs.text: Use this to move a driver from an older repository (for example a HardFOC hf-<chip>-driver ) to a new driver-<chip> built from the template. It adds the migration steps to the new driver checklist, which still applies in full. It was written during the first migrations (AS5047U over SPI, PCAL9555A over I2C, then the AT25040B EEPROM) and is updated with each one. The principle: the old repository is a source of chip knowledge : the register map, the protocol, the timing and the procedures the datasheet asks for. Its API, error model and structure are not carried over; the new driver is written on the template's architecture, and the old repository stays untouched until every driver has moved.
docs.title: Checklist: migrate an existing driver

docs.text: Some old drivers run in shipped or bench-tested firmware that used them: its hardware records cover the MAX22200, the TLE92466ED, the TMC9660, the ADS7952 and the PCAL9555A, partly the AT25040, and leave others (the AS5047U among them) with none. That evidence belongs to the old code at a given commit, on a given board, by a given procedure . A rewritten driver is new code: it inherits the knowledge, never the verification. So for a proven driver the migration adds four things: Record the evidence as it is. docs/limitations.md of the new repository lists, per chip, what was verified on hardware, with which old repository and commit, which board, which procedure and which evidence folder, and says plainly that it applies to the old driver until the new one is verified the same way. Keep every quirk the hardware taught. Comments such as "workaround", "errata", "second write", the firmware's retries and its call sites are chip knowledge (step 2). Each one becomes a fault in the chip model and a test, or a documented reason it no longer applies. Example: acknowledged writes to the PCAL9555A were lost on hardware with the old driver, so the model can drop writes and the driver reads each write back ( WriteMismatch ). Fit the firmware's real use. Before the API is final, list how the firmware's handler calls the old driver (which calls, how often, from which thread, what it does on error) and check the new API covers each one, or name the replacement. A call the firmware depends on and the new driver lacks blocks the merge (the PCAL9555A migration found four: output-latch read-back, a verified write, variant choice, retry guidance). Verify on the same bench before claiming it. The status stays "not yet verified on hardware" until the new driver runs behind the same handler on the same board, through the same procedure, and its evidence folder is linked from docs/limitations.md with the driver's commit. Only then does the README's status say "verified on hardware: , ". Order the migrations so that a proven driver is moved when its firmware user can take the new version to the bench soon after; a driver with no hardware user can move at any time. ### 0. Before starting - [ ] Hardware evidence found and recorded (section above): old commit, board, procedure, evidence folder; and the firmware's handler and call sites read - [ ] Licence and authorship of the old code checked ( `LICENSE` , `git log --format='%an <%ae>' | sort | uniq -c` ). Relicensing (for example GPL-3.0 to MIT) needs every copyright holder's agreement; commits made with an employer address may belong to the employer. Record the decision in the tracking issue before the repository is made public - [ ] The chip's real part number decided; it becomes the repository name, the namespace and every file name (an old repository name may be misspelt: `hf-pcal95555-driver` drives the PCAL9555A) - [ ] Datasheet URL and revision noted; the PDF is never copied (ADR-0019) ### 1. Scaffold (no chip code yet) - [ ] `gh repo create kokeb-labs/driver-<chip> --private --template kokeb-labs/driver-template` ; public only after the licence decision and the first green CI - [ ] `git switch -c feat/initial-driver` , then `python3 tools/setup.py --non-interactive --bus <bus> --description "..." --datasheet <url>` - [ ] The scaffold's own host tests pass; commit that state alone ( `git commit -s -m "Scaffold <CHIP> from driver-template"` ) ### 2. Extract the chip knowledge from the old driver - [ ] Register addresses, field positions and reset values (cross-checked against the datasheet, figure by figure) - [ ] Frame or transaction format, CRC or PEC, read latency (for example "the reply answers the previous frame") - [ ] Timing: power-up, reset, conversion, programming times - [ ] Multi-step procedures (OTP or NVM burn, calibration) with their datasheet step numbers - [ ] Error and status bits, and which of them mean "the value is not a measurement" - [ ] The bus's burst semantics (auto-increment, or a pointer that toggles within a register pair) and the longest burst the driver needs ( `kMaxBurst` ) - [ ] For a family with variants (PCA9555 and PCAL9555A): what the datasheets guarantee about a register a variant lacks. Configure the variant ( `Config` field) unless detection is guaranteed, and never write a register before the variant is confirmed - [ ] Old behaviour that is deliberately dropped is listed in the PR (for example `printf` dumps, retry parameters, sticky global flags, `std::function` callbacks) ### 3. Write the driver, in this order - [ ] `inc/<chip>_registers.hpp` : addresses, masks and shifts as `constexpr` ; no bit-field unions (their layout depends on the compiler) - [ ] `inc/<chip>_types.hpp` : base `Error` set unchanged; chip-specific values from 16, each returned somewhere; unreturned base values listed on the API guide; `Config{}` equals the chip's reset state; `Validate()` - [ ] `inc/<chip>_<bus>_interface.hpp` : the bus's standard hooks; remove hooks the chip has no use for. No reset pin: delete `CtrlPin` , `GpioSignal` , `GpioSet` , the `DeclaresGpioSet` / `HasGpioSet` concepts, `HardwareReset()` , `pulseResetPin()` and the `gpio_set_returns_void` compile-fail test - [ ] `DelayUs` stays required only if some call waits (a reset, a conversion, a programming time); then the `port_without_delay` compile-fail test calls that operation. A chip with no timed procedure drops the hook, the `detail::DelayUs` helper and the test - [ ] I2C: replace the scaffold's default address ( `0x48` ) with the chip's, and check the address range in `EnsureInitialized()` ( `InvalidArgument` , no I/O) - [ ] Lifecycle per [ ADR-0021 ]( ../adr/0021-one-start-up-entry-point.md ): `Config` is the constructor's last parameter, the start-up is a private `initialize()` , `EnsureInitialized()` is the only public start - [ ] A chip with neither an ID register nor a reset (a GPIO expander): the identity check is "write every register, read every one back", and the missing reset and ID are listed as deviations on the Contract page - [ ] `Validate()` returns `InvalidArgument` , or `Unsupported` for a setting the configured variant lacks - [ ] `inc/<chip>.hpp` and `src/<chip>.ipp` : every fallible call returns `Result<T>` ; every port failure propagates; destructive operations need an explicit confirmation argument - [ ] A `Config` flag that leaves the chip's settings alone (an OTP- or NVM-programmed part) also reads them back into `GetConfig()` , so a later setter cannot write defaults over the programmed values - [ ] Every register field the chip has is a `Config` field or deliberately kept as read (Dia bits, reserved); none is silently cleared by a write - [ ] Multi-step procedures with a compare step use the protected frame format for every frame, reads included - [ ] `tests/mock_<chip>.hpp` : a model at the protocol level (frames, latency, CRC, clear-on-read registers, timed procedures) with fault injection, not a register array. It has its own register map with datasheet page references and does not include `<chip>_registers.hpp` ; `tests/test_model.cpp` static_asserts the two maps against each other (KB-TST-030) - [ ] Every header has the KB-CPP-019 include guard ( `python checks/source_checks.py guard --repo . <path>` from the handbook prints it); no `#pragma once` is left - [ ] `inc/<chip>_<bus>_interface.hpp` declares the bus requirements as `constexpr` (KB-CPP-123), the Porting page lists them, and each example port static_asserts its settings against them - [ ] A single-shot raw access and a `GetLast*()` accessor (KB-CPP-129); clear-on-read flags ORed into one latch with `GetLatched*()` / `ClearLatched*()` (KB-CPP-119) - [ ] The hardware-proven rules on the driver contract: replies proven before they are decoded, line patterns refused, resync after a failed transfer, idempotent bounded retries, setters that change only what they name, start-up that waits for ready and clears inherited faults ([driver.md](../standards/driver.md#replies-retries-and-resynchronisation)) ### 4. Tests - [ ] Behaviour of every public call, including each error it documents - [ ] The lifecycle: a second `EnsureInitialized()` does no I/O, a failed start is retried, reads before the start return `NotInitialized` and send nothing, `Deinitialize()` then `EnsureInitialized()` restarts, `ApplyConfig()` before the start stores without I/O - [ ] `test_bus_faults.cpp` : every transfer of every operation failed in turn, each reported as `Bus` - [ ] `test_errors.cpp` : each chip-specific error produced by a real call - [ ] `test_kconfig.cpp` and `_config/Kconfig` : only options that map to `Config` fields - [ ] Compile-fail tests for every compile-time contract that remains (missing hook, wrong signature) - [ ] `tests/docs/*.cpp` : every snippet the pages show, rewritten for the new API - [ ] `tests/fuzz/fuzz_<chip>.cpp` : the bus under the fuzzer's control (failed, corrupted, replaced and, where the bus allows it, lost transfers), the driver's promises checked after every call, the corpus replayed as a CTest; every crash it finds is fixed with a unit test and kept as a `regress-*` input - [ ] Every quirk found on hardware is a fault in the model and a test (section above) ### 5. Local gates (the same tools and versions as CI) - [ ] A few GB free on the disk: the coverage, clang-tidy and docs builds each create their own build directory - [ ] `ctest` passes with GCC and Clang - [ ] clang-format 20.1.8 clean over `.hpp` , `.cpp` and `.ipp` . It reflows tables inside comment blocks into one paragraph: wrap a Doxygen comment that holds a table in `// clang-format off` / `// clang-format on` - [ ] clang-tidy 20.1.0 clean with the compile database. CI runs it on Linux (libstdc++), which reports checks a macOS run (libc++) misses, such as `modernize-use-std-numbers` and `modernize-use-integer-sign-comparison` : treat CI's lint as the authority ( `-DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON -D<CHIP>_BUILD_TESTS=ON` ); intentional findings in tests (out-of-range enum casts that test `Validate()` ) carry a `NOLINT` with the check name - [ ] lizard 1.24.1 with the files listed explicitly ( `inc/*.hpp src/*.ipp` ): within the level's limits - [ ] gcovr 8.7 on GCC `-O0 --coverage -fcondition-coverage` over every CTest binary, with `--merge-lines` as CI uses (ci-tools 1.5.2): at or above the level's floors. Without it each template instance counts separately - [ ] `ru-handbook-check` locally: `python3 tools/handbook_check/handbook_check.py --repo .` from ci-tools, 0 errors - [ ] The handbook's source checks: `python3 checks/source_checks.py scan --repo <driver>` from the handbook, 0 findings (include guards, bus requirements, raw access) ### 6. Documentation - [ ] Every page rewritten for the chip; nothing about the template's example chip remains, in `.claude/skills/` too (including `new-driver-from-template` ) - [ ] Facts from the datasheet text, not from memory: a fetched PDF comes back as raw data, so extract it locally ( `pdftotext -layout` ) and cite sections and figures - [ ] Chip-specific pages added where the chip needs them (an OTP or calibration procedure) - [ ] `kokeb-docs figures && kokeb-docs gen && kokeb-docs check` , `mkdocs build --strict` , markdownlint - [ ] Hardware-dependent statements marked **not verified on hardware** , with bench steps ### 7. Pull request and release - [ ] PR from `feat/initial-driver` lists: what was carried over, what was dropped and why, the gate figures (coverage, complexity) and the hardware steps still to run - [ ] `CI gate / gate` green - [ ] Owner applies [ repository setup ]( https://github.com/kokeb-labs/driver-template/blob/main/docs/repo-setup.md ) and decides visibility; `v0.1.0` released through the gated flow - [ ] The old repository is not archived or deleted until every driver has moved and kb-core is in place; its README may point to the new repository

docs.text: Finding Where it was fixed lizard skips .ipp files in a directory, so the complexity gate never measured a header-only implementation ci-tools 1.5.1 lists the files itself The lint default extensions left .ipp out of clang-format ci-tools 1.5.1 default, template lint caller Coverage counted each template instance separately: a happy-path example made failure paths look untested (73.8 % instead of 94.5 % of branches) ci-tools 1.5.2 ( --merge-lines ) clang-tidy on Linux reports checks a macOS run misses Step 5: CI's lint is the authority Two public start-up calls ( Initialize , EnsureInitialized ) ADR-0021: one entry point A GPIO expander has no ID register and no reset Step 3: write-and-read-back identity, deviations recorded An old repository name was misspelt ( pcal95555 ) Step 0: decide the real part number first Old drivers are GPL-3.0, some commits under an employer address Step 0: licence decision before going public clang-format merged the rows of the hook tables in the Doxygen comments (the template has the same) Step 5 note; template fix A burned part's settings were overwritten by the first setter after write_settings = false Step 3: read the settings back The OTP compare reads ran without CRC in 16-bit mode Step 3: protected frames for the whole procedure The fuzzer found that a lost data frame of a two-frame write turned the next command into data: losing "PROG = PROGOTP" let the next read burn the AS5047U's OTP Driver: a NOP read after any failed transfer; step 4: fuzz every driver SetZeroHere() left the zero at 0 when its angle read failed (fuzzer) Driver: restore the old zero; a failed call has no side effect The firmware checks the PCAL9555A's output latch after every write because the bench lost acknowledged writes Driver: read-back calls and verify_writes ; section above The port's Log() hook was a C variadic function, and the examples passed driver text as a format string Plain-text hook; clang-tidy cert-* A dead bus passed the old EEPROM probe: a MISO floating low reads 0x00, the same as an idle AT25040B, twice Driver: an active identity check (toggle the write enable latch, which a stuck line cannot follow); step 3: prefer a check the chip must answer over one a line can fake One status byte lost to noise read "idle" during a write cycle, so a read went ahead and returned the busy chip's 0xFF as data (fuzzer) Driver: an idle status counts only when a second read confirms it The old handler released WP for every probe and read and parked it only after a successful write Driver: WP raised only for a write, parked after on success and failure; the fuzzer checks "WP parked after every call" The scaffold wrote "EEPROMs It follows" when the description had no full stop driver-template: the description gets a full stop in AGENTS.md README docs and API links pointed at GitHub Pages, which a private repository on the free plan does not serve README links to docs/ ; the site link waits for the repository to be public

docs.text: Checklist: new board HAL ¶ Copy this list into the tracking issue for a new board HAL. Board HALs live in the product's organization or repository. hal.md is the contract. ### Repository - [ ] Created from `kokeb-labs/board-hal-template` when it exists, else from the example in `kb-hal-common` ; named for the board in the product's organization; settings and rulesets applied there - [ ] Submodules `lib/core` (kb-core) and `lib/common` (kb-hal-common), both pinned to release tags; `version_lock.txt` checked in CI - [ ] Board pin table in `board/<board>/` , written with the generic `pincfg` framework - [ ] `CODEOWNERS` , `AGENTS.md` , `CLAUDE.md` , `.claude/skills/verify/` and `bump-pin/` ; licence chosen by the product owner; org clang configs - [ ] [ Root layout ]( ../standards/repo-governance.md#repository-root ): tool configuration ( `mkdocs.yml` with `docs_dir: ../docs` , `Doxyfile` , clang configs) in `_config/` , no symlinks; at the root only what a tool needs there ( `CMakePresets.json` , `version_lock.txt` ) besides the usual files ### Structure - [ ] `board/<board>/` : bus table, chip list, pin table, product choices passed to kb-core (masks, profile tables); data only - [ ] `bsp_bind/<family>/` implements the `kb::hal::bind` interface for the MCU with kb-core's `mcu/<family>/` classes; `bsp_bind/host/` with fakes and a settable clock - [ ] The bind stores every object statically, sized by `kMax*` constants; `Create*` / `Destroy*` by slot - [ ] Common managers come from `kb-hal-common` ; only board-specific managers live here, each deriving from `ManagerBase` - [ ] Managers reach chips only through handler APIs or `VisitDriver()` ; no driver includes - [ ] Every fallible manager method returns `kb::Status` ; `GetLastError()` ; no local error enum - [ ] Facade `<board>::Hal` derives from `FacadeBase` ; start-up order fixed and documented; fail-closed; safety-relevant managers not optional - [ ] The facade gives the kb-core logger its sink - [ ] No ESP-IDF, FreeRTOS or `mcu/<family>/` includes outside `bsp_bind/` ; `kb::rtos` for locks and delays; `kb::MonotonicUs()` for time - [ ] No allocation after start-up; start-up allocations allowlisted ### CI, tests and docs - [ ] The `kb-hal-common` lints (boundary, driver access, allocation, lock) run and pass - [ ] Host build with the host bind; tests for start-up order, fail-closed with a failure injected into each manager, diagnostics - [ ] `examples/esp32` (or the board's family) builds for the board's MCU with `CONFIG_FREERTOS_HZ=1000` - [ ] HAL page set with the board card, pin table, manager table, start-up order and `docs/contract.md` - [ ] Bench list for first bring-up written in the tracking issue

docs.text: Checklist: new driver ¶ Copy this list into the tracking issue or the first PR of a new driver-<chip> . Each item links the rule it checks; driver.md is the contract. ### Repository - [ ] Created from `kokeb-labs/driver-template` with `tools/setup.py --kind driver` , public, named `driver-<chip>` - [ ] Metadata added in `org/` of `kokeb-labs/.github` ; merge settings, security, rulesets and labels applied by an owner - [ ] `CODEOWNERS` , `AGENTS.md` , `CLAUDE.md` ( `@AGENTS.md` ), `.claude/skills/verify/SKILL.md` - [ ] `LICENSE` is MIT; `_config/.clang-format` and `_config/.clang-tidy` copied unchanged from the standard - [ ] Root holds only the [ allowed entries ]( ../standards/repo-governance.md#repository-root ); `Doxyfile` , `mkdocs.yml` ( `docs_dir: ../docs` ) and `Kconfig` in `_config/` ; `CONTRIBUTING.md` , `SECURITY.md` in `.github/` ; no symlinks - [ ] No org prefix anywhere: no `kb_` , `kb::` , `KB_` or other brand in names, macros, targets, files or options ### Code - [ ] Everything in `namespace <chip>` ; class `<chip>::<CHIP>` ; umbrella header `inc/<chip>.hpp` , implementation `src/<chip>.ipp` - [ ] Port base `<chip>::<Bus>Interface<Derived>` and concept `<chip>::<Bus>Port` ; required hooks not declared in the base - [ ] Hooks PascalCase, `noexcept` , `bool` , raw bytes only; the driver never configures the bus - [ ] Optional hooks detected with `requires` in one helper; a missing delay hook fails to compile - [ ] `enum class Error : uint8_t` with the base set at values 0 to 9, chip-specific values from 16, each one returned somewhere; `ToString()` - [ ] `Result<T>` / `Result<void>` with `ok()` and `[[nodiscard]]` on every fallible call - [ ] Every port failure propagates; no getter returns a stale or zero value after a failed read - [ ] `noexcept` constructor with no I/O that stores the port and the `Config` (last parameter, defaulted) - [ ] `EnsureInitialized()` is the only public start: validates, resets, checks the chip ID, applies config; idempotent with no I/O once started; retried from scratch after a failure; no public `Initialize()` - [ ] `IsInitialized()` , `Deinitialize()` , `ApplyConfig()` (stores before the start); every I/O call returns `NotInitialized` and sends nothing before the start; no read or write starts the chip - [ ] `Config` struct with unit-suffixed fields and datasheet defaults; Kconfig only through `inc/<chip>_kconfig.hpp` - [ ] Product choices (channels, features, profiles) are `Config` fields, not compile-time switches - [ ] No heap, exceptions, RTTI, `std::function` , `std::string` , `printf` , static mutable state; no locking, no RTOS - [ ] Destructive operations take explicit data or confirmation; no default triggers them - [ ] Names and units per the naming standard; `clang-tidy` clean on `inc/` and `src/` - [ ] Every header has its `#ifndef` include guard named per [ KB-CPP-019 ]( ../rules/cpp.md#kb-cpp-019 ); no `#pragma` - [ ] Bus requirements as `constexpr` in `inc/<chip>_<bus>_interface.hpp` , listed on Porting, static_asserted by each example port ([KB-CPP-123](../rules/cpp.md#kb-cpp-123)) - [ ] Control pins listed on Porting with their idle level; ports drive the inactive level before enabling the output ([KB-HW-018](../rules/hardware.md#kb-hw-018)) - [ ] Single-shot raw access and a `GetLast*()` accessor; clear-on-read flags in a driver-owned latch ([KB-CPP-129](../rules/cpp.md#kb-cpp-129), [ KB-CPP-119 ]( ../rules/cpp.md#kb-cpp-119 )) - [ ] The [ hardware-proven driver rules ]( ../standards/driver.md#replies-retries-and-resynchronisation ) hold: proven replies, refused line patterns, resync, bounded idempotent retries, start-up waits for ready ### Build - [ ] C++20; version only in `cmake/<chip>_build_settings.cmake` ( `<CHIP>_VERSION_*` ); generated `<chip>_version.h` - [ ] `EXPORT_NAME <chip>` and alias `<chip>::<chip>` ; `find_package(<chip>)` ; install rules for every header, the `.ipp` and the package config - [ ] Options `<CHIP>_BUILD_TESTS` and `<CHIP>_ENABLE_WARNINGS` - [ ] Root `CMakeLists.txt` is also the ESP-IDF component ( `ESP_PLATFORM` , `KCONFIG _config/Kconfig` ); no `idf_component.yml` , no wrapper component - [ ] No SDK, RTOS or vendor header in `inc/` or `src/` , and no `ESP_PLATFORM` test there; platform code only in `examples/<platform>/` , each with its own port - [ ] `examples/host/` built and run by the host tests; `examples/esp32` with `EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS` at the root and `CONFIG_FREERTOS_HZ=1000` in `sdkconfig.defaults` - [ ] `driver.yml` with `bus` , `mcus` , `peripheral` (if MCU-bound) and `kb_core_min` ; checked against the build settings in CI - [ ] CI from `kokeb-labs/ci-tools` at `@v1` , ending in the `CI gate` job with the DCO check in its `needs` ; `CI gate / gate` required once it has run ### Tests - [ ] `tests/mock_<chip>.hpp` register model with its own register map (no driver register header) and a `static_assert` cross-check against the driver's map ([KB-TST-030](../rules/testing.md#kb-tst-030)) - [ ] The model has StuckLow, FloatHigh, Echo and Deaf line modes, and a virtual clock when the chip has timing - [ ] Host suite on gcc and clang with `-Werror -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti` : not-initialised, ID mismatch, bus failure on every path, argument checks, register traffic - [ ] `tests/docs/` compiles every snippet on the site - [ ] `tests/install_consumer/` builds against `find_package(<chip>)` and `<chip>::<chip>` - [ ] Version agreement test (CMake, Doxyfile, `driver.yml` , `GetDriverVersion()` ) ### Docs - [ ] The driver page set, including `docs/contract.md` and `docs/platforms.md` ; site config `_config/mkdocs.yml` - [ ] Doxygen clean with `EXTRACT_ALL = NO` and warnings as errors on `inc/` - [ ] Quickstart checks every return value; Porting shows a complete, compiled port - [ ] README sections per the README standard; `docs/datasheets.yml` names each datasheet's number, revision and SHA-256, and no vendor PDF is committed ([ADR-0019](../adr/0019-datasheets.md)) - [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` with `## [Unreleased]` ### kb-core (separate PRs, after the first release) - [ ] Submodule `drivers/driver-<chip>/` in kb-core pinned to the release tag; `catalog/compat.yml` entry - [ ] Handler per the [ new handler checklist ]( new-handler.md ) ### Exceptions (only if they apply) - [ ] MCU-bound: README, Contract page and `driver.yml` say so; the peripheral backend lives in kb-core `interfaces/mcu/<family>/` ; MCU gate row added - [ ] Protocol client: remote identity check replaces the chip-ID check

class `<chip>::<CHIP>` ; umbrella header `inc/<chip>.hpp` , implementation `src/<chip>.ipp` - [ ] Port base `<chip>::<Bus>Interface<Derived>` and concept `<chip>::<Bus>Port` ; required hooks not declared in the base - [ ] Hooks PascalCase, `noexcept` , `bool` , raw bytes only; the driver never configures the bus - [ ] Optional hooks detected with `requires` in one helper; a missing delay hook fails to compile - [ ] `enum class Error : uint8_t` with the base set at values 0 to 9, chip-specific values from 16, each one returned somewhere; `ToString()` - [ ] `Result<T>` / `Result<void>` with `ok()` and `[[nodiscard]]` on every fallible call - [ ] Every port failure propagates; no getter returns a stale or zero value after a failed read - [ ] `noexcept` constructor with no I/O that stores the port and the `Config` (last parameter, defaulted) - [ ] `EnsureInitialized()` is the only public start: validates, resets, checks the chip ID, applies config; idempotent with no I/O once started; retried from scratch after a failure; no public `Initialize()` - [ ] `IsInitialized()` , `Deinitialize()` , `ApplyConfig()` (stores before the start); every I/O call returns `NotInitialized` and sends nothing before the start; no read or write starts the chip - [ ] `Config` struct with unit-suffixed fields and datasheet defaults; Kconfig only through `inc/<chip>_kconfig.hpp` - [ ] Product choices (channels, features, profiles) are `Config` fields, not compile-time switches - [ ] No heap, exceptions, RTTI, `std::function` , `std::string` , `printf` , static mutable state; no locking, no RTOS - [ ] Destructive operations take explicit data or confirmation; no default triggers them - [ ] Names and units per the naming standard; `clang-tidy` clean on `inc/` and `src/` - [ ] Every header has its `#ifndef` include guard named per [ KB-CPP-019 ]( ../rules/cpp.md#kb-cpp-019 ); no `#pragma` - [ ] Bus requirements as `constexpr` in `inc/<chip>_<bus>_interface.hpp` , listed on Porting, static_asserted by each example port ([KB-CPP-123](../rules/cpp.md#kb-cpp-123)) - [ ] Control pins listed on Porting with their idle level; ports drive the inactive level before enabling the output ([KB-HW-018](../rules/hardware.md#kb-hw-018)) - [ ] Single-shot raw access and a `GetLast*()` accessor; clear-on-read flags in a driver-owned latch ([KB-CPP-129](../rules/cpp.md#kb-cpp-129), [ KB-CPP-119 ]( ../rules/cpp.md#kb-cpp-119 )) - [ ] The [ hardware-proven driver rules ]( ../standards/driver.md#replies-retries-and-resynchronisation ) hold: proven replies, refused line patterns, resync, bounded idempotent retries, start-up waits for ready ### Build - [ ] C++20; version only in `cmake/<chip>_build_settings.cmake` ( `<CHIP>_VERSION_*` ); generated `<chip>_version.h` - [ ] `EXPORT_NAME <chip>` and alias `<chip>::<chip>` ; `find_package(<chip>)` ; install rules for every header, the `.ipp` and the package config - [ ] Options `<CHIP>_BUILD_TESTS` and `<CHIP>_ENABLE_WARNINGS` - [ ] Root `CMakeLists.txt` is also the ESP-IDF component ( `ESP_PLATFORM` , `KCONFIG _config/Kconfig` ); no `idf_component.yml` , no wrapper component - [ ] No SDK, RTOS or vendor header in `inc/` or `src/` , and no `ESP_PLATFORM` test there; platform code only in `examples/<platform>/` , each with its own port - [ ] `examples/host/` built and run by the host tests; `examples/esp32` with `EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS` at the root and `CONFIG_FREERTOS_HZ=1000` in `sdkconfig.defaults` - [ ] `driver.yml` with `bus` , `mcus` , `peripheral` (if MCU-bound) and `kb_core_min` ; checked against the build settings in CI - [ ] CI from `kokeb-labs/ci-tools` at `@v1` , ending in the `CI gate` job with the DCO check in its `needs` ; `CI gate / gate` required once it has run ### Tests - [ ] `tests/mock_<chip>.hpp` register model with its own register map (no driver register header) and a `static_assert` cross-check against the driver's map ([KB-TST-030](../rules/testing.md#kb-tst-030)) - [ ] The model has StuckLow, FloatHigh, Echo and Deaf line modes, and a virtual clock when the chip has timing - [ ] Host suite on gcc and clang with `-Werror -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti` : not-initialised, ID mismatch, bus failure on every path, argument checks, register traffic - [ ] `tests/docs/` compiles every snippet on the site - [ ] `tests/install_consumer/` builds against `find_package(<chip>)` and `<chip>::<chip>` - [ ] Version agreement test (CMake, Doxyfile, `driver.yml` , `GetDriverVersion()` ) ### Docs - [ ] The driver page set, including `docs/contract.md` and `docs/platforms.md` ; site config `_config/mkdocs.yml` - [ ] Doxygen clean with `EXTRACT_ALL = NO` and warnings as errors on `inc/` - [ ] Quickstart checks every return value; Porting shows a complete, compiled port - [ ] README sections per the README standard; `docs/datasheets.yml` names each datasheet's number, revision and SHA-256, and no vendor PDF is committed ([ADR-0019](../adr/0019-datasheets.md)) - [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` with `## [Unreleased]` ### kb-core (separate PRs, after the first release) - [ ] Submodule `drivers/driver-<chip>/` in kb-core pinned to the release tag; `catalog/compat.yml` entry - [ ] Handler per the [ new handler checklist ]( new-handler.md ) ### Exceptions (only if they apply) - [ ] MCU-bound: README, Contract page and `driver.yml` say so; the peripheral backend lives in kb-core `interfaces/mcu/<family>/` ; MCU gate row added - [ ] Protocol client: remote identity check replaces the chip-ID check

docs.text: Checklist: new handler ¶ Copy this list into the PR that adds kb-core/handlers/<chip>/ . handler.md is the contract. The driver is released and pinned in kb-core first. ### Files and build - [ ] Driver submodule at `drivers/driver-<chip>/` , pinned to a release tag; entry in `catalog/compat.yml` from its `driver.yml` - [ ] `handlers/<chip>/<Chip>Handler.h/.cpp` with class `kb::<Chip>Handler` - [ ] Adapter `Hal<Bus><Chip>Comm` deriving from the driver's port base, using the shared adapter base from `handlers/common/` - [ ] `KB_ENABLE_<CHIP>` compiles the handler and links `<chip>::<chip>` ; listed on the Build options page - [ ] MCU-bound driver: row in the MCU gate table in `cmake/kb_build_settings.cmake` , matching `catalog/compat.yml` - [ ] Includes only the driver, `kb/interfaces/Base*.h` , `kb/rtos/` , `kb/utils/` and `kb/handlers/common/` ; no `#ifdef` for an MCU or product ### Shape - [ ] Constructor stores references only: no I/O, no driver creation, no allocation; not copyable or movable - [ ] Driver stored in place ( `std::optional<Driver>` ); no `make_unique` , `new` or `shared_ptr` - [ ] `EnsureInitialized()` returns `kb::Result<void>` , retries cleanly after a failure - [ ] `Deinitialize()` and `IsInitialized()` - [ ] Own `RtosMutex` taken by every public method; optional bus mutex, taken after the handler mutex - [ ] Typed methods return `kb::Result<T>` ; no driver result types, `esp_err_t` or `bool` for fallible calls - [ ] `ToStatus(<chip>::Error)` in the adapter header: every enumerator listed, no `default:` - [ ] `VisitDriver(fn)` returns `kb::Status` , refuses before init; no public `GetDriver()` or driver pointer - [ ] `GetDiagnostics()` returns a struct starting with `kb::DiagnosticsHeader` , updated on every call - [ ] Wrappers (if any) owned in fixed storage, created by `EnsureInitialized()` - [ ] Product choices come in through the handler config or a table passed in ### Tests and docs - [ ] Host test over fake `Base*` objects and the driver's mock, with `KB_RTOS=NONE` and `KB_MCU=HOST` : no I/O in the constructor, retry after failed init, bus failure maps to `Status::Bus` , `VisitDriver()` before init, diagnostics counts - [ ] Handler page in `kb-core/docs/handlers/` : API, chip-specific `Error` mapping, locking, diagnostics fields - [ ] kb-core `CHANGELOG.md` entry under `## [Unreleased]`

docs.text: Checklist: release one repository ¶ Copy this list into the Release vX.Y.Z PR. release.md is the rule; the wave order is on that page. ### Before - [ ] Every repository this one pins is released, and the pins point at those tags; `version_lock.txt` or `catalog/compat.yml` updated - [ ] CI green on `main` with the pinned ESP-IDF; no open `safety` issues against this version - [ ] `## [Unreleased]` complete: every breaking change under `### Breaking` with what callers change; headings normalised - [ ] Version chosen: breaking → next minor (0.y+1.0), otherwise next patch; `-rc.N` while benching ### Prepare (prepare-release workflow, or by hand) - [ ] `## [Unreleased]` rolled into `## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD` , empty `## [Unreleased]` left above it - [ ] Version bumped in the build settings ( `cmake/<chip>_build_settings.cmake` or `cmake/kb_build_settings.cmake` ), `driver.yml` , `PROJECT_NUMBER` in `_config/Doxyfile` and any hand-written header; the version test passes - [ ] Builds with `add_subdirectory()` and with `find_package()` ( `<chip>::<chip>` , or each `kb::<part>` ) in the install-consumer test - [ ] kb-core: `catalog/compat.yml` regenerated, MCU gate table agrees, train name `kb YYYY.N` set - [ ] PR titled `Release vX.Y.Z` , every commit signed off, CI gate green, squash-merged ### Tag - [ ] Tag `vX.Y.Z` (or `vX.Y.Z-rc.N` ) on the merge commit on `main` ; pushed with the App token so workflows run - [ ] Release workflow passed: tag matches the declared version, commit is on `main` , body is the changelog section - [ ] Release notes state the bench status: MCU, board and test list, or **CI-only** ; kb-core notes list every pinned driver and the train - [ ] Products: `.bin` , `.elf` , `sha256` and `sdkconfig` attached; NVS or partition changes carry the erase or migration step - [ ] Docs published for the tag; an `-rc` did not move `latest` ### After - [ ] Consumers' pin-bump PRs opened (bump bot or by hand), linking this release - [ ] For an rc that passed the bench: the same commit tagged `vX.Y.Z`

docs.text: Coding agents ¶ How coding agents work in Kokeb Labs repositories, held to the same rules as people. Rule Level Applies to Verified KB-AGT-001 Every repository tells agents its rules must all planned KB-AGT-002 An agent never merges, releases or changes settings without the maintainer's go-ahead must all checked KB-AGT-003 An agent follows the whole standard, and the person who asked owns the change must all review KB-AGT-004 CLAUDE.md only points to AGENTS.md must all planned KB-AGT-005 AGENTS.md is short, specific to the repository, and links rules instead of restating them should all planned KB-AGT-006 The organisation's AGENTS.md points to the agents standard must docs planned KB-AGT-007 Every repository carries the skills its kind needs must driver, library, hal, firmware, tooling, template planned KB-AGT-008 A skill is one task in .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md , with when to use it must all planned KB-AGT-009 A skill holds no secrets and never tells an agent to bypass a check or merge must all planned KB-AGT-010 A change is done only when the definition of done holds must all checked KB-AGT-011 The agent runs every CI check locally before it pushes should driver, library, hal, firmware, tooling, template review KB-AGT-012 Anything that needs hardware is marked not verified on hardware, with bench steps must driver, library, hal, firmware, template planned KB-AGT-013 Changes that can move or energise hardware get the safety label and a human review must driver, library, hal, firmware, template planned KB-AGT-014 An agent signs off only as the person who owns the task, and only when asked must all checked KB-AGT-015 An agent adds no attribution or AI-disclosure line must all planned KB-AGT-016 An agent works on a branch and opens a pull request, never on main must all checked KB-AGT-017 An agent never force-pushes a shared branch or turns on auto-merge by itself must all checked KB-AGT-018 The diff stays on the task should all review KB-AGT-019 The pull request description is plain and follows the template should all review KB-AGT-020 A failing check is fixed, never weakened must all planned KB-AGT-021 The author reads their own diff before asking for review should all review KB-AGT-022 Before changing a public API, find and list its callers should driver, library, hal review KB-AGT-023 Use the repository's skill when one covers the task should all review KB-AGT-024 Read AGENTS.md, the layer contract and the checklist before starting guide all none KB-AGT-025 An agent reviewer triages first, then reviews architecture, then details guide all none KB-AGT-026 Review objections cite the rule ID they rest on should all review KB-AGT-027 Review comments are tagged by severity, specific and few guide all none KB-AGT-028 An agent never approves a diff it has not read, nor a safety change in a person's place must all review KB-AGT-001: Every repository tells agents its rules ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-01-15, then fails CI. MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-01-15 AGENTS.md (with CLAUDE.md pointing to it) states the repository's build and test commands and carries the handbook sections generated for its kind and level. Verified by: agents-files (planned): AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md exist and the handbook sections generated into them are current Explained in: standards/agents.md KB-AGT-002: An agent never merges, releases or changes settings without the maintainer's go-ahead ¶ MUST · all · since 1.0 A coding agent proposes changes as pull requests. Merging, releasing, deleting, and changing repository or organisation settings need the maintainer's explicit approval in the session. Verified by: rulesets (implemented): branch and tag rulesets as declared in .github/org/rulesets (PR only, linear history, tags kept) review: The pull request was opened by an agent and merged by the maintainer, or with their recorded approval. Explained in: standards/agents.md KB-AGT-003: An agent follows the whole standard, and the person who asked owns the change ¶ MUST · all · since 1.0 A coding agent is held to every rule in this handbook, like any contributor. The person who asked for the change is responsible for it as if they had written it, and their name is on the pull request. Verified by: review: The pull request names the person who asked for the change, and it meets the same rules as theirs. Explained in: standards/agents.md KB-AGT-004: CLAUDE.md only points to AGENTS.md ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 AGENTS.md is the single file agents read for a repository. CLAUDE.md contains the one line @AGENTS.md and nothing else; any other tool that wants its own file name gets the same pointer. Verified by: claude-md-pointer (planned): CLAUDE.md contains exactly the line @AGENTS.md and nothing else Explained in: standards/agents.md KB-AGT-005: AGENTS.md is short, specific to the repository, and links rules instead of restating them ¶ SHOULD · all · since 1.0 AGENTS.md opens with one sentence on what the repository is and a link to the standard, then has the sections Layout, Build and check, and Rules specific to this repo. It links handbook rules rather than copying them, so it cannot drift from them. Verified by: agents-files (planned): AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md exist and the handbook sections generated into them are current review: AGENTS.md has the standard sections and adds only what is specific to this repository. Explained in: standards/agents.md KB-AGT-006: The organisation's AGENTS.md points to the agents standard ¶ MUST · docs · since 1.0 The root of kokeb-labs/.github has an AGENTS.md that links standards/agents.md , so an agent working on organisation files finds the same rules as one working in a repository. Verified by: agents-files (planned): AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md exist and the handbook sections generated into them are current review: kokeb-labs/.github AGENTS.md links standards/agents.md. Explained in: standards/agents.md KB-AGT-007: Every repository carries the skills its kind needs ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, tooling, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Every code repository has .claude/skills/verify ; a repository with submodules also has bump-pin , a released repository release , and a driver add-driver-feature . Repositories add skills for their own recurring tasks. Verified by: skills-present (planned): .claude/skills has the skills the repository's kind requires: verify in code repositories, bump-pin when .gitmodules is not empty, release when released, add-driver-feature in drivers Explained in: standards/agents.md KB-AGT-008: A skill is one task in .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md , with when to use it ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Each skill is a folder named in kebab case for its task, holding SKILL.md with YAML front matter ( name equal to the folder, a one-line description that says when to use it) followed by the steps. Verified by: skill-format (planned): every .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md has YAML front matter with name equal to the kebab-case folder and a one-line description , followed by steps Explained in: standards/agents.md KB-AGT-009: A skill holds no secrets and never tells an agent to bypass a check or merge ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A skill contains no credentials, tokens or private URLs. It never tells an agent to skip a check, bypass a ruleset, use an admin override or merge a pull request. Verified by: skill-content-scan (planned): gitleaks finds no secret under .claude/, and no SKILL.md tells an agent to merge, use an admin bypass, --no-verify, a bare NOLINT or skip a check review: A changed SKILL.md asks for no merge, bypass, skipped check or secret. Explained in: standards/agents.md KB-AGT-010: A change is done only when the definition of done holds ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 An agent reports a change as done only when every item of the definition of done in the agents standard holds, and the pull request carries that checklist with each item ticked or marked not applicable with a reason. Verified by: pr-body-dod (planned): the pull-request body has the definition-of-done checklist with every item ticked or marked not applicable with a reason, and the hardware line filled (verified, or not verified on hardware with bench steps) ci-gate (implemented): one required check that passes only when every job of the workflow passed review: Every definition-of-done item is ticked or justified as not applicable. Explained in: standards/agents.md KB-AGT-011: The agent runs every CI check locally before it pushes ¶ SHOULD · driver, library, hal, firmware, tooling, template · since 1.0 Before each push the agent runs the verify skill, which runs locally what CI runs, and fixes what it finds. The pull request says which checks ran locally and which only CI can run. Verified by: review: The pull request says the verify skill ran, and lists checks that only CI can run. Explained in: standards/agents.md KB-AGT-012: Anything that needs hardware is marked not verified on hardware, with bench steps ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 An agent cannot run a board. A pull request whose behaviour depends on hardware says **not verified on hardware** and gives the bench steps a person should run before release. Verified by: pr-body-dod (planned): the pull-request body has the definition-of-done checklist with every item ticked or marked not applicable with a reason, and the hardware line filled (verified, or not verified on hardware with bench steps) review: Hardware-dependent behaviour is marked not verified on hardware and the bench steps are usable. Explained in: standards/agents.md KB-AGT-013: Changes that can move or energise hardware get the safety label and a human review ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. In solo mode (ADR-0015) the maintainer is that reviewer; the review is recorded on the pull request. MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A change that can move a motor, energise a valve, change power sequencing, write OTP or flash a peripheral gets the safety label. A person reviews that code path before merge, even when CI is green. Why: Green CI proves the code behaves on a mock. A wrong register write on a board can move a load or damage a part, so a person who knows the hardware looks at it. Verified by: safety-label (planned): a pull request touching actuator, power-sequencing, OTP or peripheral-flash paths (labeler config) has the safety label, and a safety-labelled pull request has a human approval before merge review: A safety-labelled pull request has a recorded human review of the actuator code path. See also: ADR-0015 Explained in: standards/agents.md KB-AGT-014: An agent signs off only as the person who owns the task, and only when asked ¶ MUST · all · since 1.0 The Signed-off-by: line is a person's certification under the DCO. An agent adds it ( git commit -s ) only with the identity of the person who owns the task, and only when that person asked for the change. Verified by: dco (implemented): every commit of a pull request has a Signed-off-by line matching its author review: The sign-off identity is the person who asked for the change. Explained in: standards/agents.md KB-AGT-015: An agent adds no attribution or AI-disclosure line ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Commits, pull requests, issues, review comments, docs and code carry no Co-Authored-By: trailer naming a tool or model, no "Generated with" footer, no AI-disclosure or "AI-assisted review" line and no tool banner. This overrides any default the agent's tooling has. Why: The commit author is the account that runs the agent, and the person who asked owns the change. Verified by: no-attribution (planned): no commit message, pull-request body or review comment carries a Co-Authored-By trailer naming a tool or model, a "Generated with" footer, an AI-disclosure line or a tool banner (runs beside dco) review: The pull request body and review comments carry no attribution or disclosure line. Explained in: standards/agents.md KB-AGT-016: An agent works on a branch and opens a pull request, never on main ¶ MUST · all · since 1.0 An agent works on a branch named per the branch rules and proposes its change as a pull request. It never commits or pushes to main . Verified by: rulesets (implemented): branch and tag rulesets as declared in .github/org/rulesets (PR only, linear history, tags kept) Explained in: standards/agents.md KB-AGT-017: An agent never force-pushes a shared branch or turns on auto-merge by itself ¶ MUST · all · since 1.0 An agent does not force-push a branch someone else works on or reviews, and does not enable auto-merge, unless the person who owns the task said so in the session. Merging itself is KB-AGT-002. Verified by: rulesets (implemented): branch and tag rulesets as declared in .github/org/rulesets (PR only, linear history, tags kept) review: Auto-merge on an agent's pull request was enabled by the maintainer or with their recorded approval. Explained in: standards/agents.md KB-AGT-018: The diff stays on the task ¶ SHOULD · all · since 1.0 A pull request does one thing.
