scheme and default to the smallest build must library planned KB-BLD-024 Enabling a module enables what it depends on, never the reverse should library planned KB-BLD-025 kb-core links each driver's target and never copies its file lists must library review KB-BLD-026 ESP-IDF REQUIRES follow the enabled options should library, hal review KB-BLD-027 Configure prints a summary of what is built should library, hal review KB-BLD-028 Keep CMake plain and linear guide driver, library, hal, firmware, template none KB-BLD-029 Depend on as little as possible guide driver, library, hal none KB-BLD-001: The installed package works with find_package ¶ MUST · driver, library, template · since 1.0 A library or driver installs a CMake package ( <name>Config.cmake with an exported <name>::<name> target) that a separate project finds with find_package and links; CI builds such a consumer. Verified by: cmake-consumer (implemented): the installed package is found and linked by a separate CMake project (find_package) Explained in: standards/driver.md KB-BLD-002: No file(GLOB) for library sources ¶ MUST · driver, library, hal, template · since 1.0 Library targets list their sources explicitly; file(GLOB) is not used for sources or headers. Why: A glob hides an added or removed file from review and from the build system's dependency tracking. Verified by: forbidden-patterns/cmake-glob (implemented): a source scan for a construct the handbook bans; the parameter names the pattern set KB-BLD-003: The root CMakeLists.txt is also the ESP-IDF component ¶ MUST · driver, library, template · since 1.0 Under ESP_PLATFORM the root CMakeLists.txt registers the repository as an ESP-IDF component and returns before project() ; there is no separate wrapper component. examples/esp32/ reaches it through EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS pointing at the repository root, and kb-core maps its CONFIG_KB_* values onto its CMake options in that one place. Why: One CMake entry point for every build system means the ESP-IDF build cannot drift from the host and find_package builds. Verified by: esp-idf-examples (planned): every app in examples/esp32 builds with the pinned ESP-IDF, using the repository root as its component (runs today in driver-template esp32-examples-build-ci.yml through ci-tools ru-build) review: The root CMakeLists.txt is the ESP-IDF component; no wrapper component or extra CMake entry point. See also: ADR-0011 Explained in: standards/driver.md KB-BLD-004: One build-settings file holds the version, target name and source list ¶ MUST · driver, library, template · since 1.0 cmake/<chip>_build_settings.cmake ( cmake/kb_build_settings.cmake for kb-core, one version for all its parts) is the only place the version, the target name, the options and the source list are written. It is guarded with include_guard(GLOBAL) , and the variables it sets carry the unbranded <CHIP>_ prefix. Why: A value written twice is eventually written differently. Verified by: version-copies (planned): project(), the package version, the generated version header, Doxyfile PROJECT_NUMBER, driver.yml and the version getter all equal the version in the build settings (driver-template version ctests, less driver.yml) review: Version, target name, options and sources are set only in the build-settings file. See also: ADR-0012 ; ADR-0013 ; IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 8.1.1 (configuration item identification) Explained in: standards/driver.md KB-BLD-005: Every copy of the version derives from or is tested against the build settings ¶ MUST · driver, library, template · since 1.0 project() , the package version file, the generated <chip>_version.h ( <CHIP>_VERSION_* ), Doxyfile PROJECT_NUMBER , driver.yml and GetDriverVersion() either derive from the build settings or are compared with them by a test. A release changes the version in the build settings and the test proves the copies agree. Verified by: version-copies (planned): project(), the package version, the generated version header, Doxyfile PROJECT_NUMBER, driver.yml and the version getter all equal the version in the build settings (driver-template version ctests, less driver.yml) review: A release pull request bumps the version only in the build settings and the version tests pass. See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 8.1.1 KB-BLD-006: The same <chip>::<chip> target through add_subdirectory and find_package ¶ MUST · driver, library, template · since 1.0 The library target has the alias <chip>::<chip> and EXPORT_NAME <chip> , so a consumer writes the same target_link_libraries line whether it uses add_subdirectory() or the installed package. Targets carry no organisation prefix. Why: Submodule consumers and package consumers then differ only in how they find the code, never in what they link. Verified by: cmake-consumer (implemented): the installed package is found and linked by a separate CMake project (find_package) host-tests (implemented): the unit tests build and pass on the host with gcc and clang See also: ADR-0012 Explained in: standards/driver.md KB-BLD-007: Install rules install every header the public API reaches ¶ MUST · driver, library, template · since 1.0 cmake --install installs every header the umbrella header includes, every .ipp , the generated version header and the package configuration and version files, keeping the relative layout the includes rely on. Verified by: cmake-consumer (implemented): the installed package is found and linked by a separate CMake project (find_package) KB-BLD-008: Standard options <CHIP>_BUILD_TESTS and <CHIP>_ENABLE_WARNINGS , both off by default ¶ MUST · driver, template · since 1.0 The root CMakeLists.txt offers <CHIP>_BUILD_TESTS and <CHIP>_ENABLE_WARNINGS , both OFF by default, so a consumer builds neither the tests nor the warning set unless it asks. Verified by: cmake-configure/standard-options (planned): a CMake configure test asserts the named property: standard-options, dev-warnings, kb-core-targets, backend-selection, mcu-gates (a wrong-MCU enable must fail), option-defaults, single-toggles review: The two options exist with the standard names and default OFF. Explained in: standards/driver.md KB-BLD-009: Compile flags and definitions are set per target, never globally ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 CMake files set flags, definitions and include paths with target_* commands. add_compile_options , add_definitions , include_directories and writes to CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS are not used. Why: A global flag leaks into every consumer's build and into code it was never reviewed against. Verified by: forbidden-patterns/cmake-global-flags (planned): a source scan for a construct the handbook bans; the parameter names the pattern set KB-BLD-010: CMake configures without developer warnings ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 The project configures cleanly with -Werror=dev --warn-uninitialized , for the host build and for every option combination CI exercises. Verified by: cmake-configure/dev-warnings (planned): a CMake configure test asserts the named property: standard-options, dev-warnings, kb-core-targets, backend-selection, mcu-gates (a wrong-MCU enable must fail), option-defaults, single-toggles KB-BLD-011: Header-only libraries are INTERFACE targets; compiled ones are STATIC ¶ SHOULD · driver, library, template · since 1.0 A library with no sources is an INTERFACE target and one with sources is STATIC . Switching between the two changes only the source list in the build settings. Verified by: review: The target type matches whether the build settings list sources. KB-BLD-012: The root CMakeLists.txt declares the org's CMake minimum, 3.16 ¶ SHOULD · driver, library, template · since 1.0 The root CMakeLists.txt starts with cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.16) ; a repository raises it only with a reason in the pull request. Why: ESP-IDF 5 and the vendor toolchains in use all ship CMake 3.16 or newer; asking for more locks some out. Verified by: review: cmake_minimum_required is 3.16, or the pull request says why it is higher. KB-BLD-013: Kconfig lives in _config/Kconfig and defines every CONFIG_ value the code reads ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, library, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A component with ESP-IDF options ships _config/Kconfig , registered through KCONFIG in the root CMakeLists.txt. Code reads no CONFIG_* symbol that this file (or ESP-IDF itself) does not define, and compiles with every such value unset. Why: A CONFIG_ name with no Kconfig behind it is silently never set, and its feature is silently off. Verified by: kconfig-symbols (planned): every CONFIG_ symbol the sources read is defined in _config/Kconfig or by ESP-IDF host-tests (implemented): the unit tests build and pass on the host with gcc and clang KB-BLD-014: The exported target itself builds warning-free with the org flag set ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, library, hal, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 CI compiles the library's own sources and every public header with <CHIP>_ENABLE_WARNINGS=ON , the org warning set, -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti and -Werror , not only the test targets that include them. Why: Today the flags reach a compiled library's sources only through the tests, so a STATIC target can ship code the warning set never saw. Verified by: exported-target-flags (planned): the library target's own sources and every public header compile with <CHIP>_ENABLE_WARNINGS=ON, the org warning set and -Werror exceptions-rtti-off (planned): the exported library target compiles with -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti, not only the tests KB-BLD-015: Supported compilers and toolchains are pinned and listed ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 The repository lists the compilers it supports (host gcc and clang, arm-none-eabi-gcc, the ESP-IDF release) with exact versions, and CI builds with exactly those versions. Changing one is a pull request of its own. Why: An unpinned toolchain changes the warnings, the code generated and the static-analysis findings without any commit to blame; clang-tidy 18 and 20 already disagree on the same code. Verified by: toolchain-pins (planned): the repository lists exact versions of every supported compiler and ESP-IDF, and every CI build uses exactly those versions See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 8.1.2 (SOUP identification, for the toolchain) KB-BLD-016: Release builds are reproducible ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. SHOULD · library, hal, firmware (high level and above) · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Building the same tag twice with the pinned toolchain gives byte-identical artefacts: no __DATE__ or __TIME__ , build paths stripped with -ffile-prefix-map , and timestamps taken from SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH . Why: An evidence package is only worth something if anyone can rebuild the binary it describes. Verified by: reproducible-build (planned): two clean builds of the same commit in different directories produce byte-identical artefacts See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 8.1.1 KB-BLD-017: Image size and stack usage stay within recorded budgets ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware (high level and above) · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Firmware and example images are built with -fstack-usage . The repository records a flash, RAM and per-task stack budget, and CI fails when a build exceeds one or a function's stack use is unbounded. Why: Stack overflow on a microcontroller corrupts memory silently; a budget turns it into a build failure. Verified by: size-budget (planned): flash and RAM use of each built image stays within the budget recorded in the repository stack-usage (planned): the target build with -fstack-usage reports every task entry and ISR within the stack budget in the repository's budget file; unbounded (dynamic) frames fail See also: NASA/JPL Power of Ten Rule 1 (no recursion, so stack use is bounded) KB-BLD-018: Firmware reports its version and the exact source of every pinned component ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Firmware embeds a header generated by CMake with its own version, the release train and the tag and commit SHA of every pinned submodule, and reports them at start-up and on request. No version is hard-coded. Verified by: provenance-header (planned): the firmware's generated provenance header names its version, release train and the tag and SHA of every submodule, matching .gitmodules and git describe See also: ADR-0007 ; IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 8.1.3 (identify the system configuration) Explained in: standards/product.md KB-BLD-019: ESP-IDF builds set a 1 kHz FreeRTOS tick in sdkconfig.defaults ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Every ESP-IDF project, including driver examples, sets CONFIG_FREERTOS_HZ=1000 in sdkconfig.defaults . ThreadX builds should set TX_TIMER_TICKS_PER_SECOND to 1000. Verified by: sdkconfig-defaults/freertos-hz (planned): sdkconfig.defaults of every ESP-IDF project sets the named value (freertos-hz is CONFIG_FREERTOS_HZ=1000) See also: ADR-0006 ; ADR-0018 Explained in: standards/threading-and-timing.md KB-BLD-020: kb-core parts are separate targets with distinct include roots ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · library · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 kb-core builds kb::utils , kb::rtos , kb::interfaces and kb::handlers as separate targets, each with one include root reached as "kb/<part>/<Header>.h" ; no two parts install the same path. Each part is usable through add_subdirectory() and through its installed package. Verified by: cmake-configure/kb-core-targets (planned): a CMake configure test asserts the named property: standard-options, dev-warnings, kb-core-targets, backend-selection, mcu-gates (a wrong-MCU enable must fail), option-defaults, single-toggles installed-header-collisions (planned): the install trees of the kb-core packages contain no path twice See also: ADR-0013 Explained in: standards/library.md KB-BLD-021: Each build selects exactly one MCU family and one RTOS backend ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · library · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 KB_MCU (ESP32, STM32, HOST or NONE) and KB_RTOS (FREERTOS, THREADX or NONE) each select exactly one backend and define exactly one macro for it. KB_MCU=NONE builds the MCU-independent base only and KB_MCU=HOST is the test backend; the API is the same on every backend. Verified by: cmake-configure/backend-selection (planned): a CMake configure test asserts the named property: standard-options, dev-warnings, kb-core-targets, backend-selection, mcu-gates (a wrong-MCU enable must fail), option-defaults, single-toggles See also: ADR-0013 ; ADR-0014 Explained in: standards/library.md KB-BLD-022: Enabling an MCU-bound driver for the wrong MCU fails at configure time ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · library · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Drivers bound to an MCU family or peripheral are listed in KB_MCU_GATES , generated from catalog/compat.yml and never edited by hand. Enabling one for another MCU stops the CMake configure step with a message naming the gate. A kb-core release regenerates the table and checks it agrees with compat.yml . Verified by: cmake-configure/mcu-gates (planned): a CMake configure test asserts the named property: standard-options, dev-warnings, kb-core-targets, backend-selection, mcu-gates (a wrong-MCU enable must fail), option-defaults, single-toggles review: compat.yml was regenerated for the release and the gate table matches it. See also: ADR-0007 ; ADR-0014 Explained in: standards/layers.md KB-BLD-023: kb-core options use the KB_ scheme and default to the smallest build ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · library · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 kb-core's options are KB_MCU , KB_RTOS , KB_ENABLE_<CHIP> , KB_ENABLE_<FEATURE> and KB_BUILD_TESTS . Each enable option has an explicit default, OFF unless the pull request justifies otherwise, so an unconfigured build is the base only. KB_ENABLE_<CHIP> is the only switch that compiles a handler. Verified by: cmake-configure/option-defaults (planned): a CMake configure test asserts the named property: standard-options, dev-warnings, kb-core-targets, backend-selection, mcu-gates (a wrong-MCU enable must fail), option-defaults, single-toggles See also: ADR-0013 Explained in: standards/library.md KB-BLD-024: Enabling a module enables what it depends on, never the reverse ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. SHOULD · library · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Turning on one option also turns on the modules it needs: a driver enables the interfaces it uses, and an interface never enables a driver. Every option configures and builds when it is the only one switched on. Verified by: cmake-configure/single-toggles (planned): a CMake configure test asserts the named property: standard-options, dev-warnings, kb-core-targets, backend-selection, mcu-gates (a wrong-MCU enable must fail), option-defaults, single-toggles Explained in: standards/layers.md KB-BLD-025: kb-core links each driver's target and never copies its file lists ¶ MUST · library · since 1.0 kb-core consumes a driver by linking <chip>::<chip> from its pinned submodule. kb_build_settings.cmake holds the version, options, targets and gate table, and no driver source or include path. Why: A copied file list breaks the day the driver adds a file, and bypasses the driver's own flags. Verified by: review: kb-core CMake names no file or include directory inside a driver submodule. See also: ADR-0007 ; ADR-0013 Explained in: standards/library.md KB-BLD-026: ESP-IDF REQUIRES follow the enabled options ¶ SHOULD · library, hal · since 1.0 Under ESP-IDF the component's REQUIRES list is built from the enabled options, without duplicates, so a disabled module pulls in no component. A component that exists only in some ESP-IDF releases is checked for and reported, not assumed. Verified by: review: Each REQUIRES entry is added by the option that needs it. KB-BLD-027: Configure prints a summary of what is built ¶ SHOULD · library, hal · since 1.0 A library or HAL with options prints one configuration summary at the end of configure: MCU, RTOS, enabled drivers and features, and their count. Why: A CI log then says what was actually built without anyone reproducing the configure step. Verified by: review: The configure log shows the summary block. KB-BLD-028: Keep CMake plain and linear ¶ GUIDE · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 Build settings read top to bottom as a list of settings: no logic hidden in helper functions, paths derived from CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR and overridable as cache variables where a consumer may need to. KB-BLD-029: Depend on as little as possible ¶ GUIDE · driver, library, hal · since 1.0 Add a dependency only when it removes more than it costs, keep the dependency list of a published component accurate, and prefer a compatible change to a breaking one.

MUST · driver, library, hal, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 CI compiles the library's own sources and every public header with <CHIP>_ENABLE_WARNINGS=ON , the org warning set, -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti and -Werror , not only the test targets that include them. Why: Today the flags reach a compiled library's sources only through the tests, so a STATIC target can ship code the warning set never saw. Verified by: exported-target-flags (planned): the library target's own sources and every public header compile with <CHIP>_ENABLE_WARNINGS=ON, the org warning set and -Werror exceptions-rtti-off (planned): the exported library target compiles with -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti, not only the tests
docs.title: KB-BLD-014: The exported target itself builds warning-free with the org flag set

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 The repository lists the compilers it supports (host gcc and clang, arm-none-eabi-gcc, the ESP-IDF release) with exact versions, and CI builds with exactly those versions. Changing one is a pull request of its own. Why: An unpinned toolchain changes the warnings, the code generated and the static-analysis findings without any commit to blame; clang-tidy 18 and 20 already disagree on the same code. Verified by: toolchain-pins (planned): the repository lists exact versions of every supported compiler and ESP-IDF, and every CI build uses exactly those versions See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 8.1.2 (SOUP identification, for the toolchain)
docs.title: KB-BLD-015: Supported compilers and toolchains are pinned and listed

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. SHOULD · library, hal, firmware (high level and above) · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Building the same tag twice with the pinned toolchain gives byte-identical artefacts: no __DATE__ or __TIME__ , build paths stripped with -ffile-prefix-map , and timestamps taken from SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH . Why: An evidence package is only worth something if anyone can rebuild the binary it describes. Verified by: reproducible-build (planned): two clean builds of the same commit in different directories produce byte-identical artefacts See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 8.1.1
docs.title: KB-BLD-016: Release builds are reproducible

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware (high level and above) · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Firmware and example images are built with -fstack-usage . The repository records a flash, RAM and per-task stack budget, and CI fails when a build exceeds one or a function's stack use is unbounded. Why: Stack overflow on a microcontroller corrupts memory silently; a budget turns it into a build failure. Verified by: size-budget (planned): flash and RAM use of each built image stays within the budget recorded in the repository stack-usage (planned): the target build with -fstack-usage reports every task entry and ISR within the stack budget in the repository's budget file; unbounded (dynamic) frames fail See also: NASA/JPL Power of Ten Rule 1 (no recursion, so stack use is bounded)
docs.title: KB-BLD-017: Image size and stack usage stay within recorded budgets

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Firmware embeds a header generated by CMake with its own version, the release train and the tag and commit SHA of every pinned submodule, and reports them at start-up and on request. No version is hard-coded. Verified by: provenance-header (planned): the firmware's generated provenance header names its version, release train and the tag and SHA of every submodule, matching .gitmodules and git describe See also: ADR-0007 ; IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 8.1.3 (identify the system configuration) Explained in: standards/product.md
docs.title: KB-BLD-018: Firmware reports its version and the exact source of every pinned component

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Every ESP-IDF project, including driver examples, sets CONFIG_FREERTOS_HZ=1000 in sdkconfig.defaults . ThreadX builds should set TX_TIMER_TICKS_PER_SECOND to 1000. Verified by: sdkconfig-defaults/freertos-hz (planned): sdkconfig.defaults of every ESP-IDF project sets the named value (freertos-hz is CONFIG_FREERTOS_HZ=1000) See also: ADR-0006 ; ADR-0018 Explained in: standards/threading-and-timing.md
docs.title: KB-BLD-019: ESP-IDF builds set a 1 kHz FreeRTOS tick in sdkconfig.defaults

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · library · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 kb-core builds kb::utils , kb::rtos , kb::interfaces and kb::handlers as separate targets, each with one include root reached as "kb/<part>/<Header>.h" ; no two parts install the same path. Each part is usable through add_subdirectory() and through its installed package. Verified by: cmake-configure/kb-core-targets (planned): a CMake configure test asserts the named property: standard-options, dev-warnings, kb-core-targets, backend-selection, mcu-gates (a wrong-MCU enable must fail), option-defaults, single-toggles installed-header-collisions (planned): the install trees of the kb-core packages contain no path twice See also: ADR-0013 Explained in: standards/library.md
docs.title: KB-BLD-020: kb-core parts are separate targets with distinct include roots

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · library · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 KB_MCU (ESP32, STM32, HOST or NONE) and KB_RTOS (FREERTOS, THREADX or NONE) each select exactly one backend and define exactly one macro for it. KB_MCU=NONE builds the MCU-independent base only and KB_MCU=HOST is the test backend; the API is the same on every backend. Verified by: cmake-configure/backend-selection (planned): a CMake configure test asserts the named property: standard-options, dev-warnings, kb-core-targets, backend-selection, mcu-gates (a wrong-MCU enable must fail), option-defaults, single-toggles See also: ADR-0013 ; ADR-0014 Explained in: standards/library.md
docs.title: KB-BLD-021: Each build selects exactly one MCU family and one RTOS backend

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · library · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Drivers bound to an MCU family or peripheral are listed in KB_MCU_GATES , generated from catalog/compat.yml and never edited by hand. Enabling one for another MCU stops the CMake configure step with a message naming the gate. A kb-core release regenerates the table and checks it agrees with compat.yml . Verified by: cmake-configure/mcu-gates (planned): a CMake configure test asserts the named property: standard-options, dev-warnings, kb-core-targets, backend-selection, mcu-gates (a wrong-MCU enable must fail), option-defaults, single-toggles review: compat.yml was regenerated for the release and the gate table matches it. See also: ADR-0007 ; ADR-0014 Explained in: standards/layers.md
docs.title: KB-BLD-022: Enabling an MCU-bound driver for the wrong MCU fails at configure time

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · library · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 kb-core's options are KB_MCU , KB_RTOS , KB_ENABLE_<CHIP> , KB_ENABLE_<FEATURE> and KB_BUILD_TESTS . Each enable option has an explicit default, OFF unless the pull request justifies otherwise, so an unconfigured build is the base only. KB_ENABLE_<CHIP> is the only switch that compiles a handler. Verified by: cmake-configure/option-defaults (planned): a CMake configure test asserts the named property: standard-options, dev-warnings, kb-core-targets, backend-selection, mcu-gates (a wrong-MCU enable must fail), option-defaults, single-toggles See also: ADR-0013 Explained in: standards/library.md
docs.title: KB-BLD-023: kb-core options use the KB_ scheme and default to the smallest build

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. SHOULD · library · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Turning on one option also turns on the modules it needs: a driver enables the interfaces it uses, and an interface never enables a driver. Every option configures and builds when it is the only one switched on. Verified by: cmake-configure/single-toggles (planned): a CMake configure test asserts the named property: standard-options, dev-warnings, kb-core-targets, backend-selection, mcu-gates (a wrong-MCU enable must fail), option-defaults, single-toggles Explained in: standards/layers.md
docs.title: KB-BLD-024: Enabling a module enables what it depends on, never the reverse

docs.text: MUST · library · since 1.0 kb-core consumes a driver by linking <chip>::<chip> from its pinned submodule. kb_build_settings.cmake holds the version, options, targets and gate table, and no driver source or include path. Why: A copied file list breaks the day the driver adds a file, and bypasses the driver's own flags. Verified by: review: kb-core CMake names no file or include directory inside a driver submodule. See also: ADR-0007 ; ADR-0013 Explained in: standards/library.md
docs.title: KB-BLD-025: kb-core links each driver's target and never copies its file lists

docs.text: SHOULD · library, hal · since 1.0 Under ESP-IDF the component's REQUIRES list is built from the enabled options, without duplicates, so a disabled module pulls in no component. A component that exists only in some ESP-IDF releases is checked for and reported, not assumed. Verified by: review: Each REQUIRES entry is added by the option that needs it.
docs.title: KB-BLD-026: ESP-IDF REQUIRES follow the enabled options

docs.text: SHOULD · library, hal · since 1.0 A library or HAL with options prints one configuration summary at the end of configure: MCU, RTOS, enabled drivers and features, and their count. Why: A CI log then says what was actually built without anyone reproducing the configure step. Verified by: review: The configure log shows the summary block.
docs.title: KB-BLD-027: Configure prints a summary of what is built

docs.text: GUIDE · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 Build settings read top to bottom as a list of settings: no logic hidden in helper functions, paths derived from CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR and overridable as cache variables where a consumer may need to.
docs.title: KB-BLD-028: Keep CMake plain and linear

docs.text: GUIDE · driver, library, hal · since 1.0 Add a dependency only when it removes more than it costs, keep the dependency list of a published component accurate, and prefer a compatible change to a breaking one.
docs.title: KB-BLD-029: Depend on as little as possible

docs.text: C code ¶ Most Kokeb Labs code is C++, but C still appears: C APIs that kb-core keeps for compatibility, MCU vendor code and code generated by CubeMX or ESP-IDF. These rules say how our own C is written and how vendor and generated C is kept apart. The C++ rules on heap, errors, integers and static analysis apply to C as well. Rule Level Applies to Verified KB-CC-001 C is C17 without compiler extensions must driver, library, hal, firmware, template planned KB-CC-002 C headers work from C++ and expose only C types must driver, library, hal, firmware, template planned KB-CC-003 C names are snake_case with the repository prefix; file-local functions are static must driver, library, hal, firmware, template planned KB-CC-004 C APIs return an error enum whose zero is success, and the result is used must driver, library, hal, firmware, template review KB-CC-005 Every C function has a prototype must driver, library, hal, firmware, template checked KB-CC-006 Generated vendor code is edited only between its user-code markers must hal, firmware planned KB-CC-007 Vendor and third-party code lives in excluded directories must driver, library, hal, firmware, template review KB-CC-001: C is C17 without compiler extensions ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Our own C sources build as ISO C17 ( CMAKE_C_STANDARD 17 , CMAKE_C_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON , CMAKE_C_EXTENSIONS OFF ). Vendor and generated code keeps the standard its supplier uses. Why: Neither source handbook fixed a C standard. The pinned GCC toolchains default to C17 with GNU extensions; turning the extensions off keeps the code portable to clang on the host. Verified by: forbidden-patterns/cmake-c-standard (planned): a source scan for a construct the handbook bans; the parameter names the pattern set KB-CC-002: C headers work from C++ and expose only C types ¶ MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 A header that declares a C API wraps its declarations in extern "C" guarded by __cplusplus , and its signatures use only C types ( <stdint.h> , <stdbool.h> , plain structs and enums), so C and C++ callers see the same ABI. Verified by: header-self-contained (planned): every public header compiles on its own as the first include of a translation unit review: Each C API header has the extern "C" guard and uses only C types in its signatures. KB-CC-003: C names are snake_case with the repository prefix; file-local functions are static ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. Needs C-specific naming options for .c files in place of the C++ ones config/.clang-tidy applies today. MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 C functions and variables are snake_case and public ones start with the repository prefix ( kb_ , <chip>_ ); typedefs end in _t with that prefix, and enumerators are UPPER_SNAKE with the type's prefix. Functions used only in one file are static . Why: C has no namespaces, so the prefix is the namespace. The org .clang-tidy naming options are written for C++ and today also lint .c files. Verified by: c-naming (planned): clang-tidy readability-identifier-naming with C options (snake_case functions and variables, *_t typedefs, UPPER_CASE enumerators, repository prefix) run on .c files and C API headers See also: ADR-0008 KB-CC-004: C APIs return an error enum whose zero is success, and the result is used ¶ MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 A C function that can fail returns its module's error enum, with the success value equal to 0, and is declared with __attribute__((warn_unused_result)) (or the project's macro for it) so a caller cannot drop the result. Verified by: review: Each new fallible C function returns the module's error enum and is marked warn_unused_result. See also: ADR-0001 ; SEI CERT C ERR33-C KB-CC-005: Every C function has a prototype ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. The C build must add both flags with -Werror. MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Every C function is declared with a full prototype ( void f(void) , never void f() ), and every function with external linkage has a prototype in a header before it is defined. Verified by: compiler-warnings/-Wstrict-prototypes (implemented): the build is warning-free with the named flag and -Werror compiler-warnings/-Wmissing-prototypes (implemented): the build is warning-free with the named flag and -Werror KB-CC-006: Generated vendor code is edited only between its user-code markers ¶ MUST · hal, firmware · since 1.0 Code generated by CubeMX or another vendor tool is changed only between its USER CODE BEGIN / END markers; any other change is recorded in PATCHES.md beside it. Regenerating from the committed project file reproduces the committed code. Why: Changes outside the markers are lost silently at the next regeneration. Verified by: vendor-regen-diff (planned): CI regenerates vendor code (CubeMX) from the committed project file and fails if the result differs from the committed sources outside user-code markers and PATCHES.md review: Edits to generated files are inside user-code markers or listed in PATCHES.md. KB-CC-007: Vendor and third-party code lives in excluded directories ¶ MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 Vendor, generated and third-party sources live under third_party/ , external/ , managed_components/ or the generator's own directory, which format and lint exclude. Our code is never placed there to avoid the checks. Why: Reformatting vendor code makes every vendor update a conflict, so it is excluded, which only holds if the exclusion covers vendor code and nothing else. Verified by: review: Code written by us is not under an excluded directory. See also: ADR-0009

docs.text: CI and supply chain ¶ What workflows may run and how they are written. Rule Level Applies to Verified KB-CI-001 Only allow-listed actions, pinned to a full commit SHA must all checked KB-CI-002 Least privilege in every workflow must all planned KB-CI-003 Workflows call the shared ci-tools workflows at @v1 must all planned KB-CI-004 The CI gate needs every other job, including DCO must all checked KB-CI-005 Code from a fork never runs with secrets must all planned KB-CI-006 Dependabot keeps the actions current should all planned KB-CI-007 Public repositories run GitHub's security features must all planned KB-CI-008 No credentials, private datasheets or personal data are committed must all planned KB-CI-009 Tags that start workflows are pushed with a GitHub App token should all review KB-CI-010 Every example builds in CI, and a platform arrives with its job must driver, library, hal, firmware, template planned KB-CI-011 kb-core CI builds every part for every MCU family and for no MCU must library planned KB-CI-012 Tables generated from compat.yml are never stale must library planned KB-CI-013 Every board HAL runs the kb-hal-common lints must hal planned KB-CI-014 version_lock.txt matches the submodule pins must hal, firmware planned KB-CI-015 ESP-IDF builds run the declared IDF matrix, validated first guide driver, library, hal, firmware, template review KB-CI-016 CI keeps the test and coverage reports as artifacts should driver, library, hal, firmware (high level and above) planned KB-CI-001: Only allow-listed actions, pinned to a full commit SHA ¶ MUST · all · since 1.0 Workflows use GitHub's own actions, the organisation's, or a third-party action on the allow-list in .github/org/actions-allowlist.json , always pinned to a full commit SHA with the version in a comment. Verified by: actions-allowlist (implemented): only allow-listed actions, pinned to a full commit SHA, can run (organisation Actions policy) KB-CI-002: Least privilege in every workflow ¶ Proposed Enforced in ci-tools' own workflows today; the reusable check is planned. MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-01-15 Each workflow sets permissions: at the top (read or none) and each job asks only for what it needs; a workflow never interpolates untrusted input into a shell command. Verified by: workflow-permissions (planned): every workflow sets permissions at the top and grants each job the least it needs actionlint (planned): actionlint and zizmor find nothing in the repository's workflows KB-CI-003: Workflows call the shared ci-tools workflows at @v1 ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. driver-template's host tests still use their own workflow rather than ru-host-ci. The v1 side is enforced today by ci-tools' release.yml and the major-tags ruleset. MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Lint, analysis, build, docs and release jobs call kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/<name>.yml@v1 , never @main or a copy. ci-tools stays at 1.x and moves v1 only to its highest 1.x release. Verified by: shared-workflows (planned): every lint, analysis, build, docs and release job calls a kokeb-labs/ci-tools reusable workflow at @v1, and none at @main review: A job that does not use a ci-tools workflow says why in a comment beside it. Explained in: standards/repo-governance.md KB-CI-004: The CI gate needs every other job, including DCO ¶ MUST · all · since 1.0 The workflow's last job comes from ru-ci-gate, runs with if: always() and lists every other job in needs , so a skipped or failed job, an unsigned commit or a [skip ci] run cannot merge. Verified by: ci-gate (implemented): one required check that passes only when every job of the workflow passed dco (implemented): every commit of a pull request has a Signed-off-by line matching its author See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 8.2 (a change is verified before it is accepted) Explained in: standards/repo-governance.md KB-CI-005: Code from a fork never runs with secrets ¶ MUST · all · since 1.0 Workflows triggered by a fork's pull request get no secrets and a read-only token; pull_request_target and workflow_run never check out or run the pull request's code. Fork runs wait for a maintainer's approval. Verified by: actionlint (planned): actionlint and zizmor find nothing in the repository's workflows review: No workflow triggered by pull_request_target or workflow_run checks out the pull request head. Explained in: standards/repo-governance.md KB-CI-006: Dependabot keeps the actions current ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. driver-template has the file; org-standard-check does not ask for it. SHOULD · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Every repository with workflows has .github/dependabot.yml updating github-actions weekly with the dependencies label and the ci prefix, plus pip where it has Python tooling. It never manages submodules. Verified by: dependabot-config (planned): .github/dependabot.yml updates github-actions weekly with label dependencies and prefix ci, pip where Python tooling exists, and has no gitsubmodule ecosystem Explained in: standards/repo-governance.md KB-CI-007: Public repositories run GitHub's security features ¶ MUST · all · since 1.0 Secret scanning with push protection, Dependabot alerts and security updates, private vulnerability reporting and CodeQL default setup are on for every public repository. Verified by: org-settings-drift (planned): a scheduled kokeb_org.py --check finds no drift between org/ and the repository's live settings review: kokeb_org.py --check --section security reports no drift for the repository. Explained in: standards/repo-governance.md KB-CI-008: No credentials, private datasheets or personal data are committed ¶ MUST · all · since 1.0 Tokens, keys, passwords, private datasheet material and personal data never enter a commit, a log or an artifact. A secret that reached a commit is revoked, not just removed. Verified by: secret-scan (planned): gitleaks finds no secret in the pull request's commits review: Nothing in the diff, the logs or the artifacts is a credential or confidential material. Explained in: standards/agents.md KB-CI-009: Tags that start workflows are pushed with a GitHub App token ¶ SHOULD · all · since 1.0 A workflow that pushes a tag other workflows react to uses a token from actions/create-github-app-token , because tags pushed with GITHUB_TOKEN start no workflow. Verified by: review: A tag push meant to trigger release or docs workflows uses a GitHub App token. Explained in: standards/release.md KB-CI-010: Every example builds in CI, and a platform arrives with its job ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. driver-template builds its ESP32 example through ru-build today; nothing maps example folders to jobs. MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Each examples/<platform>/ has a CI job that builds it (ru-build for ESP-IDF). A platform is added only in the pull request that adds that job. Verified by: examples-build (planned): every examples/<platform>/ folder is built by a job of the repository's CI Explained in: standards/driver.md KB-CI-011: kb-core CI builds every part for every MCU family and for no MCU ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. The standard describes this matrix as enforced; ci-tools has none. docs.text: MUST · all · since 1.0 Workflows use GitHub's own actions, the organisation's, or a third-party action on the allow-list in .github/org/actions-allowlist.json , always pinned to a full commit SHA with the version in a comment. docs.text: Proposed Enforced in ci-tools' own workflows today; the reusable check is planned. docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. driver-template's host tests still use their own workflow rather than ru-host-ci. Verified by: shared-workflows (planned): every lint, analysis, build, docs and release job calls a kokeb-labs/ci-tools reusable workflow at @v1, and none at @main review: A job that does not use a ci-tools workflow says why in a comment beside it. docs.title: KB-CI-003: Workflows call the shared ci-tools workflows at @v1

docs.text: MUST · all · since 1.0 The workflow's last job comes from ru-ci-gate, runs with if: always() and lists every other job in needs , so a skipped or failed job, an unsigned commit or a [skip ci] run cannot merge. Verified by: ci-gate (implemented): one required check that passes only when every job of the workflow passed dco (implemented): every commit of a pull request has a Signed-off-by line matching its author See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 8.2 (a change is verified before it is accepted) Explained in: standards/repo-governance.md
docs.title: KB-CI-004: The CI gate needs every other job, including DCO

docs.text: MUST · all · since 1.0 Workflows triggered by a fork's pull request get no secrets and a read-only token; pull_request_target and workflow_run never check out or run the pull request's code. Fork runs wait for a maintainer's approval. Verified by: actionlint (planned): actionlint and zizmor find nothing in the repository's workflows review: No workflow triggered by pull_request_target or workflow_run checks out the pull request head. Explained in: standards/repo-governance.md
docs.title: KB-CI-005: Code from a fork never runs with secrets

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. driver-template has the file; org-standard-check does not ask for it. SHOULD · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Every repository with workflows has .github/dependabot.yml updating github-actions weekly with the dependencies label and the ci prefix, plus pip where it has Python tooling. It never manages submodules. Verified by: dependabot-config (planned): .github/dependabot.yml updates github-actions weekly with label dependencies and prefix ci, pip where Python tooling exists, and has no gitsubmodule ecosystem Explained in: standards/repo-governance.md
docs.title: KB-CI-006: Dependabot keeps the actions current

docs.text: MUST · all · since 1.0 Secret scanning with push protection, Dependabot alerts and security updates, private vulnerability reporting and CodeQL default setup are on for every public repository. Verified by: org-settings-drift (planned): a scheduled kokeb_org.py --check finds no drift between org/ and the repository's live settings review: kokeb_org.py --check --section security reports no drift for the repository. docs.title: KB-CI-007: Public repositories run GitHub's security features

docs.text: MUST · all · since 1.0 Tokens, keys, passwords, private datasheet material and personal data never enter a commit, a log or an artifact. A secret that reached a commit is revoked, not just removed. Verified by: secret-scan (planned): gitleaks finds no secret in the pull request's commits review: Nothing in the diff, the logs or the artifacts is a credential or confidential material. Explained in: standards/agents.md
docs.title: KB-CI-008: No credentials, private datasheets or personal data are committed

docs.text: SHOULD · all · since 1.0 A workflow that pushes a tag other workflows react to uses a token from actions/create-github-app-token , because tags pushed with GITHUB_TOKEN start no workflow. Verified by: review: A tag push meant to trigger release or docs workflows uses a GitHub App token. Explained in: standards/release.md
docs.title: KB-CI-009: Tags that start workflows are pushed with a GitHub App token

docs.text: Coverage ¶ How the must rules are verified. Checked : a tool verifies it in CI today. Planned : the rule names a check that is not built yet. Review : verified in review against the pull-request checklist. Area Must rules Checked Planned Review Checked share Coding agents 17 5 10 2 29% Architecture 31 3 18 10 9% Build and CMake 21 5 15 1 23% C code 7 1 4 2 14% CI and supply chain 12 2 10 0 16% C++ code 108 47 42 19 43% Documentation 35 15 13 7 42% Git, review and release 21 6 14 1 28% Hardware and porting 9 0 8 1 0% Repository 16 12 4 0 75% Testing 21 8 11 2 38% All 298 104 149 45 34% Checks still to build ¶ actionlint : actionlint and zizmor find nothing in the repository's workflows agents-files : AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md exist and the handbook sections generated into them are current allocation-allowlist : a host run with malloc and operator new wrapped records every allocation; any outside start-up or not on the HAL's allowlist fails anomaly-list : the evidence package lists every open bug affecting the release, with impact and workaround ast-rules : a clang-query or libclang script over the compile database for one structural rule; the parameter names it (global-scope, driver-virtual, handler-names, handler-lock-guard, base-nvi, base-tostatus, detail-branch, deadline-compare, isr-calls, bitfield-frames) branch-name : the pull request's head branch matches ^(feat|fix|docs|ci|chore)/[a-z0-9-]+$ or release/<x>.<y> c-naming : clang-tidy readability-identifier-naming with C options (snake_case functions and variables, *_t typedefs, UPPER_CASE enumerators, repository prefix) run on .c files and C API headers changelog : CHANGELOG.md follows Keep a Changelog; a new version section is the next SemVer step, dated, not empty changelog-breaking : a pull request labelled breaking adds an entry under changelog-entry : a pull request that changes files outside docs/ and .github/ changes CHANGELOG.md under [Unreleased], unless it carries the no-changelog label changelog-frozen : a pull request's diff of CHANGELOG.md changes only the [Unreleased] section, a new release section and link lines claude-md-pointer : CLAUDE.md contains exactly the line @AGENTS.md and nothing else cmake-configure : a CMake configure test asserts the named property: standard-options, dev-warnings, kb-core-targets, backend-selection, mcu-gates (a wrong-MCU enable must fail), option-defaults, single-toggles codeowners : .github/CODEOWNERS has a * rule naming at least one owner compat-table : regenerating the tables derived from catalog/compat.yml leaves the tree unchanged config-drift : _config/.clang-format and _config/.clang-tidy equal the handbook's config/ files apart from the header conformance-tests : every kb::interfaces method has a conformance test, and each mcu/<family> port runs and passes the suite coverage-justification : every uncovered line, branch or condition is in docs/coverage-justification.yml, and nothing else is ctest-timeouts : every test ctest lists has a TIMEOUT property cubemx-discipline : the .ioc sets ProjectManager.CoupleFile=true and the library-copy option, and regenerating from the .ioc reproduces the committed tree except for USER CODE blocks and the patches listed in PATCHES.md dependabot-config : .github/dependabot.yml updates github-actions weekly with label dependencies and prefix ci, pip where Python tooling exists, and has no gitsubmodule ecosystem doc-file-names : every file under docs/ is lower-case kebab-case; root README, CHANGELOG, CONTRIBUTING, AGENTS, CLAUDE and LICENSE are exempt doc-snippets : every C++ block on the documentation site is a snippet from tests/docs/ and those files compile against the current headers (driver-template doc_snippets ctest and the kokeb-docs check) docs-drift : kokeb-docs check finds no generated region (README quickstart, examples list) or figure that differs from what the code generates docs-inline-code : no C++ fence longer than one line in docs/ or README.md is written inline; each comes from tests/docs via a --8<-- include or a generated region docs-nav : docs/.nav.yml has exactly the five tabs Home, Get started, Concepts, Guides, Reference in order, and contract.md sits under Concepts right after Architecture docs-page-set : docs/ has every page the documentation standard requires for the repository's declared kind, and each is in the navigation docs-touched : warns when a pull request changes inc/, a Kconfig or a CMake option without touching README.md, docs/ or CHANGELOG.md doxyfile-baseline : _config/Doxyfile exists and sets INPUT to the public headers, EXTRACT_ALL and EXTRACT_PRIVATE to NO, WARN_NO_PARAMDOC to YES and the org mainpage, compared with the ci-tools baseline driver-names : the driver's namespace, class, CMake target, macro prefix and Kconfig prefix all derive from the chip name in the repository name (driver-<chip>) duplicate-code : jscpd finds no block in a board HAL that duplicates kb-hal-common code above the configured threshold error-enum-values : a compiled test asserts the enumerator values of an error enum against the table on the errors page; the parameter names the enum (driver, kb-status) error-paths-tested : every error value the public API can return is asserted by at least one host test esp-idf-examples : every app in examples/esp32 builds with the pinned ESP-IDF, using the repository root as its component (runs today in driver-template esp32-examples-build-ci.yml through ci-tools ru-build) examples-build : every examples/<platform>/ folder is built by a job of the repository's CI exceptions-rtti-off : the exported library target compiles with -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti, not only the tests exported-target-flags : the library target's own sources and every public header compile with <CHIP>_ENABLE_WARNINGS=ON, the org warning set and -Werror file-names : source and test file names match the pattern for the repository's kind frozen-specs : a pull request changes no specification file whose frozen: field is set fuzzing : each parser's libFuzzer target runs on the host for a fixed time under ASan and UBSan without a finding hal-lint : the kb-hal-common lints run in a board HAL's or product's CI; the parameter names the lint (boundary, driver-access, allocation, lock) hal-lints : the kb-hal-common boundary, driver-access, allocation and lock lints pass in the board HAL hal-startup-test : a HAL host test with the host bind injects a failure into each manager in turn and checks that start-up stops, deinitialises the started managers in reverse and reports the failing ManagerId header-self-contained : every public header compiles on its own as the first include of a translation unit heading-skeleton : a Markdown file's headings match a required skeleton in order (parameter: contract, readme, adr, hf-hal-readme, hf-board-spec, hf-protocol-spec) hf-spec-metadata : each HardFOC specification starts with the metadata block (spec type, name, revision, status, covered repos or boards, authored, last reviewed, frozen) and the values validate against a schema hf-spec-names : HardFOC board specification files are named <board>-rev<X.Y[.Z]>.md, one file per revision hil-evidence : a hardware test record (commit, board and revision, toolchain, tests, results, date) exists for the release and each supported board, in the evidence format host-tests-matrix : the host tests pass with gcc and clang for each configuration of the named matrix (kb-rtos: KB_RTOS=FREERTOS host shim and KB_RTOS=NONE, with KB_MCU=HOST) include-graph : every #include in library code is allowed by the Layers include table for its folder; the parameter names the layer (driver, utils, rtos, interfaces, mcu, handlers, hal, product) or all installed-header-collisions : the install trees of the kb-core packages contain no path twice kb-core-catalog : every drivers/driver-<chip> gitlink is the commit of a v* release tag, has a handlers/<chip>/ folder and a catalog/compat.yml entry, and regenerating compat.yml and the MCU gate table from the pinned driver.yml files changes nothing kb-rtos-matrix : kb-core builds and its host tests pass with KB_RTOS set to FREERTOS (host shim), THREADX and NONE kconfig-symbols : every CONFIG_ symbol the sources read is defined in _config/Kconfig or by ESP-IDF layer-deps : kb-core's CMake targets link only downward (kb::utils <- kb::rtos <- kb::interfaces <- kb::handlers), read from the CMake file API, and each builds alone with KB_MCU=NONE and KB_MCU=HOST lighthouse : Lighthouse scores of the built site meet the org budget for accessibility, performance, best practices and SEO (ru-mkdocs-publish runs Lighthouse; register it as implemented once its failing job is confirmed) mcu-foundation-set : each real family under interfaces/mcu/ implements the eight foundation Base* interfaces, and enabling an optional one the family lacks fails at CMake configure time mcu-header-guards : every header under interfaces/mcu/<family>/ starts with an #error guard on KB_MCU_<FAMILY> mcu-matrix : kb-core CI builds every target for each MCU family (STM32 with stub headers), KB_MCU=HOST and NONE misra-checker : a commercial MISRA C++:2023 / C:2025 checker run, mapped to the compliance matrix (safety level) model-virtual-clock : a chip model for a driver whose port has DelayUs or DelayMs advances a virtual clock in those hooks, and a test runs a delayed-ready mode against it no-attribution : no commit message, pull-request body or review comment carries a Co-Authored-By trailer naming a tool or model, a "Generated with" footer, an AI-disclosure line or a tool banner (runs beside dco) no-heap-link : a test binary that links the library with operator new, malloc and free removed builds and runs open-safety-issues : the release workflow fails while an open issue labelled safety names the version or its milestone org-settings-drift : a scheduled kokeb_org.py --check finds no drift between org/ and the repository's live settings pin-bump-isolated : a pull request that moves a gitlink changes nothing else except version_lock.txt, compat.yml and CHANGELOG pin-check : every submodule points at a commit tagged v*.*.* on its own main and matching the manifest or catalog/compat.yml; warns on pull requests to main, fails on release/* and tag pushes pin-table-lint : a HardFOC pin table compiles in a host test that rejects names longer than 32 characters or starting with CORE_, COMM_, SYS_ or INTERNAL_ port-conformance : the Base* conformance suite passes for the named MCU family, on the host against a mocked SDK and, on a scheduled job with a board, as loopback tests pr-body-dod : the pull-request body has the definition-of-done checklist with every item ticked or marked not applicable with a reason, and the hardware line filled (verified, or not verified on hardware with bench steps) pr-template : the pull request body keeps the template's summary, why and verification headings, each non-empty, and every checklist box is ticked or marked not applicable pr-title : the pull request title is at most 72 characters, has no trailing period and no Conventional Commits prefix; a release pull request is titled Release vX.Y.Z with the version of the new changelog section prose-style : Vale with the Kokeb style; the parameter names the style rule provenance-header : the firmware's generated provenance header names its version, release train and the tag and SHA of every submodule, matching .gitmodules and git describe register-layout-asserts : every register or wire frame struct has static_assert on its size and field offsets release-artifacts : a product release has .bin, .elf, SHA-256 sums and the effective sdkconfig attached, or fails release-branch-protection : a ruleset on release/* allows changes only by pull request, squash, linear history and no deletion release-evidence : a release carries SHA256SUMS, an SBOM and build provenance; at safety level the evidence package too release-notes : the GitHub Release body equals the version's changelog section and has a Bench status: line release-tag : on a v* tag: the tag matches the declared version, the commit is on main or release/*, its CI gate passed, and a final tag points at the same commit as the latest rc of that version reproducible-build : two clean builds of the same commit in different directories produce byte-identical artefacts result-type-traits : static_asserts that the driver's Result<T> is [[nodiscard]], has ok() and an explicit bool conversion, and that T is default-constructible and trivially copyable safety-label : a pull request touching actuator, power-sequencing, OTP or peripheral-flash paths (labeler config) has the safety label, and a safety-labelled pull request has a human approval before merge sbom : the release attaches an SPDX SBOM listing every component and submodule the build contains sdkconfig-defaults : sdkconfig.defaults of every ESP-IDF project sets the named value (freertos-hz is CONFIG_FREERTOS_HZ=1000) secret-scan : gitleaks finds no secret in the pull request's commits security-policy : SECURITY.md exists in .github/ or is inherited from the organisation and names private reporting shared-workflows : every lint, analysis, build, docs and release job calls a kokeb-labs/ci-tools reusable workflow at @v1, and none at @main signed-tags : the release tag is a signed annotated tag and the evidence package has a valid signature (safety level) size-budget : flash and RAM use of each built image stays within the budget recorded in the repository skill-content-scan : gitleaks finds no secret under .claude/, and no SKILL.md tells an agent to merge, use an admin bypass, --no-verify, a bare NOLINT or skip a check skill-format : every .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md has YAML front matter with name equal to the kebab-case folder and a one-line description , followed by steps skills-present : .claude/skills has the skills the repository's kind requires: verify in code repositories, bump-pin when .gitmodules is not empty, release when released, add-driver-feature in drivers spdx-headers : every source file carries an SPDX licence identifier (REUSE) spelling : typos finds no misspelling (project words in config/typos.toml) stack-usage : the target build with -fstack-usage reports every task entry and ISR within the stack budget in the repository's budget file; unbounded (dynamic) frames fail submodule-graph : walking .gitmodules across the org's repositories finds no cycle and no submodule that points up the stack (product -> board HAL -> kb-hal-common and kb-core -> drivers) test-naming : host test sources are named test_<unit>.cpp after an existing unit of the library test-presence : every unit of the named kind has a test (handler: tests/host/test_<chip>_handler.cpp; public-function: each public function is called by a host test) test-repeat : ctest --repeat until-fail:20 --schedule-random passes, so no test depends on luck or order test-report : host test jobs upload a JUnit report and a line and branch coverage report as artifacts third-party-licences : every third_party/<name>/ has a licence file, and REUSE or scancode finds only MIT-compatible licences timing-budget : an on-target benchmark job compares measured worst-case times with the stored baseline and fails beyond its margin toolchain-pins : the repository lists exact versions of every supported compiler and ESP-IDF, and every CI build uses exactly those versions tsan : the concurrency host tests pass under ThreadSanitizer unused-error-codes : every chip-specific Error enumerator (16 and up) is returned somewhere in src/ or inc/ vendor-regen-diff : CI regenerates vendor code (CubeMX) from the committed project file and fails if the result differs from the committed sources outside user-code markers and PATCHES.md version-copies : project(), the package version, the generated version header, Doxyfile PROJECT_NUMBER, driver.yml and the version getter all equal the version in the build settings (driver-template version ctests, less driver.yml) version-lock : each version_lock.txt line REF_<repo>=vX.Y.Z@<sha> matches the submodule's pinned commit and its tag workflow-permissions : every workflow sets docs.text: actionlint : actionlint and zizmor find nothing in the repository's workflows agents-files : AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md exist and the handbook sections generated into them are current allocation-allowlist : a host run with malloc and operator new wrapped records every allocation; any outside start-up or not on the HAL's allowlist fails anomaly-list : the evidence package lists every open bug affecting the release, with impact and workaround ast-rules : a clang-query or libclang script over the compile database for one structural rule; the parameter names it (global-scope, driver-virtual, handler-names, handler-lock-guard, base-nvi, base-tostatus, detail-branch, deadline-compare, isr-calls, bitfield-frames) branch-name : the pull request's head branch matches ^(feat|fix|docs|ci|chore)/[a-z0-9-]+$ or release/<x>.<y> c-naming : clang-tidy readability-identifier-naming with C options (snake_case functions and variables, *_t typedefs, UPPER_CASE enumerators, repository prefix) run on .c files and C API headers changelog : CHANGELOG.md follows Keep a Changelog; a new version section is the next SemVer step, dated, not empty changelog-breaking : a pull request labelled breaking adds an entry under changelog-entry : a pull request that changes files outside docs/ and .github/ changes CHANGELOG.md under [Unreleased], unless it carries the no-changelog label changelog-frozen : a pull request's diff of CHANGELOG.md changes only the [Unreleased] section, a new release section and link lines claude-md-pointer : CLAUDE.md contains exactly the line @AGENTS.md and nothing else cmake-configure : a CMake configure test asserts the named property: standard-options, dev-warnings, kb-core-targets, backend-selection, mcu-gates (a wrong-MCU enable must fail), option-defaults, single-toggles codeowners : .github/CODEOWNERS has a * rule naming at least one owner compat-table : regenerating the tables derived from catalog/compat.yml leaves the tree unchanged config-drift : _config/.clang-format and _config/.clang-tidy equal the handbook's config/ files apart from the header conformance-tests : every kb::interfaces method has a conformance test, and each mcu/<family> port runs and passes the suite coverage-justification : every uncovered line, branch or condition is in docs/coverage-justification.yml, and nothing else is ctest-timeouts : every test ctest lists has a TIMEOUT property cubemx-discipline : the .ioc sets ProjectManager.CoupleFile=true and the library-copy option, and regenerating from the .ioc reproduces the committed tree except for USER CODE blocks and the patches listed in PATCHES.md dependabot-config : .github/dependabot.yml updates github-actions weekly with label dependencies and prefix ci, pip where Python tooling exists, and has no gitsubmodule ecosystem doc-file-names : every file under docs/ is lower-case kebab-case; root README, CHANGELOG, CONTRIBUTING, AGENTS, CLAUDE and LICENSE are exempt doc-snippets : every C++ block on the documentation site is a snippet from tests/docs/ and those files compile against the current headers (driver-template doc_snippets ctest and the kokeb-docs check) docs-drift : kokeb-docs check finds no generated region (README quickstart, examples list) or figure that differs from what the code generates docs-inline-code : no C++ fence longer than one line in docs/ or README.md is written inline; each comes from tests/docs via a --8<-- include or a generated region docs-nav : docs/.nav.yml has exactly the five tabs Home, Get started, Concepts, Guides, Reference in order, and contract.md sits under Concepts right after Architecture docs-page-set : docs/ has every page the documentation standard requires for the repository's declared kind, and each is in the navigation docs-touched : warns when a pull request changes inc/, a Kconfig or a CMake option without touching README.md, docs/ or CHANGELOG.md doxyfile-baseline : _config/Doxyfile exists and sets INPUT to the public headers, EXTRACT_ALL and EXTRACT_PRIVATE to NO, WARN_NO_PARAMDOC to YES and the org mainpage, compared with the ci-tools baseline driver-names : the driver's namespace, class, CMake target, macro prefix and Kconfig prefix all derive from the chip name in the repository name (driver-<chip>) duplicate-code : jscpd finds no block in a board HAL that duplicates kb-hal-common code above the configured threshold error-enum-values : a compiled test asserts the enumerator values of an error enum against the table on the errors page; the parameter names the enum (driver, kb-status) error-paths-tested : every error value the public API can return is asserted by at least one host test esp-idf-examples : every app in examples/esp32 builds with the pinned ESP-IDF, using the repository root as its component (runs today in driver-template esp32-examples-build-ci.yml through ci-tools ru-build) examples-build : every examples/<platform>/ folder is built by a job of the repository's CI exceptions-rtti-off : the exported library target compiles with -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti, not only the tests exported-target-flags : the library target's own sources and every public header compile with <CHIP>_ENABLE_WARNINGS=ON, the org warning set and -Werror file-names : source and test file names match the pattern for the repository's kind frozen-specs : a pull request changes no specification file whose frozen: field is set fuzzing : each parser's libFuzzer target runs on the host for a fixed time under ASan and UBSan without a finding hal-lint : the kb-hal-common lints run in a board HAL's or product's CI; the parameter names the lint (boundary, driver-access, allocation, lock) hal-lints : the kb-hal-common boundary, driver-access, allocation and lock lints pass in the board HAL hal-startup-test : a HAL host test with the host bind injects a failure into each manager in turn and checks that start-up stops, deinitialises the started managers in reverse and reports the failing ManagerId header-self-contained : every public header compiles on its own as the first include of a translation unit heading-skeleton : a Markdown file's headings match a required skeleton in order (parameter: contract, readme, adr, hf-hal-readme, hf-board-spec, hf-protocol-spec) hf-spec-metadata : each HardFOC specification starts with the metadata block (spec type, name, revision, status, covered repos or boards, authored, last reviewed, frozen) and the values validate against a schema hf-spec-names : HardFOC board specification files are named <board>-rev<X.Y[.Z]>.md, one file per revision hil-evidence : a hardware test record (commit, board and revision, toolchain, tests, results, date) exists for the release and each supported board, in the evidence format host-tests-matrix : the host tests pass with gcc and clang for each configuration of the named matrix (kb-rtos: KB_RTOS=FREERTOS host shim and KB_RTOS=NONE, with KB_MCU=HOST) include-graph : every #include in library code is allowed by the Layers include table for its folder; the parameter names the layer (driver, utils, rtos, interfaces, mcu, handlers, hal, product) or all installed-header-collisions : the install trees of the kb-core packages contain no path twice kb-core-catalog : every drivers/driver-<chip> gitlink is the commit of a v* release tag, has a handlers/<chip>/ folder and a catalog/compat.yml entry, and regenerating compat.yml and the MCU gate table from the pinned driver.yml files changes nothing kb-rtos-matrix : kb-core builds and its host tests pass with KB_RTOS set to FREERTOS (host shim), THREADX and NONE kconfig-symbols : every CONFIG_ symbol the sources read is defined in _config/Kconfig or by ESP-IDF layer-deps : kb-core's CMake targets link only downward (kb::utils <- kb::rtos <- kb::interfaces <- kb::handlers), read from the CMake file API, and each builds alone with KB_MCU=NONE and KB_MCU=HOST lighthouse : Lighthouse scores of the built site meet the org budget for accessibility, performance, best practices and SEO (ru-mkdocs-publish runs Lighthouse; register it as implemented once its failing job is confirmed) mcu-foundation-set : each real family under interfaces/mcu/ implements the eight foundation Base* interfaces, and enabling an optional one the family lacks fails at CMake configure time mcu-header-guards : every header under interfaces/mcu/<family>/ starts with an #error guard on KB_MCU_<FAMILY> mcu-matrix : kb-core CI builds every target for each MCU family (STM32 with stub headers), KB_MCU=HOST and NONE misra-checker : a commercial MISRA C++:2023 / C:2025 checker run, mapped to the compliance matrix (safety level) model-virtual-clock : a chip model for a driver whose port has DelayUs or DelayMs advances a virtual clock in those hooks, and a test runs a delayed-ready mode against it no-attribution : no commit message, pull-request body or review comment carries a Co-Authored-By trailer naming a tool or model, a "Generated with" footer, an AI-disclosure line or a tool banner (runs beside dco) no-heap-link : a test binary that links the library with operator new, malloc and free removed builds and runs open-safety-issues : the release workflow fails while an open issue labelled safety names the version or its milestone org-settings-drift : a scheduled kokeb_org.py --check finds no drift between org/ and the repository's live settings pin-bump-isolated : a pull request that moves a gitlink changes nothing else except version_lock.txt, compat.yml and CHANGELOG pin-check : every submodule points at a commit tagged v*.*.* on its own main and matching the manifest or catalog/compat.yml; warns on pull requests to main, fails on release/* and tag pushes pin-table-lint : a HardFOC pin table compiles in a host test that rejects names longer than 32 characters or starting with CORE_, COMM_, SYS_ or INTERNAL_ port-conformance : the Base* conformance suite passes for the named MCU family, on the host against a mocked SDK and, on a scheduled job with a board, as loopback tests pr-body-dod : the pull-request body has the definition-of-done checklist with every item ticked or marked not applicable with a reason, and the hardware line filled (verified, or not verified on hardware with bench steps) pr-template : the pull request body keeps the template's summary, why and verification headings, each non-empty, and every checklist box is ticked or marked not applicable pr-title : the pull request title is at most 72 characters, has no trailing period and no Conventional Commits prefix; a release pull request is titled Release vX.Y.Z with the version of the new changelog section prose-style : Vale with the Kokeb style; the parameter names the style rule provenance-header : the firmware's generated provenance header names its version, release train and the tag and SHA of every submodule, matching .gitmodules and git describe register-layout-asserts : every register or wire frame struct has static_assert on its size and field offsets release-artifacts : a product release has .bin, .elf, SHA-256 sums and the effective sdkconfig attached, or fails release-branch-protection : a ruleset on release/* allows changes only by pull request, squash, linear history and no deletion release-evidence : a release carries SHA256SUMS, an SBOM and build provenance; at safety level the evidence package too release-notes : the GitHub Release body equals the version's changelog section and has a Bench status: line release-tag : on a v* tag: the tag matches the declared version, the commit is on main or release/*, its CI gate passed, and a final tag points at the same commit as the latest rc of that version reproducible-build : two clean builds of the same commit in different directories produce byte-identical artefacts result-type-traits : static_asserts that the driver's Result<T> is [[nodiscard]], has ok() and an explicit bool conversion, and that T is default-constructible and trivially copyable safety-label : a pull request touching actuator, power-sequencing, OTP or peripheral-flash paths (labeler config) has the safety label, and a safety-labelled pull request has a human approval before merge sbom : the release attaches an SPDX SBOM listing every component and submodule the build contains sdkconfig-defaults : sdkconfig.defaults of every ESP-IDF project sets the named value (freertos-hz is CONFIG_FREERTOS_HZ=1000) secret-scan : gitleaks finds no secret in the pull request's commits security-policy : SECURITY.md exists in .github/ or is inherited from the organisation and names private reporting shared-workflows : every lint, analysis, build, docs and release job calls a kokeb-labs/ci-tools reusable workflow at @v1, and none at @main signed-tags : the release tag is a signed annotated tag and the evidence package has a valid signature (safety level) size-budget : flash and RAM use of each built image stays within the budget recorded in the repository skill-content-scan : gitleaks finds no secret under .claude/, and no SKILL.md tells an agent to merge, use an admin bypass, --no-verify, a bare NOLINT or skip a check skill-format : every .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md has YAML front matter with name equal to the kebab-case folder and a one-line description , followed by steps skills-present : .claude/skills has the skills the repository's kind requires: verify in code repositories, bump-pin when .gitmodules is not empty, release when released, add-driver-feature in drivers spdx-headers : every source file carries an SPDX licence identifier (REUSE) spelling : typos finds no misspelling (project words in config/typos.toml) stack-usage : the target build with -fstack-usage reports every task entry and ISR within the stack budget in the repository's budget file; unbounded (dynamic) frames fail submodule-graph : walking .gitmodules across the org's repositories finds no cycle and no submodule that points up the stack (product -> board HAL -> kb-hal-common and kb-core -> drivers) test-naming : host test sources are named test_<unit>.cpp after an existing unit of the library test-presence : every unit of the named kind has a test (handler: tests/host/test_<chip>_handler.cpp; public-function: each public function is called by a host test) test-repeat : ctest --repeat until-fail:20 --schedule-random passes, so no test depends on luck or order test-report : host test jobs upload a JUnit report and a line and branch coverage report as artifacts third-party-licences : every third_party/<name>/ has a licence file, and REUSE or scancode finds only MIT-compatible licences timing-budget : an on-target benchmark job compares measured worst-case times with the stored baseline and fails beyond its margin toolchain-pins : the repository lists exact versions of every supported compiler and ESP-IDF, and every CI build uses exactly those versions tsan : the concurrency host tests pass under ThreadSanitizer unused-error-codes : every chip-specific Error enumerator (16 and up) is returned somewhere in src/ or inc/ vendor-regen-diff : CI regenerates vendor code (CubeMX) from the committed project file and fails if the result differs from the committed sources outside user-code markers and PATCHES.md version-copies : project(), the package version, the generated version header, Doxyfile PROJECT_NUMBER, driver.yml and the version getter all equal the version in the build settings (driver-template version ctests, less driver.yml) version-lock : each version_lock.txt line REF_<repo>=vX.Y.Z@<sha> matches the submodule's pinned commit and its tag workflow-permissions : every workflow sets permissions at the top and grants each job the least it needs
