See also: C++ Core Guidelines CP.20 Explained in: standards/handler.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-063: Every public handler method holds the handler's mutex for its whole duration

docs.text: MUST · library, hal · since 1.0 Locks are taken in the order manager, handler, bus, and all are released before the call returns. A lock is never held across a long delay, a callback or a call into another handler. Why: One global order makes deadlock impossible by construction. Verified by: review: New lock acquisitions follow manager, handler, bus order and no lock is held across a callback. See also: SEI CERT C++ CON53-CPP; C++ Core Guidelines CP.22 Explained in: standards/threading-and-timing.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-064: Locks follow the fixed order and are held for one call only

docs.text: MUST · library · since 1.0 A handler has no public GetDriver() and returns no raw pointer or reference to its driver. VisitDriver(fn) takes the handler's locks, returns NotInitialized without calling fn when uninitialised, and fn must not keep the reference. Verified by: forbidden-patterns/get-driver (planned): a source scan for a construct the handbook bans; the parameter names the pattern set host-tests (implemented): the unit tests build and pass on the host with gcc and clang review: No VisitDriver callback stores the driver reference. Explained in: standards/handler.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-065: Handlers lend their driver only through VisitDriver

docs.text: MUST · library · since 1.0 A handler's adapter derives from the driver's port base and implements each hook with Base* calls, turning a kb_*_err_t failure into false . Its delay hooks call kb::DelayUs / kb::DelayMs and its Log hook forwards to the kb-core logger. Verified by: review: The adapter's hooks call only Base*, kb::Delay* and the kb-core logger. See also: ADR-0003 Explained in: standards/handler.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-066: The bus adapter implements the driver's port with Base calls only

docs.text: MUST · library · since 1.0 Every handler has GetDiagnostics() returning a struct whose first member is DiagnosticsHeader , updated on every call and copied out under the handler's lock. Verified by: host-tests (implemented): the unit tests build and pass on the host with gcc and clang review: The diagnostics struct starts with DiagnosticsHeader and is copied under the lock. Explained in: standards/handler.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-067: Every handler reports diagnostics with the common header first

docs.text: MUST · library · since 1.0 Per-channel wrappers a handler hands out live in a fixed array it owns, are created by EnsureInitialized() and forward through the handler's locked API. They are never shared_ptr s and never created on first use. Verified by: review: Wrappers are array members built in EnsureInitialized. See also: ADR-0004 Explained in: standards/handler.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-068: Channel wrappers live in a fixed array created at start-up

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · library · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Each Base<Periph>.h defines its kb_<periph>_err_t values with an X-macro list and a ToStatus() that maps every value to kb::Status . Verified by: ast-rules/base-tostatus (planned): a clang-query or libclang script over the compile database for one structural rule; the parameter names it (global-scope, driver-virtual, handler-names, handler-lock-guard, base-nvi, base-tostatus, detail-branch, deadline-compare, isr-calls, bitfield-frames) See also: ADR-0001 Explained in: standards/library.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-069: Each Base interface keeps its error list and a ToStatus mapping

docs.text: MUST · library · since 1.0 A Base* Initialize() is idempotent and EnsureInitialized() initialises on first use; neither allocates after start-up. An optional capability a port lacks (interrupts, statistics, diagnostics) returns the interface's unsupported code rather than failing silently. Verified by: host-tests (implemented): the unit tests build and pass on the host with gcc and clang See also: ADR-0002 Explained in: standards/library.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-070: Base interfaces start idempotently and report missing features as Unsupported

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. SHOULD · library · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A Base* class exposes its operations as non-virtual public functions that call protected virtual *Impl() functions; only capability queries ( IsPinAvailable , GetMaxPins , SupportsInterrupts ) are public virtual. Callers cannot set a raw electrical level. Why: The public wrapper is one place to check arguments, lock and count, whatever the MCU port does. Verified by: ast-rules/base-nvi (planned): a clang-query or libclang script over the compile database for one structural rule; the parameter names it (global-scope, driver-virtual, handler-names, handler-lock-guard, base-nvi, base-tostatus, detail-branch, deadline-compare, isr-calls, bitfield-frames)
docs.title: KB-CPP-071: Base interfaces expose operations through non-virtual public functions

docs.text: MUST · library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 A function that overrides a virtual function, including every MCU port's *Impl() , is marked override (or final ) and not repeated as virtual . Verified by: clang-tidy/modernize-use-override (implemented): a clang-tidy check from config/.clang-tidy, run with the CMake compile database See also: C++ Core Guidelines C.128
docs.title: KB-CPP-072: Every overriding function says override

docs.text: SHOULD · library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 A CRTP driver is never stored or passed as void* . Code that needs to treat different drivers alike goes through a Base* interface or a template. Verified by: review: No driver object is held as void*.
docs.title: KB-CPP-073: Drivers are never stored type-erased as void pointers

docs.text: GUIDE · library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 Keep hot paths (tight loops, single call sites above 1 kHz) on templates rather than Base* calls, and move code to a different dispatch only when a measurement shows the cost. Change dispatch step by step: add the new overload or interface, migrate callers, then delete the old one. See also: C++ Core Guidelines Per.6
docs.title: KB-CPP-074: Dispatch is chosen by measurement and changed incrementally

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 The RTOS backends create tasks, queues, mutexes and semaphores with the static-allocation API ( xTaskCreateStatic , xSemaphoreCreateMutexStatic ), never the heap-allocating variants. Verified by: forbidden-patterns/rtos-dynamic-create (planned): a source scan for a construct the handbook bans; the parameter names the pattern set See also: ADR-0004 ; NASA/JPL Power of Ten Rule 3
docs.title: KB-CPP-075: RTOS objects are statically allocated

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Above the platform bind, code never calls xTaskCreate , xSemaphoreTake , vTaskDelay or another raw RTOS function, and never uses std::thread or std::mutex . The only mutex is kb::RtosMutex with MutexLockGuard ; no other mutex wrapper is written. Why: The same code then runs on the FreeRTOS, ThreadX and no-RTOS backends. Verified by: forbidden-patterns/raw-rtos (planned): a source scan for a construct the handbook bans; the parameter names the pattern set Explained in: standards/threading-and-timing.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-076: Above the bind, threads, locks and delays go through kb::rtos only

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · library · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Code that uses kb::rtos works with KB_RTOS=FREERTOS , THREADX and NONE ; anything specific to one backend stays in that backend. Verified by: kb-rtos-matrix (planned): kb-core builds and its host tests pass with KB_RTOS set to FREERTOS (host shim), THREADX and NONE Explained in: standards/threading-and-timing.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-077: Code above kb::rtos builds and runs on every RTOS backend

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Above the bind, time is read only with kb::MonotonicUs() (64-bit, monotonic, safe in an ISR); never esp_timer_get_time , xTaskGetTickCount , HAL_GetTick or std::chrono::steady_clock . Waits that may exceed the tick counter's wrap (about 71 minutes) use it too. Verified by: forbidden-patterns/raw-clock (planned): a source scan for a construct the handbook bans; the parameter names the pattern set See also: ADR-0006 Explained in: standards/threading-and-timing.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-078: The only clock above the bind is kb::MonotonicUs

docs.text: MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 Durations and timestamps are uint32_t or uint64_t with a unit suffix. A deadline is checked by signed subtraction ( static_cast<int32_t>(now - deadline) >= 0 ), never with > on raw values, so it survives wrap-around. Verified by: ast-rules/deadline-compare (planned): a clang-query or libclang script over the compile database for one structural rule; the parameter names it (global-scope, driver-virtual, handler-names, handler-lock-guard, base-nvi, base-tostatus, detail-branch, deadline-compare, isr-calls, bitfield-frames) review: New deadline checks use signed subtraction. See also: ADR-0006 Explained in: standards/threading-and-timing.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-079: Durations are unsigned integers with a unit, and deadlines compare by subtraction

docs.text: MUST · library · since 1.0 A delay waits at least the time asked for. os_delay_msec rounds up to whole ticks and adds one; kb::DelayUs busy-waits on kb::MonotonicUs() below 1 ms and rounds 1000 us or more up to a millisecond delay; a delay of 0 returns at once or yields and never waits a tick. Why: A datasheet wait that is one tick short works on the bench and fails in the field. Verified by: host-tests (implemented): the unit tests build and pass on the host with gcc and clang See also: ADR-0006 Explained in: standards/threading-and-timing.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-080: Delays never return early

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Code that calls the RTOS converts milliseconds with pdMS_TO_TICKS() or the kb::rtos helpers and never passes a raw tick count. Verified by: forbidden-patterns/raw-ticks (planned): a source scan for a construct the handbook bans; the parameter names the pattern set See also: ADR-0006 Explained in: standards/threading-and-timing.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-081: Ticks are converted from milliseconds, never written as raw counts

docs.text: SHOULD · library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 Busy-waits longer than about 100 us are avoided in tasks above idle priority; use an RTOS delay or a timer. Verified by: review: No new busy-wait over 100 us runs above idle priority. Explained in: standards/threading-and-timing.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-082: Long busy-waits stay off normal task priorities

docs.text: MUST · library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 Work that must run at a fixed rate uses kb::PeriodicTimer or a loop that waits until the next absolute deadline, never a chain of relative delays. Verified by: review: Periodic work is driven by PeriodicTimer or absolute deadlines. Explained in: standards/threading-and-timing.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-083: Fixed-rate work uses a periodic timer or a drift-corrected loop

docs.text: MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 An interrupt handler never takes a mutex, waits or calls a function that may; it signals a task with OsEventFlags or a SignalSemaphore and returns. A manager or handler method that locks is never called from an ISR. Verified by: ast-rules/isr-calls (planned): a clang-query or libclang script over the compile database for one structural rule; the parameter names it (global-scope, driver-virtual, handler-names, handler-lock-guard, base-nvi, base-tostatus, detail-branch, deadline-compare, isr-calls, bitfield-frames) review: Every function documented as ISR context calls only ISR-safe functions. See also: SEI CERT C SIG31-C Explained in: standards/threading-and-timing.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-084: Interrupt handlers never block

docs.text: MUST · library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 Data read and written by more than one task is protected by one kb::RtosMutex , passed through an OsQueue , or published with a SeqlockSnapshot . A plain counter or flag may instead be a lock-free std::atomic with its memory order stated. Verified by: review: Each new piece of cross-task state names its guard. See also: C++ Core Guidelines CP.2 Explained in: standards/threading-and-timing.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-085: Data shared between tasks has exactly one guard

docs.text: MUST · library, hal · since 1.0 Only MCU port and bind code touches memory-mapped registers, through volatile -qualified accesses wrapped in a function that names the register. Drivers and code above the bind never touch MMIO. Verified by: review: MMIO access is volatile, inside mcu/ or bsp_bind/, and names its register. See also: SEI CERT C EXP32-C (never access a volatile object through a non-volatile reference)
docs.title: KB-CPP-086: Memory-mapped registers are accessed through volatile, only in the MCU port

docs.text: SHOULD · driver, library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 An interrupt handler declares no large local buffer and makes no deep or unbounded call chain; anything substantial is deferred to a task. Verified by: review: New ISR code has no large locals or deep call chains.
docs.title: KB-CPP-087: Interrupt handlers keep their stack small

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. config/.clang-tidy must enable misc-no-recursion first. MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware (high level and above) · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Target code is not recursive, and each task and interrupt stack has a budget that the compiler's stack-usage report ( -fstack-usage ) shows it stays within. Why: A stack overflow on a microcontroller corrupts memory silently long before anything faults. Verified by: stack-usage (planned): the target build with -fstack-usage reports every task entry and ISR within the stack budget in the repository's budget file; unbounded (dynamic) frames fail clang-tidy/misc-no-recursion (implemented): a clang-tidy check from config/.clang-tidy, run with the CMake compile database See also: NASA/JPL Power of Ten Rule 1 (no recursion)
docs.title: KB-CPP-088: Stack use is bounded, measured and within budget

docs.text: MUST · firmware · since 1.0 A product names every task's stack size, priority and core affinity in one header ( <board>::app::kTaskConfig ) and creates tasks through kb::rtos with those values, never with literals at the call site. Verified by: forbidden-patterns/literal-task-config (planned): a source scan for a construct the handbook bans; the parameter names the pattern set review: New tasks take their stack, priority and core from kTaskConfig. Explained in: standards/product.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-089: Task stacks, priorities and core affinity are named in one header

docs.text: SHOULD · firmware · since 1.0 Application code delays through the OS abstraction and never calls a sleep or wait-for-interrupt primitive ( esp_light_sleep_start , __WFI ) directly; the HAL chooses power modes. Verified by: review: No application code calls a CPU sleep primitive.
docs.title: KB-CPP-090: Applications never put the CPU to sleep themselves

docs.text: MUST · hal · since 1.0 Managers are objects in static storage owned by the board facade, which is the only way to reach them; there are no per-manager singletons. Any allocation during Initialize is on the HAL's start-up allowlist. Verified by: allocation-allowlist (planned): a host run with malloc and operator new wrapped records every allocation; any outside start-up or not on the HAL's allowlist fails review: New managers are facade members and add no GetInstance(). See also: ADR-0004 ; ADR-0005 Explained in: standards/hal.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-091: Managers live in static storage owned by the board facade

docs.text: MUST · hal · since 1.0 Every manager method either holds the manager's kb::RtosMutex or delegates to a thread-safe handler. Every fallible call returns kb::Status ; the manager keeps the last non- Ok status for GetLastError() until ClearLastError() , and while a dependency has failed every call returns DependencyNotReady . Verified by: host-tests (implemented): the unit tests build and pass on the host with gcc and clang review: Each manager method is locked or delegates to a locked handler. Explained in: standards/hal.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-092: Managers are thread-safe and report failure state consistently

docs.text: MUST · hal · since 1.0 The facade's CollectDiagnostics() visits every manager, and each manager writes its state and its handlers' diagnostics headers into the sink without logging. During start-up the facade gives the kb-core logger its sink. Verified by: host-tests (implemented): the unit tests build and pass on the host with gcc and clang review: New managers contribute to CollectDiagnostics and do not log from it. See also: ADR-0005 Explained in: standards/hal.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-093: Diagnostics are collected through one facade call into a sink

docs.text: MUST · hal · since 1.0 Bind functions are named Create* , Destroy* or Acquire* ; Create* returns nullptr or false on failure and is idempotent per slot. Buses are slots numbered below kMax* , and the bind stores its objects statically. Verified by: host-tests (implemented): the unit tests build and pass on the host with gcc and clang review: New bind functions use the Create/Destroy/Acquire verbs and slot limits. Explained in: standards/hal.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-094: The platform bind uses fixed verbs and fixed slots

docs.text: Retired Duplicate of KB-ARCH-017, merged when the rules were loaded. Replaced by KB-ARCH-017. MUST · hal, firmware · since 1.0 GPIO numbers and other physical pin identifiers appear only in the board's pin table and the bind; managers and products use functional names. Verified by: forbidden-patterns/raw-pins (planned): a source scan for a construct the handbook bans; the parameter names the pattern set review: No pin number appears outside the pin table and bind. Explained in: standards/hal.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-095: Raw pin numbers appear only in the pin table and the bind

docs.text: MUST · library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 A reference or pointer to an object owned elsewhere (a manager's component, a handler's driver, a caller's buffer) is never stored beyond the owner's lifetime. Getters return references to objects the owner keeps. Verified by: clang-tidy/bugprone-dangling-handle (implemented): a clang-tidy check from config/.clang-tidy, run with the CMake compile database review: No new member stores a borrowed reference that can outlive its owner.
docs.title: KB-CPP-096: Borrowed references never outlive their owner

docs.text: SHOULD · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 A lock, critical section, chip select or other resource held for a scope is released by a guard object's destructor, never by a matching manual call on every path; guards delete their copy operations. Hardware is still acquired in Initialize() , not in a constructor (KB-CPP-057). Verified by: review: New scoped resources are released by a guard. See also: C++ Core Guidelines R.1
docs.title: KB-CPP-097: Scoped resources are released by RAII guards

docs.text: SHOULD · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 Constants and simple functions are constexpr variables, enums or constexpr functions, not macros. Macros are left for conditional compilation and the few cases that need the preprocessor. Verified by: clang-tidy/cppcoreguidelines-macro-usage (implemented): a clang-tidy check from config/.clang-tidy, run with the CMake compile database clang-tidy/modernize-macro-to-enum (implemented): a clang-tidy check from config/.clang-tidy, run with the CMake compile database See also: C++ Core Guidelines ES.31
docs.title: KB-CPP-098: Constants are constexpr, not macros

docs.text: SHOULD · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 Member functions that do not change the object are const , and reference parameters are const& unless the function changes the argument. Locals and members that never change are const or constexpr . Verified by: clang-tidy/readability-make-member-function-const (implemented): a clang-tidy check from config/.clang-tidy, run with the CMake compile database See also: C++ Core Guidelines Con.2
docs.title: KB-CPP-099: Const by default

docs.text: SHOULD · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 Parameters that are expensive to copy are passed by const& ; cheap types by value. Where a value's ownership passes to the callee, it is moved rather than copied. Verified by: clang-tidy/performance-unnecessary-value-param (implemented): a clang-tidy check from config/.clang-tidy, run with the CMake compile database See also: C++ Core Guidelines F.16
docs.title: KB-CPP-100: Large objects are passed by const reference, and moved when ownership moves

docs.text: MUST · library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 No object with static storage is initialised from another translation unit's static object. Objects that need each other are initialised explicitly, in order, at start-up. Verified by: clang-tidy/cppcoreguidelines-interfaces-global-init (implemented): a clang-tidy check from config/.clang-tidy, run with the CMake compile database review: New static objects do not read other translation units' statics during initialisation. See also: C++ Core Guidelines I.22; SEI CERT C++ DCL56-CPP
docs.title: KB-CPP-101: Static initialisation never depends on translation-unit order

docs.text: MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 Constructor initialiser lists name members in the order they are declared, and reference members are initialised there rather than assigned in the body; members that depend on each other are declared in dependency order. Verified by: compiler-warnings/-Wreorder (implemented): the build is warning-free with the named flag and -Werror clang-tidy/cppcoreguidelines-prefer-member-initializer (implemented): a clang-tidy check from config/.clang-tidy, run with the CMake compile database See also: C++ Core Guidelines C.47
docs.title: KB-CPP-102: Members are initialised in declaration order

docs.text: SHOULD · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 Register values, wire fields, counters and anything whose width matters use <cstdint> fixed-width types ( uint8_t , int32_t ); size_t for sizes and indices, and bool for truth values. Plain int and long are not used for such data. Verified by: review: New register, frame and counter fields use fixed-width types.
docs.title: KB-CPP-103: Fixed-width integer types where size matters

docs.text: MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 Arithmetic on sizes, offsets, register values and durations cannot overflow a signed type or narrow without an explicit, range-checked conversion. The build is clean with -Wconversion and -Wsign-conversion . Verified by: compiler-warnings/-Wconversion (implemented): the build is warning-free with the named flag and -Werror compiler-warnings/-Wsign-conversion (implemented): the build is warning-free with the named flag and -Werror clang-tidy/bugprone-narrowing-conversions (implemented): a clang-tidy check from config/.clang-tidy, run with the CMake compile database clang-tidy/bugprone-implicit-widening-of-multiplication-result (implemented): a clang-tidy check from config/.clang-tidy, run with the CMake compile database See also: SEI CERT C INT31-C; SEI CERT C INT32-C; C++ Core Guidelines ES.46
docs.title: KB-CPP-104: Integer arithmetic does not overflow or narrow silently

docs.text: MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 Masks, shifts and bit tests use unsigned operands, and no shift count is negative or at least the width of the shifted type. Verified by: cppcheck/shiftTooManyBits (implemented): cppcheck in strict mode; the parameter names the cppcheck message id cppcheck/shiftNegative (implemented): cppcheck in strict mode; the parameter names the cppcheck message id review: New bit manipulation uses unsigned operands. See also: SEI CERT C INT34-C; C++ Core Guidelines ES.101
docs.title: KB-CPP-105: Bit operations use unsigned operands and shifts stay within the width

docs.text: MUST · driver, library, hal, template · since 1.0 Register fields and multi-byte wire values are built and read with masks, shifts and explicit byte order. Bit fields do not describe hardware or wire layouts, and a byte buffer is never cast or memcpy 'd into a multi-byte integer whose byte order is assumed. Why: Bit-field order and padding are implementation-defined, and byte order differs between targets. Verified by: ast-rules/bitfield-frames (planned): a clang-query or libclang script over the compile database for one structural rule; the parameter names it (global-scope, driver-virtual, handler-names, handler-lock-guard, base-nvi, base-tostatus, detail-branch, deadline-compare, isr-calls, bitfield-frames) review: New register and frame code uses masks, shifts and explicit byte order. See also: SEI CERT C EXP39-C
docs.title: KB-CPP-106: Register fields and wire bytes are packed with masks, shifts and explicit byte order

docs.text: GUIDE · driver, template · since 1.0 Describe a chip's registers once, as a table (an X-macro list or constexpr array of address, width, reset value and access), and derive accessors from it, rather than scattering addresses through the code.
docs.title: KB-CPP-107: Register maps are written as tables

docs.text: MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 Code that parses bytes from outside the program (bus frames, CANopen, Modbus, OTA images, CRC-protected records) checks length, type and range before reading any field and returns an error for malformed input. Verified by: sanitizers (implemented): host tests pass under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer review: Each new parser rejects short, oversized and mistyped input before reading fields. See also: SEI CERT C ARR30-C; NASA/JPL Power of Ten Rule 7
docs.title: KB-CPP-108: Parsers of external input check length and type before use

docs.text: Retired Duplicate of KB-TST-020, merged when the rules were loaded. Replaced by KB-TST-020. MUST · driver, library, hal (high level and above) · since 1.0 Each parser of external input has a libFuzzer target built on the host and run in CI for a fixed time with AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer. Verified by: fuzzing (planned): each parser's libFuzzer target runs on the host for a fixed time under ASan and UBSan without a finding
docs.title: KB-CPP-109: Frame, CRC and protocol parsers have fuzz targets

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware (safety level and above) · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Repositories at the safety level follow the MISRA C++:2023 and MISRA C:2025 subset the compliance matrix adopts, checked by a MISRA-capable analyser, and every departure is a recorded deviation. Verified by: misra-checker (planned): a commercial MISRA C++:2023 / C:2025 checker run, mapped to the compliance matrix (safety level) misra-matrix (implemented): the MISRA C++:2023 compliance matrix lists all 179 guidelines once, never weakens a category, names a verification for each, and its deviations cite existing non-mandatory guidelines (checks/misra_matrix.py) See also: MISRA C++:2023; MISRA C:2025 Explained in: deviations.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-110: At the safety level, code follows the MISRA subset in the compliance matrix

docs.text: SHOULD · all · since 1.0 Comments say why the code does what it does, not what it does. A reference to a datasheet names the document, section and table or register. Verified by: review: New comments explain intent and datasheet references name section and table. Explained in: standards/naming-and-style.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-111: Comments explain why, and datasheet references are exact

docs.text: MUST · all · since 1.0 Source files contain no commented-out code, no TODO without an issue link, no author, date or copyright banner (the SPDX line carries the licence), and no line crediting a tool or agent. Why: Git already records who wrote what and when; banners go stale and attribution lines leak tooling. Verified by: forbidden-patterns/comment-hygiene (planned): a source scan for a construct the handbook bans; the parameter names the pattern set review: The change adds no commented-out code, untracked TODO, banner or attribution line. Explained in: standards/naming-and-style.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-112: No commented-out code, untracked TODOs, author banners or tool attribution

docs.text: GUIDE · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 Within a class, list public members first, then protected, then private; constructors and destructor first in their section and data members last.
docs.title: KB-CPP-113: Class members are grouped by access

docs.text: GUIDE · library, hal, firmware · since 1.0 A start-up step that can take long (probing a bus with retries, waiting for a chip to boot) is either behind a configuration option or reported to the caller, so a board does not appear to hang at boot.
docs.title: KB-CPP-114: Slow start-up steps are opt-in or visible

docs.text: MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 Every function in library code stays within the limits of the repository's level, measured by lizard with the modified cyclomatic complexity: standard 15 / 80 lines / 7 parameters; high 15 / 60 / 6; safety 10 / 60 / 6. A function over a limit that is clearer as one piece has a deviation record. Why: Complex functions are where defects hide and where tests miss paths; the numbers and their sources are in ADR-0020. Verified by: complexity/level (implemented): lizard finds no library function over the complexity, length or parameter limit of the level (ADR-0020) See also: ADR-0020 ; NASA/JPL Power of Ten Rule 4; C++ Core Guidelines F.3 Explained in: deviations.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-115: Functions stay within the complexity, length and parameter limits of their level

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A reply that a stuck, floating or looped-back line can produce (all zeros, all ones, the command echoed back, the same word repeated) is never returned as a value: the driver maps it to NoDevice or another error. A ready or idle status that a line could fake counts only when a second read confirms it. Why: Observed on hardware: a floating input reads as a plausible value and hides an absent or unpowered chip; an idle status read from a line held high let a driver go on to write into nothing. Verified by: error-paths-tested (planned): every error value the public API can return is asserted by at least one host test review: The chip model has StuckLow, FloatHigh, Echo and Deaf line modes, and a test runs each against the start-up and every read path and expects an error, never a value. Explained in: standards/driver.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-116: A reply a stuck or floating line can produce is never data

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. Sharpens the identity step of KB-CPP-058. MUST · driver, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 The start-up identity check needs an active answer from the chip: a select-and-echo, a bit the chip must toggle, or a write followed by a read-back. A stuck, looped-back or deaf line cannot pass it, and a partial, bit-shifted or phantom ID is refused. A chip that answers its ID but is not ready still fails (KB-CPP-124). Why: Observed on hardware: a passive ID read is satisfied by line states, so identity checks passed on dead buses and on a looped-back data line. Verified by: host-tests (implemented): the unit tests build and pass on the host with gcc and clang review: The line modes of KB-CPP-116 applied to EnsureInitialized() each fail start-up; a shifted or partial ID is refused with DeviceIdMismatch . Explained in: standards/driver.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-117: The identity check is one a dead or looped bus cannot pass

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 After a transfer that failed, or whose outcome is unknown, the driver first brings the chip's protocol back to a known point before it sends a new command: a no-op that is harmless both as a command and as data, a frame that closes an open sequence, or the command byte sent again. A lost half of a multi-frame command never turns the next command into data. Why: Observed on hardware and in the fuzzer: a lost first half of a two-frame write made the next command data, which desynchronised the chip and in one model armed an irreversible write. Verified by: fuzzing (planned): each parser's libFuzzer target runs on the host for a fixed time under ASan and UBSan without a finding review: The fuzz harness's lost-transfer mode runs against the driver's invariants and the resync is documented. Explained in: standards/driver.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-118: After a failed transfer the chip's protocol state is restored first

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Every read of a clear-on-read or write-1-to-clear flag that the driver makes, internal reads included (a ready poll, a verify read), ORs the flags into one latch the driver owns. The caller reads it with a Get* accessor that does no I/O and empties it with an explicit Clear* call. A write-1-to-clear write is never verified by reading it back. Why: Observed on hardware: internal reads consumed fault and warning flags the caller never saw, so a fault output fired with no recorded cause. Verified by: review: Each clear-on-read flag is ORed into the latch on every read path; a model test raises a flag, triggers an internal read, and still finds the flag in the latch. Explained in: standards/driver.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-119: Clear-on-read and write-1-to-clear flags collect in one driver-owned latch

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A setter changes the driver's copy of a setting only after the frame that changes the chip succeeded. When the chip applies a change later (a pipeline, the next chip-select edge, a separate program bit), the setter completes the change before it returns, or discards the replies taken before it. Why: Observed on hardware: a copy that disagreed with the chip produced conversions off by a factor of two and channels that silently stayed off. Verified by: host-tests (implemented): the unit tests build and pass on the host with gcc and clang review: A model test fails the change frame and expects the getter to return the old value. Explained in: standards/driver.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-120: A setter updates the driver's copy only after the chip accepted the change

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A setter never changes another setting as a side effect (a mode, another channel's enable, a shared field). When the chip accepts a change only in some state (all channels off, standby, sleep), a call outside that state returns a chip-specific error and sends nothing. Why: Observed on hardware: the chip ignored a change made in the wrong state, and a setter rewrote a shared mode field, so a duty-cycle setting became a current setting and another channel's enable was cleared. Verified by: review: Each state-gated field has a model test that calls the setter in the wrong state and sees no frame. Explained in: standards/driver.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-121: A setter changes only what it names; state-gated changes are refused outside their state

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Control and output registers are written as a whole from the driver's validated copy. A read-modify-write uses only a read validated per KB-ARCH-042, so a corrupt read cannot flip other fields (enables, resets, restart bits). Why: Observed on hardware, a corrupt read inside a read-modify-write flipped unrelated control bits. Verified by: review: Every control-register write comes from the copy, or from a read that passed its integrity checks. Explained in: standards/driver.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-122: Control and output registers are written whole from the driver's copy

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 inc/<chip>_<bus>_interface.hpp declares what the chip needs from the bus as constexpr values. SPI: kSpiMode , kMsbFirst , kMaxClockHz , kMinCsHighNs , kCsSetupNs , kCsHoldNs and kContinuousWord (a word must be clocked with no idle between bytes). I2C: kI2cAddress (the 7-bit address, or the base address when pins select it), kMaxClockHz and kRepeatedStart (a read needs a combined write-read). UART: kMaxBaudRate and kTurnaroundUs . Turnaround and inter-frame gaps the chip needs are added the same way. The Porting page lists them, and the example ports check their settings against them with static_assert . Why: Observed on hardware: requirements kept as prose were violated: idle clocks inside a word, a clock above what the chip's firmware accepts, the wrong mode on a shared bus. Constants make the port prove its settings at compile time. Verified by: bus-requirements (implemented): for every SPI, I2C or UART bus in driver.yml, inc/<chip>_<bus>_interface.hpp declares the KB-CPP-123 constants as constexpr review: Each example port and the board config static_assert their bus settings against the constants. Explained in: standards/driver.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-123: The bus requirements are constexpr in the bus interface header

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. Works with KB-CPP-080 and KB-CPP-114. MUST · driver, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Start-up waits for the chip's own ready indication: first the datasheet minimum, then a bounded poll of the ready, busy or ID bit with a deadline from Config . A fixed delay alone is not enough, a correct ID is not readiness, and a delay never returns early. An expired deadline returns Timeout or NotReady . Why: Observed on hardware: chips answered their ID before they were ready, and the wake time varied with the supply ramp by more than ten times. Verified by: model-virtual-clock (planned): a chip model for a driver whose port has DelayUs or DelayMs advances a virtual clock in those hooks, and a test runs a delayed-ready mode against it review: A model with a virtual clock and a delayed-ready mode shows the driver neither returns early nor waits past its deadline. See also: NASA/JPL Power of Ten Rule 2 (fixed upper bound on loops) Explained in: standards/driver.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-124: Start-up waits for the chip's own ready indication, bounded by a Config deadline

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Before its first variant-specific write the driver confirms the variant: detected from the chip, or configured and then checked. An inconclusive detection fails start-up; where detection is not guaranteed, the variant is a Config field. Why: Observed on hardware: a write to a register the variant lacks, or a formula taken from the other variant, gave errors up to 256 times the intended value. Verified by: review: Every variant-specific path runs after the variant check; a model test covers each mismatch. Explained in: standards/driver.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-125: The chip variant is confirmed before any variant-specific write

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Arguments and Config fields are checked against the datasheet's operating range, not the register's range, and a value outside it returns InvalidArgument ; nothing is silently clamped. When a value is quantised, the call returns or exposes the value actually programmed. A conversion that lacks an input it needs returns an error, never 0 or a sentinel. Why: Observed on hardware: silent clamps and zero returns produced plausible but wrong outputs, a move to position zero and a reading 17 % off. Verified by: error-paths-tested (planned): every error value the public API can return is asserted by at least one host test review: Each range comes from the datasheet's operating conditions; quantised setters report what was set. See also: MISRA C++:2023 Dir 0.3.2 (preconditions are checked, not assumed) Explained in: standards/driver.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-126: Values are checked against the operating range and never silently clamped

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A reading that is not a measurement (a settling sentinel, frozen feedback, the first conversion after a reset, a sensor not fitted, a magnet or gain warning) is returned as NotReady or a chip-specific error, never as a value. A multi-item read reports validity per item; it neither fails the whole group nor fills in zeros. Why: Observed on hardware, settling sentinels and frozen feedback decoded as confident wrong values. Verified by: review: Each sentinel the datasheet names has a model test that expects an error or an invalid item. Explained in: standards/driver.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-127: A state that is not a measurement is an error, never a number

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A conversion that depends on another chip setting (a chopping frequency, a timebase, counts per revolution, a period register) takes it from the validated copy or reads it, never from a fixed default. Why: Observed on hardware, scale factors computed from a default setting were off by 3 to 460 times. Verified by: review: Every conversion lists the settings it depends on and reads each from the copy or the chip. Explained in: standards/driver.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-128: A conversion that depends on another setting uses the chip's actual setting

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A driver offers a single-shot raw access with no retries (a raw register read or a frame trace) and a GetLast* accessor, with no I/O, for the last raw reply or status byte. Diagnostic reads have no side effects, or their documentation names them. Why: Observed on hardware: the raw single-shot access located a deaf input and a host bus fault that the retried paths hid. Verified by: raw-access (implemented): the driver header declares a single-shot raw access (ReadRegister..., ReadRaw... or Trace...) and a no-I/O GetLast... accessor review: The raw access does not retry and the API guide names any side effect of a diagnostic read. Explained in: standards/driver.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-129: Every driver offers single-shot raw access and the last raw reply

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 An I2C driver documents which transfers the chip NACKs by design (a reset command, a busy chip) and does not report those as bus errors. It never probes with an empty or zero-length transfer, and it uses a combined write-read (repeated START) wherever the chip requires one ( kRepeatedStart , KB-CPP-123). Why: Observed on hardware: empty probes locked up a device and corrupted later reads, and a write-STOP-read sequence was NACKed by a chip that needs a repeated START. Verified by: forbidden-patterns/zero-length-i2c (planned): a source scan for a construct the handbook bans; the parameter names the pattern set review: The Porting page lists the NACK-by-design transfers and the driver's handling of each. Explained in: standards/driver.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-130: An I2C driver handles NACK-by-design, sends no empty probe, and uses repeated START

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A driver turns on a load-dependent diagnostic (open load, plunger or motion detection) only for channels the Config declares as loaded, and sets the routing of faults to a shared fault pin from the same declaration before the chip is armed. Why: Observed on hardware: open-load warnings on unloaded channels held the shared fault line and looked like a failing chip. Verified by: review: A model test arms the chip with an unloaded channel and sees no load diagnostic and no fault output. Explained in: standards/driver.md
docs.title: KB-CPP-131: Load-dependent diagnostics run only on channels Config declares as loaded

Verified by: markdownlint/all (implemented): markdownlint-cli2 with the org config; the parameter names the rule (markdownlint/MD040) KB-DOC-002: The documentation site builds strictly ¶ MUST · driver, library, hal, tooling, docs, template · since 1.0 A repository with a documentation site builds it with mkdocs --strict : no broken internal link, no page left out of the navigation. Verified by: mkdocs-strict (implemented): the documentation site builds with mkdocs --strict (no broken internal link, every page in the nav) Explained in: standards/docs.md KB-DOC-003: No broken links on the built site ¶ MUST · driver, library, hal, tooling, docs, template · since 1.0 Every link on the built site resolves, internal and external. Verified by: link-check (implemented): lychee finds no broken link on the built site KB-DOC-004: Every public API is documented and Doxygen is warning-free ¶ MUST · driver, library, hal, template · since 1.0 Every public type, function and parameter in inc/ has a Doxygen comment; Doxygen runs with WARN_IF_UNDOCUMENTED = YES and WARN_AS_ERROR = FAIL_ON_WARNINGS . Verified by: doxygen-warnings (implemented): Doxygen with WARN_AS_ERROR = FAIL_ON_WARNINGS and WARN_IF_UNDOCUMENTED reports nothing Explained in: standards/docs.md KB-DOC-005: Every public repository publishes a versioned MkDocs site ¶ MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, tooling, docs, template · since 1.0 Every public repository publishes its documentation at https://kokeb-labs.github.io/<repo>/ through ru-mkdocs-publish , built with kokeb-mkdocs-theme and versioned per v* tag; a code repository merges its Doxygen reference under api/ . A -rc tag publishes its version without moving the latest alias. Why: One platform and one theme mean a reader finds the same layout on every site, and a pinned version per tag means the page a user reads matches the code they built. Verified by: mkdocs-strict (implemented): the documentation site builds with mkdocs --strict (no broken internal link, every page in the nav) review: The docs workflow calls ru-mkdocs-publish and the site is live at kokeb-labs.github.io/<repo>/. Explained in: standards/docs.md KB-DOC-006: Pages live in docs/ and the site config in _config/mkdocs.yml ¶ MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, tooling, docs, template · since 1.0 Pages live in docs/ . The site configuration is _config/mkdocs.yml with docs_dir: ../docs , and the docs workflow is passed mkdocs_config: _config/mkdocs.yml and, in a code repository, doxygen_config: _config/Doxyfile . Verified by: mkdocs-strict (implemented): the documentation site builds with mkdocs --strict (no broken internal link, every page in the nav) review: The docs workflow passes mkdocs_config and doxygen_config with the _config/ paths. See also: ADR-0011 Explained in: standards/docs.md KB-DOC-007: The navigation has the five standard tabs ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, tooling, docs, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 docs/.nav.yml has exactly five top-level tabs, in this order: Home, Get started, Concepts, Guides, Reference. Deep dives go under Concepts and configuration references under Guides. Verified by: docs-nav (planned): docs/.nav.yml has exactly the five tabs Home, Get started, Concepts, Guides, Reference in order, and contract.md sits under Concepts right after Architecture Explained in: standards/docs.md KB-DOC-008: The site has the page set for its kind ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, tooling, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 docs/ holds every page the documentation standard lists for the repository's kind (driver, standalone library, kb-core, HAL, product, CI and tools). A page that cannot apply, such as Configuration for a driver with no Config , is left out rather than kept empty. Why: A fixed page set lets a reader move between repositories without relearning where things are, and lets a check say what is missing. Verified by: docs-page-set (planned): docs/ has every page the documentation standard requires for the repository's declared kind, and each is in the navigation Explained in: standards/docs.md KB-DOC-009: Every code repository has a Contract page under Concepts ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Every driver, library, kb-core, HAL and product has docs/contract.md , listed under Concepts right after Architecture. Verified by: docs-page-set (planned): docs/ has every page the documentation standard requires for the repository's declared kind, and each is in the navigation docs-nav (planned): docs/.nav.yml has exactly the five tabs Home, Get started, Concepts, Guides, Reference in order, and contract.md sits under Concepts right after Architecture Explained in: standards/docs.md KB-DOC-010: The Contract page has the standard sections in order ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 docs/contract.md has the sections Promises, Depends on, Threading, Errors, Memory, Platform and Deviations from the standard, in that order, after a one-line purpose. Why: The Contract is the short normative summary a caller or an auditor reads first; fixed sections make a missing promise visible. Verified by: heading-skeleton/contract (planned): a Markdown file's headings match a required skeleton in order (parameter: contract, readme, adr, hf-hal-readme, hf-board-spec, hf-protocol-spec) See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 5.4.3 (detailed design of software unit interfaces) Explained in: standards/docs.md KB-DOC-011: The Contract page lists every handbook rule the repository does not meet ¶ MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 The Deviations section names, by rule ID, each handbook rule the repository does not meet yet, with its issue or waiver. An empty section says "None". Verified by: review: Every waiver in .kokeb/handbook.yml and every known unmet rule appears in the Deviations section with its issue. Explained in: deviations.md KB-DOC-012: Repository docs link the handbook instead of restating it ¶ SHOULD · all · since 1.0 The handbook is the single source of the rules. A repository's docs, Contract page, templates and CI link the rule they follow and state only what is specific to the repository; no repository keeps a copy of the handbook or of its pages. Why: A copied rule drifts from the original the first time either is edited. Verified by: review: No page restates a handbook rule that it could link; no vendored copy of handbook pages. Explained in: standards/docs.md KB-DOC-013: CONTRIBUTING.md links the handbook ¶ SHOULD · all · since 1.0 A repository's CONTRIBUTING.md, or the organisation default it inherits, links the handbook. AGENTS.md links it as KB-AGT-005 requires. Verified by: review: CONTRIBUTING.md (own or the org default) links kokeb-labs.github.io/handbook. KB-DOC-014: A change to behaviour or API updates its docs in the same pull request ¶ SHOULD · all · since 1.0 A pull request that changes behaviour, the public API, a pin, a default or a build option updates the README, the pages under docs/ and the CHANGELOG entry that describe it, in the same pull request. Why: Docs updated later are docs that are wrong in between, and usually stay wrong. Verified by: docs-touched (planned): warns when a pull request changes inc/, a Kconfig or a CMake option without touching README.md, docs/ or CHANGELOG.md review: Every page that describes the changed behaviour is updated in this pull request. KB-DOC-015: The README has the standard sections in order ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. SHOULD · driver, library, hal, firmware, tooling, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 The README has, in order and only where they apply: title and hero line, true badges, the bold docs link, a plain-language paragraph, one figure, At a glance (with the status), Datasheet, Try it on your PC, Use it on your MCU, What it does, Install, Documentation (with "Read it when you want to"), Tests and quality, License. Verified by: heading-skeleton/readme (planned): a Markdown file's headings match a required skeleton in order (parameter: contract, readme, adr, hf-hal-readme, hf-board-spec, hf-protocol-spec) Explained in: standards/docs.md KB-DOC-016: The README is short and leaves the reference to the site ¶ SHOULD · all · since 1.0 A README has no table of contents, no emoji walls, no check-mark feature lists, no badge that links nowhere or states something untrue, and no API tables that duplicate the site. Verified by: prose-style/emoji (planned): Vale with the Kokeb style; the parameter names the style rule review: The README has none of the banned elements and every badge is live and true. Explained in: standards/docs.md KB-DOC-017: A driver's README names the chip and the part, not the organisation ¶ MUST · driver, template · since 1.0 A driver's README and site name the chip and part it drives; the organisation appears only in links and the licence line, so the driver reads as usable on its own. Verified by: forbidden-patterns/readme-org-name (planned): a source scan for a construct the handbook bans; the parameter names the pattern set review: The README names the chip and part; no Kokeb Labs or HardFOC branding outside links. See also: ADR-0012 Explained in: standards/docs.md KB-DOC-018: The README licence line matches LICENSE and the package metadata ¶ MUST · all · since 1.0 The README's License line, LICENSE and every package manifest ( idf_component.yml , library.json and the like) name the same licence: MIT for code, CERN-OHL-P-2.0 for a hardware design. Verified by: review: README License line, LICENSE and package manifests name the same licence. Verified by: review: The repository name is the tested part; the README lists the other family members and their status. Explained in: standards/driver.md KB-DOC-020: Every C++ block on the site compiles ¶ MUST · driver, library, hal, template · since 1.0 A C++ snippet longer than one line lives in tests/docs/*.cpp between --8<-- section markers, is built by the host build with warnings on, and is included in the page; it is never pasted inline. Why: An example that does not compile teaches the wrong API, and nobody notices until a user pastes it. Verified by: host-tests (implemented): the unit tests build and pass on the host with gcc and clang docs-inline-code (planned): no C++ fence longer than one line in docs/ or README.md is written inline; each comes from tests/docs via a --8<-- include or a generated region Explained in: standards/docs.md KB-DOC-021: Examples check every result ¶ MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 Every example on the site and in the README checks each Result and Status it gets and shows what to do with an error; no example ignores a return value or elides code with // ... . Verified by: compiler-warnings/-Wunused-result (implemented): the build is warning-free with the named flag and -Werror review: Each example handles every returned Result or Status. Explained in: standards/docs.md KB-DOC-022: Generated regions and figures match the code ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. ru-mkdocs-publish runs the drift check today; once its job is named in the registry the check is implemented and this rule can be active. MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 The README quickstart, examples lists and figures are generated regions ( kokeb-docs ), and CI fails when one no longer matches the code it is generated from. kokeb-docs check runs the same check locally. Verified by: docs-drift (planned): kokeb-docs check finds no generated region (README quickstart, examples list) or figure that differs from what the code generates Explained in: standards/docs.md KB-DOC-023: The Porting page shows a complete, compiled port for each bus ¶ MUST · driver, template · since 1.0 A driver's Porting page shows the full port for every bus it supports, compiled from tests/docs/ , and lists every extra protocol hook with the same contract as the core interface methods. Verified by: host-tests (implemented): the unit tests build and pass on the host with gcc and clang review: Each supported bus has a compiled port on the Porting page; every extra hook is listed. Explained in: standards/driver.md KB-DOC-024: The API guide lists the errors each call can return ¶ SHOULD · driver, template · since 1.0 A driver's API guide lists, for each call, the error values it can return and what each means, matching the @retval lines in the headers. Verified by: review: The API guide's error table matches the @return/@retval documentation in inc/. Explained in: standards/driver.md KB-DOC-025: Every image has alt text ¶ MUST · all · since 1.0 Every image and figure has alt text: one sentence saying what it shows, never just "diagram" or "image". Verified by: markdownlint/MD045 (implemented): markdownlint-cli2 with the org config; the parameter names the rule (markdownlint/MD040) review: Alt text says what the figure shows. Explained in: standards/docs.md KB-DOC-026: Figures are generated, themed, and drawn with the right tool ¶ SHOULD · all · since 1.0 Architecture and code-derived figures are figkit figures with light and dark variants; sequences and state machines are Mermaid. A vendor image is an SVG or compressed PNG on a .kb-plate , never a screenshot of a PDF. Verified by: review: New figures use figkit or Mermaid; vendor images are SVG/PNG with .kb-plate. Colour shows ownership in at most three tones, with about eight cards at most. KB-DOC-028: The site's changelog page includes CHANGELOG.md ¶ MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, tooling, template · since 1.0 docs/changelog.md has a title and purpose line and pulls in CHANGELOG.md with a snippet include; it never holds a copy. Verified by: review: docs/changelog.md uses --8<-- "CHANGELOG.md" and has no copied entries. Explained in: standards/docs.md KB-DOC-029: The changelog keeps [Unreleased] first and the standard subsections in order ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. The planned changelog check must cover the [Unreleased]-first and subsection-order rules (Breaking is not a Keep a Changelog heading). MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 ## [Unreleased] is always the first section. Within a section the subsections are Breaking, Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed and Security, in that order, each only when it has an entry. Verified by: changelog (planned): CHANGELOG.md follows Keep a Changelog; a new version section is the next SemVer step, dated, not empty Explained in: standards/release.md KB-DOC-030: A released changelog section is never edited ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A released section ## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD is not edited after its release, except for its link lines; a correction goes in the next release's entry. Verified by: changelog-frozen (planned): a pull request's diff of CHANGELOG.md changes only the [Unreleased] section, a new release section and link lines Explained in: standards/release.md KB-DOC-031: Changelog entries describe what a user sees ¶ GUIDE · all · since 1.0 A changelog entry says what changes for the user of the release (an API, a behaviour, a default, a fix to a symptom), not which commits went in. Explained in: standards/release.md KB-DOC-032: ADRs use the standard format and are numbered in acceptance order ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A decision record has a Status line and the sections Context, Decision and Consequences, and is numbered NNNN-<slug>.md in the order decisions are accepted. Verified by: heading-skeleton/adr (planned): a Markdown file's headings match a required skeleton in order (parameter: contract, readme, adr, hf-hal-readme, hf-board-spec, hf-protocol-spec) Explained in: standards/docs.md KB-DOC-033: An accepted decision is superseded, never rewritten ¶ MUST · all · since 1.0 Once an ADR is accepted its Decision is not edited to change it; a new ADR supersedes it, and the old one's Status links its successor. Why: The record is only useful if it shows what was decided at the time, and why. Verified by: review: A pull request that edits an accepted ADR changes only its Status, links or typos. Explained in: standards/docs.md KB-DOC-034: Cross-repository decisions are handbook ADRs; local ones stay in the repository ¶ SHOULD · all · since 1.0 A decision that affects more than one repository is an ADR in the handbook's docs/adr/ . A decision local to one repository, including a product's, is an ADR in its own docs/adr/ in the same format. Verified by: review: A new ADR is in the handbook when it binds other repositories. Explained in: standards/docs.md KB-DOC-035: Datasheets are referenced by exact revision, never committed ¶ MUST · driver, hal, template · since 1.0 No datasheet, reference manual or application note is committed. docs/datasheets.yml lists each document the code was written against: vendor, title, document number, revision, date, URL and the SHA-256 of the PDF that was used. Verified by: tracked-files/datasheets (implemented): git tracks no file of a banned kind; the parameter names it (tracked-files/symlinks, tracked-files/sdkconfig, tracked-files/idf-component) review: docs/datasheets.yml names the document number, revision and SHA-256 of every datasheet the code cites. See also: ADR-0019 KB-DOC-036: Markdown wraps at 120 columns ¶ MUST · all · since 1.0 Prose lines in Markdown are at most 120 characters; tables and code blocks are exempt. Verified by: markdownlint/MD013 (implemented): markdownlint-cli2 with the org config; the parameter names the rule (markdownlint/MD040) Explained in: standards/naming-and-style.md KB-DOC-037: Every page has one title, a purpose line and sections in reading order ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. config/.markdownlint.json must enable MD025 and MD041 (MD041 with front matter allowed, for hide: ). SHOULD · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A page starts with exactly one # title matching its navigation entry, then a one-sentence purpose line, then ## sections in the order a reader needs them, ending with a next step when there is an obvious one. Verified by: markdownlint/MD025 (implemented): markdownlint-cli2 with the org config; the parameter names the rule (markdownlint/MD040) markdownlint/MD041 (implemented): markdownlint-cli2 with the org config; the parameter names the rule (markdownlint/MD040) review: The page has a purpose line under its title. KB-DOC-038: Headings step one level at a time and code fences name their language ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. config/.markdownlint.json must enable MD040. MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Heading levels go down one at a time and use # style throughout. Every fenced code block names its language ( cpp , yaml , mermaid , text ). Verified by: markdownlint/MD001 (implemented): markdownlint-cli2 with the org config; the parameter names the rule (markdownlint/MD040) markdownlint/MD003 (implemented): markdownlint-cli2 with the org config; the parameter names the rule (markdownlint/MD040) markdownlint/MD040 (implemented): markdownlint-cli2 with the org config; the parameter names the rule (markdownlint/MD040) KB-DOC-039: Links are relative, by file, with descriptive text ¶ SHOULD · all · since 1.0 Pages link other pages by file ( porting.md#threads ), repository files relatively, and the API reference by api/...html ; no page links its own site or repository by absolute URL. Link text says where it goes, and external links go to the primary source. Verified by: markdownlint/MD059 (implemented): markdownlint-cli2 with the org config; the parameter names the rule (markdownlint/MD040) forbidden-patterns/absolute-self-links (planned): a source scan for a construct the handbook bans; the parameter names the pattern set review: External links point at the primary source (vendor, datasheet, specification). Explained in: standards/docs.md KB-DOC-040: Documentation is Markdown ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. SHOULD · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Documentation is written in Markdown in the repository; no Word, PDF or slide files stand in for pages. Vendor datasheets (KB-DOC-035) are the only exception. Verified by: forbidden-patterns/office-docs (planned): a source scan for a construct the handbook bans; the parameter names the pattern set KB-DOC-041: No Jekyll front matter or Liquid; front matter only for hide ¶ MUST · all · since 1.0 Pages have no Jekyll front matter and no Liquid tags. Material front matter is used only for hide: , for example on the home page. Verified by: mkdocs-strict (implemented): the documentation site builds with mkdocs --strict (no broken internal link, every page in the nav) Explained in: standards/docs.md KB-DOC-042: Page file names are lower-case kebab-case ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. SHOULD · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Files under docs/ are named in lower-case kebab-case ( api-guide.md , contract.md ). The conventional root files (README.md, CHANGELOG.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, LICENSE) keep their upper-case names. Verified by: doc-file-names (planned): every file under docs/ is lower-case kebab-case; root README, CHANGELOG, CONTRIBUTING, AGENTS, CLAUDE and LICENSE are exempt KB-DOC-043: Write in the second person, present tense and active voice ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. The Vale rules report at warning level for passive voice. SHOULD · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Pages address the reader as "you", in the present tense and active voice, in short sentences of one idea each. A page does not describe itself ("this document describes"). Verified by: prose-style/passive-voice (planned): Vale with the Kokeb style; the parameter names the style rule prose-style/future-tense (planned): Vale with the Kokeb style; the parameter names the style rule prose-style/self-reference (planned): Vale with the Kokeb style; the parameter names the style rule Explained in: standards/docs.md KB-DOC-044: No hype or filler words ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. SHOULD · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Pages are plain and specific: numbers, names and units instead of "simply", "just", "easily", "powerful", "comprehensive", "seamless" or "robust". Verified by: prose-style/hype-words (planned): Vale with the Kokeb style; the parameter names the style rule KB-DOC-045: No emoji, exclamation marks or walls of bold ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. SHOULD · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Headings, lists and tables carry no emoji; prose has no exclamation marks and no runs of bold text. Verified by: prose-style/emoji (planned): Vale with the Kokeb style; the parameter names the style rule prose-style/exclamation (planned): Vale with the Kokeb style; the parameter names the style rule KB-DOC-046: Titles and headings are in sentence case ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. SHOULD · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Every title and heading, the page title included, is in sentence case ("Bus settings"). Verified by: prose-style/sentence-case (planned): Vale with the Kokeb style; the parameter names the style rule KB-DOC-047: Pages never mention how they were produced ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 No page says it was generated or written by a tool or an assistant, and no page names one as its author. Generated-region markers are comments, not prose. Verified by: prose-style/provenance (planned): Vale with the Kokeb style; the parameter names the style rule KB-DOC-048: Spelling is correct and one variant is used per repository ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. SHOULD · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Pages have no misspellings, and a repository uses British or American spelling consistently; project words are listed in config/typos.toml . Verified by: spelling (planned): typos finds no misspelling (project words in config/typos.toml) prose-style/spelling-variant (planned): Vale with the Kokeb style; the parameter names the style rule KB-DOC-049: Every name and number on a page is checked against its source ¶ MUST · all · since 1.0 Every API name, signature, pin, register and number is checked against the headers or the datasheet. A timing or performance figure is measured, with its conditions, or says that it is derived. Why: A plausible wrong number costs a user more than a missing one. Verified by: review: Numbers and names on changed pages match the headers or datasheet; derived figures say so. KB-DOC-050: Use a table for three or more like items, with units in the header ¶ GUIDE · all · since 1.0 Pins, registers, parameters, options, commands and error codes go in a table once there are three or more, with units in the header ( Range (V) ), names in code font and long prose below the table. KB-DOC-051: Use the theme's components instead of inventing markup ¶ GUIDE · all · since 1.0 Admonitions, tabs, chip cards, steps and API links use the theme's components. A page has at most two warning or danger admonitions, kept for damage or lost hours. KB-DOC-052: Guides teach a task with complete examples and say why ¶ GUIDE · all · since 1.0 A guide page is organised by task, gives the smallest complete example for each step, and says why a step is needed as well as how. KB-DOC-053: No undated future-plans sections ¶ GUIDE · all · since 1.0 Pages describe what exists. Plans go in issues or discussions, not in "future work" or "roadmap" sections of the docs. KB-DOC-054: The site meets the Lighthouse accessibility budget ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. SHOULD · driver, library, hal, firmware, tooling, docs, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 The built site scores at or above the org Lighthouse budget for accessibility, performance, best practices and SEO. Verified by: lighthouse (planned): Lighthouse scores of the built site meet the org budget for accessibility, performance, best practices and SEO (ru-mkdocs-publish runs Lighthouse; register it as implemented once its failing job is confirmed) KB-DOC-055: Interrupt wiring is documented ¶ SHOULD · driver, hal, template · since 1.0 When a driver or HAL needs an interrupt, its docs say which callback or vector handler the user wires, which context it runs in, and what it may call. Verified by: review: The Porting or Contract page names the ISR hook, its context and what it may call. KB-DOC-056: kb-core has one page per handler ¶ MUST · library · since 1.0 kb-core documents each handler on its own page under docs/handlers/ , with its API, error mapping, locking and diagnostics. Verified by: review: Every handlers/<chip> folder has a docs/handlers/ page with the four sections. Explained in: standards/handler.md KB-DOC-057: A utility collection has one guide page per utility ¶ SHOULD · library · since 1.0 A library that is a collection of utilities has one guide page per utility, with its purpose, a compiled example and its complexity and memory use. Verified by: review: Each public utility header has a guide page with purpose, example, complexity and memory. Explained in: standards/library.md KB-DOC-058: A product documents its fault catalogue on the Operation page ¶ MUST · firmware · since 1.0 A product keeps one fault catalogue (ID, protocol code, severity, reaction) and documents it on its Operation page. Verified by: review: The Operation page lists every fault in the catalogue with its code, severity and reaction. Explained in: standards/product.md KB-DOC-059: Release trains are announced with their bench status ¶ SHOULD · library · since 1.0 A kb-core release train is announced in its release notes and on the Release trains page, with the bench status of each member. Verified by: review: The release notes and Release trains page list the train's members and bench status. Explained in: standards/release.md KB-DOC-060: Patches to vendor-generated code are listed in PATCHES.md ¶ SHOULD · hal · since 1.0 Any edit to vendor-generated code (STM32Cube and the like) after generation is listed in PATCHES.md beside it, with why; the aim is none. Verified by: review: A diff against the regenerated output matches what PATCHES.md lists. KB-DOC-061: The Doxyfile lives in _config/ and Doxygen runs from the root ¶ MUST · driver, library, hal, template · since 1.0 Each code repository keeps its Doxyfile at _config/Doxyfile , derived from the shared settings in ci-tools, and runs doxygen _config/Doxyfile from the repository root so its paths are root-relative. Verified by: doxyfile-baseline (planned): _config/Doxyfile exists and sets INPUT to the public headers, EXTRACT_ALL and EXTRACT_PRIVATE to NO, WARN_NO_PARAMDOC to YES and the org mainpage, compared with the ci-tools baseline review: _config/Doxyfile exists and its paths are relative to the root. See also: ADR-0011 Explained in: standards/docs.md KB-DOC-062: Doxygen reads only the public headers and keeps private members out ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. driver-template matches; ci-tools' shared Doxyfile uses INPUT = README.md ... with RECURSIVE = YES and must be brought in line. MUST · driver, library, hal, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 The Doxyfile sets INPUT to the public headers only ( inc/ for a driver), EXTRACT_ALL = NO , EXTRACT_PRIVATE = NO , WARN_NO_PARAMDOC = YES , USE_MDFILE_AS_MAINPAGE = docs/_doxygen/mainpage.md , and generates HTML that is merged into the site under api/ . Why: With EXTRACT_ALL off, an undocumented symbol is a warning instead of an empty entry, so KB-DOC-004 can fail on it. Verified by: doxyfile-baseline (planned): _config/Doxyfile exists and sets INPUT to the public headers, EXTRACT_ALL and EXTRACT_PRIVATE to NO, WARN_NO_PARAMDOC to YES and the org mainpage, compared with the ci-tools baseline Explained in: standards/docs.md KB-DOC-063: A public function's comment gives units, errors and whether it blocks ¶ MUST · driver, library, hal, template · since 1.0 Each public symbol has a brief description. Each public function documents every parameter with its unit, its return value and the error values it can return, and whether it does I/O or blocks. Verified by: doxygen-warnings (implemented): Doxygen with WARN_AS_ERROR = FAIL_ON_WARNINGS and WARN_IF_UNDOCUMENTED reports nothing review: Changed public functions document units, error values and whether they do I/O or block. See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 5.4.2 (detailed design of each software unit) Explained in: standards/docs.md KB-DOC-064: Each test says what it verifies, with its data and expected result ¶ SHOULD · driver, library, hal, firmware, template (safety level and above) · since 1.0 At safety level each test case has a Doxygen comment naming the requirement or behaviour it verifies, the input data and the expected result. Why: The comment is the trace from a requirement to its test that an assessor reads. Verified by: review: Each new or changed test has a comment naming what it verifies, its data and expected result. KB-DOC-065: A driver's docs trace each part of the driver to its datasheet section ¶ MUST · driver, template · since 1.0 docs/datasheets.yml lists, besides the documents, one topic per thing the driver takes from them: the datasheet's section and printed page, the driver API and the docs pages that explain it. The README and home page carry the generated datasheet card, docs/datasheet.md the generated map, and each page a topic names the generated box of the sections it relies on. Why: A reader, a reviewer or an assessor can check any behaviour against the source document in one step, and a new datasheet revision shows exactly which parts of the driver to re-check. Verified by: docs-drift (planned): kokeb-docs check finds no generated region (README quickstart, examples list) or figure that differs from what the code generates review: Each topic names the right section and page; every docs page that rests on the datasheet has its box. See also: ADR-0019 Explained in: standards/docs.md

Verified by: mkdocs-strict (implemented): the documentation site builds with mkdocs --strict (no broken internal link, every page in the nav) Explained in: standards/docs.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-002: The documentation site builds strictly
