docs.text: MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, tooling, docs, template · since 1.0 Every public repository publishes its documentation at https://kokeb-labs.github.io/<repo>/ through ru-mkdocs-publish , built with kokeb-mkdocs-theme and versioned per v* tag; a code repository merges its Doxygen reference under api/ . A -rc tag publishes its version without moving the latest alias. Why: One platform and one theme mean a reader finds the same layout on every site, and a pinned version per tag means the page a user reads matches the code they built. Verified by: mkdocs-strict (implemented): the documentation site builds with mkdocs --strict (no broken internal link, every page in the nav) review: The docs workflow calls ru-mkdocs-publish and the site is live at kokeb-labs.github.io/<repo>/. Explained in: standards/docs.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-005: Every public repository publishes a versioned MkDocs site

docs.text: MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, tooling, docs, template · since 1.0 Pages live in docs/ . The site configuration is _config/mkdocs.yml with docs_dir: ../docs , and the docs workflow is passed mkdocs_config: _config/mkdocs.yml and, in a code repository, doxygen_config: _config/Doxyfile . Verified by: mkdocs-strict (implemented): the documentation site builds with mkdocs --strict (no broken internal link, every page in the nav) review: The docs workflow passes mkdocs_config and doxygen_config with the _config/ paths. See also: ADR-0011 Explained in: standards/docs.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-006: Pages live in docs/ and the site config in _config/mkdocs.yml

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, tooling, docs, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 docs/.nav.yml has exactly five top-level tabs, in this order: Home, Get started, Concepts, Guides, Reference. Deep dives go under Concepts and configuration references under Guides. Verified by: docs-nav (planned): docs/.nav.yml has exactly the five tabs Home, Get started, Concepts, Guides, Reference in order, and contract.md sits under Concepts right after Architecture Explained in: standards/docs.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-007: The navigation has the five standard tabs

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, tooling, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 docs/ holds every page the documentation standard lists for the repository's kind (driver, standalone library, kb-core, HAL, product, CI and tools). A page that cannot apply, such as Configuration for a driver with no Config , is left out rather than kept empty. Why: A fixed page set lets a reader move between repositories without relearning where things are, and lets a check say what is missing. Verified by: docs-page-set (planned): docs/ has every page the documentation standard requires for the repository's declared kind, and each is in the navigation Explained in: standards/docs.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-008: The site has the page set for its kind

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Every driver, library, kb-core, HAL and product has docs/contract.md , listed under Concepts right after Architecture. Verified by: docs-page-set (planned): docs/ has every page the documentation standard requires for the repository's declared kind, and each is in the navigation docs-nav (planned): docs/.nav.yml has exactly the five tabs Home, Get started, Concepts, Guides, Reference in order, and contract.md sits under Concepts right after Architecture Explained in: standards/docs.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-009: Every code repository has a Contract page under Concepts

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 docs/contract.md has the sections Promises, Depends on, Threading, Errors, Memory, Platform and Deviations from the standard, in that order, after a one-line purpose. Why: The Contract is the short normative summary a caller or an auditor reads first; fixed sections make a missing promise visible. Verified by: heading-skeleton/contract (planned): a Markdown file's headings match a required skeleton in order (parameter: contract, readme, adr, hf-hal-readme, hf-board-spec, hf-protocol-spec) See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 5.4.3 (detailed design of software unit interfaces) Explained in: standards/docs.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-010: The Contract page has the standard sections in order

docs.text: MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 The Deviations section names, by rule ID, each handbook rule the repository does not meet yet, with its issue or waiver. An empty section says "None". Verified by: review: Every waiver in .kokeb/handbook.yml and every known unmet rule appears in the Deviations section with its issue. Explained in: deviations.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-011: The Contract page lists every handbook rule the repository does not meet

docs.text: SHOULD · all · since 1.0 The handbook is the single source of the rules. A repository's docs, Contract page, templates and CI link the rule they follow and state only what is specific to the repository; no repository keeps a copy of the handbook or of its pages. Why: A copied rule drifts from the original the first time either is edited. Verified by: review: No page restates a handbook rule that it could link; no vendored copy of handbook pages. Explained in: standards/docs.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-012: Repository docs link the handbook instead of restating it

docs.text: SHOULD · all · since 1.0 A repository's CONTRIBUTING.md, or the organisation default it inherits, links the handbook. AGENTS.md links it as KB-AGT-005 requires. Verified by: review: CONTRIBUTING.md (own or the org default) links kokeb-labs.github.io/handbook.
docs.title: KB-DOC-013: CONTRIBUTING.md links the handbook

docs.text: SHOULD · all · since 1.0 A pull request that changes behaviour, the public API, a pin, a default or a build option updates the README, the pages under docs/ and the CHANGELOG entry that describe it, in the same pull request. Why: Docs updated later are docs that are wrong in between, and usually stay wrong. Verified by: docs-touched (planned): warns when a pull request changes inc/, a Kconfig or a CMake option without touching README.md, docs/ or CHANGELOG.md review: Every page that describes the changed behaviour is updated in this pull request.
docs.title: KB-DOC-014: A change to behaviour or API updates its docs in the same pull request

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. SHOULD · driver, library, hal, firmware, tooling, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 The README has, in order and only where they apply: title and hero line, true badges, the bold docs link, a plain-language paragraph, one figure, At a glance (with the status), Datasheet, Try it on your PC, Use it on your MCU, What it does, Install, Documentation (with "Read it when you want to"), Tests and quality, License. Verified by: heading-skeleton/readme (planned): a Markdown file's headings match a required skeleton in order (parameter: contract, readme, adr, hf-hal-readme, hf-board-spec, hf-protocol-spec) Explained in: standards/docs.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-015: The README has the standard sections in order

docs.text: SHOULD · all · since 1.0 A README has no table of contents, no emoji walls, no check-mark feature lists, no badge that links nowhere or states something untrue, and no API tables that duplicate the site. Verified by: prose-style/emoji (planned): Vale with the Kokeb style; the parameter names the style rule review: The README has none of the banned elements and every badge is live and true. Explained in: standards/docs.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-016: The README is short and leaves the reference to the site

docs.text: MUST · driver, template · since 1.0 A driver's README and site name the chip and part it drives; the organisation appears only in links and the licence line, so the driver reads as usable on its own. Verified by: forbidden-patterns/readme-org-name (planned): a source scan for a construct the handbook bans; the parameter names the pattern set review: The README names the chip and part; no Kokeb Labs or HardFOC branding outside links. See also: ADR-0012 Explained in: standards/docs.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-017: A driver's README names the chip and the part, not the organisation

docs.text: MUST · all · since 1.0 The README's License line, LICENSE and every package manifest ( idf_component.yml , library.json and the like) name the same licence: MIT for code, CERN-OHL-P-2.0 for a hardware design. Verified by: review: README License line, LICENSE and package manifests name the same licence. See also: ADR-0009
docs.title: KB-DOC-018: The README licence line matches LICENSE and the package metadata

docs.text: SHOULD · driver · since 1.0 A driver that covers a chip family is named after the part it was written and tested for; the README lists the other members it supports and how far each is tested. Verified by: review: The repository name is the tested part; the README lists the other family members and their status. Explained in: standards/driver.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-019: A family driver is named after the member it was written for

docs.text: MUST · driver, library, hal, template · since 1.0 A C++ snippet longer than one line lives in tests/docs/*.cpp between --8<-- section markers, is built by the host build with warnings on, and is included in the page; it is never pasted inline. Why: An example that does not compile teaches the wrong API, and nobody notices until a user pastes it. Verified by: host-tests (implemented): the unit tests build and pass on the host with gcc and clang docs-inline-code (planned): no C++ fence longer than one line in docs/ or README.md is written inline; each comes from tests/docs via a --8<-- include or a generated region Explained in: standards/docs.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-020: Every C++ block on the site compiles

docs.text: MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 Every example on the site and in the README checks each Result and Status it gets and shows what to do with an error; no example ignores a return value or elides code with // ... . Verified by: compiler-warnings/-Wunused-result (implemented): the build is warning-free with the named flag and -Werror review: Each example handles every returned Result or Status. Explained in: standards/docs.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-021: Examples check every result

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. ru-mkdocs-publish runs the drift check today; once its job is named in the registry the check is implemented and this rule can be active. MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 The README quickstart, examples lists and figures are generated regions ( kokeb-docs ), and CI fails when one no longer matches the code it is generated from. kokeb-docs check runs the same check locally. Verified by: docs-drift (planned): kokeb-docs check finds no generated region (README quickstart, examples list) or figure that differs from what the code generates Explained in: standards/docs.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-022: Generated regions and figures match the code

docs.text: MUST · driver, template · since 1.0 A driver's Porting page shows the full port for every bus it supports, compiled from tests/docs/ , and lists every extra protocol hook with the same contract as the core interface methods. Verified by: host-tests (implemented): the unit tests build and pass on the host with gcc and clang review: Each supported bus has a compiled port on the Porting page; every extra hook is listed. Explained in: standards/driver.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-023: The Porting page shows a complete, compiled port for each bus

docs.text: SHOULD · driver, template · since 1.0 A driver's API guide lists, for each call, the error values it can return and what each means, matching the @retval lines in the headers. Verified by: review: The API guide's error table matches the @return/@retval documentation in inc/. Explained in: standards/driver.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-024: The API guide lists the errors each call can return

docs.text: MUST · all · since 1.0 Every image and figure has alt text: one sentence saying what it shows, never just "diagram" or "image". Verified by: markdownlint/MD045 (implemented): markdownlint-cli2 with the org config; the parameter names the rule (markdownlint/MD040) review: Alt text says what the figure shows. Explained in: standards/docs.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-025: Every image has alt text

docs.text: SHOULD · all · since 1.0 Architecture and code-derived figures are figkit figures with light and dark variants; sequences and state machines are Mermaid. A vendor image is an SVG or compressed PNG on a .kb-plate , never a screenshot of a PDF. Verified by: review: New figures use figkit or Mermaid; vendor images are SVG/PNG with .kb-plate. Explained in: standards/docs.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-026: Figures are generated, themed, and drawn with the right tool

docs.text: GUIDE · all · since 1.0 A figure reads in one direction, stated in its subtitle; solid arrows call, dashed arrows carry data, and an arrow is labelled when its verb is not obvious. Colour shows ownership in at most three tones, with about eight cards at most.
docs.title: KB-DOC-027: A figure has one reading direction, verbs on its arrows and three tones at most

docs.text: MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, tooling, template · since 1.0 docs/changelog.md has a title and purpose line and pulls in CHANGELOG.md with a snippet include; it never holds a copy. Verified by: review: docs/changelog.md uses --8<-- "CHANGELOG.md" and has no copied entries. Explained in: standards/docs.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-028: The site's changelog page includes CHANGELOG.md

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. The planned changelog check must cover the [Unreleased]-first and subsection-order rules (Breaking is not a Keep a Changelog heading). MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 ## [Unreleased] is always the first section. Within a section the subsections are Breaking, Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed and Security, in that order, each only when it has an entry. Verified by: changelog (planned): CHANGELOG.md follows Keep a Changelog; a new version section is the next SemVer step, dated, not empty Explained in: standards/release.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-029: The changelog keeps [Unreleased] first and the standard subsections in order

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A released section ## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD is not edited after its release, except for its link lines; a correction goes in the next release's entry. Verified by: changelog-frozen (planned): a pull request's diff of CHANGELOG.md changes only the [Unreleased] section, a new release section and link lines Explained in: standards/release.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-030: A released changelog section is never edited

docs.text: GUIDE · all · since 1.0 A changelog entry says what changes for the user of the release (an API, a behaviour, a default, a fix to a symptom), not which commits went in. Explained in: standards/release.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-031: Changelog entries describe what a user sees

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A decision record has a Status line and the sections Context, Decision and Consequences, and is numbered NNNN-<slug>.md in the order decisions are accepted. Verified by: heading-skeleton/adr (planned): a Markdown file's headings match a required skeleton in order (parameter: contract, readme, adr, hf-hal-readme, hf-board-spec, hf-protocol-spec) Explained in: standards/docs.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-032: ADRs use the standard format and are numbered in acceptance order

docs.text: MUST · all · since 1.0 Once an ADR is accepted its Decision is not edited to change it; a new ADR supersedes it, and the old one's Status links its successor. Why: The record is only useful if it shows what was decided at the time, and why. Verified by: review: A pull request that edits an accepted ADR changes only its Status, links or typos. Explained in: standards/docs.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-033: An accepted decision is superseded, never rewritten

docs.text: SHOULD · all · since 1.0 A decision that affects more than one repository is an ADR in the handbook's docs/adr/ . A decision local to one repository, including a product's, is an ADR in its own docs/adr/ in the same format. Verified by: review: A new ADR is in the handbook when it binds other repositories. Explained in: standards/docs.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-034: Cross-repository decisions are handbook ADRs; local ones stay in the repository

docs.text: MUST · driver, hal, template · since 1.0 No datasheet, reference manual or application note is committed. docs/datasheets.yml lists each document the code was written against: vendor, title, document number, revision, date, URL and the SHA-256 of the PDF that was used. Verified by: tracked-files/datasheets (implemented): git tracks no file of a banned kind; the parameter names it (tracked-files/symlinks, tracked-files/sdkconfig, tracked-files/idf-component) review: docs/datasheets.yml names the document number, revision and SHA-256 of every datasheet the code cites. See also: ADR-0019
docs.title: KB-DOC-035: Datasheets are referenced by exact revision, never committed

docs.text: MUST · all · since 1.0 Prose lines in Markdown are at most 120 characters; tables and code blocks are exempt. Verified by: markdownlint/MD013 (implemented): markdownlint-cli2 with the org config; the parameter names the rule (markdownlint/MD040) Explained in: standards/naming-and-style.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-036: Markdown wraps at 120 columns

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. config/.markdownlint.json must enable MD025 and MD041 (MD041 with front matter allowed, for hide: ). SHOULD · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A page starts with exactly one # title matching its navigation entry, then a one-sentence purpose line, then ## sections in the order a reader needs them, ending with a next step when there is an obvious one. Verified by: markdownlint/MD025 (implemented): markdownlint-cli2 with the org config; the parameter names the rule (markdownlint/MD040) markdownlint/MD041 (implemented): markdownlint-cli2 with the org config; the parameter names the rule (markdownlint/MD040) review: The page has a purpose line under its title.
docs.title: KB-DOC-037: Every page has one title, a purpose line and sections in reading order

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. config/.markdownlint.json must enable MD040. MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Heading levels go down one at a time and use # style throughout. Every fenced code block names its language ( cpp , yaml , mermaid , text ). Verified by: markdownlint/MD001 (implemented): markdownlint-cli2 with the org config; the parameter names the rule (markdownlint/MD040) markdownlint/MD003 (implemented): markdownlint-cli2 with the org config; the parameter names the rule (markdownlint/MD040) markdownlint/MD040 (implemented): markdownlint-cli2 with the org config; the parameter names the rule (markdownlint/MD040)
docs.title: KB-DOC-038: Headings step one level at a time and code fences name their language

docs.text: SHOULD · all · since 1.0 Pages link other pages by file ( porting.md#threads ), repository files relatively, and the API reference by api/...html ; no page links its own site or repository by absolute URL. Link text says where it goes, and external links go to the primary source. Verified by: markdownlint/MD059 (implemented): markdownlint-cli2 with the org config; the parameter names the rule (markdownlint/MD040) forbidden-patterns/absolute-self-links (planned): a source scan for a construct the handbook bans; the parameter names the pattern set review: External links point at the primary source (vendor, datasheet, specification). Explained in: standards/docs.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-039: Links are relative, by file, with descriptive text

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. SHOULD · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Documentation is written in Markdown in the repository; no Word, PDF or slide files stand in for pages. Vendor datasheets (KB-DOC-035) are the only exception. Verified by: forbidden-patterns/office-docs (planned): a source scan for a construct the handbook bans; the parameter names the pattern set
docs.title: KB-DOC-040: Documentation is Markdown

docs.text: MUST · all · since 1.0 Pages have no Jekyll front matter and no Liquid tags. Material front matter is used only for hide: , for example on the home page. Verified by: mkdocs-strict (implemented): the documentation site builds with mkdocs --strict (no broken internal link, every page in the nav) Explained in: standards/docs.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-041: No Jekyll front matter or Liquid; front matter only for hide

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. SHOULD · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Files under docs/ are named in lower-case kebab-case ( api-guide.md , contract.md ). The conventional root files (README.md, CHANGELOG.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, LICENSE) keep their upper-case names. Verified by: doc-file-names (planned): every file under docs/ is lower-case kebab-case; root README, CHANGELOG, CONTRIBUTING, AGENTS, CLAUDE and LICENSE are exempt
docs.title: KB-DOC-042: Page file names are lower-case kebab-case

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. The Vale rules report at warning level for passive voice. SHOULD · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Pages address the reader as "you", in the present tense and active voice, in short sentences of one idea each. A page does not describe itself ("this document describes"). Verified by: prose-style/passive-voice (planned): Vale with the Kokeb style; the parameter names the style rule prose-style/future-tense (planned): Vale with the Kokeb style; the parameter names the style rule prose-style/self-reference (planned): Vale with the Kokeb style; the parameter names the style rule Explained in: standards/docs.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-043: Write in the second person, present tense and active voice

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. SHOULD · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Pages are plain and specific: numbers, names and units instead of "simply", "just", "easily", "powerful", "comprehensive", "seamless" or "robust". Verified by: prose-style/hype-words (planned): Vale with the Kokeb style; the parameter names the style rule
docs.title: KB-DOC-044: No hype or filler words

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. SHOULD · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Headings, lists and tables carry no emoji; prose has no exclamation marks and no runs of bold text. Verified by: prose-style/emoji (planned): Vale with the Kokeb style; the parameter names the style rule prose-style/exclamation (planned): Vale with the Kokeb style; the parameter names the style rule
docs.title: KB-DOC-045: No emoji, exclamation marks or walls of bold

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. SHOULD · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Every title and heading, the page title included, is in sentence case ("Bus settings"). Verified by: prose-style/sentence-case (planned): Vale with the Kokeb style; the parameter names the style rule
docs.title: KB-DOC-046: Titles and headings are in sentence case

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 No page says it was generated or written by a tool or an assistant, and no page names one as its author. Generated-region markers are comments, not prose. Verified by: prose-style/provenance (planned): Vale with the Kokeb style; the parameter names the style rule
docs.title: KB-DOC-047: Pages never mention how they were produced

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. SHOULD · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Pages have no misspellings, and a repository uses British or American spelling consistently; project words are listed in config/typos.toml . Verified by: spelling (planned): typos finds no misspelling (project words in config/typos.toml) prose-style/spelling-variant (planned): Vale with the Kokeb style; the parameter names the style rule
docs.title: KB-DOC-048: Spelling is correct and one variant is used per repository

docs.text: MUST · all · since 1.0 Every API name, signature, pin, register and number is checked against the headers or the datasheet. A timing or performance figure is measured, with its conditions, or says that it is derived. Why: A plausible wrong number costs a user more than a missing one. Verified by: review: Numbers and names on changed pages match the headers or datasheet; derived figures say so.
docs.title: KB-DOC-049: Every name and number on a page is checked against its source

docs.text: GUIDE · all · since 1.0 Pins, registers, parameters, options, commands and error codes go in a table once there are three or more, with units in the header ( Range (V) ), names in code font and long prose below the table.
docs.title: KB-DOC-050: Use a table for three or more like items, with units in the header

docs.text: GUIDE · all · since 1.0 Admonitions, tabs, chip cards, steps and API links use the theme's components. A page has at most two warning or danger admonitions, kept for damage or lost hours.
docs.title: KB-DOC-051: Use the theme's components instead of inventing markup

docs.text: GUIDE · all · since 1.0 A guide page is organised by task, gives the smallest complete example for each step, and says why a step is needed as well as how.
docs.title: KB-DOC-052: Guides teach a task with complete examples and say why

docs.text: GUIDE · all · since 1.0 Pages describe what exists. Plans go in issues or discussions, not in "future work" or "roadmap" sections of the docs.
docs.title: KB-DOC-053: No undated future-plans sections

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. SHOULD · driver, library, hal, firmware, tooling, docs, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 The built site scores at or above the org Lighthouse budget for accessibility, performance, best practices and SEO. Verified by: lighthouse (planned): Lighthouse scores of the built site meet the org budget for accessibility, performance, best practices and SEO (ru-mkdocs-publish runs Lighthouse; register it as implemented once its failing job is confirmed)
docs.title: KB-DOC-054: The site meets the Lighthouse accessibility budget

docs.text: SHOULD · driver, hal, template · since 1.0 When a driver or HAL needs an interrupt, its docs say which callback or vector handler the user wires, which context it runs in, and what it may call. Verified by: review: The Porting or Contract page names the ISR hook, its context and what it may call.
docs.title: KB-DOC-055: Interrupt wiring is documented

docs.text: MUST · library · since 1.0 kb-core documents each handler on its own page under docs/handlers/ , with its API, error mapping, locking and diagnostics. Verified by: review: Every handlers/<chip> folder has a docs/handlers/ page with the four sections. Explained in: standards/handler.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-056: kb-core has one page per handler

docs.text: SHOULD · library · since 1.0 A library that is a collection of utilities has one guide page per utility, with its purpose, a compiled example and its complexity and memory use. Verified by: review: Each public utility header has a guide page with purpose, example, complexity and memory. Explained in: standards/library.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-057: A utility collection has one guide page per utility

docs.text: MUST · firmware · since 1.0 A product keeps one fault catalogue (ID, protocol code, severity, reaction) and documents it on its Operation page. Verified by: review: The Operation page lists every fault in the catalogue with its code, severity and reaction. Explained in: standards/product.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-058: A product documents its fault catalogue on the Operation page

docs.text: SHOULD · library · since 1.0 A kb-core release train is announced in its release notes and on the Release trains page, with the bench status of each member. Verified by: review: The release notes and Release trains page list the train's members and bench status. Explained in: standards/release.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-059: Release trains are announced with their bench status

docs.text: SHOULD · hal · since 1.0 Any edit to vendor-generated code (STM32Cube and the like) after generation is listed in PATCHES.md beside it, with why; the aim is none. Verified by: review: A diff against the regenerated output matches what PATCHES.md lists.
docs.title: KB-DOC-060: Patches to vendor-generated code are listed in PATCHES.md

docs.text: MUST · driver, library, hal, template · since 1.0 Each code repository keeps its Doxyfile at _config/Doxyfile , derived from the shared settings in ci-tools, and runs doxygen _config/Doxyfile from the repository root so its paths are root-relative. Verified by: doxyfile-baseline (planned): _config/Doxyfile exists and sets INPUT to the public headers, EXTRACT_ALL and EXTRACT_PRIVATE to NO, WARN_NO_PARAMDOC to YES and the org mainpage, compared with the ci-tools baseline review: _config/Doxyfile exists and its paths are relative to the root. See also: ADR-0011 Explained in: standards/docs.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-061: The Doxyfile lives in _config/ and Doxygen runs from the root

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. driver-template matches; ci-tools' shared Doxyfile uses INPUT = README.md ... with RECURSIVE = YES and must be brought in line. MUST · driver, library, hal, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 The Doxyfile sets INPUT to the public headers only ( inc/ for a driver), EXTRACT_ALL = NO , EXTRACT_PRIVATE = NO , WARN_NO_PARAMDOC = YES , USE_MDFILE_AS_MAINPAGE = docs/_doxygen/mainpage.md , and generates HTML that is merged into the site under api/ . Why: With EXTRACT_ALL off, an undocumented symbol is a warning instead of an empty entry, so KB-DOC-004 can fail on it. Verified by: doxyfile-baseline (planned): _config/Doxyfile exists and sets INPUT to the public headers, EXTRACT_ALL and EXTRACT_PRIVATE to NO, WARN_NO_PARAMDOC to YES and the org mainpage, compared with the ci-tools baseline Explained in: standards/docs.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-062: Doxygen reads only the public headers and keeps private members out

docs.text: MUST · driver, library, hal, template · since 1.0 Each public symbol has a brief description. Each public function documents every parameter with its unit, its return value and the error values it can return, and whether it does I/O or blocks. Verified by: doxygen-warnings (implemented): Doxygen with WARN_AS_ERROR = FAIL_ON_WARNINGS and WARN_IF_UNDOCUMENTED reports nothing review: Changed public functions document units, error values and whether they do I/O or block. See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 5.4.2 (detailed design of each software unit) Explained in: standards/docs.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-063: A public function's comment gives units, errors and whether it blocks

docs.text: SHOULD · driver, library, hal, firmware, template (safety level and above) · since 1.0 At safety level each test case has a Doxygen comment naming the requirement or behaviour it verifies, the input data and the expected result. Why: The comment is the trace from a requirement to its test that an assessor reads. Verified by: review: Each new or changed test has a comment naming what it verifies, its data and expected result.
docs.title: KB-DOC-064: Each test says what it verifies, with its data and expected result

docs.text: MUST · driver, template · since 1.0 docs/datasheets.yml lists, besides the documents, one topic per thing the driver takes from them: the datasheet's section and printed page, the driver API and the docs pages that explain it. The README and home page carry the generated datasheet card, docs/datasheet.md the generated map, and each page a topic names the generated box of the sections it relies on. Why: A reader, a reviewer or an assessor can check any behaviour against the source document in one step, and a new datasheet revision shows exactly which parts of the driver to re-check. Verified by: docs-drift (planned): kokeb-docs check finds no generated region (README quickstart, examples list) or figure that differs from what the code generates review: Each topic names the right section and page; every docs page that rests on the datasheet has its box. See also: ADR-0019 Explained in: standards/docs.md
docs.title: KB-DOC-065: A driver's docs trace each part of the driver to its datasheet section

Otherwise, during review, push new commits so reviewers see what changed; the squash merge tidies them. Verified by: review: The branch history was rewritten only to repair sign-off or to rebase, not to hide review changes. Explained in: standards/repo-governance.md KB-GIT-010: One logical change per pull request ¶ GUIDE · all · since 1.0 A pull request does one thing, ideally in under about 400 changed lines; larger work is split into a series of green pull requests. Verified by: review: The pull request has one purpose, and mechanical clean-ups are not mixed into it. Explained in: standards/repo-governance.md KB-GIT-011: The pull request template is filled in ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. The org template exists in kokeb-labs/.github; nothing checks it. MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Every pull request states what changed, why, and how it was verified (CI, host tests, MCU and board, or not verified on hardware), and ticks or marks not applicable each item of the template's checklist. Verified by: pr-template (planned): the pull request body keeps the template's summary, why and verification headings, each non-empty, and every checklist box is ticked or marked not applicable review: The verification section says what was actually run. See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 8.2 (change requests are documented) Explained in: standards/repo-governance.md KB-GIT-012: Every change in behaviour adds a changelog entry under Unreleased ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. ci-tools' changelog.py checks its own changelog only; the reusable check is not built. MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A pull request that changes what a user of the repository sees adds an entry under ## [Unreleased] in CHANGELOG.md, written for that user. A pull request with nothing to record says so with the no-changelog label. Verified by: changelog-entry (planned): a pull request that changes files outside docs/ and .github/ changes CHANGELOG.md under [Unreleased], unless it carries the no-changelog label See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 8.3 (configuration status accounting) Explained in: standards/release.md KB-GIT-013: Every breaking change is listed under Breaking with what a caller must change ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A breaking change, including a change to a stored settings layout such as NVS, gets a ### Breaking entry that tells a caller what to change. A pull request labelled breaking without one is not merged. Verified by: changelog-breaking (planned): a pull request labelled breaking adds an entry under review: Public API, build-setting and stored-layout changes are either absent or listed under Breaking. See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 8.2 (impact of a change is recorded) Explained in: standards/release.md KB-GIT-014: A pull request names every rule it does not follow ¶ MUST · all · since 1.0 Not following a should rule is stated in the pull request with the rule ID and the reason. A must rule is set aside only by a waiver (KB-REPO-003) linked from the pull request with its tracking issue. Verified by: review: Every rule the change does not follow is named with its ID, and each must has a waiver. Explained in: deviations.md KB-GIT-015: Every review conversation is resolved before merge ¶ MUST · all · since 1.0 The main-review ruleset blocks the merge while a review thread is open. Verified by: rulesets (implemented): branch and tag rulesets as declared in .github/org/rulesets (PR only, linear history, tags kept) See also: ADR-0015 Explained in: standards/repo-governance.md KB-GIT-016: Approvals follow the organisation's review mode ¶ MUST · all · since 1.0 In solo mode the owner merges their own pull requests with no approval once the gate is green. With two or more maintainers, one code-owner approval is required and a new push dismisses it. Auto-merge is allowed. Verified by: rulesets (implemented): branch and tag rulesets as declared in .github/org/rulesets (PR only, linear history, tags kept) See also: ADR-0015 ; IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 8.2 (approval of changes) Explained in: standards/repo-governance.md KB-GIT-017: Review starts with architecture and layering, then the details ¶ SHOULD · all · since 1.0 A reviewer first checks that the change sits in the right layer and obeys the include table and the kind's checklist, and asks for changes if it does not. A design that is wrong at the root is closed and redone, not patched in review. Verified by: review: The layer, include and checklist questions were answered before line-level comments. Explained in: standards/layers.md KB-GIT-018: Contributions come in under the repository's licence, with no CLA ¶ GUIDE · all · since 1.0 The DCO sign-off (KB-GIT-001) is the only contributor agreement. Kokeb Labs asks for no CLA and no copyright assignment. Verified by: review: No contributor was asked to sign anything beyond the DCO. See also: ADR-0009 ; ADR-0015 Explained in: standards/repo-governance.md KB-GIT-019: Each repository has its own SemVer, starting at 0.1.0 ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. ci-tools is the exception, at 1.x (KB-CI-003). MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Versions are independent per repository. While at 0.x a breaking change bumps the minor and anything else the patch; 1.0.0 is declared by decision record when the API is meant to hold. Verified by: changelog (planned): CHANGELOG.md follows Keep a Changelog; a new version section is the next SemVer step, dated, not empty See also: ADR-0007 ; IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 8.1 (version identification) Explained in: standards/release.md KB-GIT-020: A release tag matches the declared version on a green commit of main ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. The standard describes release.yml failing on a version mismatch or a commit off main; ru-release-with-artifacts has neither check yet. MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 vX.Y.Z (or vX.Y.Z-rc.N ) tags a commit on main or release/x.y whose CI gate passed and whose declared version is X.Y.Z. A release candidate is promoted by tagging the same commit; any change makes the next rc. Verified by: release-tag (planned): on a v* tag: the tag matches the declared version, the commit is on main or release/*, its CI gate passed, and a final tag points at the same commit as the latest rc of that version See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 5.8 (software release); IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 8.1 Explained in: standards/release.md KB-GIT-021: A release is a Release vX.Y.Z pull request ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. The prepare-release workflow the standard names is not built; until it is, the maintainer does each step by hand (ci-tools uses changelog.py bump ). SHOULD · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 The release pull request rolls [Unreleased] into the dated [X.Y.Z] section, bumps every version declaration, is signed off, passes the gate and is squash-merged; merging it tags the commit. Verified by: pr-title (planned): the pull request title is at most 72 characters, has no trailing period and no Conventional Commits prefix; a release pull request is titled Release vX.Y.Z with the version of the new changelog section review: Every version declaration in the repository names the new version. Explained in: standards/release.md KB-GIT-022: Release notes are the changelog section and state the bench status ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. ci-tools' own release.yml publishes the changelog section; ru-release-with-artifacts, which other repositories call, still generates notes. MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 The GitHub Release body is the version's changelog section, not generated notes, and says where it ran: MCU, board and tests, or CI-only. A repository no board has run yet releases as CI-only. Verified by: release-notes (planned): the GitHub Release body equals the version's changelog section and has a Bench status: line See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 5.8 (documented release) Explained in: standards/release.md KB-GIT-023: A product release attaches its binaries, checksums and effective sdkconfig ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. ru-release-with-artifacts has fail_on_no_artifacts , but it defaults to false. MUST · firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A product release tag builds the firmware and attaches .bin , .elf , their SHA-256 and the effective sdkconfig; a missing artifact fails the release. A release that changes NVS or partitions states the erase or migration step. Verified by: release-artifacts (planned): a product release has .bin, .elf, SHA-256 sums and the effective sdkconfig attached, or fails review: A release that changes NVS or the partition table states the erase or migration step. See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 5.8 (archived release artifacts) Explained in: standards/product.md KB-GIT-024: Releases at high level carry checksums, provenance and an SBOM ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware (high level and above) · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Each release of a high or safety component attaches SHA256SUMS , build provenance and an SPDX SBOM of everything it contains or pulls in, all produced by the release workflow. Verified by: release-evidence (planned): a release carries SHA256SUMS, an SBOM and build provenance; at safety level the evidence package too sbom (planned): the release attaches an SPDX SBOM listing every component and submodule the build contains See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 5.8; IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 8.1 (SOUP and configuration items) Explained in: evidence.md KB-GIT-025: At safety level, release tags and the evidence package are signed ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware (safety level and above) · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A safety component's release tag is a signed annotated tag, and its evidence package carries a signature over the whole package that a manufacturer can verify. Verified by: signed-tags (planned): the release tag is a signed annotated tag and the evidence package has a valid signature (safety level) See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 5.8; IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 8.1 Explained in: evidence.md KB-GIT-026: Safety issues come first, and no release ships with one open against it ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 An issue labelled safety is fixed before other work. A version is not released while a safety issue is open against it. Verified by: open-safety-issues (planned): the release workflow fails while an open issue labelled safety names the version or its milestone review: Open safety issues were triaged before any other work in the release. See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 9 (problem resolution); IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 5.8 Explained in: checklists/release.md KB-GIT-027: At safety level, a release lists its known anomalies ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware (safety level and above) · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A safety release exports every open defect that affects the released code, with its impact and workaround, into its evidence package. Verified by: anomaly-list (planned): the evidence package lists every open bug affecting the release, with impact and workaround See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 5.8 (known residual anomalies); IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 9 Explained in: evidence.md KB-GIT-028: Submodules pin release-tag commits, and code is never edited inside one ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. The standard lists a pin-check workflow in ci-tools; it does not exist yet. MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Every submodule points at a commit that carries a release tag on the submodule's main, never at a branch or an untagged commit. A fix to a submodule is made in its own repository first. Verified by: pin-check (planned): every submodule points at a commit tagged v*.*.* on its own main and matching the manifest or catalog/compat.yml; warns on pull requests to main, fails on release/* and tag pushes See also: ADR-0007 ; IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 8.1 (identification of configuration items) Explained in: standards/release.md KB-GIT-029: A pin bump is its own pull request, opened by the bump bot or by hand ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. The bump bot that opens these pull requests after a release is not built; until it is, the maintainer opens them. SHOULD · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A pull request that moves a submodule changes nothing else except the lock or compatibility files, links the release it pulls in and notes its API and build-setting changes. Dependabot never bumps submodules. Verified by: pin-bump-isolated (planned): a pull request that moves a gitlink changes nothing else except version_lock.txt, compat.yml and CHANGELOG review: The pull request links the release it pulls in and lists what callers must change. See also: ADR-0007 ; IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 8.2 Explained in: standards/release.md KB-GIT-030: Changes and releases travel up the stack one layer at a time ¶ SHOULD · all · since 1.0 A change across layers is one pull request per repository, merged bottom-up: ci-tools, drivers, kb-core, kb-hal-common, board HALs, products. Each layer re-pins and releases before the one above it. Verified by: review: Every repository below this one is merged, released and re-pinned first. See also: ADR-0007 Explained in: standards/release.md KB-GIT-031: A release wave stabilises through release candidates ¶ GUIDE · all · since 1.0 Drivers a board uses get an rc in each wave; the wave tags rc.1 bottom-up, runs the bench, then promotes the same commits or cuts rc.2. Drivers only CI has run may skip the rc. Verified by: review: Each benched driver in the wave was released from a promoted release candidate. Explained in: standards/release.md KB-GIT-032: A release train names one kb-core release and the drivers it pins ¶ SHOULD · library · since 1.0 A train is called kb YYYY.N and is cut from that kb-core release's catalog/compat.yml . Trains are never patched: a fix makes a new kb-core release and a new train. Verified by: review: The train name and its driver list come from the tagged compat.yml. See also: ADR-0007 ; ADR-0013 ; IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 8.1 Explained in: standards/release.md KB-GIT-033: A change of decision comes with its decision record, in the same pull request ¶ SHOULD · docs · since 1.0 A handbook change that alters a decision adds a new or superseding ADR, updates every page, checklist and config it touches, and stays open for comment at least seven days unless it fixes a defect. Verified by: review: The ADR, pages, checklists and configs agree, and the comment period was kept or waived as a defect. Explained in: adr/index.md KB-GIT-034: When a repository and the handbook disagree, the handbook wins ¶ GUIDE · all · since 1.0 New code follows the handbook at once. An existing repository that does not yet comply gets an issue that tracks the gap; it is not silently exempted. Verified by: review: Each known gap between the repository and the handbook has an open issue or a waiver. Explained in: how-rules-work.md
