docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. The org template exists in kokeb-labs/.github; nothing checks it. MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Every pull request states what changed, why, and how it was verified (CI, host tests, MCU and board, or not verified on hardware), and ticks or marks not applicable each item of the template's checklist. Verified by: pr-template (planned): the pull request body keeps the template's summary, why and verification headings, each non-empty, and every checklist box is ticked or marked not applicable review: The verification section says what was actually run. See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 8.2 (change requests are documented) Explained in: standards/repo-governance.md
docs.title: KB-GIT-011: The pull request template is filled in

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. ci-tools' changelog.py checks its own changelog only; the reusable check is not built. MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A pull request that changes what a user of the repository sees adds an entry under ## [Unreleased] in CHANGELOG.md, written for that user. A pull request with nothing to record says so with the no-changelog label. Verified by: changelog-entry (planned): a pull request that changes files outside docs/ and .github/ changes CHANGELOG.md under [Unreleased], unless it carries the no-changelog label See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 8.3 (configuration status accounting) Explained in: standards/release.md
docs.title: KB-GIT-012: Every change in behaviour adds a changelog entry under Unreleased

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A breaking change, including a change to a stored settings layout such as NVS, gets a ### Breaking entry that tells a caller what to change. A pull request labelled breaking without one is not merged. Verified by: changelog-breaking (planned): a pull request labelled breaking adds an entry under review: Public API, build-setting and stored-layout changes are either absent or listed under Breaking. See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 8.2 (impact of a change is recorded) Explained in: standards/release.md
docs.title: KB-GIT-013: Every breaking change is listed under Breaking with what a caller must change

docs.text: MUST · all · since 1.0 Not following a should rule is stated in the pull request with the rule ID and the reason. A must rule is set aside only by a waiver (KB-REPO-003) linked from the pull request with its tracking issue. Verified by: review: Every rule the change does not follow is named with its ID, and each must has a waiver. Explained in: deviations.md
docs.title: KB-GIT-014: A pull request names every rule it does not follow

docs.text: MUST · all · since 1.0 The main-review ruleset blocks the merge while a review thread is open. Verified by: rulesets (implemented): branch and tag rulesets as declared in .github/org/rulesets (PR only, linear history, tags kept) See also: ADR-0015 Explained in: standards/repo-governance.md
docs.title: KB-GIT-015: Every review conversation is resolved before merge

docs.text: MUST · all · since 1.0 In solo mode the owner merges their own pull requests with no approval once the gate is green. With two or more maintainers, one code-owner approval is required and a new push dismisses it. Auto-merge is allowed. Verified by: rulesets (implemented): branch and tag rulesets as declared in .github/org/rulesets (PR only, linear history, tags kept) See also: ADR-0015 ; IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 8.2 (approval of changes) Explained in: standards/repo-governance.md
docs.title: KB-GIT-016: Approvals follow the organisation's review mode

docs.text: SHOULD · all · since 1.0 A reviewer first checks that the change sits in the right layer and obeys the include table and the kind's checklist, and asks for changes if it does not. A design that is wrong at the root is closed and redone, not patched in review. Verified by: review: The layer, include and checklist questions were answered before line-level comments. Explained in: standards/layers.md
docs.title: KB-GIT-017: Review starts with architecture and layering, then the details

docs.text: GUIDE · all · since 1.0 The DCO sign-off (KB-GIT-001) is the only contributor agreement. Kokeb Labs asks for no CLA and no copyright assignment. Verified by: review: No contributor was asked to sign anything beyond the DCO. See also: ADR-0009 ; ADR-0015 Explained in: standards/repo-governance.md
docs.title: KB-GIT-018: Contributions come in under the repository's licence, with no CLA

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. ci-tools is the exception, at 1.x (KB-CI-003). MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Versions are independent per repository. While at 0.x a breaking change bumps the minor and anything else the patch; 1.0.0 is declared by decision record when the API is meant to hold. Verified by: changelog (planned): CHANGELOG.md follows Keep a Changelog; a new version section is the next SemVer step, dated, not empty See also: ADR-0007 ; IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 8.1 (version identification) Explained in: standards/release.md
docs.title: KB-GIT-019: Each repository has its own SemVer, starting at 0.1.0

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. The standard describes release.yml failing on a version mismatch or a commit off main; ru-release-with-artifacts has neither check yet. MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 vX.Y.Z (or vX.Y.Z-rc.N ) tags a commit on main or release/x.y whose CI gate passed and whose declared version is X.Y.Z. A release candidate is promoted by tagging the same commit; any change makes the next rc. Verified by: release-tag (planned): on a v* tag: the tag matches the declared version, the commit is on main or release/*, its CI gate passed, and a final tag points at the same commit as the latest rc of that version See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 5.8 (software release); IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 8.1 Explained in: standards/release.md
docs.title: KB-GIT-020: A release tag matches the declared version on a green commit of main

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. The prepare-release workflow the standard names is not built; until it is, the maintainer does each step by hand (ci-tools uses changelog.py bump ). SHOULD · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 The release pull request rolls [Unreleased] into the dated [X.Y.Z] section, bumps every version declaration, is signed off, passes the gate and is squash-merged; merging it tags the commit. Verified by: pr-title (planned): the pull request title is at most 72 characters, has no trailing period and no Conventional Commits prefix; a release pull request is titled Release vX.Y.Z with the version of the new changelog section review: Every version declaration in the repository names the new version. Explained in: standards/release.md
docs.title: KB-GIT-021: A release is a Release vX.Y.Z pull request

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. ci-tools' own release.yml publishes the changelog section; ru-release-with-artifacts, which other repositories call, still generates notes. MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 The GitHub Release body is the version's changelog section, not generated notes, and says where it ran: MCU, board and tests, or CI-only. A repository no board has run yet releases as CI-only. Verified by: release-notes (planned): the GitHub Release body equals the version's changelog section and has a Bench status: line See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 5.8 (documented release) Explained in: standards/release.md
docs.title: KB-GIT-022: Release notes are the changelog section and state the bench status

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. ru-release-with-artifacts has fail_on_no_artifacts , but it defaults to false. MUST · firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A product release tag builds the firmware and attaches .bin , .elf , their SHA-256 and the effective sdkconfig; a missing artifact fails the release. A release that changes NVS or partitions states the erase or migration step. Verified by: release-artifacts (planned): a product release has .bin, .elf, SHA-256 sums and the effective sdkconfig attached, or fails review: A release that changes NVS or the partition table states the erase or migration step. See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 5.8 (archived release artifacts) Explained in: standards/product.md
docs.title: KB-GIT-023: A product release attaches its binaries, checksums and effective sdkconfig

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware (high level and above) · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Each release of a high or safety component attaches SHA256SUMS , build provenance and an SPDX SBOM of everything it contains or pulls in, all produced by the release workflow. Verified by: release-evidence (planned): a release carries SHA256SUMS, an SBOM and build provenance; at safety level the evidence package too sbom (planned): the release attaches an SPDX SBOM listing every component and submodule the build contains See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 5.8; IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 8.1 (SOUP and configuration items) Explained in: evidence.md
docs.title: KB-GIT-024: Releases at high level carry checksums, provenance and an SBOM

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware (safety level and above) · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A safety component's release tag is a signed annotated tag, and its evidence package carries a signature over the whole package that a manufacturer can verify. Verified by: signed-tags (planned): the release tag is a signed annotated tag and the evidence package has a valid signature (safety level) See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 5.8; IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 8.1 Explained in: evidence.md
docs.title: KB-GIT-025: At safety level, release tags and the evidence package are signed

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 An issue labelled safety is fixed before other work. A version is not released while a safety issue is open against it. Verified by: open-safety-issues (planned): the release workflow fails while an open issue labelled safety names the version or its milestone review: Open safety issues were triaged before any other work in the release. See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 9 (problem resolution); IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 5.8 Explained in: checklists/release.md
docs.title: KB-GIT-026: Safety issues come first, and no release ships with one open against it

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware (safety level and above) · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A safety release exports every open defect that affects the released code, with its impact and workaround, into its evidence package. Verified by: anomaly-list (planned): the evidence package lists every open bug affecting the release, with impact and workaround See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 5.8 (known residual anomalies); IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 9 Explained in: evidence.md
docs.title: KB-GIT-027: At safety level, a release lists its known anomalies

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. The standard lists a pin-check workflow in ci-tools; it does not exist yet. MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Every submodule points at a commit that carries a release tag on the submodule's main, never at a branch or an untagged commit. A fix to a submodule is made in its own repository first. Verified by: pin-check (planned): every submodule points at a commit tagged v*.*.* on its own main and matching the manifest or catalog/compat.yml; warns on pull requests to main, fails on release/* and tag pushes See also: ADR-0007 ; IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 8.1 (identification of configuration items) Explained in: standards/release.md
docs.title: KB-GIT-028: Submodules pin release-tag commits, and code is never edited inside one

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. The bump bot that opens these pull requests after a release is not built; until it is, the maintainer opens them. SHOULD · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A pull request that moves a submodule changes nothing else except the lock or compatibility files, links the release it pulls in and notes its API and build-setting changes. Dependabot never bumps submodules. Verified by: pin-bump-isolated (planned): a pull request that moves a gitlink changes nothing else except version_lock.txt, compat.yml and CHANGELOG review: The pull request links the release it pulls in and lists what callers must change. See also: ADR-0007 ; IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 8.2 Explained in: standards/release.md
docs.title: KB-GIT-029: A pin bump is its own pull request, opened by the bump bot or by hand

docs.text: SHOULD · all · since 1.0 A change across layers is one pull request per repository, merged bottom-up: ci-tools, drivers, kb-core, kb-hal-common, board HALs, products. Each layer re-pins and releases before the one above it. Verified by: review: Every repository below this one is merged, released and re-pinned first. See also: ADR-0007 Explained in: standards/release.md
docs.title: KB-GIT-030: Changes and releases travel up the stack one layer at a time

docs.text: GUIDE · all · since 1.0 Drivers a board uses get an rc in each wave; the wave tags rc.1 bottom-up, runs the bench, then promotes the same commits or cuts rc.2. Drivers only CI has run may skip the rc. Verified by: review: Each benched driver in the wave was released from a promoted release candidate. Explained in: standards/release.md
docs.title: KB-GIT-031: A release wave stabilises through release candidates

docs.text: SHOULD · library · since 1.0 A train is called kb YYYY.N and is cut from that kb-core release's catalog/compat.yml . Trains are never patched: a fix makes a new kb-core release and a new train. Verified by: review: The train name and its driver list come from the tagged compat.yml. See also: ADR-0007 ; ADR-0013 ; IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 8.1 Explained in: standards/release.md
docs.title: KB-GIT-032: A release train names one kb-core release and the drivers it pins

docs.text: SHOULD · docs · since 1.0 A handbook change that alters a decision adds a new or superseding ADR, updates every page, checklist and config it touches, and stays open for comment at least seven days unless it fixes a defect. Verified by: review: The ADR, pages, checklists and configs agree, and the comment period was kept or waived as a defect. Explained in: adr/index.md
docs.title: KB-GIT-033: A change of decision comes with its decision record, in the same pull request

docs.text: GUIDE · all · since 1.0 New code follows the handbook at once. An existing repository that does not yet comply gets an issue that tracks the gap; it is not silently exempted. Verified by: review: Each known gap between the repository and the handbook has an open issue or a waiver. Explained in: how-rules-work.md
docs.title: KB-GIT-034: When a repository and the handbook disagree, the handbook wins

docs.text: Hardware and porting ¶ Porting the stack to an MCU family, bringing up a board, working with vendor-generated code, and what shipping firmware must do on the hardware. The MCU port lives in kb-core's interfaces/mcu/<family>/; the board side is in the board HAL's bind. Rule Level Applies to Verified KB-HW-001 Every MCU family implements the foundation interfaces must library planned KB-HW-002 A port passes the conformance suite before it is done must library, hal planned KB-HW-003 The port owns vendor-callback bridging, one entry point per interrupt family must library, hal review KB-HW-004 Configure peripherals the way the vendor SDK expects guide library, hal none KB-HW-005 Clock speeds and bus settings come from configuration, not literals should library, hal review KB-HW-006 A port publishes its measured performance should library review KB-HW-007 A board HAL starts from a complete hardware picture guide hal none KB-HW-008 STM32 ports use CubeMX, the STM32 HAL, CMake and FreeRTOS by default guide library, hal none KB-HW-009 Vendor-generated code is regenerable and never hand-edited outside its markers must hal, firmware planned KB-HW-010 Heavily used buses use DMA, with a timed-out polled fallback should library, hal review KB-HW-011 Hardware and protocol changes update the specification in the same pull request should driver, hal, firmware review KB-HW-012 Shipping firmware enables the watchdog, serviced from a supervisor task must firmware planned KB-HW-013 Shipping firmware configures brownout reset must firmware planned KB-HW-014 Over-the-air updates verify signatures and can roll back must firmware planned KB-HW-015 Firmware logs why it booted and what it is should firmware review KB-HW-016 Firmware reports its health and keeps a crash record should firmware review KB-HW-017 A factory test mode exists and is documented should firmware review KB-HW-018 Control outputs reach their inactive level before they are enabled must driver, library, hal, firmware, template planned KB-HW-019 Port conformance covers the shared-bus faults found on hardware must library, hal planned KB-HW-001: Every MCU family implements the foundation interfaces ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. The foundation set is new to the Kokeb standard. MUST · library · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Each real MCU family in interfaces/mcu/<family>/ implements BaseSpi , BaseI2c , BaseGpio , BaseAdc , BaseNvs , BaseLogger , BaseTemperature and BasePeriodicTimer . Other Base* interfaces are implemented when the MCU has the hardware and a consumer needs it; there are no stubs, and enabling one the family lacks fails at CMake configure time. Why: Every handler, manager and HAL then compiles on a new family without change. A stub that compiles but does nothing turns a configuration mistake into a bench fault. Verified by: mcu-foundation-set (planned): each real family under interfaces/mcu/ implements the eight foundation Base* interfaces, and enabling an optional one the family lacks fails at CMake configure time See also: ADR-0014 Explained in: standards/library.md KB-HW-002: A port passes the conformance suite before it is done ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · library, hal · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A new or changed MCU port passes the Base* conformance tests: on the host against a mocked vendor SDK where the SDK allows, and as loopback tests on a board (SPI MOSI to MISO, UART TX to RX, GPIO pairs). After a port, vendor-callback wiring, MCU-gated drivers and the family's build options are re-tested on the board. Verified by: port-conformance (planned): the Base* conformance suite passes for the named MCU family, on the host against a mocked SDK and, on a scheduled job with a board, as loopback tests review: The pull request links the loopback run on a board, or is marked not verified on hardware. Explained in: checklists/new-board-hal.md KB-HW-003: The port owns vendor-callback bridging, one entry point per interrupt family ¶ MUST · library, hal · since 1.0 The family's port bridges vendor callbacks ( HAL_GPIO_EXTI_Callback , DMA completion) to its objects through a static dispatch table or a handle lookup, with one documented entry point per interrupt family. The bridge takes no mutex; it sets an OsEventFlags bit or gives a SignalSemaphore and returns. Verified by: review: Each interrupt family has one entry point documented in the port header, and no code reached from it takes a mutex. Explained in: standards/threading-and-timing.md KB-HW-004: Configure peripherals the way the vendor SDK expects ¶ GUIDE · library, hal · since 1.0 Where the vendor's culture is a configuration tool (STM32CubeMX, MCUXpresso), the port wraps the generated handles; where the SDK has a full run-time API (ESP-IDF), the port configures the peripheral itself from a spec. Either way the rest of the stack sees only the Base* interface. Explained in: standards/library.md KB-HW-005: Clock speeds and bus settings come from configuration, not literals ¶ SHOULD · library, hal · since 1.0 A port object takes clock speed, mode and pins from its constructor spec or the board config; it hard-codes none of them. Verified by: review: Bus clocks, modes and pins in the port come from the spec or the board config. Explained in: standards/hal.md KB-HW-006: A port publishes its measured performance ¶ SHOULD · library · since 1.0 A port's documentation lists measured timings for the foundation operations (an 8-byte SPI transfer, a GPIO set, an ADC read, a 2-byte I2C transfer, periodic-timer jitter) with the clock rates used, so HAL authors can tell whether a hot path needs more. Verified by: review: The port's documentation has a measured timing table for the foundation operations. KB-HW-007: A board HAL starts from a complete hardware picture ¶ GUIDE · hal · since 1.0 Before writing a board HAL, have the schematic and pin-out, the full chip list, the chosen MCU variant, and a released driver and kb-core support for every chip and peripheral on the board. A missing peripheral goes into kb-core first. Explained in: checklists/new-board-hal.md KB-HW-008: STM32 ports use CubeMX, the STM32 HAL, CMake and FreeRTOS by default ¶ GUIDE · library, hal · since 1.0 Start an STM32 family with STM32CubeMX for clocks and pins, the STM32 HAL (LL where latency needs it), CMake, and FreeRTOS or ThreadX at a 1 kHz tick. See also: ADR-0006 KB-HW-009: Vendor-generated code is regenerable and never hand-edited outside its markers ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · hal, firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A CubeMX project generates peripheral initialisation as .c / .h pairs, copies only the needed libraries and never uses the single- main.c option. The .ioc and the generated tree are committed; hand-written code goes only between USER CODE markers or in separate files (vendor weak callbacks are overridden in the project's own interrupt file), and any other patch to generated files is listed in PATCHES.md . Why: Regenerating from the .ioc must not lose work or silently revert a fix. Verified by: cubemx-discipline (planned): the .ioc sets ProjectManager.CoupleFile=true and the library-copy option, and regenerating from the .ioc reproduces the committed tree except for USER CODE blocks and the patches listed in PATCHES.md KB-HW-010: Heavily used buses use DMA, with a timed-out polled fallback ¶ SHOULD · library, hal · since 1.0 SPI, I2C and UART ports use DMA when the board wires a DMA channel and fall back to polled transfers otherwise; both paths have a timeout and both are tested. Verified by: review: The DMA and polled paths both have a timeout and a test. KB-HW-011: Hardware and protocol changes update the specification in the same pull request ¶ SHOULD · driver, hal, firmware · since 1.0 A change that follows a hardware or protocol change updates the affected Hardware page, board specification or protocol description in the same pull request. Verified by: review: The Hardware or protocol documentation matches the change. KB-HW-012: Shipping firmware enables the watchdog, serviced from a supervisor task ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Release firmware enables the hardware or task watchdog, and one supervisor task services it only while the tasks it watches report progress. Why: A hung task with a live actuator must end in a reset, not a stuck output. Verified by: sdkconfig-defaults/watchdog (planned): sdkconfig.defaults of every ESP-IDF project sets the named value (freertos-hz is CONFIG_FREERTOS_HZ=1000) review: The supervisor services the watchdog only when every watched task has reported. KB-HW-013: Shipping firmware configures brownout reset ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Release firmware enables brownout detection with reset, at a threshold above the board's minimum supply. Verified by: sdkconfig-defaults/brownout (planned): sdkconfig.defaults of every ESP-IDF project sets the named value (freertos-hz is CONFIG_FREERTOS_HZ=1000) KB-HW-014: Over-the-air updates verify signatures and can roll back ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Firmware that updates over the air keeps the previous image and rolls back to it when the new one fails to confirm itself. A product that signs its images verifies the signature before booting an update. Verified by: sdkconfig-defaults/ota (planned): sdkconfig.defaults of every ESP-IDF project sets the named value (freertos-hz is CONFIG_FREERTOS_HZ=1000) review: The good-update and rollback paths were exercised on a board before release. KB-HW-015: Firmware logs why it booted and what it is ¶ SHOULD · firmware · since 1.0 On every start the firmware logs the reset reason from the bind and its own version, release train and provenance header. Verified by: review: The boot log has the reset reason and the version and provenance. Explained in: standards/product.md KB-HW-016: Firmware reports its health and keeps a crash record ¶ SHOULD · firmware · since 1.0 Firmware captures free heap, the largest free block and uptime periodically in its diagnostics, and persists a crash record (reason, task, program counter) to NVS or external storage for the next boot. Verified by: review: Health figures are in the diagnostics and a crash record survives a reset. KB-HW-017: A factory test mode exists and is documented ¶ SHOULD · firmware · since 1.0 Production firmware has a factory test mode, entered by a documented method (an NVS flag or a button held at boot), and the product's documentation describes what it tests. Verified by: review: The factory mode, how to enter it and what it tests are documented. KB-HW-018: Control outputs reach their inactive level before they are enabled ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. The polarity half is KB-CPP-038. MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A port drives every control output (reset, enable, soft chip-select, command/data, write-protect) to its inactive level before it enables the pin's output driver and before the first frame; a soft chip-select is written high before its pin is configured as an output. Each pin's idle level and polarity are stated once in the port contract (the driver's Porting page) as logical ACTIVE and INACTIVE. Why: Observed on hardware: GPIO defaults left an active-low reset asserted and two chip-selects low together until the first driver call. Verified by: port-conformance (planned): the Base* conformance suite passes for the named MCU family, on the host against a mocked SDK and, on a scheduled job with a board, as loopback tests review: Each port sets the output level before the direction; the Porting page lists every control pin with its idle level; on a real MCU the bench bring-up checks the pins at reset. See also: ADR-0003 Explained in: standards/driver.md KB-HW-019: Port conformance covers the shared-bus faults found on hardware ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. The buffer ownership half is KB-CPP-040 and KB-CPP-043. MUST · library, hal · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Port conformance (KB-HW-002) also proves: the first frame after any mode or clock change is intact; chip-select lines are at their idle level before any driver starts; UART input is flushed before a transmit and never between transmit and receive, and the turnaround is observed; an I2C bus clear runs before a retried start-up; every operation is bounded by a timeout; transfer buffers live in memory the bus and its DMA can reach, owned by the driver object, never on a caller's stack or in a function-local static. Why: Observed on hardware, each of these host faults looked like a chip fault on the bench. Verified by: port-conformance (planned): the Base* conformance suite passes for the named MCU family, on the host against a mocked SDK and, on a scheduled job with a board, as loopback tests review: The MCU-specific items (DMA-capable memory, first frame after a clock change) are run on the bench. Explained in: standards/hal.md
docs.title: Hardware and porting

docs.text: Porting the stack to an MCU family, bringing up a board, working with vendor-generated code, and what shipping firmware must do on the hardware. The MCU port lives in kb-core's interfaces/mcu/<family>/; the board side is in the board HAL's bind. Rule Level Applies to Verified KB-HW-001 Every MCU family implements the foundation interfaces must library planned KB-HW-002 A port passes the conformance suite before it is done must library, hal planned KB-HW-003 The port owns vendor-callback bridging, one entry point per interrupt family must library, hal review KB-HW-004 Configure peripherals the way the vendor SDK expects guide library, hal none KB-HW-005 Clock speeds and bus settings come from configuration, not literals should library, hal review KB-HW-006 A port publishes its measured performance should library review KB-HW-007 A board HAL starts from a complete hardware picture guide hal none KB-HW-008 STM32 ports use CubeMX, the STM32 HAL, CMake and FreeRTOS by default guide library, hal none KB-HW-009 Vendor-generated code is regenerable and never hand-edited outside its markers must hal, firmware planned KB-HW-010 Heavily used buses use DMA, with a timed-out polled fallback should library, hal review KB-HW-011 Hardware and protocol changes update the specification in the same pull request should driver, hal, firmware review KB-HW-012 Shipping firmware enables the watchdog, serviced from a supervisor task must firmware planned KB-HW-013 Shipping firmware configures brownout reset must firmware planned KB-HW-014 Over-the-air updates verify signatures and can roll back must firmware planned KB-HW-015 Firmware logs why it booted and what it is should firmware review KB-HW-016 Firmware reports its health and keeps a crash record should firmware review KB-HW-017 A factory test mode exists and is documented should firmware review KB-HW-018 Control outputs reach their inactive level before they are enabled must driver, library, hal, firmware, template planned KB-HW-019 Port conformance covers the shared-bus faults found on hardware must library, hal planned
docs.title: Hardware and porting

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. The foundation set is new to the Kokeb standard. MUST · library · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Each real MCU family in interfaces/mcu/<family>/ implements BaseSpi , BaseI2c , BaseGpio , BaseAdc , BaseNvs , BaseLogger , BaseTemperature and BasePeriodicTimer . Other Base* interfaces are implemented when the MCU has the hardware and a consumer needs it; there are no stubs, and enabling one the family lacks fails at CMake configure time. Why: Every handler, manager and HAL then compiles on a new family without change. A stub that compiles but does nothing turns a configuration mistake into a bench fault. Verified by: mcu-foundation-set (planned): each real family under interfaces/mcu/ implements the eight foundation Base* interfaces, and enabling an optional one the family lacks fails at CMake configure time See also: ADR-0014 Explained in: standards/library.md
docs.title: KB-HW-001: Every MCU family implements the foundation interfaces

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · library, hal · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A new or changed MCU port passes the Base* conformance tests: on the host against a mocked vendor SDK where the SDK allows, and as loopback tests on a board (SPI MOSI to MISO, UART TX to RX, GPIO pairs). After a port, vendor-callback wiring, MCU-gated drivers and the family's build options are re-tested on the board. Verified by: port-conformance (planned): the Base* conformance suite passes for the named MCU family, on the host against a mocked SDK and, on a scheduled job with a board, as loopback tests review: The pull request links the loopback run on a board, or is marked not verified on hardware. Explained in: checklists/new-board-hal.md
docs.title: KB-HW-002: A port passes the conformance suite before it is done

docs.text: MUST · library, hal · since 1.0 The family's port bridges vendor callbacks ( HAL_GPIO_EXTI_Callback , DMA completion) to its objects through a static dispatch table or a handle lookup, with one documented entry point per interrupt family. The bridge takes no mutex; it sets an OsEventFlags bit or gives a SignalSemaphore and returns. Verified by: review: Each interrupt family has one entry point documented in the port header, and no code reached from it takes a mutex. Explained in: standards/threading-and-timing.md
docs.title: KB-HW-003: The port owns vendor-callback bridging, one entry point per interrupt family

docs.text: GUIDE · library, hal · since 1.0 Where the vendor's culture is a configuration tool (STM32CubeMX, MCUXpresso), the port wraps the generated handles; where the SDK has a full run-time API (ESP-IDF), the port configures the peripheral itself from a spec. Either way the rest of the stack sees only the Base* interface. Explained in: standards/library.md
docs.title: KB-HW-004: Configure peripherals the way the vendor SDK expects

docs.text: SHOULD · library, hal · since 1.0 A port object takes clock speed, mode and pins from its constructor spec or the board config; it hard-codes none of them. Verified by: review: Bus clocks, modes and pins in the port come from the spec or the board config. Explained in: standards/hal.md
docs.title: KB-HW-005: Clock speeds and bus settings come from configuration, not literals

docs.text: SHOULD · library · since 1.0 A port's documentation lists measured timings for the foundation operations (an 8-byte SPI transfer, a GPIO set, an ADC read, a 2-byte I2C transfer, periodic-timer jitter) with the clock rates used, so HAL authors can tell whether a hot path needs more. Verified by: review: The port's documentation has a measured timing table for the foundation operations.
docs.title: KB-HW-006: A port publishes its measured performance

docs.text: GUIDE · hal · since 1.0 Before writing a board HAL, have the schematic and pin-out, the full chip list, the chosen MCU variant, and a released driver and kb-core support for every chip and peripheral on the board. A missing peripheral goes into kb-core first. Explained in: checklists/new-board-hal.md
docs.title: KB-HW-007: A board HAL starts from a complete hardware picture

docs.text: GUIDE · library, hal · since 1.0 Start an STM32 family with STM32CubeMX for clocks and pins, the STM32 HAL (LL where latency needs it), CMake, and FreeRTOS or ThreadX at a 1 kHz tick. See also: ADR-0006
docs.title: KB-HW-008: STM32 ports use CubeMX, the STM32 HAL, CMake and FreeRTOS by default

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · hal, firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A CubeMX project generates peripheral initialisation as .c / .h pairs, copies only the needed libraries and never uses the single- main.c option. The .ioc and the generated tree are committed; hand-written code goes only between USER CODE markers or in separate files (vendor weak callbacks are overridden in the project's own interrupt file), and any other patch to generated files is listed in PATCHES.md . Why: Regenerating from the .ioc must not lose work or silently revert a fix. Verified by: cubemx-discipline (planned): the .ioc sets ProjectManager.CoupleFile=true and the library-copy option, and regenerating from the .ioc reproduces the committed tree except for USER CODE blocks and the patches listed in PATCHES.md
docs.title: KB-HW-009: Vendor-generated code is regenerable and never hand-edited outside its markers

docs.text: SHOULD · library, hal · since 1.0 SPI, I2C and UART ports use DMA when the board wires a DMA channel and fall back to polled transfers otherwise; both paths have a timeout and both are tested. Verified by: review: The DMA and polled paths both have a timeout and a test.
docs.title: KB-HW-010: Heavily used buses use DMA, with a timed-out polled fallback

docs.text: SHOULD · driver, hal, firmware · since 1.0 A change that follows a hardware or protocol change updates the affected Hardware page, board specification or protocol description in the same pull request. Verified by: review: The Hardware or protocol documentation matches the change.
docs.title: KB-HW-011: Hardware and protocol changes update the specification in the same pull request

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Release firmware enables the hardware or task watchdog, and one supervisor task services it only while the tasks it watches report progress. Why: A hung task with a live actuator must end in a reset, not a stuck output. Verified by: sdkconfig-defaults/watchdog (planned): sdkconfig.defaults of every ESP-IDF project sets the named value (freertos-hz is CONFIG_FREERTOS_HZ=1000) review: The supervisor services the watchdog only when every watched task has reported.
docs.title: KB-HW-012: Shipping firmware enables the watchdog, serviced from a supervisor task

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Release firmware enables brownout detection with reset, at a threshold above the board's minimum supply. Verified by: sdkconfig-defaults/brownout (planned): sdkconfig.defaults of every ESP-IDF project sets the named value (freertos-hz is CONFIG_FREERTOS_HZ=1000)
docs.title: KB-HW-013: Shipping firmware configures brownout reset

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Firmware that updates over the air keeps the previous image and rolls back to it when the new one fails to confirm itself. A product that signs its images verifies the signature before booting an update. Verified by: sdkconfig-defaults/ota (planned): sdkconfig.defaults of every ESP-IDF project sets the named value (freertos-hz is CONFIG_FREERTOS_HZ=1000) review: The good-update and rollback paths were exercised on a board before release.
docs.title: KB-HW-014: Over-the-air updates verify signatures and can roll back

docs.text: SHOULD · firmware · since 1.0 On every start the firmware logs the reset reason from the bind and its own version, release train and provenance header. Verified by: review: The boot log has the reset reason and the version and provenance. Explained in: standards/product.md
docs.title: KB-HW-015: Firmware logs why it booted and what it is

docs.text: SHOULD · firmware · since 1.0 Firmware captures free heap, the largest free block and uptime periodically in its diagnostics, and persists a crash record (reason, task, program counter) to NVS or external storage for the next boot. Verified by: review: Health figures are in the diagnostics and a crash record survives a reset.
docs.title: KB-HW-016: Firmware reports its health and keeps a crash record

docs.text: SHOULD · firmware · since 1.0 Production firmware has a factory test mode, entered by a documented method (an NVS flag or a button held at boot), and the product's documentation describes what it tests. Verified by: review: The factory mode, how to enter it and what it tests are documented.
docs.title: KB-HW-017: A factory test mode exists and is documented

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. The polarity half is KB-CPP-038. MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A port drives every control output (reset, enable, soft chip-select, command/data, write-protect) to its inactive level before it enables the pin's output driver and before the first frame; a soft chip-select is written high before its pin is configured as an output. Each pin's idle level and polarity are stated once in the port contract (the driver's Porting page) as logical ACTIVE and INACTIVE. Why: Observed on hardware: GPIO defaults left an active-low reset asserted and two chip-selects low together until the first driver call. Verified by: port-conformance (planned): the Base* conformance suite passes for the named MCU family, on the host against a mocked SDK and, on a scheduled job with a board, as loopback tests review: Each port sets the output level before the direction; the Porting page lists every control pin with its idle level; on a real MCU the bench bring-up checks the pins at reset. See also: ADR-0003 Explained in: standards/driver.md
docs.title: KB-HW-018: Control outputs reach their inactive level before they are enabled

docs.text: Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. The buffer ownership half is KB-CPP-040 and KB-CPP-043. MUST · library, hal · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Port conformance (KB-HW-002) also proves: the first frame after any mode or clock change is intact; chip-select lines are at their idle level before any driver starts; UART input is flushed before a transmit and never between transmit and receive, and the turnaround is observed; an I2C bus clear runs before a retried start-up; every operation is bounded by a timeout; transfer buffers live in memory the bus and its DMA can reach, owned by the driver object, never on a caller's stack or in a function-local static. Why: Observed on hardware, each of these host faults looked like a chip fault on the bench. Verified by: port-conformance (planned): the Base* conformance suite passes for the named MCU family, on the host against a mocked SDK and, on a scheduled job with a board, as loopback tests review: The MCU-specific items (DMA-capable memory, first frame after a clock change) are run on the bench. Explained in: standards/hal.md
docs.title: KB-HW-019: Port conformance covers the shared-bus faults found on hardware

docs.text: Repository ¶ What every repository contains and declares. Rule Level Applies to Verified KB-REPO-001 Required root files must all checked KB-REPO-002 Each repository declares the handbook version, kind and level it follows must all checked KB-REPO-003 Waivers name a rule, a reason, an approver and an expiry must all checked KB-REPO-004 Every source file carries an SPDX licence identifier should driver, library, hal, firmware, tooling, template planned KB-REPO-005 The root holds only the entries listed for the repository's kind must all checked KB-REPO-006 A driver has the driver layout must driver, template checked KB-REPO-007 File names follow the layer's convention should driver, library, hal, template planned KB-REPO-008 A standalone library starts from driver-template and keeps its layout must library checked KB-REPO-009 kb-core keeps its monorepo layout must library checked KB-REPO-010 A board HAL has the board HAL layout must hal checked KB-REPO-011 A product has the product layout must firmware checked KB-REPO-012 Board HALs and products live in the product's organisation guide hal, firmware review KB-REPO-013 Each example platform stands alone, and sources have one home should driver, library, template checked KB-REPO-014 No symlinks anywhere in a repository must all planned KB-REPO-015 _config/ holds the org's tool configs unchanged, and tools are pointed at it must driver, library, hal, firmware, template planned KB-REPO-016 ESP-IDF projects commit sdkconfig.defaults, never sdkconfig must driver, library, hal, firmware, template checked KB-REPO-017 No ESP-IDF wrapper component or idf_component.yml unless the registry is chosen should driver, library, template planned KB-REPO-018 Every driver declares itself in driver.yml must driver, template checked KB-REPO-019 Third-party code keeps its own licence under third_party/ must all planned KB-REPO-020 Hardware is CERN-OHL-P-2.0; a product owner picks the board HAL licence should all review KB-REPO-021 CODEOWNERS gives every path a default owner should all planned KB-REPO-022 Vulnerabilities are reported privately, as SECURITY.md says must all planned KB-REPO-023 Issues use the org forms and labels should all planned KB-REPO-024 Repository settings are code in the .github repository must all checked KB-REPO-025 A new repository starts from its kind's template and is declared first should all review KB-REPO-026 A superseded repository is marked legacy and archived should all review KB-REPO-027 CubeMX code is committed with the .ioc it came from should hal, firmware review KB-REPO-001: Required root files ¶ MUST · all · since 1.0 Every repository has README.md, LICENSE (MIT for code), CHANGELOG.md and .github/CODEOWNERS at its root. Verified by: org-standard-files (implemented): README.md, LICENSE (MIT), CHANGELOG.md and .github/CODEOWNERS exist See also: ADR-0009 ; ADR-0011 KB-REPO-002: Each repository declares the handbook version, kind and level it follows ¶ MUST · all · since 1.0 .kokeb/handbook.yml names a released handbook version, the repository's kind and its assurance level, and lists its waivers. Verified by: handbook-declaration (implemented): .kokeb/handbook.yml exists and names a released handbook version, a kind and a level Explained in: how-rules-work.md KB-REPO-003: Waivers name a rule, a reason, an approver and an expiry ¶ MUST · all · since 1.0 A rule is set aside only by a waiver in .kokeb/handbook.yml that names the rule ID, why, who approved it and the date it expires. An expired waiver fails CI. Verified by: waivers (implemented): every waiver names an existing rule, a reason, an approver and an expiry date that has not passed Explained in: deviations.md KB-REPO-004: Every source file carries an SPDX licence identifier ¶ Proposed Not enforced yet. SHOULD · driver, library, hal, firmware, tooling, template · since 1.0 Each source file starts with SPDX-License-Identifier: and a copyright line, as REUSE checks it. Verified by: spdx-headers (planned): every source file carries an SPDX licence identifier (REUSE) KB-REPO-005: The root holds only the entries listed for the repository's kind ¶ MUST · all · since 1.0 Tool configuration lives in _config/ , not at the root. An extra root file a tool insists on is listed, with the tool, in AGENTS.md; a pull request adding a root entry without such a reason is refused. Verified by: repo-layout (implemented): the committed root entries match the layout for the repository's kind (drivers and templates today) See also: ADR-0011 Explained in: standards/repo-governance.md KB-REPO-006: A driver has the driver layout ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. driver-template's self-test checks part of it, in the template only. MUST · driver, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A driver keeps inc/<chip>.hpp , inc/<chip>_<bus>_interface.hpp , inc/<chip>_types.hpp , src/<chip>.ipp , cmake/ , examples/host/ and other platforms, a flat tests/ , docs/ and _config/ . Verified by: repo-layout (implemented): the committed root entries match the layout for the repository's kind (drivers and templates today) See also: ADR-0011 ; ADR-0012 Explained in: standards/driver.md KB-REPO-007: File names follow the layer's convention ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. SHOULD · driver, library, hal, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Driver files are <chip>_<part>.hpp and .ipp ; kb-core and board HAL files are PascalCase .h and .cpp named for the class they hold; tests are test_<subject>.cpp . Verified by: file-names (planned): source and test file names match the pattern for the repository's kind See also: ADR-0008 Explained in: standards/naming-and-style.md KB-REPO-008: A standalone library starts from driver-template and keeps its layout ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. kb-core has its own layout (KB-REPO-009). MUST · library · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A library outside kb-core is generated with driver-template --kind library and keeps the driver root layout, an examples/host/ , one CMake target and one include root. Verified by: repo-layout (implemented): the committed root entries match the layout for the repository's kind (drivers and templates today) See also: ADR-0011 Explained in: standards/library.md KB-REPO-009: kb-core keeps its monorepo layout ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. Applies to kb-core only. MUST · library · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 kb-core holds utils/ , rtos/ , interfaces/ (base, mcu/<family>/ , host), handlers/ , drivers/ with one submodule per driver, cmake/kb_build_settings.cmake and catalog/compat.yml . Verified by: repo-layout (implemented): the committed root entries match the layout for the repository's kind (drivers and templates today) See also: ADR-0013 Explained in: standards/library.md KB-REPO-010: A board HAL has the board HAL layout ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · hal · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A board HAL has lib/common (kb-hal-common) and lib/core (kb-core) submodules, one board/<board>/ folder of bus, chip and pin tables (data, not logic), a bsp_bind/<family>/ per family plus bsp_bind/host/ , and _config/ . Its only root extras are CMakePresets.json and version_lock.txt . Verified by: repo-layout (implemented): the committed root entries match the layout for the repository's kind (drivers and templates today) See also: ADR-0005 ; ADR-0011 Explained in: standards/hal.md KB-REPO-011: A product has the product layout ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. Examples and test benches of the firmware kind are exempt. MUST · firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A product holds main/ (or app/ ), platform/ , hal/ , version_lock.txt , sdkconfig.defaults , partitions.csv , docs/ and _config/ . Verified by: repo-layout (implemented): the committed root entries match the layout for the repository's kind (drivers and templates today) See also: ADR-0011 Explained in: standards/product.md KB-REPO-012: Board HALs and products live in the product's organisation ¶ GUIDE · hal, firmware · since 1.0 kokeb-labs holds reusable code only. A board HAL or product lives in its product's organisation (HardFOC is one) and starts from the board HAL template. Verified by: review: A new board HAL or product repository is created in the product organisation. See also: ADR-0005 Explained in: standards/hal.md KB-REPO-013: Each example platform stands alone, and sources have one home ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. SHOULD · driver, library, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Every examples/<platform>/ has its own port, example program and README and builds on its own. Zephyr, Arduino or PlatformIO manifests are added only when a user needs them, and never copy the sources. Verified by: repo-layout (implemented): the committed root entries match the layout for the repository's kind (drivers and templates today) review: Any extra ecosystem manifest points at the existing sources. Explained in: standards/driver.md KB-REPO-014: No symlinks anywhere in a repository ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. driver-template's self-test scans for symlinks in the template only. MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A repository tracks no symbolic links. An editor that wants a config at the root gets a local, gitignored copy of the file in _config/ . Verified by: tracked-files/symlinks (planned): git tracks no file of a banned kind; the parameter names it (tracked-files/symlinks, tracked-files/sdkconfig, tracked-files/idf-component) See also: ADR-0011 Explained in: standards/repo-governance.md KB-REPO-015: _config/ holds the org's tool configs unchanged, and tools are pointed at it ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. ci-tools' own _config/ clang configs, the ru-cpp-lint defaults, differ from the handbook's and need the same fix. MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 _config/.clang-format and _config/.clang-tidy are byte copies of the handbook's config/ files, apart from the header comment. Every command and workflow passes the _config/ path to its tool. Verified by: config-drift (planned): _config/.clang-format and _config/.clang-tidy equal the handbook's config/ files apart from the header See also: ADR-0008 ; ADR-0011 Explained in: standards/naming-and-style.md KB-REPO-016: ESP-IDF projects commit sdkconfig.defaults, never sdkconfig ¶ MUST · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 The settings an ESP-IDF project needs are in sdkconfig.defaults (and sdkconfig.defaults.<target> ); the generated sdkconfig is gitignored and never committed. A firmware release attaches the effective sdkconfig instead. Verified by: tracked-files/sdkconfig (implemented): git tracks no file of a banned kind; the parameter names it (tracked-files/symlinks, tracked-files/sdkconfig, tracked-files/idf-component) See also: ADR-0018 Explained in: standards/driver.md KB-REPO-017: No ESP-IDF wrapper component or idf_component.yml unless the registry is chosen ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. SHOULD · driver, library, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A driver or library has no wrapper component folder and no idf_component.yml , unless a decision record chooses to publish it to the ESP Component Registry. Verified by: tracked-files/idf-component (planned): git tracks no file of a banned kind; the parameter names it (tracked-files/symlinks, tracked-files/sdkconfig, tracked-files/idf-component) See also: ADR-0007 ; ADR-0011 Explained in: standards/driver.md KB-REPO-018: Every driver declares itself in driver.yml ¶ MUST · driver, template · since 1.0 A driver's root driver.yml gives its name, version, bus, supported MCUs, peripheral and minimum kb-core version, and CI checks it against the build settings and the examples it builds. Verified by: driver-manifest (implemented): driver.yml exists, validates against its schema, and its version, MCUs and examples match the build settings and the examples folder See also: ADR-0007 ; ADR-0011 Explained in: standards/driver.md KB-REPO-019: Third-party code keeps its own licence under third_party/ ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. ADR-0011's root list does not yet include third_party/ . MUST · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Code copied in from elsewhere is MIT-compatible and sits in third_party/<name>/ with its original licence and notice. It is never mixed into the repository's own sources. Verified by: third-party-licences (planned): every third_party/<name>/ has a licence file, and REUSE or scancode finds only MIT-compatible licences See also: ADR-0009 ; IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 8.1 (SOUP identification) Explained in: standards/repo-governance.md KB-REPO-020: Hardware is CERN-OHL-P-2.0; a product owner picks the board HAL licence ¶ SHOULD · all · since 1.0 Hardware designs are licensed CERN-OHL-P-2.0. A board HAL in a product organisation carries the licence its product owner chooses in LICENSE. No licence grants use of the Kokeb Labs name or logos. Verified by: review: LICENSE, README badges and package manifests name the same licence. See also: ADR-0009 Explained in: standards/repo-governance.md KB-REPO-021: CODEOWNERS gives every path a default owner ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. org-standard-check confirms only that the file is not empty. SHOULD · all · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 .github/CODEOWNERS starts with a * line naming the maintainer ( @N3b3x , later @kokeb-labs/maintainers ), so every path has an owner. Verified by: codeowners (planned): .github/CODEOWNERS has a * rule naming at least one owner See also: ADR-0015 Explained in: standards/repo-governance.md KB-REPO-022: Vulnerabilities are reported privately, as SECURITY.md says ¶ MUST · all · since 1.0 SECURITY.md and CONTRIBUTING.md live in .github/ or are inherited from the organisation. A vulnerability is reported through a private security advisory, never a public issue. Verified by: security-policy (planned): SECURITY.md exists in .github/ or is inherited from the organisation and names private reporting review: A vulnerability reported in public was moved to a private advisory and the issue hidden. See also: ADR-0015 ; IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 9 (problem reports) Explained in: standards/repo-governance.md KB-REPO-023: Issues use the org forms and labels ¶ SHOULD · all · since 1.0 Issues are opened with the organisation's Bug, Driver request or Feature forms, blank issues are off and questions go to Discussions. Every repository uses the org label set (bug, enhancement, safety, breaking, …). Verified by: org-settings-drift (planned): a scheduled kokeb_org.py --check finds no drift between org/ and the repository's live settings review: The repository adds no issue templates or labels of its own outside org/labels.json. See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 9 (problem reports are classified) Explained in: standards/repo-governance.md KB-REPO-024: Repository settings are code in the .github repository ¶ MUST · all · since 1.0 Merge settings, rulesets, security features, labels, description, homepage and topics are declared in kokeb-labs/.github org/ , changed by pull request, and applied by an organisation owner with kokeb_org.py --apply . Verified by: rulesets (implemented): branch and tag rulesets as declared in .github/org/rulesets (PR only, linear history, tags kept) org-settings-drift (planned): a scheduled kokeb_org.py --check finds no drift between org/ and the repository's live settings review: The setting was changed in org/ by pull request, not in the GitHub UI. See also: ADR-0015 ; IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 8.2 (controlled changes to the environment) Explained in: standards/repo-governance.md KB-REPO-025: A new repository starts from its kind's template and is declared first ¶ SHOULD · all · since 1.0 A repository is added to org/repos.json by pull request, then created public from its kind's template (drivers and libraries through tools/setup.py ) and follows the kind's checklist. Verified by: review: The repository is in org/repos.json and was generated from its kind's template. Explained in: standards/repo-governance.md KB-REPO-026: A superseded repository is marked legacy and archived ¶ SHOULD · all · since 1.0 When a repository is replaced, it gets the legacy topic, a [Legacy] description and a README note naming its successor, and is then archived. Verified by: review: The archived repository's topic, description and README name its successor. Explained in: standards/repo-governance.md KB-REPO-027: CubeMX code is committed with the .ioc it came from ¶ SHOULD · hal, firmware · since 1.0 Generated STM32CubeMX code is committed together with its .ioc project, so a reviewer can regenerate it and diff. docs.text: Testing ¶ What every change proves before it merges. Host tests run on every pull request; the high and safety levels add sanitizers, coverage and cross-compilation. Rule Level Applies to Verified KB-TST-001 Host tests build and pass with gcc and clang must driver, library, hal, template checked KB-TST-002 API misuse is proved to be a compile error must driver, library, template checked KB-TST-003 Tests pass under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer must driver, library, hal, template (high level and above) checked KB-TST-004 Coverage floor per assurance level must driver, library, hal (high level and above) checked KB-TST-005 Compiles for every supported target must driver, library (high level and above) checked KB-TST-006 Host tests compile every header with the firmware's flags and no platform paths must driver, library, template checked KB-TST-007 Driver tests run against a register-level model of the chip must driver, template review KB-TST-008 Host tests cover the failure paths, not only the happy path must driver, library, hal, template planned KB-TST-009 Every driver ships a host example that CI builds and runs must driver, template checked KB-TST-010 Every code block on the documentation site is compiled must driver, library, template planned KB-TST-011 kb-core host tests run on every RTOS backend's host build must library planned KB-TST-012 Every handler has a host test of its contract must library planned KB-TST-013 A board HAL builds and is tested on the host must hal review KB-TST-014 Firmware logic that needs no hardware is host-tested should firmware review KB-TST-015 Tests are deterministic and independent of order must driver, library, hal, template planned KB-TST-016 Every test has a timeout must driver, library, hal, template planned KB-TST-017 Test files and cases name what they test should driver, library, hal, template planned KB-TST-018 Every public function is exercised by a test should driver, library, hal, template planned KB-TST-019 Share test setup through fixtures and helpers guide driver, library, hal, template none KB-TST-020 Frame, CRC and protocol parsers are fuzzed must driver, library (high level and above) planned KB-TST-021 Protocol and CRC code passes reference vectors should driver, library review KB-TST-023 Hardware test runs leave a structured record must driver, hal, firmware (high level and above) planned KB-TST-024 Real-time paths have a measured worst-case time and a regression check should driver, library, hal, firmware (high level and above) planned KB-TST-025 Concurrent code is tested under ThreadSanitizer must library, hal (high level and above) planned KB-TST-026 OTA updates are tested on both the update and the rollback path should firmware review KB-TST-027 At safety level, every decision has full MC/DC coverage must driver, library, hal (safety level and above) checked KB-TST-028 At safety level, every uncovered item is justified must driver, library, hal (safety level and above) planned KB-TST-029 At safety level, mutation testing checks that the tests check something guide driver, library, hal (safety level and above) none KB-TST-030 Hardware findings become model faults and tests; the model stands alone must driver, template planned KB-TST-001: Host tests build and pass with gcc and clang ¶ MUST · driver, library, hal, template · since 1.0 Every driver and library has unit tests that run on the host without hardware, against a mock port, and pass with both gcc and clang on every pull request. Verified by: host-tests (implemented): the unit tests build and pass on the host with gcc and clang See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 5.5.5 (software unit verification) KB-TST-002: API misuse is proved to be a compile error ¶ MUST · driver, library, template · since 1.0 Each constraint the public API enforces at compile time (a port missing a hook, a wrong hook signature) has a test that must fail to compile, and CI checks that it does. Verified by: compile-fail-tests (implemented): a misuse of the public API is a compile error, proved by a test that must fail to compile KB-TST-003: Tests pass under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer ¶ MUST · driver, library, hal, template (high level and above) · since 1.0 The host tests also run in a build with -fsanitize=address,undefined and pass with no report. Verified by: sanitizers (implemented): host tests pass under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer See also: SEI CERT C++ EXP53-CPP; SEI CERT C INT32-C KB-TST-004: Coverage floor per assurance level ¶ MUST · driver, library, hal (high level and above) · since 1.0 Coverage of library code by the host tests, measured with gcovr over a GCC -O0 --coverage build, stays at or above the floor of the repository's level: high, 85% of lines and 75% of branches; safety, 100% of reachable lines and branches. Tests, examples and compile-only targets are not counted. Why: A floor that is defined by tool, build and scope can be reproduced by anyone; ADR-0020 says why these numbers. Verified by: coverage-floor/level (implemented): gcovr coverage of library code by the host tests at or above the floor (coverage-floor/level for lines and branches, coverage-floor/mcdc for condition coverage), as ADR-0020 defines it See also: ADR-0020 ; IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 5.5.5; IEC 61508-3:2010 Table B.2 KB-TST-005: Compiles for every supported target ¶ MUST · driver, library (high level and above) · since 1.0 Drivers and libraries compile warning-free with arm-none-eabi-gcc (Cortex-M) and for ESP-IDF in CI, not only on the host. Verified by: cross-build/arm-none-eabi (implemented): the code compiles warning-free for the named target (arm-none-eabi Cortex-M cores, esp-idf, riscv32) cross-build/esp-idf (implemented): the code compiles warning-free for the named target (arm-none-eabi Cortex-M cores, esp-idf, riscv32) KB-TST-006: Host tests compile every header with the firmware's flags and no platform paths ¶ MUST · driver, library, template · since 1.0 The host test build compiles every public header with -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti -Wall -Wextra -Werror (the template adds -Wpedantic -Wshadow -Wconversion -Wsign-conversion and an -O2 build) and with no ESP-IDF, vendor or board include path on the search path. Why: A header that builds on the host with no platform in reach is proved MCU-agnostic. Verified by: host-tests (implemented): the unit tests build and pass on the host with gcc and clang compiler-warnings/-Wall (implemented): the build is warning-free with the named flag and -Werror compiler-warnings/-Wextra (implemented): the build is warning-free with the named flag and -Werror compiler-warnings/-Wconversion (implemented): the build is warning-free with the named flag and -Werror review: The test targets add no platform or vendor include directory. See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 5.5.5 KB-TST-007: Driver tests run against a register-level model of the chip ¶ MUST · driver, template · since 1.0 tests/mock_<chip>.hpp implements the driver's port as a model of the chip's registers and wire protocol, and every host test drives the driver through it. Drivers are not tested through virtual mocks of their own API. Why: A register model catches wrong addresses, orders and bit masks; a mock of the API catches none of them. Verified by: review: tests/mock_<chip>.hpp models registers behind the CRTP port and all driver tests use it. See also: ADR-0003 Explained in: standards/driver.md KB-TST-008: Host tests cover the failure paths, not only the happy path ¶ MUST · driver, library, hal, template · since 1.0 Host tests show that a call before EnsureInitialized() returns NotInitialized and sends nothing, a second EnsureInitialized() does no I/O, a failed start is retried, a wrong chip ID is refused, a failing bus hook is reported on every path that uses it, invalid arguments are rejected, and the expected register traffic is sent. New behaviour arrives with tests of its failure paths. Verified by: review: Every new error path, including a failing hook and a call before EnsureInitialized, has a test. error-paths-tested (planned): every error value the public API can return is asserted by at least one host test See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 5.5.4 (additional unit acceptance criteria: fault handling) Explained in: standards/driver.md KB-TST-009: Every driver ships a host example that CI builds and runs ¶ MUST · driver, template · since 1.0 examples/host/ runs the driver on the host against the register model. It is built with the test flags and run as one of the host tests. Verified by: host-tests (implemented): the unit tests build and pass on the host with gcc and clang See also: ADR-0011 Explained in: standards/driver.md KB-TST-010: Every code block on the documentation site is compiled ¶ MUST · driver, library, template · since 1.0 C++ shown on the documentation site is included from tests/docs/ , and the host test build compiles those files against the current headers. Verified by: doc-snippets (planned): every C++ block on the documentation site is a snippet from tests/docs/ and those files compile against the current headers (driver-template doc_snippets ctest and the kokeb-docs check) review: New code blocks on the site are snippets from tests/docs/, not inline code. Explained in: standards/docs.md KB-TST-011: kb-core host tests run on every RTOS backend's host build ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · library · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 kb-core's host tests live in tests/host/ and run with gcc and clang for KB_RTOS=FREERTOS (against the host shim) and KB_RTOS=NONE , with KB_MCU=HOST . Verified by: host-tests-matrix/kb-rtos (planned): the host tests pass with gcc and clang for each configuration of the named matrix (kb-rtos: KB_RTOS=FREERTOS host shim and KB_RTOS=NONE, with KB_MCU=HOST) See also: ADR-0013 ; IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 5.5.5 Explained in: standards/library.md KB-TST-012: Every handler has a host test of its contract ¶ MUST · library · since 1.0 Each handler has tests/host/test_<chip>_handler.cpp , run with KB_RTOS=NONE and KB_MCU=HOST , showing that construction does no I/O, retries happen as documented, a bus failure maps to Status::Bus , VisitDriver refuses when it should, and the diagnostics counters count. Verified by: test-presence/handler (planned): every unit of the named kind has a test (handler: tests/host/test_<chip>_handler.cpp; public-function: each public function is called by a host test) review: The handler test covers construction, retry, bus errors, VisitDriver and diagnostics. Explained in: standards/handler.md KB-TST-013: A board HAL builds and is tested on the host ¶ MUST · hal · since 1.0 A HAL builds on the host with its host bind, and its tests cover the start-up order, that each manager fails closed, and CollectDiagnostics . pincfg builds for the host with an empty pin table. Verified by: review: The HAL host tests cover start-up order, fail-closed managers and diagnostics. Explained in: standards/hal.md KB-TST-014: Firmware logic that needs no hardware is host-tested ¶ SHOULD · firmware · since 1.0 Application logic that does not touch hardware has host tests that run against the HAL's host bind. Verified by: review: New hardware-free application logic has host tests. Explained in: standards/product.md KB-TST-015: Tests are deterministic and independent of order ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, library, hal, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A test gives the same result on every run and in any order: no unseeded randomness, wall-clock dependence or state shared between tests. CI runs the suite repeatedly and in random order. Why: A flaky test teaches people to re-run CI instead of reading it. Verified by: test-repeat (planned): ctest --repeat until-fail:20 --schedule-random passes, so no test depends on luck or order KB-TST-016: Every test has a timeout ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, library, hal, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Every ctest test has a TIMEOUT property, so a hung test fails in bounded time instead of stalling CI. Verified by: ctest-timeouts (planned): every test ctest lists has a TIMEOUT property KB-TST-017: Test files and cases name what they test ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. SHOULD · driver, library, hal, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Host test files are named test_<unit>.cpp after the unit they exercise, and each test case name states the behaviour it checks. Verified by: test-naming (planned): host test sources are named test_<unit>.cpp after an existing unit of the library KB-TST-018: Every public function is exercised by a test ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. SHOULD · driver, library, hal, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Each function of the public API is called by at least one host test. Verified by: test-presence/public-function (planned): every unit of the named kind has a test (handler: tests/host/test_<chip>_handler.cpp; public-function: each public function is called by a host test) See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 5.5.5 KB-TST-019: Share test setup through fixtures and helpers ¶ GUIDE · driver, library, hal, template · since 1.0 Setup used by more than one test lives in a fixture or a helper in tests/ , not copied into each test. KB-TST-020: Frame, CRC and protocol parsers are fuzzed ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, library (high level and above) · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Every function that parses bytes from a bus or a host (frames, CRCs, protocol messages) has a libFuzzer target, built with the sanitizers, that CI runs for a fixed time on each pull request; its corpus is committed and every crash it found is kept as a regression test. Why: Parsers face input nobody wrote a test for; a fuzzer writes those tests. Verified by: fuzzing (planned): each parser's libFuzzer target runs on the host for a fixed time under ASan and UBSan without a finding See also: SEI CERT C INT32-C; SEI CERT C++ CTR50-CPP KB-TST-021: Protocol and CRC code passes reference vectors ¶ SHOULD · driver, library · since 1.0 An implementation of a published protocol or CRC is tested against the reference vectors of its specification or datasheet, with the source of each vector named in the test. Verified by: review: Protocol and CRC tests use vectors from the specification and cite it. KB-TST-022: Every MCU port passes the interface conformance tests ¶ Retired Duplicate of KB-HW-002, merged when the rules were loaded. Replaced by KB-HW-002. MUST · library, hal · since 1.0 kb::interfaces has a conformance suite per interface, and every mcu/<family>/ port runs it. A new interface method arrives with its conformance test. Verified by: conformance-tests (planned): every kb::interfaces method has a conformance test, and each mcu/<family> port runs and passes the suite review: A new interface method adds a conformance test. See also: ADR-0014 ; IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 5.6 (integration testing) KB-TST-023: Hardware test runs leave a structured record ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, hal, firmware (high level and above) · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Tests that need a board live in tests/hardware/ . Each run on a bench or a self-hosted runner writes a record of the commit SHA, board and revision, toolchain, test list, results and date, kept with the release; a change not run on hardware says so in its pull request. Verified by: hil-evidence (planned): a hardware test record (commit, board and revision, toolchain, tests, results, date) exists for the release and each supported board, in the evidence format See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 5.7 (software system testing records) Explained in: evidence.md KB-TST-024: Real-time paths have a measured worst-case time and a regression check ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. SHOULD · driver, library, hal, firmware (high level and above) · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 A function with a timing requirement documents its worst-case execution time measured on the target, and a benchmark job compares it with the stored baseline and fails on a regression beyond the recorded margin. Verified by: timing-budget (planned): an on-target benchmark job compares measured worst-case times with the stored baseline and fails beyond its margin KB-TST-025: Concurrent code is tested under ThreadSanitizer ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · library, hal (high level and above) · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Code that shares state between tasks (kb::rtos, thread-safe managers) has host stress tests with many concurrent callers that pass under -fsanitize=thread , with no failure attributed to contention. Verified by: tsan (planned): the concurrency host tests pass under ThreadSanitizer KB-TST-026: OTA updates are tested on both the update and the rollback path ¶ SHOULD · firmware · since 1.0 Before firmware with over-the-air update ships, a good update and a failed update that rolls back are both run on hardware and recorded in the release checklist. Verified by: review: The release checklist records an OTA update and an OTA rollback on hardware. KB-TST-027: At safety level, every decision has full MC/DC coverage ¶ MUST · driver, library, hal (safety level and above) · since 1.0 Library code reaches 100% modified condition/decision coverage, measured with GCC's -fcondition-coverage and gcovr; at the high level the figure is reported but not gated. Why: Branch coverage can pass while a condition inside a compound decision never decided anything; MC/DC shows each condition independently changes the outcome. Verified by: coverage-floor/mcdc (implemented): gcovr coverage of library code by the host tests at or above the floor (coverage-floor/level for lines and branches, coverage-floor/mcdc for condition coverage), as ADR-0020 defines it See also: ADR-0020 ; IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 5.5.4 (additional acceptance criteria for class C) KB-TST-028: At safety level, every uncovered item is justified ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. MUST · driver, library, hal (safety level and above) · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Each line, branch or condition the tests do not reach is listed in docs/coverage-justification.yml with the reason and who accepted it; an entry for an item the tests now reach is removed. Verified by: coverage-justification (planned): every uncovered line, branch or condition is in docs/coverage-justification.yml, and nothing else is See also: ADR-0020 Explained in: evidence.md KB-TST-029: At safety level, mutation testing checks that the tests check something ¶ GUIDE · driver, library, hal (safety level and above) · since 1.0 Each release of a safety component runs mutation testing (for example Mull) over library code and reviews the surviving mutants; each survivor gets a test or a note on why it is equivalent. Why: Coverage shows which code ran, not whether a test would notice it being wrong. See also: ADR-0020 KB-TST-030: Hardware findings become model faults and tests; the model stands alone ¶ Proposed Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. Extends KB-TST-007. MUST · driver, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01 Each behaviour found on hardware becomes a fault mode of tests/mock_<chip>.hpp and a regression test that fails on the code before the fix; the test cites the datasheet, and private evidence stays outside the repository. The model is written from the datasheet on its own: it does not include the driver's register header but carries its own register map with datasheet page references, and a test cross-checks the two maps with static_assert . A chip with timing (busy windows, settling, wake-up, pipeline latency) has a virtual clock in its model. Why: A model that includes the driver's register header shares its mistakes: a wrong constant hides behind the same wrong constant. Without a model fault, a fix found on the bench cannot be proven or kept. Verified by: model-virtual-clock (planned): a chip model for a driver whose port has DelayUs or DelayMs advances a virtual clock in those hooks, and a test runs a delayed-ready mode against it review: The pull request answers "hardware finding: model fault and test?"; tests/mock_<chip>.hpp includes no driver register header, and a test static_asserts the model's map against the driver's. Explained in: standards/driver.md
