docs.text: MUST · driver, library, hal, template · since 1.0 Every driver and library has unit tests that run on the host without hardware, against a mock port, and pass with both gcc and clang on every pull request. Verified by: host-tests (implemented): the unit tests build and pass on the host with gcc and clang See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 5.5.5 (software unit verification)
docs.title: KB-TST-001: Host tests build and pass with gcc and clang

docs.text: MUST · driver, library, template · since 1.0 Each constraint the public API enforces at compile time (a port missing a hook, a wrong hook signature) has a test that must fail to compile, and CI checks that it does. Verified by: compile-fail-tests (implemented): a misuse of the public API is a compile error, proved by a test that must fail to compile
docs.title: KB-TST-002: API misuse is proved to be a compile error

docs.text: MUST · driver, library, hal, template (high level and above) · since 1.0 The host tests also run in a build with -fsanitize=address,undefined and pass with no report. Verified by: sanitizers (implemented): host tests pass under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer See also: SEI CERT C++ EXP53-CPP; SEI CERT C INT32-C
docs.title: KB-TST-003: Tests pass under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer

docs.text: MUST · driver, library, hal (high level and above) · since 1.0 Coverage of library code by the host tests, measured with gcovr over a GCC -O0 --coverage build, stays at or above the floor of the repository's level: high, 85% of lines and 75% of branches; safety, 100% of reachable lines and branches. Tests, examples and compile-only targets are not counted. Why: A floor that is defined by tool, build and scope can be reproduced by anyone; ADR-0020 says why these numbers. Verified by: coverage-floor/level (implemented): gcovr coverage of library code by the host tests at or above the floor (coverage-floor/level for lines and branches, coverage-floor/mcdc for condition coverage), as ADR-0020 defines it See also: ADR-0020 ; IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 5.5.5; IEC 61508-3:2010 Table B.2
docs.title: KB-TST-004: Coverage floor per assurance level

docs.text: MUST · driver, library (high level and above) · since 1.0 Drivers and libraries compile warning-free with arm-none-eabi-gcc (Cortex-M) and for ESP-IDF in CI, not only on the host. Verified by: cross-build/arm-none-eabi (implemented): the code compiles warning-free for the named target (arm-none-eabi Cortex-M cores, esp-idf, riscv32) cross-build/esp-idf (implemented): the code compiles warning-free for the named target (arm-none-eabi Cortex-M cores, esp-idf, riscv32)
docs.title: KB-TST-005: Compiles for every supported target

docs.text: MUST · driver, library, template · since 1.0 The host test build compiles every public header with -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti -Wall -Wextra -Werror (the template adds -Wpedantic -Wshadow -Wconversion -Wsign-conversion and an -O2 build) and with no ESP-IDF, vendor or board include path on the search path. Why: A header that builds on the host with no platform in reach is proved MCU-agnostic. Verified by: host-tests (implemented): the unit tests build and pass on the host with gcc and clang compiler-warnings/-Wall (implemented): the build is warning-free with the named flag and -Werror compiler-warnings/-Wextra (implemented): the build is warning-free with the named flag and -Werror compiler-warnings/-Wconversion (implemented): the build is warning-free with the named flag and -Werror review: The test targets add no platform or vendor include directory. See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 5.5.5
docs.title: KB-TST-006: Host tests compile every header with the firmware's flags and no platform paths

docs.text: MUST · driver, template · since 1.0 tests/mock_<chip>.hpp implements the driver's port as a model of the chip's registers and wire protocol, and every host test drives the driver through it. Drivers are not tested through virtual mocks of their own API. Why: A register model catches wrong addresses, orders and bit masks; a mock of the API catches none of them. Verified by: review: tests/mock_<chip>.hpp models registers behind the CRTP port and all driver tests use it. See also: ADR-0003 Explained in: standards/driver.md
docs.title: KB-TST-007: Driver tests run against a register-level model of the chip

docs.text: MUST · driver, library, hal, template · since 1.0 Host tests show that a call before EnsureInitialized() returns NotInitialized and sends nothing, a second EnsureInitialized() does no I/O, a failed start is retried, a wrong chip ID is refused, a failing bus hook is reported on every path that uses it, invalid arguments are rejected, and the expected register traffic is sent. New behaviour arrives with tests of its failure paths. Verified by: review: Every new error path, including a failing hook and a call before EnsureInitialized, has a test. error-paths-tested (planned): every error value the public API can return is asserted by at least one host test See also: IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 5.5.4 (additional unit acceptance criteria: fault handling) Explained in: standards/driver.md
docs.title: KB-TST-008: Host tests cover the failure paths, not only the happy path

docs.text: MUST · driver, template · since 1.0 examples/host/ runs the driver on the host against the register model. It is built with the test flags and run as one of the host tests. Verified by: host-tests (implemented): the unit tests build and pass on the host with gcc and clang See also: ADR-0011 Explained in: standards/driver.md
docs.title: KB-TST-009: Every driver ships a host example that CI builds and runs

docs.text: Kokeb Labs engineering standard ¶ The rules every Kokeb Labs repository follows: how each layer is shaped, what it may depend on, how errors, threads and time work, how code is named and formatted, and how repositories are governed, documented and released. This directory is the single source of truth. Repository docs, templates, CI configuration and agents link here instead of restating it. When a repository and this standard disagree, the standard wins, and the repository gets an issue. The standard lives at https://github.com/kokeb-labs/.github/tree/main/standards . How to read it ¶ The key words MUST , MUST NOT , SHOULD , SHOULD NOT and MAY mean what RFC 2119 says they mean. A MUST is checked in review or CI. A SHOULD can be broken for a reason that the PR states. Each rule applies to new code at once. Existing code converges through the order of work in the decision records : a repository that does not meet a rule yet is tracked by an issue, not exempted. Contents ¶ Layer contracts ¶ Page Covers Layers The stack, what each layer promises and depends on, allowed and forbidden includes, the three kinds of "specific" Driver driver-<chip> : port, Result<T> , Error , lifecycle, config, memory, build, driver.yml , tests Library kb-core's utils , rtos and interfaces , how kb-core builds, and standalone libraries such as pincfg Handler kb-core/handlers/<chip> : one handler family, adapters, VisitDriver , diagnostics Board HAL Board HALs, the shared kb-hal-common and bsp_bind/<family> Product Product applications, which live in product organizations Cross-layer rules ¶ Page Covers Errors kb::Status , kb::Result<T> and the mapping at each layer boundary Threading and timing One lock, one clock, one delay; the 1 kHz FreeRTOS tick Naming and style Names, units, namespaces, include roots, and the org .clang-format and .clang-tidy Process ¶ Page Covers Repository governance Branches, PRs, DCO, labels, CODEOWNERS, rulesets, required checks, security, trademarks, new repositories Release SemVer 0.x, release candidates, release trains, prepare-release , changelog rules, bottom-up release order Documentation The page set, the Contract page, Doxygen settings, README sections Agents How coding agents work in Kokeb Labs repositories: AGENTS.md , skills, definition of done Records and checklists ¶ Page Covers Architecture decision records Why the rules are what they are, one decision per record New driver Copyable checklist for a new driver-<chip> New handler Copyable checklist for a new handler in kb-core New board HAL Copyable checklist for a new board HAL Release Copyable checklist for one repository's release Using the standard in a repository ¶ Link the standard from the repository's CONTRIBUTING.md (or rely on the org default) and from its AGENTS.md . Copy config/.clang-format and config/.clang-tidy into _config/ unchanged. A repository MUST NOT carry local edits to them; propose the change here. All other tool configuration lives in _config/ too, and the root follows ADR-0011 . When a PR deviates from a MUST, say so in the PR description, name the rule, and link the issue that tracks the fix. A reviewer can refuse the deviation. Start new repositories from the templates and the checklists; the checklists are the standard condensed into steps. Changing the standard ¶ The standard changes by pull request to kokeb-labs/.github , like code. A change that alters a decision gets a new ADR in adr/ (or supersedes an existing one) in the same PR. The PR updates every page the change touches, including the checklists and the configs. Once it merges, open issues in the repositories that no longer comply. Editorial fixes (wording, links, examples that do not change a rule) need no ADR. Fixed decisions ¶ These are not reopened without a superseding ADR: Decision Record Drivers keep their own <chip>::Error and Result<T> ; handlers map them to kb::Status / kb::Result<T> ADR-0001 One lifecycle: I/O-free constructor, Initialize() with a chip-ID check, EnsureInitialized() ADR-0002 Drivers are templates on a CRTP port; no virtual calls below the handler ADR-0003 No heap after start-up; none at all in drivers ADR-0004 A shared kb-hal-common repository for what board HALs have in common ADR-0005 FreeRTOS runs at 1 kHz everywhere ADR-0006 Drivers pinned in kb-core to release tags; tested sets released as trains ADR-0007 One naming scheme, enforced by clang-tidy ADR-0008 MIT for firmware and tooling; CERN-OHL-P-2.0 for hardware designs ADR-0009 C++20 in every repository ADR-0010 The root holds only required and first-read files; tool configuration in _config/ , no symlinks; one root CMakeLists.txt for CMake and ESP-IDF; platform code only in examples/<platform>/ ADR-0011 Drivers carry no brand: driver-<chip> , namespace <chip> , <chip>::<chip> ADR-0012 kb-core is one monorepo with four targets and one version ADR-0013 Chip-, MCU- and product-specific code each have one place; shared code never tests a platform macro ADR-0014 Governance for one maintainer open to contributors: squash, linear, signed, DCO ADR-0015

docs.text: Agents ¶ How coding agents work in Kokeb Labs repositories. Agents follow the whole standard like any contributor; this page adds what is specific to them. A human who asks an agent for a change is responsible for it as if they wrote it. Files every repository carries ¶ <repo>/ ├── AGENTS.md the agent entry point: what this repo is, how to build, test and check it ├── CLAUDE.md one line: @AGENTS.md └── .claude/ └── skills/ └── <name>/ └── SKILL.md one task an agent does often in this repo AGENTS.md ¶ AGENTS.md is the single source for agents; tools that read another file name get a pointer to it ( CLAUDE.md contains @AGENTS.md and nothing else). It is short, specific to the repository, and links this standard instead of restating it: # AGENTS.md <repo> is <one sentence>. It follows the Kokeb Labs engineering standard: https://github.com/kokeb-labs/.github/tree/main/standards (agents: standards/agents.md). ## Layout - `inc/` , `src/` : the driver. `tests/` : host tests and doc snippets. `docs/` : the site. ## Build and check (run all of these before pushing) cmake -S . -B build-host -D<CHIP>_BUILD_TESTS=ON cmake --build build-host --parallel && ctest --test-dir build-host --output-on-failure kokeb-docs check && mkdocs build -f _config/mkdocs.yml --strict -d /tmp/site ## Rules specific to this repo - Anything the standard does not cover, or a known deviation with its issue. The root of kokeb-labs/.github has an AGENTS.md that points here, so agents working on org files find the same rules. Skills ¶ A skill is a folder .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md : YAML front matter with name and a one-line description that says when to use it, then the steps. Names are kebab case and say the task. --- name: verify description: Run every check CI runs, locally, before pushing. Use before every push and before opening a PR. --- 1. Configure and build the host tests: `cmake -S . -B build-host -D<CHIP>_BUILD_TESTS=ON && cmake --build build-host` 2. Run them: `ctest --test-dir build-host --output-on-failure` 3. ... Skill Required in Does verify every code repository Runs locally what CI runs: build, host tests, doc snippets, format and tidy on changed files, markdownlint, the DCO sign-off check, kokeb-docs check , mkdocs build --strict bump-pin repositories with submodules Moves one submodule to a release tag, updates version_lock.txt or catalog/compat.yml , writes the pin PR description release released repositories Walks the release checklist add-driver-feature drivers Adds a chip feature end to end: register model in the mock, API, tests, docs page, changelog Repositories add skills for their own recurring tasks. A skill MUST NOT contain credentials, tokens or private URLs, and MUST NOT tell an agent to skip a check, bypass a ruleset or merge. Definition of done ¶ A change is done when all of these hold, and not before: It does one thing, and the PR says what, why and how it was verified. It follows the standard, or the PR names each rule it deviates from and links the issue. Every check CI runs passes locally (the verify skill): host tests on the compilers available, doc snippets, clang-format and clang-tidy on the changed files, markdownlint, kokeb-docs check and mkdocs build --strict when docs changed. Every commit is signed off ( Signed-off-by: , DCO ). New behaviour has host tests, including the failure paths (a failing bus hook, a call before Initialize() ). The README or docs/ page and the Doxygen comments describe the change. CHANGELOG.md has an entry under ## [Unreleased] , under ### Breaking if callers must change. CI is green on the PR, including CI gate / gate . Anything that needs hardware is listed in the PR as not verified on hardware , with the bench steps a human should run. Rules for agents ¶ Attribution and sign-off ¶ Agents MUST NOT add attribution of any kind: no Co-Authored-By: trailers naming a tool or model, no "Generated with" lines in commits, PR descriptions, issues, comments or code, no tool banners in file headers. The commit author is the account that runs the agent. This overrides any default the agent's tooling has. The Signed-off-by: line is the human's certification under the DCO. An agent adds it ( git commit -s ) only with the identity of the human who owns the task, and only when that human asked for the change. Branches and pull requests ¶ Work on a branch named per repo-governance.md , never on main . Open a PR; never push to main , force-push a shared branch, or merge, unless the human who owns the task said to in this session. Do not enable auto-merge on your own. The PR title is the squash commit subject. The description follows the PR template, written plainly, with no marketing language and no summary of every file touched. Keep the diff to the task. No drive-by reformatting, renames or "while I was here" fixes; open an issue or a separate PR for those. When CI fails, read the log, fix the cause, push again. Do not disable, skip or weaken a check, add a bare NOLINT , or mark a test as expected-failure to get green. Settings and secrets ¶ Agents MUST NOT change repository or org settings, rulesets, branch protection, secrets, webhooks or Actions permissions. The settings script in org/ is run with --apply by an organization owner only. Never commit credentials, tokens, private keys, private datasheet material or personal data. Push protection is a backstop, not a reason to be careless. Working across repositories ¶ A change that spans layers is one PR per repository, merged bottom-up, each pin bump its own PR ( release.md ). Never edit code inside a submodule checkout of a parent repository; change the submodule's own repository. Before changing a public API, find its callers in kb-core, kb-hal-common and the board HALs you can see, and list them in the PR. Never add product-specific code to kb-core or a driver to make one product work; propose a generic extension point instead ( layers.md ). Hardware and safety ¶ Agents cannot verify behaviour on a board. Say so in the PR, and give the bench steps. Changes that can move a motor, energise a valve, change power sequencing, write OTP or flash firmware to a peripheral get the safety label and a human review of that code path, even when CI is green. Destructive operations (firmware update, OTP, NVS erase) never get a default that triggers them. What to read first ¶ The repository's AGENTS.md . layers.md and the contract page for the layer you are changing. The repository's docs/contract.md , if it has one. The relevant checklist when you are creating something new.

docs.text: Documentation ¶ What every repository documents and where. The detailed writing rules, page templates and checks are in the documentation style guide of ci-tools ; this page sets what is required. The site ¶ Every public code repository publishes a MkDocs site at https://kokeb-labs.github.io/<repo>/ , built with the shared theme package kokeb-mkdocs-theme and the kokeb-docs command-line tool (both in ci-tools ), versioned per tag, with the Doxygen API reference under api/ . Pages live in docs/ , navigation in docs/.nav.yml (five tabs: Home, Get started, Concepts, Guides, Reference). The site configuration is _config/mkdocs.yml with docs_dir: ../docs ( ADR-0011 ); build with mkdocs build -f _config/mkdocs.yml --strict , and pass mkdocs_config: _config/mkdocs.yml and doxygen_config: _config/Doxyfile to the docs workflow. kokeb-docs check runs the same checks locally as the docs workflow. The build is strict: broken links, pages missing from the nav, figures or generated regions that no longer match the code, and snippets that do not compile all fail CI. Page sets ¶ Kind Required pages Driver Home, Quickstart (starting with the host example), Installation (CMake first, then ESP-IDF), Platforms, Hardware, Architecture, Contract , API guide, API reference, Examples, Porting (with Editor setup), Configuration (if it has a Config or Kconfig), Testing and CI, Troubleshooting, Changelog, Figures Standalone library Home, Quickstart (starting with the host example), Concepts, Contract , API guide (one page per utility for a collection), API reference, Integration, Platforms, Testing and CI, Changelog kb-core Home, Quickstart, Architecture (the four parts and their direction), Contract , one section per part (utils, rtos, interfaces, handlers), Handler model, one page per handler, Build options and MCU gate, Release trains and compatibility, Threading, Host build, API reference, Testing, Changelog kb-hal-common and board HALs Home with the board card, Quickstart, Hardware (block diagram, pin table, connectors, power), Architecture (managers, start-up order), Contract , one guide page per board function, API reference, Examples, Bring-up and troubleshooting, Changelog Product Home, Getting started, Architecture (tasks, data flow), Operation (modes, commands, configuration, the fault catalogue), Hardware (links the HAL site), Development, Troubleshooting, Changelog, ADRs CI and tools Home, Quickstart, one page per workflow or script, Versioning, Migration guides, Changelog What each page contains is in the style guide's standard page sets. The Contract page ¶ Every driver, library, kb-core, HAL and product has docs/contract.md , under Concepts right after Architecture. It is the short, normative summary of what the repository promises, in this order: # Contract What <repo> promises, what it needs, and the rules a caller follows. ## Promises - One bullet per guarantee a caller can rely on. ## Depends on | Dependency | Version | Why | | --- | --- | --- | ## Threading Which objects are thread-safe, which locks they take, what may run in an ISR. ## Errors The error type, every value a caller can see, and what it means. For a handler or HAL, the `kb::Status` mapping. ## Memory Allocation (none after start-up), static buffers and their sizes, stack needs of callbacks. ## Platform What is platform-free and what is not. MCU-bound drivers say so here and name the families and the peripheral. ## Deviations from the standard Each rule of the Kokeb Labs standard this repository does not meet yet, with its issue. The Contract page links the standard for the rules it inherits rather than restating them, and states only what is specific to the repository. Doxygen ¶ The API reference is generated from the public headers with the shared settings in ci-tools . Each repository keeps its Doxyfile in _config/Doxyfile and runs Doxygen from the root ( doxygen _config/Doxyfile ), so the paths inside are relative to the root: Setting Value Why INPUT inc/ (drivers), the public header folders (libraries, kb-core, HALs) Only the public API EXTRACT_ALL NO Undocumented symbols show up as warnings instead of empty entries EXTRACT_PRIVATE NO Private members are not API WARN_IF_UNDOCUMENTED YES WARN_NO_PARAMDOC YES Every parameter is documented, with its unit WARN_AS_ERROR FAIL_ON_WARNINGS CI fails on any warning in the public headers USE_MDFILE_AS_MAINPAGE docs/_doxygen/mainpage.md GENERATE_HTML YES , merged into the site under api/ Each public symbol has a brief description; each function documents its parameters with units, its return value and the error values it can return, and whether it does I/O or blocks. README ¶ The README is the front door: someone who reads only it knows what the part is, whether the driver fits their project, where the datasheet is, and how to get to a first reading. The reference stays on the site. Sections, in this order, only those that apply: # Name and a one-sentence hero line: what it is and does. Badges that are true: the main test workflow, license, C++ standard, latest release (once one exists). The documentation link in bold. One short paragraph in plain words: what the part does and what the driver gives you. One layer or block figure. At a glance : a two-column table: the part (vendor, package, supply), what it measures or does, the bus, what else it drives, the driver's properties, where it runs, and its status (version, and "not yet verified on hardware" until it is). Datasheet (drivers): the generated card ( <!-- generated: datasheet-card --> ): document, revision, where to get it, and the link to the Datasheet map. Try it on your PC : the host example in one command. Use it on your MCU : 1. a minimal wiring table, 2. one line on the port with a link to Porting, 3. the generated quickstart region ( <!-- generated: quickstart-code --> ), which checks every return value, and one line on how the driver starts ( EnsureInitialized() ). What it does : five to seven bullets. Install : the submodule line and the CMake lines. Documentation : a table of the pages with a "Read it when you want to" column. Links go to the pages in the repository ( docs/<page>.md ) while the site is not published, to /latest/ once it is. Tests and quality : one command line, and one sentence on what CI checks. License : one line (MIT, or CERN-OHL-P-2.0 for a hardware design). The datasheet trail ¶ A driver lists the vendor documents it was written against in docs/datasheets.yml ( ADR-0019 ), and, for each thing it takes from them, a topic : the datasheet's own section name and printed page, the driver API that implements it, and the docs pages that explain it. The datasheet generator (shipped in the template, tools/docs/generators/datasheet.py ) builds three regions from it, so a revision or a page number is written once: datasheet-card on the README, the home page and Hardware: document, revision, date, where to get it; datasheet-map on docs/datasheet.md : every topic with section, page, driver API and docs page; datasheet-refs at the top of each page a topic names: a collapsed box listing the sections that page relies on. Page numbers link into the PDF ( #page=N ) when the vendor publishes a stable PDF URL ( pdf , with page_offset when the printed and PDF page numbers differ). The repository never contains the PDF. A driver's README names the chip and the part, not the org: the driver is usable on its own ( ADR-0012 ). No table of contents, no emoji walls, no check-mark feature lists, no badges that link nowhere, no duplicated API tables. Code on the site ¶ Every C++ block on the site compiles: it lives in tests/docs/ and is pulled into the page as a generated region, so a change that breaks an example fails CI. Examples check every Result and Status . An example that ignores a return value teaches the wrong thing. Figures are generated ( kokeb-docs figures ) with light and dark variants and alt text. Changelog and decisions ¶ docs/changelog.md includes CHANGELOG.md ( release.md ). Decisions that affect more than one repository are ADRs here, in adr/ . Decisions local to one repository are ADRs in its own docs/adr/ , in the same format.

docs.text: Every public code repository publishes a MkDocs site at https://kokeb-labs.github.io/<repo>/ , built with the shared theme package kokeb-mkdocs-theme and the kokeb-docs command-line tool (both in ci-tools ), versioned per tag, with the Doxygen API reference under api/ . Pages live in docs/ , navigation in docs/.nav.yml (five tabs: Home, Get started, Concepts, Guides, Reference). The site configuration is _config/mkdocs.yml with docs_dir: ../docs ( ADR-0011 ); build with mkdocs build -f _config/mkdocs.yml --strict , and pass mkdocs_config: _config/mkdocs.yml and doxygen_config: _config/Doxyfile to the docs workflow. kokeb-docs check runs the same checks locally as the docs workflow. The build is strict: broken links, pages missing from the nav, figures or generated regions that no longer match the code, and snippets that do not compile all fail CI.
docs.title: The site

docs.text: Every driver, library, kb-core, HAL and product has docs/contract.md , under Concepts right after Architecture. It is the short, normative summary of what the repository promises, in this order: # Contract What <repo> promises, what it needs, and the rules a caller follows. ## Promises - One bullet per guarantee a caller can rely on. ## Depends on | Dependency | Version | Why | | --- | --- | --- | ## Threading Which objects are thread-safe, which locks they take, what may run in an ISR. ## Errors The error type, every value a caller can see, and what it means. For a handler or HAL, the `kb::Status` mapping. ## Memory Allocation (none after start-up), static buffers and their sizes, stack needs of callbacks. ## Platform What is platform-free and what is not. MCU-bound drivers say so here and name the families and the peripheral. ## Deviations from the standard Each rule of the Kokeb Labs standard this repository does not meet yet, with its issue. The Contract page links the standard for the rules it inherits rather than restating them, and states only what is specific to the repository.
docs.title: The Contract page

docs.text: The API reference is generated from the public headers with the shared settings in ci-tools . Each repository keeps its Doxyfile in _config/Doxyfile and runs Doxygen from the root ( doxygen _config/Doxyfile ), so the paths inside are relative to the root: Setting Value Why INPUT inc/ (drivers), the public header folders (libraries, kb-core, HALs) Only the public API EXTRACT_ALL NO Undocumented symbols show up as warnings instead of empty entries EXTRACT_PRIVATE NO Private members are not API WARN_IF_UNDOCUMENTED YES WARN_NO_PARAMDOC YES Every parameter is documented, with its unit WARN_AS_ERROR FAIL_ON_WARNINGS CI fails on any warning in the public headers USE_MDFILE_AS_MAINPAGE docs/_doxygen/mainpage.md GENERATE_HTML YES , merged into the site under api/ Each public symbol has a brief description; each function documents its parameters with units, its return value and the error values it can return, and whether it does I/O or blocks.
docs.title: Doxygen

docs.text: The README is the front door: someone who reads only it knows what the part is, whether the driver fits their project, where the datasheet is, and how to get to a first reading. The reference stays on the site. Sections, in this order, only those that apply: # Name and a one-sentence hero line: what it is and does. Badges that are true: the main test workflow, license, C++ standard, latest release (once one exists). The documentation link in bold. One short paragraph in plain words: what the part does and what the driver gives you. One layer or block figure. At a glance : a two-column table: the part (vendor, package, supply), what it measures or does, the bus, what else it drives, the driver's properties, where it runs, and its status (version, and "not yet verified on hardware" until it is). Datasheet (drivers): the generated card ( <!-- generated: datasheet-card --> ): document, revision, where to get it, and the link to the Datasheet map. Try it on your PC : the host example in one command. Use it on your MCU : 1. a minimal wiring table, 2. one line on the port with a link to Porting, 3. the generated quickstart region ( <!-- generated: quickstart-code --> ), which checks every return value, and one line on how the driver starts ( EnsureInitialized() ). What it does : five to seven bullets. Install : the submodule line and the CMake lines. Documentation : a table of the pages with a "Read it when you want to" column. Links go to the pages in the repository ( docs/<page>.md ) while the site is not published, to /latest/ once it is. Tests and quality : one command line, and one sentence on what CI checks. License : one line (MIT, or CERN-OHL-P-2.0 for a hardware design).
docs.title: README

docs.text: A driver lists the vendor documents it was written against in docs/datasheets.yml ( ADR-0019 ), and, for each thing it takes from them, a topic : the datasheet's own section name and printed page, the driver API that implements it, and the docs pages that explain it. The datasheet generator (shipped in the template, tools/docs/generators/datasheet.py ) builds three regions from it, so a revision or a page number is written once: datasheet-card on the README, the home page and Hardware: document, revision, date, where to get it; datasheet-map on docs/datasheet.md : every topic with section, page, driver API and docs page; datasheet-refs at the top of each page a topic names: a collapsed box listing the sections that page relies on. Page numbers link into the PDF ( #page=N ) when the vendor publishes a stable PDF URL ( pdf , with page_offset when the printed and PDF page numbers differ). The repository never contains the PDF. A driver's README names the chip and the part, not the org: the driver is usable on its own ( ADR-0012 ). No table of contents, no emoji walls, no check-mark feature lists, no badges that link nowhere, no duplicated API tables.
docs.title: The datasheet trail
