docs.text:
Driver contract ¶ What every driver- repository provides. A driver is an MCU-agnostic C++20 template on a CRTP port: the user writes the port for their MCU, and the driver works the same on ESP32, STM32, any other MCU or a host. ESP32 is the first example platform, not a dependency. A driver carries no brand ( ADR-0012 ): it is usable, and forkable, without anything else from Kokeb Labs. Examples below use a fictional ZP100 pressure sensor on I2C; replace zp100 / ZP100 with the chip. Repository layout ¶ driver-/ ├── inc/ │ ├── .hpp umbrella header: the only one users include │ ├── __interface.hpp the CRTP port base and its pin enums │ ├── _types.hpp Error, Result, Config, enums │ ├── _registers.hpp register map (optional) │ ├── _kconfig.hpp optional: maps CONFIG__* onto Config defaults │ └── _version.h.in version template, generated by CMake ├── src/.ipp template implementation, included at the end of .hpp ├── cmake/_build_settings.cmake version, target name, sources: the single source of truth ├── cmake/Config.cmake.in ├── examples/ │ ├── host/ runs on any PC: host port over the register model, built and run in CI │ └── / one self-contained folder per platform with its own port (esp32/: ESP-IDF) ├── tests/ host tests, doc snippets, install consumer ├── docs/ the driver page set (see docs.md) ├── _config/ all tool configuration: org .clang-format and .clang-tidy, Doxyfile, │ mkdocs.yml (docs_dir: ../docs), Kconfig, markdownlint, yamllint, lychee ├── .github/ workflows, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, CODEOWNERS, templates ├── .claude/ agent skills ├── CMakeLists.txt the CMake library, and under ESP_PLATFORM the ESP-IDF component ├── driver.yml driver metadata: bus, supported MCUs, minimum kb-core └── README.md, LICENSE (MIT), CHANGELOG.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .gitignore, .gitmodules The root holds only these entries ( ADR-0011 ): what GitHub or a tool needs at the root and what a reader looks for first. Tool configuration MUST live in _config/ , and every command and workflow names its path; the root MUST NOT hold copies of or symlinks to it. Names ¶ ( ADR-0012 ) Thing Name Example Repository driver- driver-pcal95555 Namespace pcal95555 Driver class :: pcal95555::PCAL95555 Umbrella header inc/.hpp inc/pcal95555.hpp CMake package and target find_package() , :: find_package(pcal95555) , pcal95555::pcal95555 Build settings cmake/_build_settings.cmake cmake/pcal95555_build_settings.cmake Macros and CMake options _* PCAL95555_VERSION_MAJOR , PCAL95555_BUILD_TESTS Kconfig CONFIG__* CONFIG_PCAL95555_I2C_ADDRESS A driver MUST NOT contain an org prefix: no kb_ , kb:: , KB_ or any other brand in a name, namespace, macro, target, file or option. A fork MUST NOT inherit one. Everything MUST be inside namespace (lower case, the part number: zp100 , tmc9660 ). Nothing is declared at global scope, including free GetDriverVersion() helpers and using declarations. The driver class MUST be :: with the part number in upper case: zp100::ZP100 . Not Device , Driver or a product name. A driver for a family names the class after the family member it was written for and lists the others in the README ( at25040::AT25040 also drives AT25010B and AT25020B). Naming inside the namespace follows naming-and-style.md . Platforms ¶ Driver code ( inc/ , src/ ) MUST NOT include an SDK, RTOS or vendor header. Platform code lives only in examples// : each folder carries its own port, an example program and a README, and builds on its own. Every driver MUST ship examples/host/ : a host port over the test register model and a program that initialises the driver and reads it, built with the test flags and run by the host tests. It is the quickstart's first step. A platform is added only with a CI job that builds its example. Plain CMake covers STM32, RP2040, nRF and the host; the root CMakeLists.txt covers ESP-IDF. Zephyr, Arduino or PlatformIO manifests are added only when a user needs them, never as a second copy of the sources. A driver that needs one MCU's peripheral is the documented case in MCU-bound drivers . The port ¶ The port is how the driver reaches the bus. The user derives a class from the driver's CRTP base and implements its hooks; the driver is a template on that class. // inc/zp100_i2c_interface.hpp namespace zp100 { enum class CtrlPin : uint8_t { Int = 0 }; // logical pins, not MCU pin numbers enum class GpioSignal : uint8_t { INACTIVE = 0 , ACTIVE = 1 }; template < typename Derived > class I2cInterface { public : I2cInterface ( const I2cInterface & ) = delete ; I2cInterface & operator = ( const I2cInterface & ) = delete ; protected : I2cInterface () = default ; ~ I2cInterface () = default ; }; /// Satisfied by a class that derives from I2cInterface

and implements the required hooks. template < typename P > concept I2cPort = std :: derived_from < P , I2cInterface < P >> && requires ( P & p , uint8_t addr , const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , size_t n ) { { p . EnsureInitialized () } -> std :: same_as < bool > ; { p . Write ( addr , tx , n ) } -> std :: same_as < bool > ; { p . WriteRead ( addr , tx , n , rx , n ) } -> std :: same_as < bool > ; }; } // namespace zp100 // The user's port, for their MCU class MyI2c : public zp100 :: I2cInterface < MyI2c > { public : bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept ; bool Write ( uint8_t addr , const uint8_t * data , size_t len ) noexcept ; bool WriteRead ( uint8_t addr , const uint8_t * tx , size_t tx_len , uint8_t * rx , size_t rx_len ) noexcept ; void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept ; // optional hook }; Rules: The base MUST be named ::{Spi,I2c,Uart,Adc}Interface and the concept ::{Spi,I2c,Uart,Adc}Port . A chip with two buses has one base per bus. There are no virtual functions. The driver template MUST be constrained by the concept ( template class ZP100 ), so a missing or misspelt hook is a compile error at the point of use. The base MUST NOT declare the required hooks itself. A forwarding hook in the base turns a missing override into infinite recursion at run time. The base MAY provide helpers built on hooks ( GpioSetActive(pin) ). Hooks MUST be PascalCase, noexcept , and return bool ( true = the transfer completed). A void hook hides bus errors and is not allowed. Hooks move raw bytes only. The driver MUST NOT configure the bus (speed, mode, pins); the port or the board does. Register addresses travel in the payload. EnsureInitialized() on the port brings the bus up on first use and is idempotent. Pins are logical: CtrlPin names the chip's function ( Reset , Int , Enable ) and GpioSignal::ACTIVE means "function asserted", whatever the electrical polarity. The port maps both to the board. Required hooks per bus ¶ Bus Hooks SPI bool Transfer(const uint8_t* tx, uint8_t* rx, size_t len) : one full-duplex transaction with chip select asserted for its whole length; tx or rx may be nullptr I2C bool Write(uint8_t addr, const uint8_t* data, size_t len) , bool WriteRead(uint8_t addr, const uint8_t* tx, size_t tx_len, uint8_t* rx, size_t rx_len) (repeated start); bool Read(uint8_t addr, uint8_t* data, size_t len) when the chip needs it UART bool Write(const uint8_t* data, size_t len) , bool Read(uint8_t* data, size_t len, uint32_t timeout_ms) (all len bytes or false ), bool FlushInput() ADC bool ReadVoltageMv(uint8_t channel, uint32_t& voltage_mv) All of them plus bool EnsureInitialized() . A chip with a protocol that does not fit (a multi-phase frame, a DMA stream) MAY add hooks; they follow the same rules and are listed on the Porting page. Bus requirements ¶ The bus interface header states what the chip needs from the bus as constexpr values, not only as prose ( KB-CPP-123 ). The Porting page lists them, and each example port checks its own settings against them with static_assert , so a port that clocks too fast or in the wrong mode does not compile. Bus Constant Meaning SPI kSpiMode The SPI mode (0 to 3) the chip samples in; a chip that accepts two names the one the driver is tested with SPI kMsbFirst true when each byte is sent most significant bit first SPI kMaxClockHz The highest SCK frequency the chip accepts SPI kMinCsHighNs The shortest time chip select stays high between frames SPI kCsSetupNs , kCsHoldNs Chip select low to the first SCK edge, last SCK edge to chip select high SPI kContinuousWord true when a frame must be clocked without idle time between its bytes I2C kI2cAddress The 7-bit address, or the base address when address pins add to it I2C kMaxClockHz The highest SCL frequency the chip accepts I2C kRepeatedStart true when a register read needs a combined write-read with a repeated START UART kMaxBaudRate , kTurnaroundUs The highest baud rate, and the time the line needs between the last byte sent and the reply // inc/zp100_spi_interface.hpp inline constexpr uint8_t kSpiMode = 0 ; // datasheet 6.2: CPOL 0, CPHA 0 inline constexpr bool kMsbFirst = true ; inline constexpr uint32_t kMaxClockHz = 10'000'000 ; inline constexpr uint32_t kMinCsHighNs = 50 ; inline constexpr uint32_t kCsSetupNs = 20 ; inline constexpr uint32_t kCsHoldNs = 20 ; inline constexpr bool kContinuousWord = false ; // examples/host/host_zp100_port.hpp static_assert ( kPortClockHz <= zp100 :: kMaxClockHz , "the port clocks the ZP100 too fast" ); A chip with a turnaround or an inter-frame gap adds a constant for it the same way. An I2C driver also documents which transfers the chip NACKs by design (a reset command, a busy chip) and never probes with a zero-length transfer ( KB-CPP-130 ). Control pins have a stated idle level. The Porting page lists each CtrlPin with its polarity and the level the port drives before the pin's output is enabled, and the port drives that inactive level before it enables the output and before the first frame ( KB-HW-018 ). Optional hooks ¶ Hook When missing void DelayUs(uint32_t us) , void DelayMs(uint32_t ms) Compile error at the first call that needs the wait. A driver whose chip has a timing requirement MUST NOT skip the wait. bool GpioSet(CtrlPin pin, GpioSignal signal) The function that needs the pin returns Error::Unsupported , or the driver uses the documented software alternative (for example a soft reset instead of the reset pin). bool GpioRead(CtrlPin pin, GpioSignal& signal) Same as GpioSet ; interrupt-driven reads fall back to polling a status register when the chip has one. void Log(LogLevel level, const char* message) No output. The message is a fixed string; the driver never formats text, and the hook is not variadic. Optional hooks MUST be detected with a C++20 requires expression in one place, never with void_t or by calling through the base: namespace zp100 :: detail { template < typename Port > void DelayUs ( Port & port , uint32_t us ) noexcept { if constexpr ( requires { port . DelayUs ( us ); }) { port . DelayUs ( us ); } else { static_assert ( sizeof ( Port ) == 0 , "zp100: the port must implement DelayUs(uint32_t)" ); } } } // namespace zp100::detail A missing hook therefore either falls back in a documented, safe way or fails to compile. It never silently skips a step. Errors and Result ¶ Each driver has its own error enum and result type, so it stays usable outside kb-core ( ADR-0001 ). Handlers map them to kb::Status ( errors.md ). namespace zp100 { enum class Error : uint8_t { // Base set: every driver declares these, with these values, in this order. Ok = 0 , NotInitialized = 1 , // an I/O call before EnsureInitialized() succeeded InvalidArgument = 2 , // a parameter outside the documented range; nothing was sent Bus = 3 , // a port hook returned false Timeout = 4 , // the chip did not become ready in time DeviceIdMismatch = 5 , // the ID register did not match the part Crc = 6 , // a frame failed its CRC or checksum Busy = 7 , // the chip refused the command because it is busy DeviceFault = 8 , // the chip reported a fault (status register, error frame) Unsupported = 9 , // the hook or feature this call needs is absent // Chip-specific values start at 16. FifoOverflow = 16 , }; [[ nodiscard ]] constexpr const char * ToString ( Error error ) noexcept ; template < typename T > struct [[ nodiscard ]] Result { T value {}; Error error { Error :: Ok }; [[ nodiscard ]] constexpr bool ok () const noexcept { return error == Error :: Ok ; } constexpr explicit operator bool () const noexcept { return ok (); } }; template <> struct [[ nodiscard ]] Result < void > { Error error { Error :: Ok }; [[ nodiscard ]] constexpr bool ok () const noexcept { return error == Error :: Ok ; } constexpr explicit operator bool () const noexcept { return ok (); } }; } // namespace zp100 Rules: Every public call that can fail MUST return Result (or Result ). No bool success flags, no out-parameter plus bool , no error code read back from a getter. The base set MUST be declared with the values above, so one mapping table serves every driver. A driver MAY never return some base values; its API guide says which. Each chip-specific value MUST be returned by at least one call. Unused values are deleted. Every port failure MUST propagate as Error::Bus (or Crc , Timeout when that is what happened). A getter that returns a stale or zero value after a failed read is a defect. T MUST be default-constructible and trivially copyable. A failed call leaves value default-initialised. Sticky chip status (fault latches, error counters) is extra: a getter MAY expose it, but it never replaces the Result of the call that hit the error. ToString() returns a static string for every value. NoDevice , Pin and NotReady , when a driver needs them, mean what errors.md says. Replies, retries and resynchronisation ¶ These rules come from testing the migrated drivers on hardware; each failure they prevent was seen on a bench. A reply is decoded only when the protocol proves it answers the request: CRC, plus the reply's type and width, plus the echoed opcode, address or tag the protocol has ( KB-ARCH-042 ). A reply a stuck, floating or looped-back line can produce (all zeros, all ones, the command echoed, one word repeated) is never data; it is NoDevice or another error, and an idle status a line could fake is confirmed by a second read ( KB-CPP-116 ). A chip that answers one or more frames later is served inside one public call, results matched on the reply's content, never its position; the Porting page states that nothing may access the chip between those frames ( KB-ARCH-043 ). After a failed transfer, or one with an unknown outcome, the next frame brings the chip's protocol back to a known point ( KB-CPP-118 ). A retry repeats only idempotent frames, never a reset, enable toggle or deinitialise the datasheet does not ask for, and every retry loop has a bound and counts its attempts ( KB-ARCH-044 ). State, shadows and latches ¶ A setter updates the driver's copy only after the chip accepted the change, and finishes a change the chip applies later before it returns ( KB-CPP-120 ). A setter changes only what it names; a change the chip accepts only in some state is refused outside it, and nothing is sent ( KB-CPP-121 ). Control and output registers are written whole from the copy; a read-modify-write uses only a validated read ( KB-CPP-122 ). Clear-on-read and write-1-to-clear flags collect in one latch the driver owns, from every read it makes, internal ones included: GetLatched*() returns it with no I/O and ClearLatched*() empties it ( KB-CPP-119 ). // Every STATUS read the driver makes, including the busy polls inside other calls: latched_status_ = static_cast < uint8_t > ( latched_status_ | ( byte & reg :: kStatusClearOnRead )); [[ nodiscard ]] Status GetLatchedStatus () const noexcept ; // no I/O void ClearLatchedStatus () noexcept ; // no I/O Start-up ¶ On top of the sequence under Lifecycle : The identity check is one the chip must answer actively (select-and-echo, a bit it must toggle, a write and a read-back), so a dead or looped bus cannot pass it ( KB-CPP-117 ). Start-up waits for the chip's own ready indication: the datasheet minimum, then a bounded poll with a deadline from Config ( KB-CPP-124 ). Nothing from before the host reset is trusted: the chip is reset or fully rewritten, and faults latched before the start are cleared or reported ( KB-CPP-058 ). The variant is confirmed before any variant-specific write ( KB-CPP-125 ). Load-dependent diagnostics are enabled only for channels Config declares as loaded, and fault routing is set from the same declaration before the chip is armed ( KB-CPP-131 ). Values and diagnostics ¶ Arguments and Config are checked against the datasheet's operating range and never silently clamped; a quantised setting reports what was programmed ( KB-CPP-126 ). A state that is not a measurement is an error, never a number; a multi-item read reports validity per item ( KB-CPP-127 ). A conversion that depends on another setting uses the chip's actual setting ( KB-CPP-128 ). Status bits are named by meaning, not raw polarity ( KB-CPP-038 ). Every driver has a single-shot raw access with no retries ( ReadRegister() or a frame trace) and a GetLast*() accessor for the last raw reply, with no I/O ( KB-CPP-129 ). Lifecycle ¶ ( ADR-0002 , ADR-0021 ) template < I2cPort Port > class ZP100 { public : explicit ZP100 ( Port & port , uint8_t address = kDefaultAddress , const Config & config = {}) noexcept ; // stores, no I/O Result < void > EnsureInitialized () noexcept ; // the one start: once, then Ok with no I/O [[ nodiscard ]] bool IsInitialized () const noexcept ; Result < void > Deinitialize () noexcept ; // chip to its safe low-power state Result < void > ApplyConfig ( const Config & config ) noexcept ; // write when running, store before Result < float > ReadPressurePa () noexcept ; Result < void > SetOversampling ( Oversampling osr ) noexcept ; }; The constructor MUST be noexcept , MUST NOT perform I/O and MUST NOT fail. It stores the port, any bus argument and the configuration (its last parameter, defaulted). EnsureInitialized() MUST be the only public way to start. Its first call MUST, in order: check the stored configuration with Validate() ( InvalidArgument , no I/O), call the port's EnsureInitialized() ( Bus on failure), reset the chip (hardware reset if the pin hook exists, else software reset), read and check the chip ID ( DeviceIdMismatch ), apply the configuration, and only then mark the driver initialised. On any failure the driver stays uninitialised and the next call starts again. Once initialised it returns Ok at once with no I/O. The sequence is a private member ( initialize() ); a driver has no public Initialize() . ApplyConfig(config) validates first; on a running driver it writes the configuration, before the start it only stores it for the first EnsureInitialized() , with no I/O. Deinitialize() puts the chip in its documented safe state (outputs off, low-power mode) and clears the initialised flag. Calling it on an uninitialised driver returns Ok . Every call that touches the bus MUST return NotInitialized , and send nothing, before EnsureInitialized() succeeded. No read or write resets or starts the chip as a side effect. Recovery after a fault is Deinitialize() then EnsureInitialized() . A chip without an ID register checks the closest equivalent (a reset value, a known status bit) and documents it. Destructive operations (firmware update, OTP write, factory reset) MUST take their data or confirmation explicitly. No default argument may trigger them. Config and Kconfig ¶ struct Config { Oversampling pressure_osr = Oversampling :: X8 ; // datasheet default unless the README says why not uint16_t odr_mhz = 50'000 ; // units as suffixes uint32_t ready_timeout_ms = 10 ; }; Run-time configuration MUST be one Config struct with unit-suffixed fields and defaults taken from the datasheet. The struct is passed to the constructor and changed with ApplyConfig() ; individual setters MAY exist for values that change at run time. What differs between products (which channels are used, which features are on, a profile table) is a field of Config (a mask, a std::span passed in), never a compile-time switch for one product ( layers.md ). Kconfig is an optional ESP-IDF layer, in _config/Kconfig (registered with KCONFIG by the root CMakeLists.txt ). If a driver ships a Kconfig , the CONFIG__* values MUST be read in exactly one header, inc/_kconfig.hpp , which produces a Config ( ::KconfigDefaults() ). Kconfig values MUST NOT appear in public signatures, constructors or other headers. A driver that reads CONFIG_* without shipping the Kconfig that defines it is a defect. ESP-IDF projects set values through sdkconfig.defaults ; a full sdkconfig is not committed. Verification is opt-in ¶ ( KB-ARCH-041 ) A call does what the datasheet needs and nothing more, so a control loop pays only for the transfer it asked for. enum class Verify : uint8_t { None , ReadBack }; Result < void > Write ( uint16_t address , std :: span < const uint8_t > data , Verify verify = Verify :: None ) noexcept ; A read-back after a write, a second read to compare, or any check the datasheet does not require is asked for per call , with a trailing Verify argument that defaults to Verify::None . One driver object then serves a control loop (no extra traffic) and a factory write ( Verify::ReadBack ) without reconfiguring. The doc comment says what ReadBack costs on that call (for example "one more I2C read per write") and what it catches. Not extra, so not optional: the start-up identity check in EnsureInitialized() , a busy poll the datasheet requires before a command, and verification steps in an irreversible procedure (an OTP or fuse burn). A host test shows that the default call sends no extra transfer, and another passes Verify::ReadBack and shows it catching the fault. Memory and threads ¶ ( ADR-0004 ) No heap ( new , malloc , std::vector , std::string ), no exceptions, no RTTI, no std::function , no printf -family calls, no static mutable state (including function-local statics and report buffers). Callbacks are a function pointer plus a void* context: using DataReadyFn = void (*)(void* ctx); . Buffers are members sized by constexpr limits, or caller-provided std::span . The driver is not thread-safe and MUST NOT lock. One driver object is used from one thread at a time; kb-core handlers own the locking. The driver MUST NOT call an RTOS. The driver MUST NOT sleep except through the port's delay hooks. Large chips ¶ A chip with many subsystems (a motor controller, an IMU with a sensor hub) MAY split its API into sub-object facades held by the driver ( driver.telemetry().ReadSupplyMv() ). Each facade follows this contract; they share the driver's port, lifecycle and Error . Build, export and versioning ¶ C++20 ( ADR-0010 ), target_compile_features(... cxx_std_20) . MIT ( ADR-0009 ). cmake/_build_settings.cmake MUST be the single source of the version ( _VERSION_MAJOR , _MINOR , _PATCH ), the target name and the source list. project() , the package version, the generated _version.h , PROJECT_NUMBER in _config/Doxyfile and the version in driver.yml all come from it or are checked against it, and a test checks that every copy agrees. The target MUST have EXPORT_NAME and a :: alias, so :: works after both add_subdirectory() and find_package() . Install rules MUST install every header the umbrella header includes, the .ipp , the generated version header and the package config. Options are _BUILD_TESTS (host tests and doc snippets, OFF by default) and _ENABLE_WARNINGS . The root CMakeLists.txt MUST also be the ESP-IDF component: under ESP_PLATFORM it calls idf_component_register() from the build settings, with KCONFIG ${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/_config/Kconfig , and returns before project() . This is build glue, not driver code: inc/ and src/ never test ESP_PLATFORM . ESP-IDF projects use the repository through EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS , a checkout under components/ , or a component-manager git dependency; there is no wrapper component and no idf_component.yml (added only if registry publishing is chosen). Every repository MUST use the shared CI, kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/.yml@v1 . The version is SemVer 0.x until the API is declared stable ( release.md ). Metadata: driver.yml ¶ Every driver carries driver.yml at the root. kb-core builds its compatibility file, catalog/compat.yml , from the driver.yml of each pinned driver ( release.md ); the file drives the CMake MCU gate, the kb command-line tool and the web configurator. name : zp100 version : 0.2.0 # checked against cmake/zp100_build_settings.cmake bus : [ i2c ] # spi, i2c, uart, adc, pio (a timed bit stream), or a protocol (canopen) mcus : [ any ] # any, or the families it needs: [esp32] peripheral : null # the MCU peripheral it needs, with mcus: RMT kb_core_min : 0.1.0 # the oldest kb-core whose handler and adapters work with this version mcus is [any] unless the driver needs one MCU's peripheral; then it names the families and peripheral names the peripheral, which becomes a row of the MCU gate table ( "WS2812:ESP32:RMT" ). kb_core_min is the only mention of kb-core in a driver, and it is metadata: the driver's code never depends on kb-core. CI checks the file against the build settings and the examples it builds. Tests ¶ tests/mock_.hpp : a register-level model of the chip implementing the port, used by every host test. It is written from the datasheet on its own: it does not include _registers.hpp , it carries its own register map with datasheet page references, and a test ( tests/test_model.cpp ) static_assert s the model's map against the driver's, so a wrong constant in the driver cannot hide behind the same constant in the model ( KB-TST-030 ). Every behaviour found on hardware becomes a fault mode of the model and a regression test, and a chip with timing has a virtual clock in its model. A host suite built on gcc and clang with -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti , run by the shared host-test workflow. It covers: every public call before EnsureInitialized() ( NotInitialized ), the chip-ID mismatch, a failing port hook on every call path ( Bus ), argument validation, and the register traffic of each feature. tests/docs/ : every code block on the documentation site compiles here ( regions). tests/install_consumer/ : installs the driver and builds a consumer with find_package() and :: . A version test: the CMake version, _config/Doxyfile , driver.yml and GetDriverVersion() agree. examples/host/ is built with the test flags and run by the host tests, and CI builds every examples// (the shared ESP32 example-build workflow for ESP32). Docs ¶ The driver page set in docs.md , plus: Doxygen with EXTRACT_ALL = NO and warnings as errors on inc/ : every public symbol is documented. The quickstart checks every return value. The Porting page shows a complete port for each bus, compiled in tests/docs/ . The API guide lists the Error values each call can return. Exceptions ¶ MCU-bound drivers ¶ A chip that only works with one MCU peripheral (WS2812 LEDs timed by the ESP32 RMT) still gets a platform-free driver: it builds frames, encodes pixels and checks arguments, and reaches the peripheral through its port. The MCU-specific part is not in the driver: In kb-core, the peripheral backend lives in interfaces/mcu// behind a Base* interface, and the driver is listed in the MCU gate table ( layers.md ). In the driver repository, the backend is the port in examples// . driver.yml names the families and the peripheral; the README and Contract page say the driver is MCU-bound. examples/host/ MAY be replaced by host tests over a mock of the peripheral. The driver keeps the repository shell, the root layout, the error model, the lifecycle and the naming. It MUST NOT include the vendor SDK in inc/ or src/ . Protocol clients ¶ A driver for a device reached over a protocol rather than a chip (a fictional motor-controller node over CANopen) skips the chip-specific rules: chip-ID check, register model, datasheet defaults and the register mock. It follows everything else: namespace, port, Result and Error , lifecycle, no heap, build, driver.yml , tests and docs. Its EnsureInitialized() checks the remote identity (device type, vendor ID) instead of a chip ID.
docs.title: Driver contract

docs.text: What every driver-<chip> repository provides. A driver is an MCU-agnostic C++20 template on a CRTP port: the user writes the port for their MCU, and the driver works the same on ESP32, STM32, any other MCU or a host. ESP32 is the first example platform, not a dependency. A driver carries no brand ( ADR-0012 ): it is usable, and forkable, without anything else from Kokeb Labs. Examples below use a fictional ZP100 pressure sensor on I2C; replace zp100 / ZP100 with the chip.
docs.title: Driver contract

docs.text: driver-<chip>/ ├── inc/ │ ├── <chip>.hpp umbrella header: the only one users include │ ├── <chip>_<bus>_interface.hpp the CRTP port base and its pin enums │ ├── <chip>_types.hpp Error, Result<T>, Config, enums │ ├── <chip>_registers.hpp register map (optional) │ ├── <chip>_kconfig.hpp optional: maps CONFIG_<CHIP>_* onto Config defaults │ └── <chip>_version.h.in version template, generated by CMake ├── src/<chip>.ipp template implementation, included at the end of <chip>.hpp ├── cmake/<chip>_build_settings.cmake version, target name, sources: the single source of truth ├── cmake/<chip>Config.cmake.in ├── examples/ │ ├── host/ runs on any PC: host port over the register model, built and run in CI │ └── <platform>/ one self-contained folder per platform with its own port (esp32/: ESP-IDF) ├── tests/ host tests, doc snippets, install consumer ├── docs/ the driver page set (see docs.md) ├── _config/ all tool configuration: org .clang-format and .clang-tidy, Doxyfile, │ mkdocs.yml (docs_dir: ../docs), Kconfig, markdownlint, yamllint, lychee ├── .github/ workflows, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, CODEOWNERS, templates ├── .claude/ agent skills ├── CMakeLists.txt the CMake library, and under ESP_PLATFORM the ESP-IDF component ├── driver.yml driver metadata: bus, supported MCUs, minimum kb-core └── README.md, LICENSE (MIT), CHANGELOG.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .gitignore, .gitmodules The root holds only these entries ( ADR-0011 ): what GitHub or a tool needs at the root and what a reader looks for first. Tool configuration MUST live in _config/ , and every command and workflow names its path; the root MUST NOT hold copies of or symlinks to it.
docs.title: Repository layout

docs.text: ( ADR-0012 ) Thing Name Example Repository driver-<chip> driver-pcal95555 Namespace <chip> pcal95555 Driver class <chip>::<CHIP> pcal95555::PCAL95555 Umbrella header inc/<chip>.hpp inc/pcal95555.hpp CMake package and target find_package(<chip>) , <chip>::<chip> find_package(pcal95555) , pcal95555::pcal95555 Build settings cmake/<chip>_build_settings.cmake cmake/pcal95555_build_settings.cmake Macros and CMake options <CHIP>_* PCAL95555_VERSION_MAJOR , PCAL95555_BUILD_TESTS Kconfig CONFIG_<CHIP>_* CONFIG_PCAL95555_I2C_ADDRESS A driver MUST NOT contain an org prefix: no kb_ , kb:: , KB_ or any other brand in a name, namespace, macro, target, file or option. A fork MUST NOT inherit one. Everything MUST be inside namespace <chip> (lower case, the part number: zp100 , tmc9660 ). Nothing is declared at global scope, including free GetDriverVersion() helpers and using declarations. The driver class MUST be <chip>::<CHIP> with the part number in upper case: zp100::ZP100 . Not Device , Driver or a product name. A driver for a family names the class after the family member it was written for and lists the others in the README ( at25040::AT25040 also drives AT25010B and AT25020B). Naming inside the namespace follows naming-and-style.md .
docs.title: Names

docs.text: Driver code ( inc/ , src/ ) MUST NOT include an SDK, RTOS or vendor header. Platform code lives only in examples/<platform>/ : each folder carries its own port, an example program and a README, and builds on its own. Every driver MUST ship examples/host/ : a host port over the test register model and a program that initialises the driver and reads it, built with the test flags and run by the host tests. It is the quickstart's first step. A platform is added only with a CI job that builds its example. Plain CMake covers STM32, RP2040, nRF and the host; the root CMakeLists.txt covers ESP-IDF. Zephyr, Arduino or PlatformIO manifests are added only when a user needs them, never as a second copy of the sources. A driver that needs one MCU's peripheral is the documented case in MCU-bound drivers .
docs.title: Platforms

docs.text:
The port is how the driver reaches the bus. The user derives a class from the driver's CRTP base and implements its hooks; the driver is a template on that class. // inc/zp100_i2c_interface.hpp namespace zp100 { enum class CtrlPin : uint8_t { Int = 0 }; // logical pins, not MCU pin numbers enum class GpioSignal : uint8_t { INACTIVE = 0 , ACTIVE = 1 }; template < typename Derived > class I2cInterface { public : I2cInterface ( const I2cInterface & ) = delete ; I2cInterface & operator = ( const I2cInterface & ) = delete ; protected : I2cInterface () = default ; ~ I2cInterface () = default ; }; /// Satisfied by a class that derives from I2cInterface

and implements the required hooks. template < typename P > concept I2cPort = std :: derived_from < P , I2cInterface < P >> && requires ( P & p , uint8_t addr , const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , size_t n ) { { p . EnsureInitialized () } -> std :: same_as < bool > ; { p . Write ( addr , tx , n ) } -> std :: same_as < bool > ; { p . WriteRead ( addr , tx , n , rx , n ) } -> std :: same_as < bool > ; }; } // namespace zp100 // The user's port, for their MCU class MyI2c : public zp100 :: I2cInterface < MyI2c > { public : bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept ; bool Write ( uint8_t addr , const uint8_t * data , size_t len ) noexcept ; bool WriteRead ( uint8_t addr , const uint8_t * tx , size_t tx_len , uint8_t * rx , size_t rx_len ) noexcept ; void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept ; // optional hook }; Rules: The base MUST be named ::{Spi,I2c,Uart,Adc}Interface and the concept ::{Spi,I2c,Uart,Adc}Port . A chip with two buses has one base per bus. There are no virtual functions. The driver template MUST be constrained by the concept ( template class ZP100 ), so a missing or misspelt hook is a compile error at the point of use. The base MUST NOT declare the required hooks itself. A forwarding hook in the base turns a missing override into infinite recursion at run time. The base MAY provide helpers built on hooks ( GpioSetActive(pin) ). Hooks MUST be PascalCase, noexcept , and return bool ( true = the transfer completed). A void hook hides bus errors and is not allowed. Hooks move raw bytes only. The driver MUST NOT configure the bus (speed, mode, pins); the port or the board does. Register addresses travel in the payload. EnsureInitialized() on the port brings the bus up on first use and is idempotent. Pins are logical: CtrlPin names the chip's function ( Reset , Int , Enable ) and GpioSignal::ACTIVE means "function asserted", whatever the electrical polarity. The port maps both to the board.
docs.title: The port

docs.text: Bus Hooks SPI bool Transfer(const uint8_t* tx, uint8_t* rx, size_t len) : one full-duplex transaction with chip select asserted for its whole length; tx or rx may be nullptr I2C bool Write(uint8_t addr, const uint8_t* data, size_t len) , bool WriteRead(uint8_t addr, const uint8_t* tx, size_t tx_len, uint8_t* rx, size_t rx_len) (repeated start); bool Read(uint8_t addr, uint8_t* data, size_t len) when the chip needs it UART bool Write(const uint8_t* data, size_t len) , bool Read(uint8_t* data, size_t len, uint32_t timeout_ms) (all len bytes or false ), bool FlushInput() ADC bool ReadVoltageMv(uint8_t channel, uint32_t& voltage_mv) All of them plus bool EnsureInitialized() . A chip with a protocol that does not fit (a multi-phase frame, a DMA stream) MAY add hooks; they follow the same rules and are listed on the Porting page.
docs.title: Required hooks per bus

docs.text: The bus interface header states what the chip needs from the bus as constexpr values, not only as prose ( KB-CPP-123 ). The Porting page lists them, and each example port checks its own settings against them with static_assert , so a port that clocks too fast or in the wrong mode does not compile. Bus Constant Meaning SPI kSpiMode The SPI mode (0 to 3) the chip samples in; a chip that accepts two names the one the driver is tested with SPI kMsbFirst true when each byte is sent most significant bit first SPI kMaxClockHz The highest SCK frequency the chip accepts SPI kMinCsHighNs The shortest time chip select stays high between frames SPI kCsSetupNs , kCsHoldNs Chip select low to the first SCK edge, last SCK edge to chip select high SPI kContinuousWord true when a frame must be clocked without idle time between its bytes I2C kI2cAddress The 7-bit address, or the base address when address pins add to it I2C kMaxClockHz The highest SCL frequency the chip accepts I2C kRepeatedStart true when a register read needs a combined write-read with a repeated START UART kMaxBaudRate , kTurnaroundUs The highest baud rate, and the time the line needs between the last byte sent and the reply // inc/zp100_spi_interface.hpp inline constexpr uint8_t kSpiMode = 0 ; // datasheet 6.2: CPOL 0, CPHA 0 inline constexpr bool kMsbFirst = true ; inline constexpr uint32_t kMaxClockHz = 10'000'000 ; inline constexpr uint32_t kMinCsHighNs = 50 ; inline constexpr uint32_t kCsSetupNs = 20 ; inline constexpr uint32_t kCsHoldNs = 20 ; inline constexpr bool kContinuousWord = false ; // examples/host/host_zp100_port.hpp static_assert ( kPortClockHz <= zp100 :: kMaxClockHz , "the port clocks the ZP100 too fast" ); A chip with a turnaround or an inter-frame gap adds a constant for it the same way. An I2C driver also documents which transfers the chip NACKs by design (a reset command, a busy chip) and never probes with a zero-length transfer ( KB-CPP-130 ). Control pins have a stated idle level. The Porting page lists each CtrlPin with its polarity and the level the port drives before the pin's output is enabled, and the port drives that inactive level before it enables the output and before the first frame ( KB-HW-018 ).
docs.title: Bus requirements

docs.text: Hook When missing void DelayUs(uint32_t us) , void DelayMs(uint32_t ms) Compile error at the first call that needs the wait. A driver whose chip has a timing requirement MUST NOT skip the wait. bool GpioSet(CtrlPin pin, GpioSignal signal) The function that needs the pin returns Error::Unsupported , or the driver uses the documented software alternative (for example a soft reset instead of the reset pin). bool GpioRead(CtrlPin pin, GpioSignal& signal) Same as GpioSet ; interrupt-driven reads fall back to polling a status register when the chip has one. void Log(LogLevel level, const char* message) No output. The message is a fixed string; the driver never formats text, and the hook is not variadic. Optional hooks MUST be detected with a C++20 requires expression in one place, never with void_t or by calling through the base: namespace zp100 :: detail { template < typename Port > void DelayUs ( Port & port , uint32_t us ) noexcept { if constexpr ( requires { port . DelayUs ( us ); }) { port . DelayUs ( us ); } else { static_assert ( sizeof ( Port ) == 0 , "zp100: the port must implement DelayUs(uint32_t)" ); } } } // namespace zp100::detail A missing hook therefore either falls back in a documented, safe way or fails to compile. It never silently skips a step.
docs.title: Optional hooks

docs.text: Each driver has its own error enum and result type, so it stays usable outside kb-core ( ADR-0001 ). Handlers map them to kb::Status ( errors.md ). namespace zp100 { enum class Error : uint8_t { // Base set: every driver declares these, with these values, in this order. Ok = 0 , NotInitialized = 1 , // an I/O call before EnsureInitialized() succeeded InvalidArgument = 2 , // a parameter outside the documented range; nothing was sent Bus = 3 , // a port hook returned false Timeout = 4 , // the chip did not become ready in time DeviceIdMismatch = 5 , // the ID register did not match the part Crc = 6 , // a frame failed its CRC or checksum Busy = 7 , // the chip refused the command because it is busy DeviceFault = 8 , // the chip reported a fault (status register, error frame) Unsupported = 9 , // the hook or feature this call needs is absent // Chip-specific values start at 16. FifoOverflow = 16 , }; [[ nodiscard ]] constexpr const char * ToString ( Error error ) noexcept ; template < typename T > struct [[ nodiscard ]] Result { T value {}; Error error { Error :: Ok }; [[ nodiscard ]] constexpr bool ok () const noexcept { return error == Error :: Ok ; } constexpr explicit operator bool () const noexcept { return ok (); } }; template <> struct [[ nodiscard ]] Result < void > { Error error { Error :: Ok }; [[ nodiscard ]] constexpr bool ok () const noexcept { return error == Error :: Ok ; } constexpr explicit operator bool () const noexcept { return ok (); } }; } // namespace zp100 Rules: Every public call that can fail MUST return Result<T> (or Result<void> ). No bool success flags, no out-parameter plus bool , no error code read back from a getter. The base set MUST be declared with the values above, so one mapping table serves every driver. A driver MAY never return some base values; its API guide says which. Each chip-specific value MUST be returned by at least one call. Unused values are deleted. Every port failure MUST propagate as Error::Bus (or Crc , Timeout when that is what happened). A getter that returns a stale or zero value after a failed read is a defect. T MUST be default-constructible and trivially copyable. A failed call leaves value default-initialised. Sticky chip status (fault latches, error counters) is extra: a getter MAY expose it, but it never replaces the Result of the call that hit the error. ToString() returns a static string for every value. NoDevice , Pin and NotReady , when a driver needs them, mean what errors.md says.
docs.title: Errors and Result<T>

docs.text: These rules come from testing the migrated drivers on hardware; each failure they prevent was seen on a bench. A reply is decoded only when the protocol proves it answers the request: CRC, plus the reply's type and width, plus the echoed opcode, address or tag the protocol has ( KB-ARCH-042 ). A reply a stuck, floating or looped-back line can produce (all zeros, all ones, the command echoed, one word repeated) is never data; it is NoDevice or another error, and an idle status a line could fake is confirmed by a second read ( KB-CPP-116 ). A chip that answers one or more frames later is served inside one public call, results matched on the reply's content, never its position; the Porting page states that nothing may access the chip between those frames ( KB-ARCH-043 ). After a failed transfer, or one with an unknown outcome, the next frame brings the chip's protocol back to a known point ( KB-CPP-118 ). A retry repeats only idempotent frames, never a reset, enable toggle or deinitialise the datasheet does not ask for, and every retry loop has a bound and counts its attempts ( KB-ARCH-044 ).
docs.title: Replies, retries and resynchronisation

docs.text: A setter updates the driver's copy only after the chip accepted the change, and finishes a change the chip applies later before it returns ( KB-CPP-120 ). A setter changes only what it names; a change the chip accepts only in some state is refused outside it, and nothing is sent ( KB-CPP-121 ). Control and output registers are written whole from the copy; a read-modify-write uses only a validated read ( KB-CPP-122 ). Clear-on-read and write-1-to-clear flags collect in one latch the driver owns, from every read it makes, internal ones included: GetLatched*() returns it with no I/O and ClearLatched*() empties it ( KB-CPP-119 ). // Every STATUS read the driver makes, including the busy polls inside other calls: latched_status_ = static_cast < uint8_t > ( latched_status_ | ( byte & reg :: kStatusClearOnRead )); [[ nodiscard ]] Status GetLatchedStatus () const noexcept ; // no I/O void ClearLatchedStatus () noexcept ; // no I/O
docs.title: State, shadows and latches

docs.text: On top of the sequence under Lifecycle : The identity check is one the chip must answer actively (select-and-echo, a bit it must toggle, a write and a read-back), so a dead or looped bus cannot pass it ( KB-CPP-117 ). Start-up waits for the chip's own ready indication: the datasheet minimum, then a bounded poll with a deadline from Config ( KB-CPP-124 ). Nothing from before the host reset is trusted: the chip is reset or fully rewritten, and faults latched before the start are cleared or reported ( KB-CPP-058 ). The variant is confirmed before any variant-specific write ( KB-CPP-125 ). Load-dependent diagnostics are enabled only for channels Config declares as loaded, and fault routing is set from the same declaration before the chip is armed ( KB-CPP-131 ).
docs.title: Start-up

docs.text: Arguments and Config are checked against the datasheet's operating range and never silently clamped; a quantised setting reports what was programmed ( KB-CPP-126 ). A state that is not a measurement is an error, never a number; a multi-item read reports validity per item ( KB-CPP-127 ). A conversion that depends on another setting uses the chip's actual setting ( KB-CPP-128 ). Status bits are named by meaning, not raw polarity ( KB-CPP-038 ). Every driver has a single-shot raw access with no retries ( ReadRegister() or a frame trace) and a GetLast*() accessor for the last raw reply, with no I/O ( KB-CPP-129 ).
docs.title: Values and diagnostics

docs.text: ( ADR-0002 , ADR-0021 ) template < I2cPort Port > class ZP100 { public : explicit ZP100 ( Port & port , uint8_t address = kDefaultAddress , const Config & config = {}) noexcept ; // stores, no I/O Result < void > EnsureInitialized () noexcept ; // the one start: once, then Ok with no I/O [[ nodiscard ]] bool IsInitialized () const noexcept ; Result < void > Deinitialize () noexcept ; // chip to its safe low-power state Result < void > ApplyConfig ( const Config & config ) noexcept ; // write when running, store before Result < float > ReadPressurePa () noexcept ; Result < void > SetOversampling ( Oversampling osr ) noexcept ; }; The constructor MUST be noexcept , MUST NOT perform I/O and MUST NOT fail. It stores the port, any bus argument and the configuration (its last parameter, defaulted). EnsureInitialized() MUST be the only public way to start. Its first call MUST, in order: check the stored configuration with Validate() ( InvalidArgument , no I/O), call the port's EnsureInitialized() ( Bus on failure), reset the chip (hardware reset if the pin hook exists, else software reset), read and check the chip ID ( DeviceIdMismatch ), apply the configuration, and only then mark the driver initialised. On any failure the driver stays uninitialised and the next call starts again. Once initialised it returns Ok at once with no I/O. The sequence is a private member ( initialize() ); a driver has no public Initialize() . ApplyConfig(config) validates first; on a running driver it writes the configuration, before the start it only stores it for the first EnsureInitialized() , with no I/O. Deinitialize() puts the chip in its documented safe state (outputs off, low-power mode) and clears the initialised flag. Calling it on an uninitialised driver returns Ok . Every call that touches the bus MUST return NotInitialized , and send nothing, before EnsureInitialized() succeeded. No read or write resets or starts the chip as a side effect. Recovery after a fault is Deinitialize() then EnsureInitialized() . A chip without an ID register checks the closest equivalent (a reset value, a known status bit) and documents it. Destructive operations (firmware update, OTP write, factory reset) MUST take their data or confirmation explicitly. No default argument may trigger them.
docs.title: Lifecycle

docs.text: struct Config { Oversampling pressure_osr = Oversampling :: X8 ; // datasheet default unless the README says why not uint16_t odr_mhz = 50'000 ; // units as suffixes uint32_t ready_timeout_ms = 10 ; }; Run-time configuration MUST be one Config struct with unit-suffixed fields and defaults taken from the datasheet. The struct is passed to the constructor and changed with ApplyConfig() ; individual setters MAY exist for values that change at run time. What differs between products (which channels are used, which features are on, a profile table) is a field of Config (a mask, a std::span passed in), never a compile-time switch for one product ( layers.md ). Kconfig is an optional ESP-IDF layer, in _config/Kconfig (registered with KCONFIG by the root CMakeLists.txt ). If a driver ships a Kconfig , the CONFIG_<CHIP>_* values MUST be read in exactly one header, inc/<chip>_kconfig.hpp , which produces a Config ( <chip>::KconfigDefaults() ). Kconfig values MUST NOT appear in public signatures, constructors or other headers. A driver that reads CONFIG_* without shipping the Kconfig that defines it is a defect. ESP-IDF projects set values through sdkconfig.defaults ; a full sdkconfig is not committed.
docs.title: Config and Kconfig

docs.text: ( KB-ARCH-041 ) A call does what the datasheet needs and nothing more, so a control loop pays only for the transfer it asked for. enum class Verify : uint8_t { None , ReadBack }; Result < void > Write ( uint16_t address , std :: span < const uint8_t > data , Verify verify = Verify :: None ) noexcept ; A read-back after a write, a second read to compare, or any check the datasheet does not require is asked for per call , with a trailing Verify argument that defaults to Verify::None . One driver object then serves a control loop (no extra traffic) and a factory write ( Verify::ReadBack ) without reconfiguring. The doc comment says what ReadBack costs on that call (for example "one more I2C read per write") and what it catches. Not extra, so not optional: the start-up identity check in EnsureInitialized() , a busy poll the datasheet requires before a command, and verification steps in an irreversible procedure (an OTP or fuse burn). A host test shows that the default call sends no extra transfer, and another passes Verify::ReadBack and shows it catching the fault.
docs.title: Verification is opt-in

docs.text: ( ADR-0004 ) No heap ( new , malloc , std::vector , std::string ), no exceptions, no RTTI, no std::function , no printf -family calls, no static mutable state (including function-local statics and report buffers). Callbacks are a function pointer plus a void* context: using DataReadyFn = void (*)(void* ctx); . Buffers are members sized by constexpr limits, or caller-provided std::span . The driver is not thread-safe and MUST NOT lock. One driver object is used from one thread at a time; kb-core handlers own the locking. The driver MUST NOT call an RTOS. The driver MUST NOT sleep except through the port's delay hooks.
docs.title: Memory and threads

docs.text: A chip with many subsystems (a motor controller, an IMU with a sensor hub) MAY split its API into sub-object facades held by the driver ( driver.telemetry().ReadSupplyMv() ). Each facade follows this contract; they share the driver's port, lifecycle and Error .
docs.title: Large chips

docs.text: C++20 ( ADR-0010 ), target_compile_features(... cxx_std_20) . MIT ( ADR-0009 ). cmake/<chip>_build_settings.cmake MUST be the single source of the version ( <CHIP>_VERSION_MAJOR , _MINOR , _PATCH ), the target name and the source list. project() , the package version, the generated <chip>_version.h , PROJECT_NUMBER in _config/Doxyfile and the version in driver.yml all come from it or are checked against it, and a test checks that every copy agrees. The target MUST have EXPORT_NAME <chip> and a <chip>::<chip> alias, so <chip>::<chip> works after both add_subdirectory() and find_package(<chip>) . Install rules MUST install every header the umbrella header includes, the .ipp , the generated version header and the package config. Options are <CHIP>_BUILD_TESTS (host tests and doc snippets, OFF by default) and <CHIP>_ENABLE_WARNINGS . The root CMakeLists.txt MUST also be the ESP-IDF component: under ESP_PLATFORM it calls idf_component_register() from the build settings, with KCONFIG ${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/_config/Kconfig , and returns before project() . This is build glue, not driver code: inc/ and src/ never test ESP_PLATFORM . ESP-IDF projects use the repository through EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS , a checkout under components/ , or a component-manager git dependency; there is no wrapper component and no idf_component.yml (added only if registry publishing is chosen). Every repository MUST use the shared CI, kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/<name>.yml@v1 . The version is SemVer 0.x until the API is declared stable ( release.md ).
docs.title: Build, export and versioning

docs.text: Every driver carries driver.yml at the root. kb-core builds its compatibility file, catalog/compat.yml , from the driver.yml of each pinned driver ( release.md ); the file drives the CMake MCU gate, the kb command-line tool and the web configurator. name : zp100 version : 0.2.0 # checked against cmake/zp100_build_settings.cmake bus : [ i2c ] # spi, i2c, uart, adc, pio (a timed bit stream), or a protocol (canopen) mcus : [ any ] # any, or the families it needs: [esp32] peripheral : null # the MCU peripheral it needs, with mcus: RMT kb_core_min : 0.1.0 # the oldest kb-core whose handler and adapters work with this version mcus is [any] unless the driver needs one MCU's peripheral; then it names the families and peripheral names the peripheral, which becomes a row of the MCU gate table ( "WS2812:ESP32:RMT" ). kb_core_min is the only mention of kb-core in a driver, and it is metadata: the driver's code never depends on kb-core. CI checks the file against the build settings and the examples it builds.
docs.title: Metadata: driver.yml

docs.text: tests/mock_<chip>.hpp : a register-level model of the chip implementing the port, used by every host test. It is written from the datasheet on its own: it does not include <chip>_registers.hpp , it carries its own register map with datasheet page references, and a test ( tests/test_model.cpp ) static_assert s the model's map against the driver's, so a wrong constant in the driver cannot hide behind the same constant in the model ( KB-TST-030 ). Every behaviour found on hardware becomes a fault mode of the model and a regression test, and a chip with timing has a virtual clock in its model. A host suite built on gcc and clang with -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti , run by the shared host-test workflow. It covers: every public call before EnsureInitialized() ( NotInitialized ), the chip-ID mismatch, a failing port hook on every call path ( Bus ), argument validation, and the register traffic of each feature. tests/docs/ : every code block on the documentation site compiles here ( <!-- generated: ... --> regions). tests/install_consumer/ : installs the driver and builds a consumer with find_package(<chip>) and <chip>::<chip> . A version test: the CMake version, _config/Doxyfile , driver.yml and GetDriverVersion() agree. examples/host/ is built with the test flags and run by the host tests, and CI builds every examples/<platform>/ (the shared ESP32 example-build workflow for ESP32).
docs.title: Tests

docs.text: The driver page set in docs.md , plus: Doxygen with EXTRACT_ALL = NO and warnings as errors on inc/ : every public symbol is documented. The quickstart checks every return value. The Porting page shows a complete port for each bus, compiled in tests/docs/ . The API guide lists the Error values each call can return.

Exceptions

docs.text: A chip that only works with one MCU peripheral (WS2812 LEDs timed by the ESP32 RMT) still gets a platform-free driver: it builds frames, encodes pixels and checks arguments, and reaches the peripheral through its port. The MCU-specific part is not in the driver: In kb-core, the peripheral backend lives in interfaces/mcu/<family>/ behind a Base* interface, and the driver is listed in the MCU gate table ( layers.md ). In the driver repository, the backend is the port in examples/<family>/ . driver.yml names the families and the peripheral; the README and Contract page say the driver is MCU-bound. examples/host/ MAY be replaced by host tests over a mock of the peripheral. The driver keeps the repository shell, the root layout, the error model, the lifecycle and the naming. It MUST NOT include the vendor SDK in inc/ or src/ .
docs.title: MCU-bound drivers

docs.text: A driver for a device reached over a protocol rather than a chip (a fictional motor-controller node over CANopen) skips the chip-specific rules: chip-ID check, register model, datasheet defaults and the register mock. It follows everything else: namespace, port, Result<T> and Error , lifecycle, no heap, build, driver.yml , tests and docs. Its EnsureInitialized() checks the remote identity (device type, vendor ID) instead of a chip ID.

docs.text: Errors ¶ One error model for the whole stack: drivers keep their own small Error enum, every layer above a driver speaks kb::Status , and the original code travels along as detail . Decision: ADR-0001 . kb::Status ¶ namespace kb { enum class Status : uint8_t { Ok = 0 , NotInitialized = 1 , // the object has not been (successfully) initialised InvalidArgument = 2 , // a parameter is out of range; nothing was done Busy = 3 , // the resource is in use; retrying later can succeed Timeout = 4 , // a wait expired Bus = 5 , // a transfer failed: NACK, CRC, framing, arbitration, transport error NotFound = 6 , // the device or resource is absent or answered with the wrong identity Fault = 7 , // the device reported a fault, or a check of its state failed Unsupported = 8 , // the operation is not available on this chip, board or build DependencyNotReady = 9 , // something this call needs (a bus, a manager, a handler) failed to start NoMemory = 10 , // a fixed-capacity pool or table is full Unknown = 11 , // anything that maps to none of the above }; [[ nodiscard ]] constexpr const char * ToString ( Status status ) noexcept ; template < typename T > struct [[ nodiscard ]] Result { T value {}; Status status { Status :: Ok }; uint16_t detail { 0 }; // the originating layer's own code (driver Error, kb_*_err_t, manager code); 0 if none [[ nodiscard ]] constexpr bool ok () const noexcept { return status == Status :: Ok ; } constexpr explicit operator bool () const noexcept { return ok (); } }; template <> struct [[ nodiscard ]] Result < void > { Status status { Status :: Ok }; uint16_t detail { 0 }; [[ nodiscard ]] constexpr bool ok () const noexcept { return status == Status :: Ok ; } constexpr explicit operator bool () const noexcept { return ok (); } }; } // namespace kb kb::Status and kb::Result<T> live in kb/utils/Status.h in kb-core's utils/general , a header with no dependencies, because utils is the lowest part of kb-core and every other part already depends on it. Drivers do not include it. Rules: New codes are added only by changing this page and the header together. Values are never renumbered. detail is diagnostic. Code MUST NOT branch on detail ; it branches on status . A Result that is ignored is a compiler warning ( [[nodiscard]] ), which CI turns into an error. ToString() returns a static string for every value. Which layer returns what ¶ Layer Returns Maps from Where the mapping lives Driver <chip>::Result<T> with <chip>::Error port hook bool results the driver interfaces Base* kb_<periph>_err_t (kept) the vendor SDK's codes each mcu/<family>/ class interfaces kb::Status ToStatus(kb_<periph>_err_t) noexcept , one per error type kb_<periph>_err_t next to the error list in base/Base<Periph>.h Handler kb::Result<T> <chip>::Error one ToStatus(<chip>::Error) per handler, in its adapter header Manager (HAL) kb::Status ; GetLastError() returns the last one handler kb::Result<T> the manager Facade (HAL) kb::Status plus the ManagerId that failed manager kb::Status FacadeBase Product its own fault catalogue (CANopen EMCY codes, fault IDs) kb::Status plus ManagerId one table in the product Each mapping happens once, at the boundary. A layer MUST NOT re-map a Status it received from below; it passes it up, possibly with its own detail . Driver Error to kb::Status ¶ The base set has fixed values ( driver.md ), so every handler starts from the same table: <chip>::Error kb::Status Ok Ok NotInitialized NotInitialized InvalidArgument InvalidArgument Bus Bus Timeout Timeout DeviceIdMismatch NotFound Crc Bus Busy Busy DeviceFault Fault Unsupported Unsupported chip-specific chosen per value by the handler, documented in the handler's page // handlers/zp100/HalI2cZp100Comm.h namespace kb { [[ nodiscard ]] constexpr Status ToStatus ( zp100 :: Error error ) noexcept { switch ( error ) { case zp100 :: Error :: Ok : return Status :: Ok ; case zp100 :: Error :: NotInitialized : return Status :: NotInitialized ; case zp100 :: Error :: InvalidArgument : return Status :: InvalidArgument ; case zp100 :: Error :: Bus : return Status :: Bus ; case zp100 :: Error :: Timeout : return Status :: Timeout ; case zp100 :: Error :: DeviceIdMismatch : return Status :: NotFound ; case zp100 :: Error :: Crc : return Status :: Bus ; case zp100 :: Error :: Busy : return Status :: Busy ; case zp100 :: Error :: DeviceFault : return Status :: Fault ; case zp100 :: Error :: Unsupported : return Status :: Unsupported ; case zp100 :: Error :: FifoOverflow : return Status :: Fault ; } return Status :: Unknown ; } template < typename T > [[ nodiscard ]] constexpr Result < T > ToResult ( const zp100 :: Result < T >& r ) noexcept { return { r . value , ToStatus ( r . error ), static_cast < uint16_t > ( r . error )}; } } // namespace kb The switch MUST list every enumerator and have no default: , so -Wswitch flags a new driver value that the handler does not map yet. Common chip-specific codes ¶ Chip-specific values are the driver's own, but three meanings come up in most drivers. When a driver needs one, it uses this name, so a reader and a handler know what it means without opening the driver ( KB-CPP-047 ): <chip>::Error Meaning Usual kb::Status NoDevice Nothing answers: the reply is one a stuck, floating or looped-back line produces ( KB-CPP-116 ) NotFound Pin A GpioSet or GpioRead hook failed Bus NotReady The chip answered but is not ready, or the value is not a measurement yet ( KB-CPP-124 , KB-CPP-127 ) Busy The base codes keep their meaning: Bus is a transfer the port reported as failed (a failed probe is Bus , not NoDevice ), Timeout a wait that expired, Crc a checksum or reply-tag mismatch, Busy a command the chip refused while busy. Interfaces codes to kb::Status ¶ The interfaces keep their per-peripheral codes (they carry more detail than a handler needs) and add one ToStatus() per type. The rules, applied by name: kb_*_err_t value names kb::Status *_SUCCESS Ok *_NOT_INITIALIZED NotInitialized *_INVALID_PARAMETER , *_NULL_POINTER , *_INVALID_CONFIGURATION , *_INVALID_* InvalidArgument *_BUSY , *_ALREADY_INITIALIZED when it means "in use" Busy *_TIMEOUT Timeout *_BUS_ERROR , *_TRANSFER_FAILED , *_COMMUNICATION_FAILURE , *_NACK , *_ARBITRATION_LOST , *_CRC* , *_CS_CONTROL_FAILED Bus *_DEVICE_NOT_FOUND , *_DEVICE_NOT_RESPONDING , *_NOT_AVAILABLE NotFound *_HARDWARE_FAULT , *_VOLTAGE_OUT_OF_RANGE , *_CLOCK_ERROR Fault *_UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION , *_NOT_SUPPORTED Unsupported *_OUT_OF_MEMORY NoMemory *_FAILURE , *_SYSTEM_ERROR , *_UNKNOWN , anything else Unknown ALREADY_INITIALIZED returned from an idempotent Initialize() is success, not an error; the Base* class handles that before mapping. Managers and the facade ¶ Every manager method that can fail returns kb::Status , and the manager records it: GetLastError() returns the last non- Ok status since ClearLastError() . A manager whose dependency (a handler, a bus from the bind) failed to start returns DependencyNotReady from every call, not the dependency's own status. The dependency's status is in its own diagnostics. The facade's start-up result is {kb::Status status; kb::hal::ManagerId manager;} : the first manager that failed and why. See hal.md . Products ¶ A product translates kb::Status plus ManagerId into its own fault catalogue in one table (for example to a CANopen EMCY code and a fault ID). Product code MUST NOT inspect detail , driver Error values or kb_*_err_t values. Fault catalogues are product-specific and never live in kb-core. What is not allowed ¶ Returning bool from a call that can fail for more than one reason. Logging an error and returning Ok . esp_err_t , HAL_StatusTypeDef or any vendor type above bsp_bind . A second error enum for a layer that already has one ( ManagerError , HalError , CommError ). Exceptions. Every repository builds with -fno-exceptions .

docs.text: Board HAL contract ¶ What a board HAL provides, what lives in the shared kb-hal-common , and the shape of the platform bind ( bsp_bind/<family> ). Decision: ADR-0005 . What lives where ¶ Repository / folder Where Contains Namespace kb-hal-common kokeb-labs ManagerBase , FacadeBase , ManagerId , the PlatformBind interface, the six common managers (NVS, LED, GPIO, ADC, temperature, comms), the diagnostics collector, the boundary lints and a board HAL example kb::hal A board HAL The product's organization or repository The board config (bus table, chip list), the board's pin table, the bind for its MCU family, the board-specific managers (for example motor, IMU or valves), the board facade, its examples <board> bsp_bind/<family>/ in the HAL The board HAL The code that creates the MCU family's Esp* / Stm* / Host* objects from the board config <board>::bsp Board HALs are product code: they live with the product, not in kokeb-labs . New board HALs start from kokeb-labs/board-hal-template once it exists, and from the example in kb-hal-common until then. A board HAL MUST NOT carry its own copy of anything in kb-hal-common . A manager that two boards need, written without anything product-specific, moves to kb-hal-common ; a manager only one board needs stays in that HAL. A board HAL consumes kb-hal-common ( lib/common ) and kb-core ( lib/core ) as submodules pinned to release tags. Managers ¶ namespace kb :: hal { enum class ManagerId : uint8_t { Nvs , Led , Gpio , Adc , Temperature , Comms , // common managers Board = 32 , // board-specific managers number from here }; class ManagerBase { public : virtual ~ ManagerBase () = default ; [[ nodiscard ]] virtual ManagerId Id () const noexcept = 0 ; [[ nodiscard ]] virtual const char * Name () const noexcept = 0 ; virtual kb :: Status Initialize () noexcept = 0 ; // idempotent virtual kb :: Status Deinitialize () noexcept = 0 ; // to the safe state [[ nodiscard ]] bool IsInitialized () const noexcept ; [[ nodiscard ]] kb :: Status GetLastError () const noexcept ; void ClearLastError () noexcept ; virtual void CollectDiagnostics ( DiagnosticsSink & sink ) const noexcept = 0 ; }; } // namespace kb::hal Rules: One manager per board function. A manager owns the handlers for its function and the Base* objects the bind created for them. Managers reach chips only through their handlers' typed API or VisitDriver() . A manager MUST NOT include a driver header or hold a driver pointer. Every fallible method returns kb::Status ( errors.md ). There is no ManagerError enum. Managers are created by the facade in static storage. No heap after start-up; allocation during Initialize() is allowed only for objects that live until reset, and the HAL's allocation lint lists them. Managers are thread-safe: each public method takes the manager's RtosMutex or delegates to a thread-safe handler. CollectDiagnostics() writes the manager's state and the DiagnosticsHeader of each handler it owns into the sink; it does not log. The common managers in kb-hal-common take everything board-specific as configuration (which channels, which LEDs, which NVS namespaces); they never name a board. Facade and start-up ¶ namespace kb :: hal { struct StartupResult { kb :: Status status = kb :: Status :: Ok ; ManagerId manager = ManagerId :: Nvs ; // the first manager that failed; meaningless when status is Ok }; class FacadeBase { public : StartupResult Initialize () noexcept ; // ordered, fail-closed void Deinitialize () noexcept ; // reverse order void CollectDiagnostics ( DiagnosticsSink & sink ) const noexcept ; protected : explicit FacadeBase ( std :: span < ManagerBase * const > start_order ) noexcept ; }; } // namespace kb::hal The board facade ( <board>::Hal ) derives from FacadeBase and passes its managers in start-up order. The order is fixed at compile time and documented on the HAL's Architecture page. Fail-closed : Initialize() starts managers in order and stops at the first failure. It then deinitialises the managers already started, in reverse, so every output is back in its safe state, and returns the failing manager and its status. A manager the board can run without is marked optional in the start order; its failure is recorded in the diagnostics and start-up continues. Safety-relevant managers (motor, valves, power) are never optional. The facade is the product's only entry point. It exposes the managers by reference and nothing below them. CollectDiagnostics() visits every manager. It is the one diagnostics call a product makes. The facade passes the kb-core logger its sink during start-up ( library.md ). The platform bind ¶ The bind turns the board config into Base* objects. It is the only code in a board HAL that names the MCU family. There is one interface, declared in kb-hal-common : namespace kb :: hal :: bind { // Peripherals, created and destroyed by slot. Specs carry raw pins resolved from the board's pin table. BaseGpio * CreateGpio ( size_t slot , const GpioSpec & spec ) noexcept ; void DestroyGpio ( size_t slot ) noexcept ; bool CreateSpiBus ( size_t bus , const SpiBusSpec & spec ) noexcept ; BaseSpi * CreateSpiDevice ( size_t bus , const SpiDeviceSpec & spec ) noexcept ; void DestroySpiBus ( size_t bus ) noexcept ; BaseI2c * CreateI2cDevice ( size_t bus , const I2cDeviceSpec & spec ) noexcept ; BaseUart * CreateUart ( const UartSpec & spec ) noexcept ; BaseCan * CreateCan ( const CanSpec & spec ) noexcept ; BaseAdc * CreateInternalAdc ( uint8_t unit , uint32_t channel_mask ) noexcept ; BaseTemperature * CreateDieTemperature () noexcept ; BaseNvs & NvsRegion ( size_t slot , const char * name_space ) noexcept ; // LED strip bool LedStripBegin ( const LedStripSpec & spec ) noexcept ; void LedStripSetPixel ( uint16_t index , uint32_t rgb ) noexcept ; bool LedStripShow () noexcept ; void LedStripEnd () noexcept ; // System uint64_t MonotonicMicros () noexcept ; uint32_t LastResetReason () noexcept ; [[ noreturn ]] void SystemRestart () noexcept ; uint32_t FreeHeapBytes () noexcept ; uint32_t LargestFreeHeapBlock () noexcept ; } // namespace kb::hal::bind Rules: Verbs are Create* / Destroy* (and Acquire* for singletons the SDK owns). Each Create* returns nullptr or false on failure and is idempotent per slot. Buses are slots ( bus , slot indices below kMax* constants), so a board with two SPI controllers and four devices each needs no new API. The bind stores every object it creates in static storage sized by the kMax* constants. It does not allocate after start-up. The bind creates the Esp* / Stm* / Host* objects that kb-core's interfaces/mcu/<family>/ provides. It does not reimplement a peripheral; a peripheral kb-core lacks is added to kb-core first. Every family the board runs on has a bind: esp32c6/ , esp32s3/ , stm32h7/ as boards need them, and host/ , which backs the host tests with fakes and a settable clock. The bind's interface header includes only Base* headers and standard headers, so the HAL above it compiles for every family. Board config ¶ One board/<board>/ folder holds the bus table, the chip list and the board's pin table, written with the generic pincfg framework ( library.md ). It contains data, not logic. Raw pin numbers appear only in the pin table and the bind; managers use functional pin names. Product choices that reach kb-core (channel masks, profile tables, limits) are declared here and passed in through configuration. Lints ¶ kb-hal-common ships the lints, run in every board HAL's CI: Lint Fails on Boundary an ESP-IDF, FreeRTOS, mcu/<family>/ or driver include outside bsp_bind/ Driver access GetDriver() , a driver pointer, or a driver call outside VisitDriver() Allocation new , malloc , make_unique , make_shared , std::vector growth outside the allowlisted start-up code Lock a raw RTOS lock, or a manager holding its lock across a call into another manager An exception goes in the lint's allowlist file in the HAL, with a comment naming the issue that removes it. Tests and docs ¶ The HAL builds on the host with the host/ bind, and tests/host/ covers start-up order, fail-closed behaviour (inject a failure into each manager in turn), and CollectDiagnostics() . Examples in examples/esp32/ (or the board's family) build in CI for the board's MCU. The HAL page set in docs.md , with the start-up order and the manager table on the Architecture page.
