docs.text: namespace kb :: hal { enum class ManagerId : uint8_t { Nvs , Led , Gpio , Adc , Temperature , Comms , // common managers Board = 32 , // board-specific managers number from here }; class ManagerBase { public : virtual ~ ManagerBase () = default ; [[ nodiscard ]] virtual ManagerId Id () const noexcept = 0 ; [[ nodiscard ]] virtual const char * Name () const noexcept = 0 ; virtual kb :: Status Initialize () noexcept = 0 ; // idempotent virtual kb :: Status Deinitialize () noexcept = 0 ; // to the safe state [[ nodiscard ]] bool IsInitialized () const noexcept ; [[ nodiscard ]] kb :: Status GetLastError () const noexcept ; void ClearLastError () noexcept ; virtual void CollectDiagnostics ( DiagnosticsSink & sink ) const noexcept = 0 ; }; } // namespace kb::hal Rules: One manager per board function. A manager owns the handlers for its function and the Base* objects the bind created for them. Managers reach chips only through their handlers' typed API or VisitDriver() . A manager MUST NOT include a driver header or hold a driver pointer. Every fallible method returns kb::Status ( errors.md ). There is no ManagerError enum. Managers are created by the facade in static storage. No heap after start-up; allocation during Initialize() is allowed only for objects that live until reset, and the HAL's allocation lint lists them. Managers are thread-safe: each public method takes the manager's RtosMutex or delegates to a thread-safe handler. CollectDiagnostics() writes the manager's state and the DiagnosticsHeader of each handler it owns into the sink; it does not log. The common managers in kb-hal-common take everything board-specific as configuration (which channels, which LEDs, which NVS namespaces); they never name a board.
docs.title: Managers

docs.text: namespace kb :: hal { struct StartupResult { kb :: Status status = kb :: Status :: Ok ; ManagerId manager = ManagerId :: Nvs ; // the first manager that failed; meaningless when status is Ok }; class FacadeBase { public : StartupResult Initialize () noexcept ; // ordered, fail-closed void Deinitialize () noexcept ; // reverse order void CollectDiagnostics ( DiagnosticsSink & sink ) const noexcept ; protected : explicit FacadeBase ( std :: span < ManagerBase * const > start_order ) noexcept ; }; } // namespace kb::hal The board facade ( <board>::Hal ) derives from FacadeBase and passes its managers in start-up order. The order is fixed at compile time and documented on the HAL's Architecture page. Fail-closed : Initialize() starts managers in order and stops at the first failure. It then deinitialises the managers already started, in reverse, so every output is back in its safe state, and returns the failing manager and its status. A manager the board can run without is marked optional in the start order; its failure is recorded in the diagnostics and start-up continues. Safety-relevant managers (motor, valves, power) are never optional. The facade is the product's only entry point. It exposes the managers by reference and nothing below them. CollectDiagnostics() visits every manager. It is the one diagnostics call a product makes. The facade passes the kb-core logger its sink during start-up ( library.md ).
docs.title: Facade and start-up

docs.text: The bind turns the board config into Base* objects. It is the only code in a board HAL that names the MCU family. There is one interface, declared in kb-hal-common : namespace kb :: hal :: bind { // Peripherals, created and destroyed by slot. Specs carry raw pins resolved from the board's pin table. BaseGpio * CreateGpio ( size_t slot , const GpioSpec & spec ) noexcept ; void DestroyGpio ( size_t slot ) noexcept ; bool CreateSpiBus ( size_t bus , const SpiBusSpec & spec ) noexcept ; BaseSpi * CreateSpiDevice ( size_t bus , const SpiDeviceSpec & spec ) noexcept ; void DestroySpiBus ( size_t bus ) noexcept ; BaseI2c * CreateI2cDevice ( size_t bus , const I2cDeviceSpec & spec ) noexcept ; BaseUart * CreateUart ( const UartSpec & spec ) noexcept ; BaseCan * CreateCan ( const CanSpec & spec ) noexcept ; BaseAdc * CreateInternalAdc ( uint8_t unit , uint32_t channel_mask ) noexcept ; BaseTemperature * CreateDieTemperature () noexcept ; BaseNvs & NvsRegion ( size_t slot , const char * name_space ) noexcept ; // LED strip bool LedStripBegin ( const LedStripSpec & spec ) noexcept ; void LedStripSetPixel ( uint16_t index , uint32_t rgb ) noexcept ; bool LedStripShow () noexcept ; void LedStripEnd () noexcept ; // System uint64_t MonotonicMicros () noexcept ; uint32_t LastResetReason () noexcept ; [[ noreturn ]] void SystemRestart () noexcept ; uint32_t FreeHeapBytes () noexcept ; uint32_t LargestFreeHeapBlock () noexcept ; } // namespace kb::hal::bind Rules: Verbs are Create* / Destroy* (and Acquire* for singletons the SDK owns). Each Create* returns nullptr or false on failure and is idempotent per slot. Buses are slots ( bus , slot indices below kMax* constants), so a board with two SPI controllers and four devices each needs no new API. The bind stores every object it creates in static storage sized by the kMax* constants. It does not allocate after start-up. The bind creates the Esp* / Stm* / Host* objects that kb-core's interfaces/mcu/<family>/ provides. It does not reimplement a peripheral; a peripheral kb-core lacks is added to kb-core first. Every family the board runs on has a bind: esp32c6/ , esp32s3/ , stm32h7/ as boards need them, and host/ , which backs the host tests with fakes and a settable clock. The bind's interface header includes only Base* headers and standard headers, so the HAL above it compiles for every family.
docs.title: The platform bind

docs.text: One board/<board>/ folder holds the bus table, the chip list and the board's pin table, written with the generic pincfg framework ( library.md ). It contains data, not logic. Raw pin numbers appear only in the pin table and the bind; managers use functional pin names. Product choices that reach kb-core (channel masks, profile tables, limits) are declared here and passed in through configuration.
docs.title: Board config

docs.text: kb-hal-common ships the lints, run in every board HAL's CI: Lint Fails on Boundary an ESP-IDF, FreeRTOS, mcu/<family>/ or driver include outside bsp_bind/ Driver access GetDriver() , a driver pointer, or a driver call outside VisitDriver() Allocation new , malloc , make_unique , make_shared , std::vector growth outside the allowlisted start-up code Lock a raw RTOS lock, or a manager holding its lock across a call into another manager An exception goes in the lint's allowlist file in the HAL, with a comment naming the issue that removes it.
docs.title: Lints

docs.text: The HAL builds on the host with the host/ bind, and tests/host/ covers start-up order, fail-closed behaviour (inject a failure into each manager in turn), and CollectDiagnostics() . Examples in examples/esp32/ (or the board's family) build in CI for the board's MCU. The HAL page set in docs.md , with the start-up order and the manager table on the Architecture page.

docs.text: Handler contract ¶ What every handler in kb-core/handlers/<chip>/ provides. A handler turns one platform-free driver into a thread-safe, kb::Status -speaking object that a board HAL can own. There is one handler family. Files and names ¶ kb-core/handlers/<chip>/ ├── <Chip>Handler.h / .cpp the handler: class kb::<Chip>Handler ├── Hal<Bus><Chip>Comm.h / .cpp the adapter: implements the driver's port with Base* calls, plus ToStatus() └── <Chip><Periph>Wrapper.h optional: presents part of the chip as a Base* (BaseAdc, BaseGpio, ...) Handlers live in namespace kb : kb::Zp100Handler , kb::Tmc9660Handler . Adapters are named Hal{Bus}{Chip}Comm : HalSpiTmc9660Comm , HalUartTmc9660Comm , HalI2cZp100Comm . Each handler compiles only when its switch is on: KB_ENABLE_<CHIP> (the single feature switch, library.md ). Its driver is a submodule in drivers/driver-<chip>/ , pinned to a release tag, and has an entry in catalog/compat.yml . Includes use one style: #include "kb/interfaces/BaseI2c.h" , #include "zp100.hpp" , #include "kb/rtos/RtosMutex.h" . Shape ¶ namespace kb { struct Zp100HandlerConfig { uint8_t address = 0x47 ; zp100 :: Config driver {}; }; struct Zp100Diagnostics { DiagnosticsHeader header ; // always first uint32_t fifo_overflows = 0 ; // chip-specific counters follow }; class Zp100Handler { public : Zp100Handler ( BaseI2c & i2c , const Zp100HandlerConfig & config = {}, RtosMutex * bus_mutex = nullptr ) noexcept ; // stores references; no I/O Zp100Handler ( const Zp100Handler & ) = delete ; Zp100Handler & operator = ( const Zp100Handler & ) = delete ; Result < void > EnsureInitialized () noexcept ; // builds the driver in place, runs its EnsureInitialized() Result < void > Deinitialize () noexcept ; [[ nodiscard ]] bool IsInitialized () const noexcept ; Result < float > ReadPressurePa () noexcept ; // the typed API: each call locks, maps, counts template < typename Fn > Status VisitDriver ( Fn && fn ) noexcept ; // fn(zp100::ZP100<HalI2cZp100Comm>&) -> Status [[ nodiscard ]] Zp100Diagnostics GetDiagnostics () const noexcept ; private : using Driver = zp100 :: ZP100 < HalI2cZp100Comm > ; HalI2cZp100Comm comm_ ; std :: optional < Driver > driver_ ; // in place: no heap Zp100HandlerConfig config_ ; mutable RtosMutex mutex_ ; RtosMutex * bus_mutex_ ; Zp100Diagnostics diag_ {}; }; } // namespace kb Rules ¶ Construction and lifecycle ¶ The constructor MUST NOT touch hardware, create the driver or allocate. It stores references to Base* interfaces that the HAL owns and that outlive the handler. Handlers are neither copyable nor movable. Driver storage is in place: std::optional<Driver> (or aligned storage) emplaced by EnsureInitialized() . make_unique , new and nothrow new are not allowed. EnsureInitialized() returns Result<void> . On first call it emplaces the driver over the adapter and runs the driver's EnsureInitialized() ; on failure it destroys the driver again, so the next call retries from scratch. It returns at once when already initialised. EnsureInitialized() is the handler's one start-up entry point ( ADR-0021 ). Reads and writes do not call it: every public method that needs the chip returns NotInitialized until the handler has been started, which the HAL does once, in its fixed start-up order. Deinitialize() runs the driver's Deinitialize() and destroys it. Locking ¶ Each handler has its own RtosMutex (from kb::rtos , threading-and-timing.md ). Every public method takes it with MutexLockGuard for its whole duration. Devices that share a bus MAY share a bus mutex passed to the constructor. The order is always handler mutex, then bus mutex, and both are released before the method returns. A handler MUST NOT call another handler while holding its locks. Driver access ¶ There is no public GetDriver() , raw driver pointer or reference. Code that needs a driver feature the typed API does not wrap uses VisitDriver() : uint32_t fifo_level = 0 ; kb :: Status s = zp100 . VisitDriver ([ & ]( auto & drv ) { auto r = drv . ReadFifoLevel (); fifo_level = r . value ; return kb :: ToStatus ( r . error ); }); VisitDriver() takes the handler lock (and the bus lock), returns NotInitialized without calling fn if the handler is not initialised, otherwise calls fn with the driver and returns its Status . fn MUST NOT store the reference. A feature used through VisitDriver() in more than one place SHOULD become a typed method. Errors ¶ Typed methods return kb::Result<T> . Driver errors are mapped once, by the ToStatus(<chip>::Error) in the adapter header ( errors.md ), with the driver code as detail . Handlers MUST NOT return driver result types, esp_err_t or bool from a call that can fail. The adapter ¶ The adapter derives from the driver's port base ( zp100::I2cInterface<HalI2cZp100Comm> ) and implements its hooks with BaseI2c / BaseSpi / BaseUart / BaseGpio calls. It translates kb_*_err_t failures into false , which the driver reports as Error::Bus . The delay hooks call kb::DelayUs() / kb::DelayMs() from handlers/common/ , which follow threading-and-timing.md ; the Log hook forwards to the kb-core logger. Shared adapter bases in handlers/common/ ( HalSpiCommBase , HalI2cCommBase , HalUartCommBase ) hold the bus reference, the CS / pin mapping and the delay and log hooks, so a new adapter only adds what is chip-specific. Diagnostics ¶ Every handler has GetDiagnostics() , returning a struct whose first member is the common header: namespace kb { struct DiagnosticsHeader { bool initialized = false ; uint32_t ok_count = 0 ; // calls that returned Ok uint32_t error_count = 0 ; // calls that returned anything else Status last_error = Status :: Ok ; uint16_t last_error_detail = 0 ; // the driver's Error value uint64_t last_error_us = 0 ; // kb::MonotonicUs() at the last error }; } // namespace kb The header is updated by the handler on every typed call and every VisitDriver() . Chip-specific counters and sticky chip status follow it. GetDiagnostics() takes the lock, copies, and returns. Wrappers ¶ A wrapper that presents part of a chip as a Base* ( Tmc9660AdcWrapper , a BaseGpio per expander pin) is owned by the handler in a fixed array, created by EnsureInitialized() , and forwards through the handler's locked API. It is not created with std::shared_ptr or on demand. Platform and product independence ¶ Handlers include only Base* headers, drivers, kb/rtos/ , kb/utils/ and kb/handlers/common/ ( layers.md ). They compile for every MCU family and on the host. A handler MUST NOT take gpio_num_t , return esp_err_t , or contain #ifdef blocks for one MCU or product. A chip that needs an MCU peripheral directly (WS2812 on the RMT) has a Base* interface for it, implemented in interfaces/mcu/<family>/ , and a row in the MCU gate table ( layers.md ). What a product chooses (channels in use, profiles, limits) comes in through the handler config or a table passed in, never through a product macro ( layers.md ). Tests ¶ Every handler has a host test in kb-core/tests/host/ that builds it over a fake Base* and the driver's mock: construction does no I/O, EnsureInitialized() retries after failure, every typed method maps a bus failure to Status::Bus , VisitDriver() refuses before init, and the diagnostics header counts. The test runs with KB_RTOS=NONE and KB_MCU=HOST .
docs.title: Handler contract

docs.text: Layers ¶ The Kokeb Labs stack, what each layer promises to the one above, what it may depend on, and which includes are allowed. The per-layer pages give the detail; this page is the contract between them. The stack ¶ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Product app product repository, product org namespace <board>::app│ │ uses the HAL facade and managers, kb::rtos, the kb-core logger │ ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Board HAL board HAL repository, product org namespace <board> │ │ board config, pin table, board managers, on kb-hal-common (kb::hal) │ │ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ Platform bind bsp_bind/<family> creates the MCU family's objects│ │ │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ kb-core handlers kb-core/handlers/<chip>, handlers/common namespace kb│ │ one handler per chip: lock, lifecycle, error mapping, VisitDriver │ ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ kb-core interfaces kb-core/interfaces: base/ (Base*), mcu/<family>/ │ ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ kb-core rtos kb-core/rtos: the only RTOS access │ ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ kb-core utils kb-core/utils/general, utils/canopen │ ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Chip drivers driver-<chip>, in kb-core/drivers/ as submodules │ │ platform-free C++20 templates on a CRTP port namespace <chip> │ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ Dependencies point down only. A layer MUST NOT include, link or call anything above it, and the submodule graph MUST stay acyclic: product → board HAL → kb-hal-common and kb-core → drivers. Inside kb-core the direction is fixed: utils ← rtos ← interfaces ← handlers . Each part MAY depend on the parts to its left and MUST NOT depend on the parts to its right. The four parts are separate CMake targets ( kb::utils , kb::rtos , kb::interfaces , kb::handlers ), so a wrong include fails to link ( library.md ). Drivers depend on nothing in kb-core, and kb-core's utils , rtos and interfaces do not depend on drivers. They meet in the handler, where an adapter implements a driver's port with Base* calls. What each layer promises and depends on ¶ Layer Promises to the layer above Depends on Page Chip driver The chip's full feature set as typed calls returning Result<T> ; no I/O before EnsureInitialized() ; no heap, no platform code The target library subset of the C++ standard library ( ADR-0017 ) and its own port driver.md utils Platform-free helpers, kb::Status , and CANopen frame builders The C++ standard library library.md rtos The only mutex, delay, thread, queue and timer types; the same API on FreeRTOS, ThreadX and none utils; the selected RTOS, only inside its backend folder library.md interfaces Base* peripheral classes with the same behaviour on every MCU family; ToStatus() for every error type; the monotonic clock utils, rtos; the vendor SDK, only inside mcu/<family>/ library.md Handler A thread-safe, typed API per chip returning kb::Result<T> ; VisitDriver() for the rest; diagnostics Drivers, Base* , rtos, utils handler.md Platform bind Base* objects for the board's buses and pins, created and destroyed by slot; reset reason, restart, heap figures, LED strip The MCU family's Esp* / Stm* / Host* classes and SDK hal.md Board HAL One facade with ordered, fail-closed start-up, one manager per board function, kb::Status everywhere, one CollectDiagnostics() kb-hal-common , handlers, Base* , rtos, pincfg , its bind hal.md Product The board's behaviour: tasks, protocols, faults The HAL facade and managers, rtos, the kb-core logger product.md Three kinds of "specific" ¶ Code is specific to a chip, to an MCU, or to a product. Each kind has one place, and the rules differ: Kind Example Where it lives Rule Chip-specific The register map and start-up sequence of a fictional ZP100 pressure sensor Its own driver ( driver-zp100 ) and its handler ( handlers/zp100/ ) Fine there. Nothing outside the driver and its handler knows the chip's registers. MCU-specific ESP-IDF I2C master calls, the STM32 HAL, the ESP32 RMT peripheral Only interfaces/mcu/<family>/ in kb-core (and, above core, a board HAL's bsp_bind/<family>/ and a product's platform/ ) The build selects one family and compiles only that folder. Each header there #error s in any other build. Product-specific A board's pin numbers, a product's fault codes, its motor limits, which channels it uses The product's board HAL or the product repository Never in kb-core or a driver. A product need becomes a generic extension point there. MCU-specific code ¶ KB_MCU=ESP32|STM32|HOST|NONE selects the family ( library.md ). Only interfaces/mcu/<family>/ for that family is compiled; the other family folders are not on the include path. Every header in interfaces/mcu/<family>/ stops a build for any other family: // interfaces/mcu/esp32/include/kb/interfaces/esp32/EspI2c.h #ifndef KB_ESP_I2C_H #define KB_ESP_I2C_H #if !defined(KB_MCU_ESP32) #error "EspI2c.h is ESP32 code; this build selects another KB_MCU" #endif // ... #endif // KB_ESP_I2C_H A driver that needs one MCU's peripheral (WS2812 timing on the ESP32 RMT) is listed in the MCU gate table in cmake/kb_build_settings.cmake . Enabling it for another MCU stops CMake at configure time instead of failing later at link time or on the bench: # <CHIP>:<MCU>:<peripheral>, generated from catalog/compat.yml (release.md) set ( KB_MCU_GATES "WS2812:ESP32:RMT" ) With KB_ENABLE_WS2812=ON and KB_MCU=STM32 , configure fails with a message naming the gate. - Differences between variants of one family (ESP32-C6 and ESP32-S3, two STM32 lines) use the vendor's capability macros ( SOC_*_SUPPORTED , the STM32 HAL_*_MODULE_ENABLED and peripheral defines) and only inside mcu/<family>/ . Product-specific code ¶ Product needs reach kb-core and drivers only as generic extension points: Instead of Use #ifdef MY_PRODUCT around a channel or a feature A config mask in the handler or driver Config ( channel_mask , features ) A hard-coded table of motor or sensor profiles A profile table the board HAL passes in ( std::span<const Profile> ) A product's own transport or storage in core A backend interface in interfaces/base/ that the board HAL implements A product's log format or sink in core An injected logger: the kb-core logger takes a sink from the HAL The test ¶ Shared code (drivers, kb-core outside interfaces/mcu/ , kb-hal-common ) MUST NOT test ESP_PLATFORM , STM32* , __ZEPHYR__ , a board or a product macro, or any similar platform switch. For any change to kb-core or a driver, ask: could a second, made-up product with a different board use it without editing core? If not, the change is product-specific and belongs in that product's board HAL or repository, or it needs a generic extension point first. Includes ¶ Paths below use the one-root-per-part layout from naming-and-style.md ( kb/interfaces/... , kb/rtos/... ). docs.text: The Kokeb Labs stack, what each layer promises to the one above, what it may depend on, and which includes are allowed. The per-layer pages give the detail; this page is the contract between them.

docs.text: ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Product app product repository, product org namespace <board>::app│ │ uses the HAL facade and managers, kb::rtos, the kb-core logger │ ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Board HAL board HAL repository, product org namespace <board> │ │ board config, pin table, board managers, on kb-hal-common (kb::hal) │ │ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ Platform bind bsp_bind/<family> creates the MCU family's objects│ │ │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ kb-core handlers kb-core/handlers/<chip>, handlers/common namespace kb│ │ one handler per chip: lock, lifecycle, error mapping, VisitDriver │ ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ kb-core interfaces kb-core/interfaces: base/ (Base*), mcu/<family>/ │ ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ kb-core rtos kb-core/rtos: the only RTOS access │ ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ kb-core utils kb-core/utils/general, utils/canopen │ ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Chip drivers driver-<chip>, in kb-core/drivers/ as submodules │ │ platform-free C++20 templates on a CRTP port namespace <chip> │ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ Dependencies point down only. A layer MUST NOT include, link or call anything above it, and the submodule graph MUST stay acyclic: product → board HAL → kb-hal-common and kb-core → drivers. Inside kb-core the direction is fixed: utils ← rtos ← interfaces ← handlers . Each part MAY depend on the parts to its left and MUST NOT depend on the parts to its right. The four parts are separate CMake targets ( kb::utils , kb::rtos , kb::interfaces , kb::handlers ), so a wrong include fails to link ( library.md ). Drivers depend on nothing in kb-core, and kb-core's utils , rtos and interfaces do not depend on drivers. They meet in the handler, where an adapter implements a driver's port with Base* calls.

docs.text: Code is specific to a chip, to an MCU, or to a product. Each kind has one place, and the rules differ: Kind Example Where it lives Rule Chip-specific The register map and start-up sequence of a fictional ZP100 pressure sensor Its own driver ( driver-zp100 ) and its handler ( handlers/zp100/ ) Fine there. Nothing outside the driver and its handler knows the chip's registers. MCU-specific ESP-IDF I2C master calls, the STM32 HAL, the ESP32 RMT peripheral Only interfaces/mcu/<family>/ in kb-core (and, above core, a board HAL's bsp_bind/<family>/ and a product's platform/ ) The build selects one family and compiles only that folder. Each header there #error s in any other build. Product-specific A board's pin numbers, a product's fault codes, its motor limits, which channels it uses The product's board HAL or the product repository Never in kb-core or a driver. A product need becomes a generic extension point there.
docs.title: Three kinds of "specific"

docs.text: KB_MCU=ESP32|STM32|HOST|NONE selects the family ( library.md ). Only interfaces/mcu/<family>/ for that family is compiled; the other family folders are not on the include path. Every header in interfaces/mcu/<family>/ stops a build for any other family: // interfaces/mcu/esp32/include/kb/interfaces/esp32/EspI2c.h #ifndef KB_ESP_I2C_H #define KB_ESP_I2C_H #if !defined(KB_MCU_ESP32) #error "EspI2c.h is ESP32 code; this build selects another KB_MCU" #endif // ... #endif // KB_ESP_I2C_H A driver that needs one MCU's peripheral (WS2812 timing on the ESP32 RMT) is listed in the MCU gate table in cmake/kb_build_settings.cmake . Enabling it for another MCU stops CMake at configure time instead of failing later at link time or on the bench: # <CHIP>:<MCU>:<peripheral>, generated from catalog/compat.yml (release.md) set ( KB_MCU_GATES "WS2812:ESP32:RMT" ) With KB_ENABLE_WS2812=ON and KB_MCU=STM32 , configure fails with a message naming the gate. - Differences between variants of one family (ESP32-C6 and ESP32-S3, two STM32 lines) use the vendor's capability macros ( SOC_*_SUPPORTED , the STM32 HAL_*_MODULE_ENABLED and peripheral defines) and only inside mcu/<family>/ .

docs.text: Library contract ¶ What the libraries between the drivers and the board HALs provide: the utils , rtos and interfaces parts of kb-core, how kb-core builds them with its handlers and drivers, and the rules for standalone libraries such as pincfg . Decision: ADR-0013 . kb-core layout ¶ kb-core/ ├── utils/ │ ├── general/ include/kb/utils/: Status.h, SoftwareVersion, ring buffers, ... │ └── canopen/ include/kb/canopen/: frame builders, CiA 402 helpers ├── rtos/ include/kb/rtos/; backends in freertos/, threadx/, none/ ├── interfaces/ │ ├── base/ include/kb/interfaces/: Base* classes, Time.h, error lists │ └── mcu/ │ ├── esp32/ include/kb/interfaces/esp32/: Esp* on ESP-IDF │ ├── stm32/ include/kb/interfaces/stm32/: Stm* on the STM32 HAL │ └── host/ include/kb/interfaces/host/: Host* for host builds and tests ├── handlers/ │ ├── common/ include/kb/handlers/common/: adapter bases, Delay.h, Logger.h, diagnostics │ └── <chip>/ one folder per handler (handler.md) ├── drivers/ │ └── driver-<chip>/ git submodules, each pinned to a driver release tag ├── catalog/compat.yml built from each driver's driver.yml (release.md) ├── cmake/kb_build_settings.cmake version, options, targets, MCU gate table ├── tests/, examples/, docs/, _config/, .github/, .claude/ └── CMakeLists.txt, README.md, LICENSE (MIT), CHANGELOG.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .gitignore, .gitmodules Every part of kb-core ¶ One CMake target per part , each with one include root: Part Target Include root Depends on utils/general , utils/canopen kb::utils kb/utils/ , kb/canopen/ The C++ standard library rtos/ kb::rtos kb/rtos/ kb::utils , the selected RTOS interfaces/ kb::interfaces kb/interfaces/ kb::rtos , kb::utils , the selected family's SDK handlers/ kb::handlers kb/handlers/ kb::interfaces , kb::rtos , kb::utils , each enabled driver's <chip>::<chip> Separately consumable : each target works after add_subdirectory() of kb-core and is also installable as its own package ( find_package(kb_utils) → kb::utils , and the same for kb_rtos , kb_interfaces , kb_handlers ). A project that needs only kb::utils gets nothing else. One version for all of kb-core, in cmake/kb_build_settings.cmake ; every package carries it. One include root per part : every public header is reached as #include "kb/<root>/<Header>.h" . Two parts MUST NOT ship headers that resolve to the same include path. No macros that leak : no MIN , MAX , ARRAY_SIZE or similar in public headers. Use std::min , std::size or a constexpr function in the library's namespace. Public macros carry the KB_ prefix. Namespace kb (or kb::<area> ). The C-style APIs kept from the code kb-core was built from ( os_* in rtos, the kb_*_t types in interfaces) keep their names; new API is C++ in kb . Host tests in tests/host/ on gcc and clang, and compiled doc snippets in tests/docs/ . A Contract page in the docs ( docs.md ), with a section per part. C++20, MIT, the org clang configs, no exceptions, no RTTI. Platform-free outside interfaces/mcu/ and the rtos backends ( layers.md ): no other file tests ESP_PLATFORM or an MCU macro. The mcu/ implementations and the RTOS backends are platform code by purpose; their portable parts ( base/ , the rtos API) still follow the rule. utils ¶ utils/general ¶ Platform-free helpers ( SoftwareVersion , VariableMonitor , TimestampedVariable , ring buffers and the like) and kb::Status / kb::Result<T> ( errors.md ). Headers and .cpp files; no RTOS, no vendor SDK, no global mutable state. A helper that needs a lock or a clock takes it as a parameter or template argument; it does not include kb/rtos/ . One guide page per helper: purpose, a compiled example, complexity and memory. utils/canopen ¶ CANopen frame builders and CiA 402 helpers over a self-contained CanFrame . No dependency on interfaces or a CAN driver; the caller sends the frame. No allocation; frames are values. rtos ¶ The only RTOS access above the bind ( threading-and-timing.md ). Provides Types Locking RtosMutex , MutexLockGuard , CriticalGuard Delay and time in ticks os_delay_msec() , OsUtility helpers Tasks BaseThread , BaseThreadsManager Communication OsQueue , OsEventFlags , SignalSemaphore , SeqlockSnapshot Timers PeriodicTimer Rules: One backend per build: KB_RTOS=FREERTOS|THREADX|NONE , which defines exactly one of KB_RTOS_FREERTOS , KB_RTOS_THREADX or KB_RTOS_NONE . Only the selected backend folder is compiled. The public API is the same on all three; the host tests run the FreeRTOS shim and none. Objects are statically allocated (FreeRTOS static API, ThreadX). No dependency other than kb::utils and the selected RTOS. interfaces ¶ The MCU interfaces: abstract Base* peripheral classes and their implementations per MCU family. Part Contains May include base/ BaseGpio , BaseAdc , BaseI2c , BaseSpi , BaseUart , BaseCan , BasePwm , BaseNvs , BasePeriodicTimer , BaseTemperature , BaseLogger , BasePio , BaseUsbSerialJtag , BaseWifi , BaseBluetooth ; HardwareTypes.h ; Time.h ( kb::MonotonicUs() , declared only) Standard headers, kb/utils/ , kb/rtos/ mcu/esp32/ Esp* implementations on ESP-IDF, and the ESP32 definition of kb::MonotonicUs() ESP-IDF mcu/stm32/ Stm* implementations on the STM32 HAL, and the STM32 definition of kb::MonotonicUs() STM32Cube HAL mcu/host/ Host* implementations for host builds and tests ( HostNvs , a settable clock) Standard headers A header in base/ declares; the selected family's mcu/<family>/ folder defines. The family is chosen by the build, which compiles only that folder, so no header in base/ tests a family macro. Rules: Base* classes are the MCU boundary, one of the three places with virtual functions ( ADR-0016 ): the bind creates the concrete object, and everything above holds a Base*& . The other two are kb-hal-common's managers and kb-core's thread bases. Each Base* keeps its kb_<periph>_err_t X-macro list and adds kb::Status ToStatus(kb_<periph>_err_t) following errors.md . Initialize() is idempotent and EnsureInitialized() lazy; neither allocates after start-up. Exactly one family is compiled, chosen by KB_MCU=ESP32|STM32|HOST|NONE . NONE builds base/ only, for consumers that bring their own implementation or fakes. Every family's sources MUST compile in CI, including STM32 (with stub SDK headers if needed). Every header in mcu/<family>/ #error s when its family is not the one selected ( layers.md ). A header in base/ MUST NOT include a file that does not exist on every family. Variant differences inside a family use the vendor's capability macros, only in that family's folder. A peripheral that only one family has (the ESP32 RMT) gets a Base* interface in base/ and an implementation in that family's folder only; the drivers that need it are rows in the MCU gate table. handlers ¶ One handler per chip, plus handlers/common/ : the adapter bases, kb::DelayUs() / kb::DelayMs() , the diagnostics header and the logger. The contract is in handler.md . The logger ( kb/handlers/common/Logger.h ) is the one logging API above the bind. It formats; drivers do not. Its sink is injected by the board HAL, so kb-core prints nothing on its own and carries no product's log format. kb-core build ¶ kb-core links each enabled driver's <chip>::<chip> target from its submodule in drivers/driver-<chip>/ . It does not copy file lists out of a driver. cmake/kb_build_settings.cmake holds the version, the options, the targets and the MCU gate table; it holds no sources of a driver. The options: Option Values Effect KB_MCU ESP32 , STM32 , HOST , NONE Compiles interfaces/mcu/<family>/ for that family only KB_RTOS FREERTOS , THREADX , NONE Compiles that rtos backend only KB_ENABLE_<CHIP> ON , OFF Compiles the handler and links its driver; nothing else turns a handler on KB_ENABLE_<FEATURE> ON , OFF Compiles an optional part ( KB_ENABLE_CANOPEN ) KB_BUILD_TESTS ON , OFF Host tests and doc snippets The MCU gate : configure fails when an enabled chip's row in the gate table names another MCU than KB_MCU ( layers.md ). The table is generated from catalog/compat.yml , and CI checks the two agree. Under ESP-IDF the root CMakeLists.txt is also the component; Kconfig options are CONFIG_KB_* and map onto the CMake options in one place. FreeRTOS builds run at 1000 Hz ( threading-and-timing.md ). Standalone libraries ¶ A library that is not part of kb-core (for example pincfg , or a utility used outside the stack) lives in its own repository, is created from kokeb-labs/driver-template ( python3 tools/setup.py --kind library ), and follows the driver root layout ( driver.md , ADR-0011 ): tool configuration in _config/ , one root CMakeLists.txt , platform code only in examples/<platform>/ , and an examples/host/ program built and run by the host tests. A library meant for ESP-IDF adds the ESP_PLATFORM branch of the root CMakeLists.txt (and _config/Kconfig if it has options) and an examples/esp32/ ; one that is not has neither. It is versioned and released like a driver, with one target and one include root. pincfg ¶ pincfg is a generic, header-only C++20 framework for pin tables: X-macro rows that name the function, the chip and the drive mode. The framework holds no board's pins. Each board HAL carries its own pin table built with it ( hal.md ). MCU pin numbers appear only in a board HAL's pin table and its bind. A host build with an empty table compiles for tests.

Rules: Base* classes are the MCU boundary, one of the three places with virtual functions ( ADR-0016 ): the bind creates the concrete object, and everything above holds a Base*& . Initialize() is idempotent and EnsureInitialized() lazy; neither allocates after start-up. Exactly one family is compiled, chosen by KB_MCU=ESP32|STM32|HOST|NONE . NONE builds base/ only, for consumers that bring their own implementation or fakes. Every family's sources MUST compile in CI, including STM32 (with stub SDK headers if needed). Every header in mcu/<family>/ #error s when its family is not the one selected ( layers.md ). A header in base/ MUST NOT include a file that does not exist on every family. Variant differences inside a family use the vendor's capability macros, only in that family's folder. A peripheral that only one family has (the ESP32 RMT) gets a Base* interface in base/ and an implementation in that family's folder only; the drivers that need it are rows in the MCU gate table.
docs.title: interfaces

docs.text: One handler per chip, plus handlers/common/ : the adapter bases, kb::DelayUs() / kb::DelayMs() , the diagnostics header and the logger. The contract is in handler.md . The logger ( kb/handlers/common/Logger.h ) is the one logging API above the bind. It formats; drivers do not. Its sink is injected by the board HAL, so kb-core prints nothing on its own and carries no product's log format.
docs.title: handlers

docs.text: kb-core links each enabled driver's <chip>::<chip> target from its submodule in drivers/driver-<chip>/ . It does not copy file lists out of a driver. cmake/kb_build_settings.cmake holds the version, the options, the targets and the MCU gate table; it holds no sources of a driver. The options: Option Values Effect KB_MCU ESP32 , STM32 , HOST , NONE Compiles interfaces/mcu/<family>/ for that family only KB_RTOS FREERTOS , THREADX , NONE Compiles that rtos backend only KB_ENABLE_<CHIP> ON , OFF Compiles the handler and links its driver; nothing else turns a handler on KB_ENABLE_<FEATURE> ON , OFF Compiles an optional part ( KB_ENABLE_CANOPEN ) KB_BUILD_TESTS ON , OFF Host tests and doc snippets The MCU gate : configure fails when an enabled chip's row in the gate table names another MCU than KB_MCU ( layers.md ). The table is generated from catalog/compat.yml , and CI checks the two agree. Under ESP-IDF the root CMakeLists.txt is also the component; Kconfig options are CONFIG_KB_* and map onto the CMake options in one place. FreeRTOS builds run at 1000 Hz ( threading-and-timing.md ).
docs.title: kb-core build

docs.text: A library that is not part of kb-core (for example pincfg , or a utility used outside the stack) lives in its own repository, is created from kokeb-labs/driver-template ( python3 tools/setup.py --kind library ), and follows the driver root layout ( driver.md , ADR-0011 ): tool configuration in _config/ , one root CMakeLists.txt , platform code only in examples/<platform>/ , and an examples/host/ program built and run by the host tests. A library meant for ESP-IDF adds the ESP_PLATFORM branch of the root CMakeLists.txt (and _config/Kconfig if it has options) and an examples/esp32/ ; one that is not has neither. It is versioned and released like a driver, with one target and one include root.
docs.title: Standalone libraries

docs.text: pincfg is a generic, header-only C++20 framework for pin tables: X-macro rows that name the function, the chip and the drive mode. The framework holds no board's pins. Each board HAL carries its own pin table built with it ( hal.md ). MCU pin numbers appear only in a board HAL's pin table and its bind. A host build with an empty table compiles for tests.
docs.title: pincfg

docs.text: Naming and style ¶ How Kokeb Labs code is named, laid out and formatted. The naming rules are enforced by readability-identifier-naming in the org .clang-tidy , and formatting by the org .clang-format . Decisions: ADR-0008 and, for drivers, ADR-0012 . Prefixes ¶ Code Namespace Macros Includes CMake A chip driver ( driver-<chip> ) <chip> <CHIP>_* , Kconfig CONFIG_<CHIP>_* "<chip>.hpp" find_package(<chip>) , <chip>::<chip> , options <CHIP>_* kb-core kb KB_* , Kconfig CONFIG_KB_* "kb/..." kb::utils , kb::rtos , kb::interfaces , kb::handlers ; options KB_* kb-hal-common kb::hal KB_HAL_* "kb/hal/..." kb::hal A driver never carries the kb prefix or any other org prefix; the prefix belongs to kb-core and the shared HAL only. Namespaces ¶ Code Namespace A chip driver <chip> ( pca9685 , tmc9660 ); internals in <chip>::detail kb-core kb , or kb::<area> ( kb::can ) kb-hal-common kb::hal A board HAL <board> ; the bind in <board>::bsp A product <board>::app Namespaces are lower case. using namespace is not allowed in headers. Anonymous namespaces are for .cpp -local helpers only. Identifiers ¶ Kind Style Examples Classes, structs, enums, unions, type aliases, concepts PascalCase Zp100Handler , Config , I2cPort A chip driver class the part number PCA9685 , TMC9660 Template parameters PascalCase Port , Derived , SpiType Functions and public / protected methods PascalCase Initialize() , ReadPressurePa() , SetDuty() Private methods camelBack writeReg() , selectBank() Parameters and local variables snake_case channel , timeout_ms Public data members (struct fields) snake_case config.ready_timeout_ms Private and protected data members snake_case_ initialized_ , bus_mutex_ Constants ( constexpr , static const , global const ) kPascalCase kNumChannels , kDefaultAddress Enumerators PascalCase Error::NotInitialized , Oversampling::X8 Macros UPPER_CASE , prefixed with the repository or part PCA9685_VERSION_MAJOR , CONFIG_ZP100_ODR_HZ , KB_ENABLE_PCA9685 Files as the main type: PascalCase in kb-core and HALs ( Zp100Handler.h ); <chip>_<part>.hpp in drivers pca9685_i2c_interface.hpp Allowed exceptions, also allowed by the tidy config: Datasheet names in UPPER_CASE for register addresses, bit fields and enumerators that mirror the datasheet ( MODE1 , PRE_SCALE , GEN_CFG1 ), and for GpioSignal::ACTIVE / INACTIVE . Vocabulary-type members ok() , begin() , end() , size() , data() , empty() , so Result<T> and containers read like the standard library. C-style APIs kb-core keeps: the os_* functions in kb::rtos and the kb_*_t types in kb::interfaces . New code does not add to them. Host test cases named test_<what> in tests/ . Verbs and units ¶ Read* touches the bus; Get* returns cached state and never does I/O; Set* / Write* change the chip; Is* / Has* return bool and do no I/O. Quantities carry their unit as a suffix, in the identifier's own case: Unit In PascalCase In snake_case milliseconds, microseconds, seconds Ms , Us , S _ms , _us , _s hertz, kilohertz Hz , Khz _hz , _khz millivolts, volts Mv , V _mv , _v milliamps, microamps, amps Ma , Ua , A _ma , _ua , _a pascals, degrees Celsius Pa , C _pa , _c revolutions per minute, degrees Rpm , Deg _rpm , _deg percent, raw counts Pct , Counts _pct , _counts SetHitCurrentMa(uint16_t current_ma) , ReadTemperatureC() , timeout_ms . Not _mA , MilliAmps or a Unit enum parameter. - SI base units and integers are preferred. A float in a public API states its unit like any other value. Include roots and headers ¶ One include root per kb-core part: #include "kb/interfaces/BaseSpi.h" , #include "kb/rtos/RtosMutex.h" , #include "kb/utils/Status.h" . Drivers use their flat inc/ : #include "pca9685.hpp" . Relative paths that climb out of a repository or part ( "../../drivers/..." ) are not allowed. Every header has an #ifndef include guard, never #pragma once (MISRA C++:2023 Rule 19.2.1). Only comments come before #ifndef GUARD / #define GUARD , and #endif is the last line. The guard is <NAME>_<FILE_STEM>_<EXT> in upper case: the repository's name (the chip, or the library's CMake package), the file name without its extension in snake case, and the extension, with the name not repeated when the stem already starts with it: File Guard inc/ads7952.hpp ADS7952_HPP inc/ads7952_types.hpp ADS7952_TYPES_HPP inc/max22200_spi_interface.hpp MAX22200_SPI_INTERFACE_HPP src/ads7952.ipp ADS7952_IPP inc/ads7952_version.h.in (configured) ADS7952_VERSION_H tests/mock_ads7952.hpp ADS7952_MOCK_ADS7952_HPP inc/ring/MovingAverage.h in ring_buffer RING_BUFFER_MOVING_AVERAGE_H No leading underscore and no double underscore: those names are reserved. No #pragma of any kind and no _Pragma ; compiler options live in the build. python checks/source_checks.py guard --repo . <path> prints the guard a file needs, and python checks/source_checks.py scan --repo . runs the check CI runs ( KB-CPP-019 ). - Include order: the file's own header, then standard headers, then other repositories, then this repository; one blank line between groups. clang-format sorts within a group. - A header includes what it uses and compiles on its own. Formatting ¶ config/.clang-format : LLVM base, 2-space indent, 100-column limit, pointer and reference attached to the type ( uint8_t* data ), attached braces, short functions only when empty, template declarations on their own line. The column limit is 100 everywhere. Markdown wraps at 120 columns (markdownlint MD013 , tables and code blocks exempt). Static analysis ¶ config/.clang-tidy enables bugprone-* , clang-analyzer-* , cppcoreguidelines-* , modernize-* , performance-* , portability-* and readability-* , turns off the checks that fight register-level code (each with its reason in the file), and sets the naming rules above. Using the configs in a repository ¶ Copy both files into the repository's _config/ unchanged. Do not add root copies or symlinks ( ADR-0011 ); every tool is given the path: clang-format --style=file:_config/.clang-format , clang-tidy --config-file=_config/.clang-tidy . Editors that find the files only by name (clangd, CLion) use a local copy listed in .gitignore . Point the lint workflow at them: uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-cpp-lint.yml@v1 with : clang_version : "20" clang_format_config : "_config/.clang-format" clang_tidy_config : "_config/.clang-tidy" The shared workflow links the files into its own checkout; the repository carries no link. 3. Fix findings in new and changed code. Existing findings are fixed in their own PRs, not mixed into features. 4. Suppress a finding only with // NOLINT(<check>): <reason> or // NOLINTNEXTLINE(<check>): <reason> . A bare NOLINT is not allowed. A rule that is wrong for every repository is changed here, in both configs and on this page together. Comments ¶ Public API is documented with Doxygen ( /// or /** */ ): what it does, parameters with units, the Error or Status values it returns, and whether it does I/O. See docs.md . Comments say why. Datasheet references name the section or table ( SBASB22 Table 7-12 ). No commented-out code, no TODO without an issue link, no author or date banners, no tool attribution lines.

docs.text: Product contract ¶ What a product repository provides: the application firmware for one board, built on that board's HAL. Products and their board HALs live in the product's own organization or repository, not in kokeb-labs . This page is the contract they follow when they build on the stack. Layout ¶ <product>/ ├── main/ or app/ the application: tasks, protocols, state machines, faults namespace <board>::app ├── platform/ the only folder that may use ESP-IDF directly ├── hal/ the board HAL: a folder, or a submodule pinned to a release tag ├── version_lock.txt the pin manifest (release.md) ├── sdkconfig.defaults CONFIG_FREERTOS_HZ=1000 and the product's settings ├── partitions.csv ├── docs/, CHANGELOG.md, LICENSE, README.md └── _config/ Rules ¶ What the application uses ¶ The application MUST use only: the HAL facade and its managers' public API, kb::rtos , and the kb-core logger. It MUST NOT include handlers, drivers, Base* headers, mcu/<family>/ classes or raw FreeRTOS outside platform/ ( layers.md ). The HAL boundary lint runs over the product too. Board functions the facade does not offer yet (for example CAN) are added to the HAL first, then used. Product-specific code stays in the product or its board HAL. A need that kb-core or a driver cannot meet is raised as an issue for a generic extension point, not patched into core ( layers.md ). platform/ ¶ Holds app_main() , partition and OTA handling, the console, and other start-up code that needs ESP-IDF. app_main() creates the facade, calls Initialize() , reports a failed start-up through the fault catalogue, and starts the application tasks. It contains no application logic. Faults ¶ The product has one fault catalogue: every fault it can report, with its ID, its protocol code (for example a CANopen EMCY code), its severity and the reaction (stop, derate, warn). kb::Status plus ManagerId map onto the catalogue in one table ( errors.md ). The catalogue is documented on the product's Operation page. A failed start-up MUST leave every actuator in its safe state, which the facade's fail-closed start-up guarantees; the product then reports the fault and does not start the control tasks. Tasks and timing ¶ Tasks, stack sizes, priorities and core affinity are named in one header ( <board>::app::kTaskConfig ) and created through kb::rtos ( threading-and-timing.md ). The product runs FreeRTOS at 1 kHz. Configuration ¶ sdkconfig.defaults only; no committed full sdkconfig . Product settings that change per unit (calibration, node ID) live in NVS through the HAL's NVS manager, with a documented layout and version. A change that moves or reformats NVS is listed under ### Breaking in the changelog with the erase or migration step. Releases ¶ A product release is a firmware release: the tag builds the firmware and attaches .bin , .elf , sha256 and the effective sdkconfig ; a missing artifact fails the release ( release.md ). The firmware reports its own version, the release train it is built on, and the tag and SHA of every pinned submodule (the provenance header). version_lock.txt lists REF_<repo>=vX.Y.Z@<sha> for every submodule, and CI checks it against the pins. Tests and docs ¶ Application logic that does not need hardware (state machines, fault mapping, protocol encoding) has host tests, built against the HAL's host bind. The product page set in docs.md ; decisions specific to the product are ADRs in its own docs/adr/ .
docs.title: Product contract

docs.text: Release ¶ How Kokeb Labs repositories are versioned, tagged and released, how tested sets become release trains, and the order a release wave follows. Decisions: ADR-0007 and ADR-0013 . Versions ¶ Independent SemVer per repository , starting at 0.1.0 . Drivers change at different rates, so a lockstep version would force empty releases. The combinations that are tested together are named by release trains instead ( Release trains ). One version for all of kb-core. kb::utils , kb::rtos , kb::interfaces and kb::handlers are released together under kb-core's version, even when they are installed as separate packages. 0.x makes no API stability promise. A breaking change bumps the minor ( 0.1.0 → 0.2.0 ); a fix or an addition bumps the patch ( 0.1.0 → 0.1.1 ). 1.0.0 is declared per repository, by ADR, when its API is meant to hold. ci-tools is the exception : it is at 1.x with a moving major tag ( v1 ) that callers pin, and follows its own versioning page. One version source per repository: cmake/<chip>_build_settings.cmake in a driver, cmake/kb_build_settings.cmake in kb-core. The generated version header, driver.yml , an idf_component.yml where one exists, and any hand-written copy are derived from it or checked against it. Licence in a release ¶ Every firmware and tooling release is MIT; a release of a hardware design is CERN-OHL-P-2.0 ( ADR-0009 ). Release notes do not grant use of the Kokeb Labs name or logos ( trademark policy ). Tags and release candidates ¶ Tags are vX.Y.Z on a commit that is on main (or on release/x.y for a maintenance release). Release candidates are vX.Y.Z-rc.N . The release-tags ruleset protects every v* tag on public repositories. A release is a named, immutable snapshot that meets all of: CI was green on that commit with the pinned ESP-IDF; the changelog section for the version is complete; it builds with add_subdirectory() and with find_package() ( <chip>::<chip> for a driver, kb::<part> for kb-core); the release notes state its bench status: the MCU, board and test list it ran on, or CI-only . A repository that no board has run yet can only be released as CI-only, and MAY skip the release candidate. A release candidate is promoted by tagging the same commit vX.Y.Z . If anything changed, the next candidate is -rc.N+1 . Changelog ¶ Every repository has a CHANGELOG.md in Keep a Changelog form: # Changelog ## [Unreleased] ### Breaking - `Initialize()` now returns `Result<void>` instead of `bool` . ### Added - `ReadFifoLevel()` . ### Fixed - Bus errors during `ReadPressurePa()` were reported as `Ok` with a stale value. ## [0.1.0] - 2026-11-17 ## [Unreleased] is always the first section, and every PR that changes behaviour adds to it. Section headings are exactly ### Breaking , ### Added , ### Changed , ### Deprecated , ### Removed , ### Fixed , ### Security , in that order, each only when it has entries. Any breaking change is listed under ### Breaking , with what a caller has to change. A PR labelled breaking without a ### Breaking entry is not merged. Released sections are ## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD and are not edited afterwards except to fix links. Entries describe the effect for a user of the repository, not the commits. The release body is the changelog section, not generated notes. Release automation ¶ These workflows come from ci-tools ( kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/<name>.yml@v1 ). Until a repository has them, a maintainer does each step by hand and checks the same conditions. Workflow Does prepare-release (manual, input version ) Normalises changelog headings, rolls ## [Unreleased] into ## [X.Y.Z] - <date> , bumps every version declaration (build settings, driver.yml , hand-written headers), and opens a Release vX.Y.Z PR. Merging it tags the merge commit. release.yml (on a v* tag) Fails if the tag does not match the declared version or the commit is not on main / release/* ; creates the GitHub Release with the changelog section as the body; for products, attaches .bin , .elf , sha256 and sdkconfig and fails if any is missing. Docs publish (on a v* tag) Publishes the versioned docs with kokeb-docs . A -rc tag publishes without moving the latest alias. Pin check Checks each submodule against a release tag and the manifest or catalog/compat.yml : warns on PRs to main , fails on release/* and tag pushes, and checks the tagged commit is on main . Bump bot Opens a pin-bump PR in kb-core when a pinned driver tags a release. Tags that trigger other workflows are pushed with a GitHub App token, not the workflow token. Release workflows call reusable workflows at @v1 , never @main . Pins and the manifest ¶ kb-core includes each driver as a submodule in drivers/driver-<chip>/ , pinned to a release tag commit . The ESP-IDF component registry is not used for the stack (most drivers are not IDF components, and the host and STM32 builds need a non-IDF path). Board HALs and products pin kb-core and kb-hal-common the same way, and carry a version_lock.txt manifest, one line per submodule: REF_kb-core=v0.1.0@3f2a9c1e5b7d... REF_kb-hal-common=v0.1.0@9be0d4c7a1f2... The firmware reports the tag and SHA of every submodule it was built from, and the release train. Tag -rc.1 bottom-up in the order above. Bench on real boards: the bench lists from the merged PRs, on the boards named in the train's test list. docs.text: Independent SemVer per repository , starting at 0.1.0 . Drivers change at different rates, so a lockstep version would force empty releases. The combinations that are tested together are named by release trains instead ( Release trains ). One version for all of kb-core. kb::utils , kb::rtos , kb::interfaces and kb::handlers are released together under kb-core's version, even when they are installed as separate packages. 0.x makes no API stability promise. A breaking change bumps the minor ( 0.1.0 → 0.2.0 ); a fix or an addition bumps the patch ( 0.1.0 → 0.1.1 ). 1.0.0 is declared per repository, by ADR, when its API is meant to hold. ci-tools is the exception : it is at 1.x with a moving major tag ( v1 ) that callers pin, and follows its own versioning page. One version source per repository: cmake/<chip>_build_settings.cmake in a driver, cmake/kb_build_settings.cmake in kb-core. The generated version header, driver.yml , an idf_component.yml where one exists, and any hand-written copy are derived from it or checked against it.

docs.text: Tags are vX.Y.Z on a commit that is on main (or on release/x.y for a maintenance release). Release candidates are vX.Y.Z-rc.N . The release-tags ruleset protects every v* tag on public repositories. A release is a named, immutable snapshot that meets all of: CI was green on that commit with the pinned ESP-IDF; the changelog section for the version is complete; it builds with add_subdirectory() and with find_package() ( <chip>::<chip> for a driver, kb::<part> for kb-core); the release notes state its bench status: the MCU, board and test list it ran on, or CI-only . A repository that no board has run yet can only be released as CI-only, and MAY skip the release candidate. A release candidate is promoted by tagging the same commit vX.Y.Z . If anything changed, the next candidate is -rc.N+1 .

docs.text: Every repository has a CHANGELOG.md in Keep a Changelog form: # Changelog ## [Unreleased] ### Breaking - `Initialize()` now returns `Result<void>` instead of `bool` . ### Added - `ReadFifoLevel()` . ### Fixed - Bus errors during `ReadPressurePa()` were reported as `Ok` with a stale value. ## [0.1.0] - 2026-11-17 ## [Unreleased] is always the first section, and every PR that changes behaviour adds to it. Released sections are ## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD and are not edited afterwards except to fix links. Entries describe the effect for a user of the repository, not the commits. The release body is the changelog section, not generated notes.

docs.text: Repository governance ¶ How every Kokeb Labs repository is set up and how changes reach main . The org has one maintainer today and is open to contributors; the rules already work for more people, and the one rule that changes when a second maintainer joins is called out below. Decision: ADR-0015 . Settings are kept as code in this repository's org/ folder ( org/kokeb_org.py ). It shows the plan without --apply ; only an organization owner runs it with --apply . Branches ¶ main is the only long-lived branch. Nobody pushes to it; every change is a pull request, including the maintainer's own. Work branches are named by kind, then a short topic in kebab case: Prefix For feat/<topic> New behaviour or API fix/<topic> A bug fix docs/<topic> Documentation only ci/<topic> Workflows, lint and build configuration chore/<topic> Pin bumps, version bumps, renames, housekeeping release/x.y A maintenance line for an older minor ( release/0.1 ), created from its tag by a maintainer, changed only by PR Branches are deleted automatically when their PR merges (see Merge settings ). A submodule never points at an unmerged branch. Pull requests ¶ Squash merge only , and the PR title becomes the commit subject on main . Write the title as a commit subject: imperative, under about 72 characters, no trailing period ( Add ZP100 FIFO read ). One logical change per PR, ideally under about 400 lines of diff. Larger work is a series of PRs, each green. The PR template ( .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md in kokeb-labs/.github , inherited by every repository without its own) is filled in: summary, why, how it was verified (CI, host tests, which MCU and board), the checklist. Docs and changelog in the same PR as the code: the README or docs/ page for any behaviour or API change, and an entry under ## [Unreleased] in CHANGELOG.md ( release.md ). A deviation from the standard is named in the PR description with the rule and the tracking issue. A pin bump is its own PR that links the PR or release it pulls in and notes API or build-setting changes. No attribution lines in commits, PR descriptions, issues or comments other than the DCO sign-off: no Co-Authored-By: trailers for tools, no "Generated with" footers. Authorship is the account that opened the PR. Review : every conversation resolved before merge. While the org has one maintainer, no approving review is required and the maintainer merges their own PRs, always through a PR. When a second maintainer joins, every PR needs one approving review from a code owner ( Review mode ). Contributions and the DCO ¶ Contributions are accepted under the repository's licence (MIT; CERN-OHL-P-2.0 for hardware designs, ADR-0009 ). There is no contributor licence agreement. Every commit carries a Signed-off-by: line certifying the Developer Certificate of Origin : git commit -s . The name and email match the commit author. CI checks every commit of a PR for the sign-off. The DCO job is one of the jobs the CI gate needs, so a PR with an unsigned commit cannot merge. A missing sign-off is fixed on the branch with git rebase --signoff main and a force-push of that branch (never of main ). Issues and labels ¶ Issues use the org forms: Bug report , Driver request and Feature request . Blank issues are off; questions go to the org discussions ( https://github.com/orgs/kokeb-labs/discussions ), and vulnerabilities to a private security advisory ( Security ). Every repository uses this label set: Label Meaning bug Something behaves wrong (set by the bug form) enhancement New capability or API change (set by the feature form) driver-request A new chip driver (set by the driver request form) safety Can damage hardware or cause unsafe motion, heat or pressure; fixed before anything else breaking Changes a public API, a config layout or NVS; needs ### Breaking in the changelog standard Brings the repository in line with this standard documentation Docs only ci Workflows and tooling dependencies Dependency and action updates (set by Dependabot) good first issue Small and well described The settings script creates the labels. CODEOWNERS ¶ GitHub has no org-wide CODEOWNERS, so each repository carries .github/CODEOWNERS : # Default reviewers for every path in this repository. * @N3b3x When the maintainers team exists, the line becomes * @kokeb-labs/maintainers . A repository started from a template already has the file. Rulesets ¶ The rulesets apply to every public repository: Ruleset Applies to Rules Bypass main-integrity default branch no deletion, no force push, linear history, signed commits nobody main-review default branch changes through a PR, squash only, resolved conversations, required check CI gate / gate ; 0 approvals while solo nobody release-tags v* tags no deletion, no moving org owners, to fix a tag pushed by mistake before its release is published Signed commits on main cost a contributor nothing: GitHub signs the squash commit it creates when a PR merges. Commits on work branches need not be signed. Review mode ¶ Maintainers main-review requires One A PR, resolved conversations and a green CI gate / gate ; 0 approvals Two or more The same, plus one approving review from a code owner; stale approvals dismissed on push The switch is one change to the ruleset, made by an owner when the second maintainer joins, together with the CODEOWNERS change above. The required check ¶ Every repository's CI ends in one gate job from the reusable ru-ci-gate.yml ( kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-ci-gate.yml@v1 ), named CI gate , so the single required status check is always: CI gate / gate The gate is required only once the repository has the job, because a required check that never runs blocks every PR. A repository created from a template has it from the first commit. The gate MUST list every other job in needs , including the DCO check, and use if: always() ; with verify_needs: true (the default) the gate checks this itself. Security ¶ Every public repository has secret scanning, push protection, Dependabot alerts, Dependabot security updates, and private vulnerability reporting . Vulnerabilities are reported through a private security advisory on the repository, never in an issue; the org SECURITY.md says how. Workflows follow least privilege: permissions: contents: read at the top, wider permissions only on the job that needs them, and no secrets in workflows triggered by forks. Dependabot ¶ Every repository with workflows has .github/dependabot.yml for GitHub Actions; repositories with Python tooling add pip : version : 2 updates : - package-ecosystem : github-actions directory : / schedule : interval : weekly labels : [ dependencies ] commit-message : prefix : "ci" Dependabot does not manage submodules: it tracks branches, and kb-core pins release tags. Submodule pins move through the bump bot and pin-bump PRs ( release.md ). Reusable workflows are pinned to the major tag ( @v1 ), which Dependabot leaves alone. Merge settings ¶ Every repository, public and private, has Automatically delete head branches on and allows squash merging only, with the PR title as the default commit title. The main-review ruleset enforces squash on public repositories; on private repositories it is the repository setting alone. Licence and trademarks ¶ Firmware, libraries, drivers and tooling are MIT. Hardware designs are CERN-OHL-P-2.0 ( ADR-0009 ). Each repository carries its own LICENSE . The MIT licence covers the code, not the Kokeb Labs name or logos. Their use is governed by the trademark policy . A fork distributed as its own project uses its own name; drivers make that easy because they carry no brand ( ADR-0012 ). Metadata ¶ Every repository's description, homepage and topics are kept with the org settings in org/ , and the portal's catalogue reads them. Change them by PR, then an owner applies them. Repository root ¶ The root holds only what GitHub or a tool requires at the root and what a reader looks for first ( ADR-0011 ). For a driver or standalone library: README.md , LICENSE , CHANGELOG.md , CMakeLists.txt , AGENTS.md , CLAUDE.md , .gitignore , .gitmodules , driver.yml (drivers), and the folders .github/ , .claude/ , _config/ , cmake/ , docs/ , examples/ , inc/ , src/ , tests/ , tools/ . Other kinds keep their own source folders (kb-core: utils/ , rtos/ , interfaces/ , handlers/ , drivers/ , catalog/ ) and list any other root file a tool requires (such as CMakePresets.json ) in their AGENTS.md . Tool configuration lives in _config/ and nowhere else; no symlinks anywhere in the repository. CONTRIBUTING.md and SECURITY.md live in .github/ (or are inherited from kokeb-labs/.github ). A reviewer refuses a PR that adds anything else to the root without a reason a tool imposes. Creating a repository ¶ Create it from the template for its kind, in the kokeb-labs org, public: gh repo create kokeb-labs/driver-<chip> --public --template kokeb-labs/driver-template gh repo clone kokeb-labs/driver-<chip> && cd driver-<chip> python3 tools/setup.py --kind driver --name <chip> --bus spi | i2c | uart | adc --description "..." The template carries the shell: CMake layout, CI workflows with the gate and the DCO check, _config/ with every tool configuration, docs page set, driver.yml , CODEOWNERS , .github/CONTRIBUTING.md , .github/SECURITY.md , AGENTS.md , CLAUDE.md and .claude/skills/ , in the root layout of ADR-0011. --platforms host,esp32 picks the example platforms ( host always). The templates by kind: Kind Template How Chip driver driver-template tools/setup.py --kind driver Standalone library driver-template tools/setup.py --kind library kb-core handler templates/handler/ in kb-core its scaffold script, see kb-core AGENTS.md Board HAL board-hal-template (planned); until then the example in kb-hal-common in the product's organization Add the metadata in org/ by PR to kokeb-labs/.github ; an owner applies it with the settings script. Apply the settings : merge settings, security, rulesets and labels, by the settings script. Require the gate once the first CI run has produced CI gate / gate ( The required check ). Wire it in : for a driver, add it to kb-core as drivers/driver-<chip>/ , pinned to its first release tag, with its handler and its catalog/compat.yml entry ( handler checklist ). Then follow the checklist for its kind in checklists/ . Archiving ¶ A repository that is superseded gets the legacy topic and a [Legacy] ... superseded by <repo>. description in the metadata, a README note pointing to its successor, and is archived. Archived repositories are skipped by the settings script.

The MIT licence covers the code, not the Kokeb Labs name or logos. Their use is governed by the trademark policy . A fork distributed as its own project uses its own name; drivers make that easy because they carry no brand ( ADR-0012 ).
docs.title: Licence and trademarks

docs.text: Every repository's description, homepage and topics are kept with the org settings in org/ , and the portal's catalogue reads them. Change them by PR, then an owner applies them.
docs.title: Metadata

docs.text: The root holds only what GitHub or a tool requires at the root and what a reader looks for first ( ADR-0011 ). For a driver or standalone library: README.md , LICENSE , CHANGELOG.md , CMakeLists.txt , AGENTS.md , CLAUDE.md , .gitignore , .gitmodules , driver.yml (drivers), and the folders .github/ , .claude/ , _config/ , cmake/ , docs/ , examples/ , inc/ , src/ , tests/ , tools/ . Other kinds keep their own source folders (kb-core: utils/ , rtos/ , interfaces/ , handlers/ , drivers/ , catalog/ ) and list any other root file a tool requires (such as CMakePresets.json ) in their AGENTS.md . Tool configuration lives in _config/ and nowhere else; no symlinks anywhere in the repository. CONTRIBUTING.md and SECURITY.md live in .github/ (or are inherited from kokeb-labs/.github ). A reviewer refuses a PR that adds anything else to the root without a reason a tool imposes.
docs.title: Repository root

docs.text: Create it from the template for its kind, in the kokeb-labs org, public: gh repo create kokeb-labs/driver-<chip> --public --template kokeb-labs/driver-template gh repo clone kokeb-labs/driver-<chip> && cd driver-<chip> python3 tools/setup.py --kind driver --name <chip> --bus spi | i2c | uart | adc --description "..." The template carries the shell: CMake layout, CI workflows with the gate and the DCO check, _config/ with every tool configuration, docs page set, driver.yml , CODEOWNERS , .github/CONTRIBUTING.md , .github/SECURITY.md , AGENTS.md , CLAUDE.md and .claude/skills/ , in the root layout of ADR-0011. --platforms host,esp32 picks the example platforms ( host always). The templates by kind: Kind Template How Chip driver driver-template tools/setup.py --kind driver Standalone library driver-template tools/setup.py --kind library kb-core handler templates/handler/ in kb-core its scaffold script, see kb-core AGENTS.md Board HAL board-hal-template (planned); until then the example in kb-hal-common in the product's organization Add the metadata in org/ by PR to kokeb-labs/.github ; an owner applies it with the settings script. Apply the settings : merge settings, security, rulesets and labels, by the settings script. Require the gate once the first CI run has produced CI gate / gate ( The required check ). Wire it in : for a driver, add it to kb-core as drivers/driver-<chip>/ , pinned to its first release tag, with its handler and its catalog/compat.yml entry ( handler checklist ). Then follow the checklist for its kind in checklists/ .

docs.text: A repository that is superseded gets the legacy topic and a [Legacy] ... superseded by <repo>. description in the metadata, a README note pointing to its successor, and is archived. Archived repositories are skipped by the settings script.

docs.text: Threading and timing ¶ One lock, one clock and one delay above the platform bind, and one tick rate everywhere. Decision for the tick: ADR-0006 . Who may call the RTOS ¶ Code RTOS access Drivers None. Drivers do not lock, sleep or create tasks; they wait only through the port's delay hooks. kb-core utils , pincfg None. kb-core interfaces/base/ None directly; MAY use kb::rtos types. mcu/<family>/ classes MAY use the SDK's own primitives internally. kb-core rtos/ The only code that includes RTOS headers, and only in the selected backend ( freertos/ , threadx/ , none/ ). Handlers, HALs, products kb::rtos only. bsp_bind/<family>/ , product platform/ MAY use the SDK and RTOS directly for start-up and family-specific work. Raw xTaskCreate , xSemaphoreTake , vTaskDelay , std::mutex or std::thread above the bind is a defect. KB_RTOS=FREERTOS|THREADX|NONE selects the backend and defines exactly one of KB_RTOS_FREERTOS , KB_RTOS_THREADX or KB_RTOS_NONE (host tests and bare-metal). Code above kb::rtos MUST work on all three; anything backend-specific stays inside the backend folder. One lock ¶ The only mutex above the bind is RtosMutex , taken with MutexLockGuard ( RtosUniqueLock<RtosMutex> ): #include "kb/rtos/RtosMutex.h" kb :: Result < float > Zp100Handler :: ReadPressurePa () noexcept { MutexLockGuard lock ( mutex_ ); // ... } No other mutex family exists above the bind: no per-HAL mutex wrappers, no private lock inside a protocol stack. A component that needs a lock takes an RtosMutex . Locks are held for the duration of one call. No lock is held across a DelayMs() longer than the operation requires, across a callback into other code, or across a call into another handler. Lock order: handler mutex, then bus mutex. Managers call handlers without holding their own lock when they can; when they cannot, the order is manager, handler, bus. ISRs never take a mutex. They set an OsEventFlags bit or give a SignalSemaphore and return. One clock ¶ The only time source above the bind is kb::MonotonicUs() ( kb/interfaces/Time.h ): microseconds since boot, 64-bit, monotonic, safe from any task and from ISRs. base/ declares it; the selected family's mcu/<family>/ folder defines it. esp_timer_get_time() , xTaskGetTickCount() , HAL_GetTick() and std::chrono::steady_clock are not used above the bind. The bind's MonotonicMicros() returns the same counter and exists so the host bind can drive a fake clock in tests. Durations are uint32_t or uint64_t with a unit suffix ( timeout_ms , period_us ). Deadlines are compared by subtraction, never with > : const uint64_t deadline_us = kb :: MonotonicUs () + timeout_us ; while ( static_cast < int64_t > ( kb :: MonotonicUs () - deadline_us ) < 0 ) { /* poll */ } Delays ¶ A delay waits at least the requested time, never less. Delay Call Behaviour 1 ms and longer os_delay_msec(ms) ( kb::rtos ) Blocks the task. Converts to ticks rounding up, then adds one tick, because the first tick can arrive at once; at 1 kHz a 1 ms delay waits between 1 and 2 ms Under 1 ms kb::DelayUs(us) ( kb/handlers/common/Delay.h ) Busy-waits on kb::MonotonicUs() until at least us have passed; no RTOS call In a driver the port's DelayUs() / DelayMs() hooks Implemented by the adapter with the two rows above kb::DelayUs() with 1000 µs or more rounds up to whole milliseconds and calls os_delay_msec() , so a datasheet minimum of 2.5 ms never becomes 2 ms. A delay of 0 returns at once (or yields, on an RTOS backend); it does not wait a tick. Busy-waits longer than 100 µs SHOULD be avoided in tasks above idle priority; restructure as a poll with a millisecond delay. kb::DelayUs() and kb::DelayMs() MUST NOT test ESP_PLATFORM or any MCU macro; the MCU-specific part is in kb::MonotonicUs() and the rtos backend. The 1 kHz tick ¶ Every FreeRTOS project runs at 1000 Hz: products, board HALs, kb-core and every driver's examples/esp32 project. ESP-IDF's default of 100 Hz turns a 1 ms wait into 10 to 20 ms, and the millisecond helpers in kb::rtos assume 1 kHz. Set CONFIG_FREERTOS_HZ=1000 in sdkconfig.defaults . A generated sdkconfig is never committed ( ADR-0018 ): a project that still has one deletes it and moves its settings into the defaults files, because a committed sdkconfig overrides them. Convert milliseconds with pdMS_TO_TICKS() (inside the rtos backend) or the kb::rtos helpers. Never pass a raw tick count that assumes a rate. At 1 kHz, pdMS_TO_TICKS() overflows its 32-bit arithmetic above about 71 minutes, and the tick counter wraps after about 49.7 days: compare tick deadlines with (int32_t)(now - deadline) > 0 . The driver and board HAL templates write the setting into new projects. CI SHOULD fail a build whose effective CONFIG_FREERTOS_HZ is not 1000. ThreadX builds SHOULD use a 1 kHz kernel tick as well, so timing behaves the same on STM32. Tasks ¶ Tasks are created through kb::rtos ( BaseThread , BaseThreadsManager ) by the product or a HAL manager, never by a handler or a driver. Stack sizes and priorities are named constants in one header per product ( <board>::app::kTaskConfig ), not literals at the call site. Core affinity is a product decision, in that header. HAL code does not assume a dual-core MCU. Work that must happen at a fixed rate uses PeriodicTimer or a task loop on os_delay_msec() with drift correction, not a chain of delays. What crosses tasks ¶ Data shared between tasks is either protected by one RtosMutex , passed through an OsQueue , or published with SeqlockSnapshot for one writer and many readers. Callbacks from handlers into the product run in the caller's task. A callback that must reach another task posts to a queue.
